tools.name: Shows a company could advertise on with particle
tools.description: Use as a buy-side prospect list: where an advertiser could go next, with the shows it already buys as the reason.

tools.name: Shows carrying a company's ads with particle
tools.description: Use for where a company advertises, ranked by volume, with the reads to sample. Pages are at most 24 rows.

tools.name: Sponsors that appear together with particle
tools.description: Use for who a sponsor shares ad breaks with: the advertisers that buy the same inventory.

tools.name: Ads in an episode with particle
tools.description: Use for exactly who advertised in one episode, with the offer and where in the episode the read sits.

tools.name: Sponsor leaderboard with particle
tools.description: Use for the biggest podcast advertisers overall, in a period, or on one network. For the top-ten snapshot use advertising/leaderboard/preview.

tools.name: Sponsor leaderboard, top ten with particle
tools.description: Use for a quick read of who is spending most on podcasts this week and who is climbing. For deeper pages, other windows or filters use advertising/leaderboard.

tools.name: Publisher advertising profile with particle
tools.description: Use for how a network is monetised and who buys across it. For its shows ranked by ad volume use advertising/publisher/shows.

tools.name: Shows of a publisher by ad volume with particle
tools.description: Use for which of a network's shows carry the advertising. For the same catalogue by popularity use podcasts/publisher/shows.

tools.name: Publisher advertising leaderboard with particle
tools.description: Use for which networks carry the most advertising, or monetise their catalogue most densely.

tools.name: Sponsors of a publisher with particle
tools.description: Use for who buys a network, and which of them buy it as a bundle: sort by podcast_coverage with a minimum.

tools.name: Show advertising profile with particle
tools.description: Use for who sponsors a show and how heavily it is monetised. For the full per-sponsor list use advertising/show/sponsors.

tools.name: Sponsors a show could pitch with particle
tools.description: Use as a prospecting list for a show selling its own inventory: who buys shows like mine and has not bought me.

tools.name: Sponsors of a show with particle
tools.description: Use for every advertiser on one show with counts and recency, or one company's brands on it. Set since and until on shows with extensive ad history to keep the query bounded.

tools.name: Sponsor profile with particle
tools.description: Use to find who is buying advertising, or to go from a sponsor back to the company paying for it. For where it runs use advertising/sponsor/shows.

tools.name: Publishers a sponsor buys across with particle
tools.description: Use to tell network buys from per-show buys: a sponsor at 60 to 100 percent coverage of several publishers is buying bundles.

tools.name: Sponsor directory with particle
tools.description: Use to find a sponsor by name or by company and pick up its id. For the biggest spenders use advertising/leaderboard.

tools.name: Ad reads of a sponsor with particle
tools.description: Use to read the actual ad reads for a sponsor, then podcasts/segment/transcript for the words of one.

tools.name: Shows a sponsor buys with particle
tools.description: Use for where an advertiser buys: the canonical footprint of one sponsor, or of a whole company across its brands.

tools.name: Trending sponsors with particle
tools.description: Use for which advertisers are ramping podcast spend right now, by airdate.

tools.name: Ad placements over time with particle
tools.description: Use for how an advertiser's podcast spend trends by week or month, optionally on one show or network, and its host-read mix.

tools.name: Publisher bias profile with particle
tools.description: Use for a network's political profile as a whole: how political its catalogue is and which way it leans.

tools.name: Publishers with shows in a bias bucket with particle
tools.description: Use for which publishers carry the most shows of one lean: the flip of a publisher's own bias profile.

tools.name: Analysed shows of a publisher with particle
tools.description: Use to list a network's shows by political lean, or only the ones in a bucket.

tools.name: Publisher bias leaderboard with particle
tools.description: Use for which networks lean furthest left or right, are most political, or most ideologically diverse.

tools.name: Show bias analysis with particle
tools.description: Use for where a show sits politically and why, with the evidence to quote. The bucket alone rides on every show record as bias.

tools.name: Entity chart edition with particle
tools.description: Use for what podcasts are talking about most this week in one domain: the most-mentioned shows, films, games, teams or players, or the most-booked guests, with movement since last edition.

tools.name: Entity charts with particle
tools.description: Use to see which charts exist (all, tv-series, movies, video-games, nfl, nba, guests and so on) and who leads each, before fetching one with charts/chart.

tools.name: Company competitors with particle
tools.description: Use for a company's competitive set with the reason each one is on it, before comparing their podcast presence or advertising.

tools.name: Company profile links with particle
tools.description: Use to get a company's handles, domain, CIK or ticker. The reverse, identifier to company, is entities/lookup.

tools.name: People at a company with particle
tools.description: Use to find executives and role holders at a company, or the marketing, brand and partnerships contacts a sponsorship conversation would go to.

tools.name: Company products with particle
tools.description: Use to see what a company sells, structured by segment and product line, for example to match an ad read's offer to a product.

tools.name: Company directory with particle
tools.description: Use to resolve a company by name, ticker, domain, CIK or Wikidata QID to the slug every company capability takes. The record itself is advertising/company.

tools.name: Entity record with particle
tools.description: Resolve one entity slug or ID to its knowledge-graph record and linked company or person. For where the entity was mentioned, use podcasts/mentions or podcasts/episodes/list with entity_id.

tools.name: Entity directory with particle
tools.description: Use for the most-discussed entities overall, in one show, or of one kind, or to fetch several entities by slug at once. Takes no free text; for a name use entities/search.

tools.name: Entity lookup by external identifier with particle
tools.description: Use when you hold a LinkedIn slug, a handle, a domain, a ticker or a CIK and need the Particle person or company: the reverse of the external-links capabilities.

tools.name: Entity search with particle
tools.description: Use to turn what someone typed into a specific person, company or entity and its slug, before asking what was said about it with podcasts/mentions or filtering episodes by it. Searching episodes directly is better when the topic, not a name, is the question.

tools.name: Topic profile with particle
tools.description: Use to place a topic in the taxonomy and see its neighbours. For the shows in it use podcasts/list with topic_id; for episodes, podcasts/episodes/list. This returns classification, not passages.

tools.name: Topics with particle
tools.description: Use to find the topic_id that podcasts/search, podcasts/list and the guest capabilities filter on. Walk down from the roots by passing parent_id.

tools.name: Types with particle
tools.description: Use to see what the type filter on entities/list can take. Skip it when listing without a filter.

tools.name: Person profile links with particle
tools.description: Use to get a person's LinkedIn or social handles. The reverse, handle to person, is entities/lookup.

tools.name: Guest profile with particle
tools.description: Use when the question is about someone as a podcast guest: how often they appear, where, and since when. For the episode list use people/guest/appearances.

tools.name: Guest appearances with particle
tools.description: Use for where someone has appeared, episode by episode, to read what they said: take episode.id to podcasts/transcript with speaker set to their name.

tools.name: Shows a guest could appear on with particle
tools.description: Use to build a pitch list for a guest: the shows most like the ones that already booked them, with the venues to cite.

tools.name: Guest directory with particle
tools.description: Use to find guests by name, by show, by topic or by how often they appear, and pick up the person slug. For who is currently making the rounds use people/guests/trending.

tools.name: Shows a guest has appeared on with particle
tools.description: Use for the set of shows behind a guest rather than the episodes: which shows book them and how often.

tools.name: Trending guests with particle
tools.description: Use for who is doing the podcast circuit right now: a book launch, a product unveil, a news moment, or someone new. For a steady-state directory use people/guests.

tools.name: Person profile with particle
tools.description: Use to go from a name on an episode to the person: who they are, where they work and worked, and their profile links. For their podcast appearances use people/guest.

tools.name: Guest roster of a show with particle
tools.description: Use for who has been on a show and how often. For who it could book next use people/show-recommended-guests.

tools.name: Guests a show could book with particle
tools.description: Use as a booking pipeline for a show: guests its peers chose that it has not had yet.

tools.name: Episode clip with particle
tools.description: Use when a segment needs to be cited as a playable range rather than as text. For its words call podcasts/clip/transcript.

tools.name: Clip directory with particle
tools.description: Use to browse quotable moments by show, speaker or kind. For clips about a subject, search episodes: matching clips ride inside each search result.

tools.name: Clip transcript with particle
tools.description: Use to quote a clip verbatim with speaker labels, or export it as subtitles with format srt.

tools.name: Podcast episode with particle
tools.description: Use episode.id from a search match to get the full record and, when available, its web URL or direct audio stream. Neither link is guaranteed. For what was said, fetch podcasts/transcript.

tools.name: Episode clips with particle
tools.description: Use for the quotable moments of an episode as bounded, playable ranges with a kind and a speaker.

tools.name: Entities in an episode with particle
tools.description: Use for what an episode was about in named things: the companies, people and products it discussed, ranked by salience. For where each one came up in the dialogue use podcasts/transcript/mentions.

tools.name: Related episodes with particle
tools.description: Use for who else covered this: the same story or subject on other shows, optionally within a week of the episode.

tools.name: Episode segments with particle
tools.description: Use to see the structure of an episode and pick the section to read: which time ranges are ads to skip, where the interview starts, what each discussion covers. Then podcasts/segment/transcript for the words.

tools.name: Episode feed with particle
tools.description: Use to poll for new episodes of a set of shows or topics as they are transcribed: a resumable, strictly ordered pull. A filter is required. For a one-off list by date use podcasts/episodes/list.

tools.name: Episode directory with particle
tools.description: Use for episode-level filtering without dialogue: every episode a person spoke on, every episode featuring a company, a show's episodes in a date range, episodes in a language. When the question is about what was said, search episodes instead.

tools.name: Episode lookup by platform id with particle
tools.description: Use when you hold a Spotify, Apple Podcasts or YouTube episode link, a platform episode id, or an RSS guid and need the Particle episode id to read its transcript. A transcript_status of transcribed means the transcript can be read now; requestable means it has not been transcribed yet. Guids match exactly as supplied.

tools.name: Episode speakers with particle
tools.description: Use to find who was on an episode and in what role, with the person slug to follow into people/profile or people/guest. Ask for the advertiser role to see who voiced the sponsor reads.

tools.name: Episode search with particle
tools.description: Use to find episodes that discussed something. This is the entry point: it returns ids the other podcast capabilities take. For every line about one person or company use podcasts/mentions instead.

tools.name: Episode counts over time with particle
tools.description: Use for a trend rather than a list: how often a person appeared by month, how a show's output changed, how many episodes discussed a term each week. One call replaces paging the episode list per period.

tools.name: Episode topics with particle
tools.description: Use to classify an episode by subject area, or to pick up a topic_id for filtering shows and episodes.

tools.name: Show directory with particle
tools.description: Use to browse shows by attribute rather than by name: a topic, a language, a brand-suitability tier, a length band, a cadence, an ad-free or interview format. For a name, podcasts/search is the canonical search.

tools.name: Show lookup by platform id with particle
tools.description: Use when you already hold an Apple collection id, Spotify show id, YouTube channel id or RSS feed URL and need the Particle podcast deterministically. For a name, use podcasts/search.

tools.name: Dialogue mentions of an entity with particle
tools.description: Use for every line of dialogue about one person or company across podcasts: the read-everything-about-X call. Resolve the subject with entities/search first. For dialogue by topic or exact phrase use podcasts/episodes/search.

tools.name: Mention counts over time with particle
tools.description: Use for how mentions of a person or company trend by day, week or month, optionally within one show or network. One call instead of paging podcasts/mentions per period.

tools.name: Publisher profile with particle
tools.description: Use to go from a show's publisher reference to the network record. For the network's shows call podcasts/publisher/shows; for its advertising, bias or suitability roll-ups use the capabilities under those concepts.

tools.name: Publisher directory with particle
tools.description: Use to find a network's slug by name before asking about its shows, advertising, bias or suitability.

tools.name: Shows of a publisher with particle
tools.description: Use to walk a network's catalogue by audience. For the same catalogue ranked by ad volume use advertising/publisher/shows.

tools.name: Show search with particle
tools.description: Use to turn a show name into its slug and record. To find what was said inside one, search episodes instead: this matches show metadata, not transcripts. For an Apple, Spotify or YouTube id use podcasts/lookup.

tools.name: Episode segment with particle
tools.description: Use to see what a matched segment is (an interview, a topic discussion, an ad) and its time range. For its text call podcasts/segment/transcript.

tools.name: Segment directory with particle
tools.description: Use to pull one kind of section across a show: every interview, every ad read, every topic discussion in a date range. For one episode's structure use podcasts/episode/segments.

tools.name: Segment transcript with particle
tools.description: Use to read the words of one segment in full and in order, at the price of a segment rather than an episode.

tools.name: Show profile with particle
tools.description: Use when a search or an episode record gave you a podcast id and the full show record is needed, including the publisher to go up to and the slug every other show capability takes.

tools.name: Episodes of a show with particle
tools.description: Use to get from a show to its episodes and their ids: the latest episode, an episode by title, or the run of episodes in a date range. A podcast slug is never an episode id; this is how you get one.

tools.name: Show platform links with particle
tools.description: Use to get a show's Apple, Spotify or YouTube ids and links, its social handles, or its website. The reverse direction, platform id to show, is podcasts/lookup.

tools.name: Show format profile with particle
tools.description: Use for the exact rates and distributions behind a show's format: how often it has guests, how long episodes run, how often it publishes and on which days. The compact form rides on every show record as format.

tools.name: Entity mentions in a show with particle
tools.description: Use for how much one show talks about a person or company: an episode-level roll-up inside one podcast. For the dialogue lines themselves, across shows, use podcasts/mentions.

tools.name: Show ratings with particle
tools.description: Use to read what listeners wrote about a show. For the averages and histogram use podcasts/show/ratings-summary.

tools.name: Show ratings summary with particle
tools.description: Use for a show's average rating and count per storefront, plus the combined figure and what recent reviews say in aggregate.

tools.name: Related shows with particle
tools.description: Use for shows like this one: competitive sets, a listener's next show, or the peer set a sponsor or guest pitch cites. Branch on band rather than on the raw score.

tools.name: Top-level topics by show count with particle
tools.description: Use to see which subject areas have the most shows. For the full taxonomy tree use entities/topics; for the shows in one topic use podcasts/list with topic_id.

tools.name: Episode transcript with particle
tools.description: Use to read a whole episode rather than the excerpt a search returned. For one passage, podcasts/segment/transcript is smaller and cheaper; for a moment, podcasts/transcript/preview.

tools.name: Entity mentions in a transcript with particle
tools.description: Use to see exactly where and how a company, person or product was discussed within one episode, with the dialogue around each mention. Across episodes, use podcasts/mentions.

tools.name: Transcript excerpt at a moment with particle
tools.description: Use to read what was being said at a timestamp, or the opening of an episode, at a fifth of the full transcript's price. For a whole episode use podcasts/transcript.

tools.name: Ranking categories with particle
tools.description: Use to find the category_slug the chart capabilities take.

tools.name: Chart entries with particle
tools.description: Use for today's chart: the US Apple overall top podcasts with no arguments, or a country and category. Use rankings/categories and rankings/countries for the valid slugs.

tools.name: Ranking countries with particle
tools.description: Use to find the country codes the chart capabilities take.

tools.name: Chart slot history with particle
tools.description: Use for how a chart looked on past days, or how one show moved within it. For one show across every chart use rankings/show/history.

tools.name: Chart movers with particle
tools.description: Use for what debuted, climbed, fell or dropped off a chart since yesterday or over a window.

tools.name: Current rankings of a show with particle
tools.description: Use for where a show charts today, everywhere it charts. For a one-number summary use rankings/show/summary.

tools.name: Ranking history of a show with particle
tools.description: Use for a show's chart trajectory over time.

tools.name: Chart presence summary with particle
tools.description: Use for how big a show is on the charts in one call: its best rank and how widely it charts.

tools.name: Ranking sources with particle
tools.description: Use to check which chart sources exist and how fresh the snapshot is.

tools.name: Publishers by exposure to a category with particle
tools.description: Use to pivot on one category for a regulated or family brand: which networks carry the most, or least, alcohol, weapons, adult or hate-speech exposure.

tools.name: Guest suitability exposure with particle
tools.description: Use for what kind of shows a guest tends to appear on, in brand-safety terms.

tools.name: Publisher suitability profile with particle
tools.description: Use for how brand-safe a network's catalogue is as a whole and where its exposure sits.

tools.name: Assessed shows of a publisher with particle
tools.description: Use to build an inclusion or exclusion list inside one network: its shows by tier, or the ones exposed in a category.

tools.name: Publisher suitability leaderboard with particle
tools.description: Use for the safest or riskiest networks to buy, or the most broadly placeable.

tools.name: Show suitability assessment with particle
tools.description: Use for whether a show is safe to advertise on and in which categories it is exposed, with the evidence. The tier alone rides on every show record as suitability_tier.

tools.name: Company enrichment with people-data-labs
tools.description: Use when you have one company and want its firmographics, funding and headcount. Give it a domain, ticker or social profile if you possibly can - a bare name is the identifier most likely to miss.

tools.name: Company search with people-data-labs
tools.description: Use to find companies by attribute - industry, headcount, funding stage, location - rather than to look one up you can already name. Each returned company costs 50 credits. Smaller pages reduce payload size.

tools.name: Get team queue status
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metrics about the team's scrape queue. Use when you need to check queue status, job counts, or concurrency limits.

tools.name: Scrape URL
tools.description: Scrapes a publicly accessible URL, optionally performing pre-scrape browser actions or extracting structured JSON using an LLM, to retrieve content in specified formats.

tools.name: Search
tools.description: Performs a web search for a query, scrapes content from the top search results using Firecrawl, and returns details in specified formats.

price.description: $0.007 per basic search with up to 10 results

tools.name: Search people with Apollo
tools.description: Search professional profile previews by role, company, keywords and location through Firecrawl Alexandria Apollo. Returns first names, masked surnames, titles, organizations and contact-availability flags, not revealed email addresses. Request one page at a time with page and per_page (maximum 100).

tools.name: Search people with FullEnrich
tools.description: Search professional profiles by current or past roles, employers, skills, education and location through Firecrawl Alexandria FullEnrich. Returns one page with provider pagination metadata. Use offset up to 10,000, then metadata.search_after with unchanged filters. Up to 6 records per page; default 2. Contact email and phone enrichment is separate. A team administrator must accept FullEnrich terms in Firecrawl before use.

tools.name: Marketing channel shares with similarweb
tools.description: Use for marketing channel shares for one complete month. Subscription availability applies. The Similarweb-only monthly credit allowance applies.

tools.name: Marketing channel traffic with similarweb
tools.description: Use for marketing channel traffic for one complete month. Subscription availability applies. The Similarweb-only monthly credit allowance applies.

tools.name: Traffic geography with similarweb
tools.description: Use for traffic geography for one complete month. Subscription availability applies. The Similarweb-only monthly credit allowance applies.

tools.name: Incoming referral domains with similarweb
tools.description: List domains sending referral traffic to the supplied domain for one complete month, using record-offset pagination. Use web/referrals when page-number pagination is preferable.

tools.name: Paid search spend with similarweb
tools.description: Use for paid search spend for one complete month. Subscription availability applies. The Similarweb-only monthly credit allowance applies.

tools.name: Referral traffic with similarweb
tools.description: List domains sending referral traffic to the supplied domain for one complete month, using page-number pagination. Use web/incoming-referrals when record-offset pagination is preferable.

tools.name: Traffic and engagement with similarweb
tools.description: Use for traffic and engagement for one complete month. Subscription availability applies. The Similarweb-only monthly credit allowance applies.

tools.name: Outgoing referrals with similarweb
tools.description: List domains that receive referral traffic from the supplied domain, optionally filtered by date, country, device, and granularity. Use incoming-referrals to find domains sending traffic to the supplied domain.

tools.name: Start an agent job
tools.description: Tool to start an agent job for agentic web extraction with multi-page navigation and interaction capabilities. Use when you need to autonomously gather data from the web with complex navigation requirements. The agent can search, navigate, and extract information across multiple pages based on your natural language prompt.

tools.name: Stop scrape interaction
tools.description: Stop a scrape job's interactive browser session, releasing browser resources and finalizing duration-based billing.

tools.name: Get team token usage
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the current team's token usage and balance information for Firecrawl's Extract feature. Use when you need to check remaining token credits, plan allocation, or billing period details.

tools.name: Get historical team token usage
tools.description: Tool to retrieve historical team token usage on a monthly basis. Use when you need to analyze token consumption patterns over time, optionally segmented by API key.

tools.name: Creative breakdown with upspring
tools.description: Use for how a market advertises: the share of hooks, personas, offers or formats across a vertical, brand or filter. Run it twice, once with min_impressions=4, to see what the winning ads over-index on.

tools.name: Browse ads with upspring
tools.description: Use to list a brand's or a vertical's ads by filter: what an advertiser is running now (advertiser_id + is_active=true), or the winners in a category (order_by=best, min_impressions=4).

tools.name: Ad detail with upspring
tools.description: Use for everything about one ad: the hook, offer, landing page and whether the page delivers what the ad promises. Add include=full for scenes, transcript, overlays and narrative.

tools.name: Search ads with upspring
tools.description: Use to find Meta ads matching a free-text idea, relevance-ranked across Upspring's competitor ad corpus. Re-rank the page by strength.impressions, then open the finalists with ads/detail. For the newest or best-performing ads without a query use ads/browse.

tools.name: Similar ads with upspring
tools.description: Use to find ads creatively like one ad, from the same brand and from its competitors.

tools.name: Advertiser brief with upspring
tools.description: Use for a brand's ad strategy at a glance: size grades, Facebook and Instagram followers, Reddit sentiment, its creative fingerprint (personas, mechanisms, hooks, media mix, funnel), hook themes and its top ads.

tools.name: Advertiser by domain with upspring
tools.description: Use when all you have is a company's website: resolves it to one advertiser and returns the same brief as advertisers/brief. Never 404s; a domain Upspring cannot source answers status unavailable and is not charged.

tools.name: Compare advertisers with upspring
tools.description: Use to put two brands' ad strategies side by side: where they overlap, where they differ, and what each leaves open.

tools.name: Peer advertisers with upspring
tools.description: Use for brands like this one: same category, vertical, geography or size band. For creative similarity instead use advertisers/similar.

tools.name: Request an advertiser with upspring
tools.description: Use when advertisers/brief answers not found or status unavailable for an advertiser id you know exists: asks Upspring to source it, then poll advertisers/brief. Idempotent; each new advertiser counts against a daily limit.

tools.name: Find advertisers with upspring
tools.description: Use to find a brand's advertiser id by name, website or Facebook page, or to list the advertisers in a vertical, category or size tier. For one brand from its domain with the full brief in one call use advertisers/by-domain.

tools.name: Similar advertisers with upspring
tools.description: Use for a brand's closest competitors: advertisers going after the same audience with comparable creative strategies.

tools.name: Vertical vocabulary with upspring
tools.description: Use, free, before filtering ads by persona, hook or another dimension: lists the valid ids in one vertical.

tools.name: Verticals and categories with upspring
tools.description: Use first, free, to learn the vertical and category ids the ads and advertiser filters accept.

required.name: full
required.description: The Firecrawl API web address. Most accounts can keep the default https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1. If you self-host Firecrawl, enter your server's address ending in /v1.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Firecrawl API key, a token starting with fc- (e.g. fc-12345...). Sign in and copy it from the API Keys page: https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys

name: Tavily
description: Tavily offers search and data retrieval solutions, helping teams quickly locate and filter relevant information from documents, databases, or web sources

tools.name: Tavily crawl
tools.description: Tool to perform intelligent graph-based website crawling with parallel path exploration and content extraction. Use when you need to traverse and extract content from multiple pages of a website following specific patterns or instructions. Supports depth/breadth controls, domain filtering, and natural language instructions for guided crawling.

tools.name: Tavily extract
tools.description: Tool to extract and parse web page content from specified URLs using Tavily's extract endpoint. Use when you need to retrieve clean, structured content from web pages with optional image extraction and content reranking based on query relevance.

tools.name: Get Tavily usage
tools.description: Tool to retrieve API key and account usage statistics from Tavily. Use when you need to check credit consumption, limits, and per-endpoint usage for search, extract, crawl, map, and research operations.

tools.name: Tavily map website
tools.description: Tool to map a website and discover its pages. Use when you need to scan a website and get a structured list of URLs/pages it contains without extracting full content.

tools.name: Tavily search
tools.description: Use this to perform a web search via the Tavily API; offers controls for search depth, content types, result count, and domain filtering. Requires an active Tavily connection (401 = auth failure). Rate limit: ~2 req/s; apply exponential backoff on HTTP 429. Results are nested under response_data.results (not a flat list). Subject to HTTP 429 on rapid bursts.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Tavily API key (starts with 'tvly-', e.g. tvly-dev-abc123). Sign in at app.tavily.com and copy it from the API Keys section; either key type works.

name: YouTube
description: YouTube is a video-sharing platform with user-generated content, live streaming, and monetization opportunities, widely used for marketing, education, and entertainment

tools.name: Add Video to Playlist
tools.description: Tool to add a video to a playlist by inserting a playlist item. Use when organizing videos into playlists or building curated collections.

tools.name: Insert Channel Section
tools.description: Tool to create a new channel section for the authenticated user's YouTube channel. Use when organizing channel content into sections like featured playlists, recent uploads, or featured channels.

tools.name: Insert Comment Reply
tools.description: Tool to create a reply to an existing YouTube comment. Use when responding to user comments or engaging in conversations on videos.

tools.name: Create Playlist
tools.description: Tool to create a new YouTube playlist on the authenticated user's channel. Use when organizing videos into collections or building curated playlists.

tools.name: Delete caption track
tools.description: Permanently deletes an owned caption track after explicit confirmation with `confirmDelete: true`.

tools.name: Delete Channel Section
tools.description: Tool to delete a YouTube channel section. Use when you need to remove a channel section from a channel. The channel section must exist and the authenticated user must have permission to delete it.

tools.name: Delete Comment
tools.description: Tool to delete a YouTube comment owned by the authenticated user or channel. Use when you need to remove a comment from a video. The comment must exist and be owned by the authenticated channel.

tools.name: Delete Live Broadcast
tools.description: Permanently delete an owned YouTube live broadcast after confirmation.

tools.name: Delete Playlist
tools.description: Tool to delete a YouTube playlist owned by the authenticated user/channel. Use when you need to permanently remove a playlist from YouTube. Requires explicit confirmation via `confirmDelete: true` to prevent accidental deletions.

tools.name: Delete Playlist Item
tools.description: Tool to delete a playlist item (remove a video from a playlist). Use when removing specific videos from playlists.

tools.name: Delete Video
tools.description: Tool to delete a YouTube video owned by the authenticated user/channel. Use when you need to permanently remove a video from YouTube. Requires explicit confirmation via `confirmDelete: true` to prevent accidental deletions. The video must exist and be owned by the authenticated channel.

tools.name: Get Channel Activities
tools.description: Gets recent activities from a YouTube channel including video uploads, playlist additions, likes, and other channel events.

tools.name: Get channel ID by handle
tools.description: Retrieves the YouTube Channel ID for a specific YouTube channel handle.

tools.name: Get Channel Statistics
tools.description: Gets detailed statistics for YouTube channels including subscriber counts, view counts, and video counts. Channels can be identified using their ID, handle (e.g., @Google), or username.

tools.name: Get Playlists by ID
tools.description: Retrieves one or more playlists by their YouTube playlist IDs.

tools.name: Video Details Batch
tools.description: Retrieves multiple YouTube video resource parts in a single batch call. Use when you need cohort-level metrics for many videos to reduce quota usage and latency.

tools.name: Get Video Rating
tools.description: Retrieves the ratings that the authorized user gave to a list of specified videos. Use when you need to check if a user has liked or disliked specific videos.

tools.name: List captions
tools.description: Retrieves a list of caption tracks for a YouTube video. Returns an empty items list if no captions are available. Raises ExecutionFailed if the video ID is invalid or not found.

tools.name: List Channels
tools.description: Lists YouTube channels by ID, handle, username, or ownership status, returning detailed channel information including metadata, statistics, and content details. Use this action when you need to retrieve comprehensive channel information by channel ID, handle (e.g., @username), or to list channels owned by or managed by the authenticated user. For finding channels by search query, use the search action instead.

tools.name: List Channel Sections
tools.description: Tool to retrieve channel sections from YouTube. Use when you need to get the layout sections of a channel's homepage. Channel sections organize content into categories like playlists, uploads, or featured channels.

tools.name: List channel videos
tools.description: Lists videos from a specified YouTube channel. This action primarily uses the playlistItems.list endpoint with the channel's uploads playlist, which is the recommended approach by YouTube. The uploads playlist ID is obtained by fetching the channel resource via the Channels API and extracting the playlist ID from contentDetails.relatedPlaylists.uploads field. If the uploads playlist returns a 404 error (which can happen due to a known YouTube API bug where the returned playlist ID doesn't actually exist), the action automatically falls back to the search.list endpoint to retrieve channel videos. Note that the search fallback has higher quota cost (100 units vs 1 unit) and is limited to 500 results. If a channel exists but has no uploads playlist (e.g., brand accounts, channels with all videos deleted, or channels that haven't uploaded any public content), an empty result set is returned instead of an error.

tools.name: List Comments
tools.description: List individual comments from YouTube videos. Returns comment details including author, text, timestamps, and engagement metrics. Use 'id' parameter to retrieve specific comments or 'parentId' to retrieve all replies to a top-level comment.

tools.name: List Comment Threads (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use YOUTUBE_LIST_COMMENT_THREADS2 instead. List comment threads from YouTube videos or channels for qualitative analysis and reporting. Returns top-level comments with optional replies (up to 5 per thread). Use the 'videoId' parameter to retrieve comments on a specific video (most common use case).

tools.name: List Comment Threads
tools.description: Tool to retrieve comment threads from YouTube videos or channels matching API request parameters. Use when you need to fetch comments with filtering by video, channel, or specific thread IDs.

tools.name: List I18n Languages
tools.description: Returns a list of application languages that the YouTube website supports. Use this when you need to retrieve all available language options for YouTube's interface or to localize content.

tools.name: List I18n Regions
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of content regions that the YouTube website supports. Returns region codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and localized region names. Use when you need to identify available geographic regions for content filtering or display.

tools.name: List Live Broadcasts
tools.description: List the connected channel's live broadcasts by lifecycle status, ID, or ownership.

tools.name: List Live Chat Messages
tools.description: Tool to list live chat messages for a specific chat. Use for monitoring live chat during broadcasts or retrieving chat history. Returns messages with author details, timestamps, and message types (text, Super Chat, moderation events).

tools.name: List Live Streams
tools.description: Lists live streams owned by the connected channel or selected by stream ID.

tools.name: List Most Popular Videos
tools.description: Tool to list the current most-popular (charts/trending) YouTube videos for a region and/or category via videos.list(chart=mostPopular). Use when you need to retrieve YouTube's official trending or most popular videos, not keyword-search approximations.

tools.name: List Playlist Images
tools.description: Tool to retrieve playlist images associated with a specific playlist. Use when fetching custom thumbnail images for playlists.

tools.name: List Playlist Items
tools.description: Tool to list videos in a playlist, with pagination support. Use when walking through a channel's uploads playlist to enumerate all videos.

tools.name: List Rated Videos
tools.description: List up to the 1,000 most recent videos liked or disliked by the authenticated YouTube user.

tools.name: List Super Chat Events
tools.description: Lists Super Chat events for a channel, showing supporter purchases during live streams. Returns Super Chat and Super Sticker events from the past 30 days. Use to track and acknowledge supporter contributions.

tools.name: List user playlists
tools.description: Retrieves playlists owned by the authenticated user, implicitly using mine=True.

tools.name: List user subscriptions
tools.description: Retrieves the authenticated user's YouTube channel subscriptions, allowing specification of response parts and pagination.

tools.name: List Video Abuse Report Reasons
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of abuse report reasons that can be used to report abusive videos on YouTube. Use when you need to display available reporting categories or before calling videos.reportAbuse. Returns localized reason labels and optional secondary categorizations.

tools.name: List Video Categories
tools.description: Tool to list YouTube video categories that can be associated with videos. Use when you need to retrieve available video categories for a specific region or get details about specific category IDs.

tools.name: Download YouTube caption track
tools.description: Downloads a specific YouTube caption track, which must be owned by the authenticated user, and returns its content as text. Note: This action requires you to own the video (YouTube Data API v3 restriction). Non-owned videos will return 403 Forbidden errors, including many auto-generated caption tracks.

tools.name: Mark Comment as Spam
tools.description: Tool to mark one or more YouTube comments as spam. Use when moderating comments to flag spam content. Note: This endpoint is deprecated but still functional according to YouTube API documentation.

tools.name: Multipart upload video
tools.description: Uploads a video to YouTube using multipart upload in a single request. Use when you want to upload both metadata and video file together. This action uploads the video file and metadata in one request, unlike resumable upload which requires two steps.

tools.name: Post Comment on Video
tools.description: Tool to post a new top-level comment on a YouTube video. Use when creating comments to engage with video content or respond to user requests.

tools.name: Query YouTube Analytics
tools.description: Query a channel or content owner's YouTube Analytics result table.

tools.name: Rate Video
tools.description: Tool to add a like or dislike rating to a YouTube video, or remove an existing rating. Use when you need to rate videos on behalf of the authenticated user.

tools.name: Report Video for Abuse
tools.description: Tool to report a YouTube video for containing abusive content. Use when you need to flag videos that violate YouTube's community guidelines or contain harmful content.

tools.name: Search YouTube
tools.description: Searches YouTube for videos, channels, or playlists using a query term, returning the raw API response.

tools.name: Set Comment Moderation Status
tools.description: Tool to set the moderation status of one or more YouTube comments. Use when moderating comments to hold for review, publish, or reject them. Optionally ban the comment author when rejecting.

tools.name: Subscribe to channel
tools.description: Subscribes the authenticated user to a specified YouTube channel, identified by its unique `channelId` which must be valid and existing.

tools.name: Unsubscribe from channel
tools.description: Tool to unsubscribe the authenticated user from a YouTube channel by deleting a subscription. Use when you need to remove an existing subscription. The subscription ID can be obtained from the `YOUTUBE_LIST_USER_SUBSCRIPTIONS` tool.

tools.name: Update caption track
tools.description: Updates a YouTube caption track's metadata such as name, language, or draft status. Use this to modify existing caption track properties without uploading new caption content. Note: Only properties specified in the snippet will be updated; unspecified properties retain their current values.

tools.name: Update channel
tools.description: Updates a channel's metadata including branding settings and localizations. Only brandingSettings, invideoPromotion, and localizations properties can be updated. Requires the channel to be owned by the authenticated user.

tools.name: Update Channel Section
tools.description: Tool to update an existing YouTube channel section by ID. Use when modifying section properties like title, position, or featured content.

tools.name: Update Comment
tools.description: Tool to modify the text of an existing YouTube comment. Use when updating or correcting a previously posted comment.

tools.name: Update Playlist
tools.description: Tool to modify an existing YouTube playlist's metadata (title, description, privacy status). Use when updating playlist information for the authenticated user's channel.

tools.name: Update Playlist Item
tools.description: Tool to modify a playlist item's properties such as position or note. Use when reordering videos in a playlist or updating item metadata.

tools.name: Update thumbnail
tools.description: Sets the custom thumbnail for a YouTube video using an image from a URL. Requirements: - The authenticated user must own the video or have permission to edit it - The YouTube channel must be verified (phone verification required) to upload custom thumbnails - Image must be JPG, PNG, or GIF; under 2MB; recommended 1280x720 resolution (16:9 aspect ratio)

tools.name: Update video
tools.description: Updates metadata for a YouTube video identified by videoId, which must exist; an empty list for tags removes all existing tags.

tools.name: Upload caption media
tools.description: Replaces the media bytes of an existing YouTube caption track.

tools.name: Upload caption track
tools.description: Creates a caption track for an owned video and uploads its caption media.

tools.name: Upload channel banner
tools.description: Upload banner media and return its URL without applying it to the channel. Apply the returned URL with a channels.update request that sets brandingSettings.image.bannerExternalUrl.

tools.name: Upload video
tools.description: Uploads a video file to a YouTube channel; the video file must be in a YouTube-supported format.

triggers.name: New YouTube Activity
triggers.description: Triggers when a new activity is detected on a YouTube channel.

triggers.name: New Item in YouTube Playlist
triggers.description: Triggers when a new item is added to a YouTube playlist.

triggers.name: New Playlist in YouTube Channel
triggers.description: Triggers when a new playlist is added to a YouTube channel.

triggers.name: New YouTube Channel Subscription
triggers.description: Triggers when a new channel is subscribed.

required.name: client_id
required.description: Client id of the app

required.name: client_secret
required.description: Client secret of the app

optional.name: oauth_redirect_uri
optional.description: Add this Redirect URL to your app's OAuth allow list.

optional.name: scopes
optional.description: Scopes to request from the user, comma separated

name: Slackbot
description: Slackbot gives agents workspace-wide read access to a Slack workspace on behalf of the installing user - search messages and files, browse channel and thread history, and look up users and channels - while continuing to post and react as the bot. Includes direct messages and user email addresses so agents can search across DMs and resolve users by email.

tools.name: Add call participants
tools.description: Registers new participants added to a Slack call.

tools.name: Add reaction to message
tools.description: Adds a specified emoji reaction to an existing message in a Slack channel, identified by its timestamp; does not remove or retrieve reactions.

tools.name: Add a remote file
tools.description: Adds a reference to an external file (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox) to Slack for discovery and sharing, requiring a unique `external_id` and an `external_url` accessible by Slack.

tools.name: Archive a Slack conversation
tools.description: Archives a Slack conversation by its ID, rendering it read-only and hidden while retaining history, ideal for cleaning up inactive channels; be aware that some channels (like #general or certain DMs) cannot be archived and this may impact connected integrations.

tools.name: Close conversation channel
tools.description: Closes a Slack direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPDM) channel, removing it from the user's sidebar without deleting history; this action affects only the calling user's view.

tools.name: Complete external file upload
tools.description: Finalize uploaded file IDs once and optionally share the files.

tools.name: Create a reminder
tools.description: Creates a Slack reminder with specified text and time; time accepts Unix timestamps, seconds from now, or natural language (e.g., 'in 15 minutes', 'every Thursday at 2pm').

tools.name: Create Slack Canvas
tools.description: Creates a new Slack Canvas with the specified title and optional content.

tools.name: Create channel
tools.description: Initiates a public or private channel-based conversation in a Slack workspace. Immediately creates the channel; invoke only after explicit user confirmation.

tools.name: Create Slack List
tools.description: Creates a new Slack List via `slackLists.create`. Provide a `name` and, optionally, a `description_blocks` description and a `schema` of typed columns. You can instead copy an existing List's structure with `copy_from_list_id` (and its rows via `include_copied_list_records`), or enable task-tracking columns with `todo_mode`. Returns the new List's `list_id`. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Create Slack List item
tools.description: Creates a new item (row) in a Slack List via `slackLists.items.create`. Set initial cell values with `initial_fields`; text columns require Block Kit `rich_text` (a plain string is wrapped automatically). Optionally duplicate an existing row with `duplicated_item_id` or create a subtask with `parent_item_id`. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Create a Slack user group
tools.description: Creates a new User Group (often referred to as a subteam) in a Slack workspace.

tools.name: Customize URL unfurl
tools.description: Customizes URL previews (unfurling) in a specific Slack message using a URL-encoded JSON in `unfurls` to define custom content or remove existing previews.

tools.name: Delete Slack Canvas
tools.description: Deletes a Slack Canvas permanently and irreversibly. Always confirm with the user before calling this tool.

tools.name: Delete a file by ID
tools.description: Permanently deletes an existing file from a Slack workspace using its unique file ID; this action is irreversible and also removes any associated comments or shares.

tools.name: Delete file comment
tools.description: Deletes a specific comment from a file in Slack; this action is irreversible.

tools.name: Delete Slack List access
tools.description: Revokes sharing access on a Slack List via `slackLists.access.delete`. Provide the `list_id` and EXACTLY ONE of `channel_ids` or `user_ids` (they are mutually exclusive) to remove access for those channels or users. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Delete Slack List item
tools.description: Deletes an item (row) from a Slack List via `slackLists.items.delete`. Identify the List with `list_id` and the row to remove with `id`. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Delete multiple Slack List items
tools.description: Deletes several items (rows) from a Slack List in one call via `slackLists.items.deleteMultiple`. This operation is ALL-OR-NOTHING: Slack returns a single `{"ok": true}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": ...}` on failure, with NO per-item result array, so partial state cannot be reported. On failure, treat the whole batch as not deleted and retry the entire batch. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Delete a Slack reminder
tools.description: Deletes an existing Slack reminder, typically when it is no longer relevant or a task is completed; this operation is irreversible.

tools.name: Delete a message from a chat
tools.description: Deletes a message, identified by its channel ID and timestamp, from a Slack channel, private group, or direct message conversation; the authenticated user or bot must be the original poster.

tools.name: Delete scheduled chat message
tools.description: Deletes a pending, unsent scheduled message from the specified Slack channel, identified by its `scheduled_message_id`.

tools.name: Disable a Slack user group
tools.description: Disables a specified, currently enabled Slack User Group by its unique ID, effectively archiving it by setting its 'date_delete' timestamp; the group is not permanently deleted and can be re-enabled.

tools.name: Download Slack file
tools.description: Tool to download Slack file content and convert it to a publicly accessible URL. Use when you need to retrieve and download files that have been shared in Slack channels or conversations.

tools.name: Edit Slack Canvas
tools.description: Edits a Slack Canvas with granular control over content placement. Supports replace, insert (before/after/start/end) operations for flexible content management.

tools.name: Share file public url
tools.description: Enables public sharing for an existing Slack file by generating a publicly accessible URL; this action does not create new files. Once enabled, the file is accessible to anyone with the URL — verify intent before sharing sensitive or confidential files.

tools.name: Enable a user group
tools.description: Enables a disabled User Group in Slack using its ID, reactivating it for mentions and permissions; this action only changes the enabled status and cannot create new groups or modify other properties.

tools.name: End a call
tools.description: Ends an ongoing Slack call, identified by its ID (obtained from `calls.add`), optionally specifying the call's duration.

tools.name: Fetch conversation history
tools.description: Fetches a chronological list of messages and events from a specified Slack conversation, accessible by the authenticated user/bot, with options for pagination and time range filtering. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: This action only returns messages from the main channel timeline. Threaded replies are NOT returned by this endpoint. To retrieve threaded replies, use the SLACK_FETCH_MESSAGE_THREAD_FROM_A_CONVERSATION action (conversations.replies API) instead. The oldest/latest timestamp filters work reliably for filtering the main channel timeline, but cannot be used to retrieve individual threaded replies - even if you know the exact reply timestamp, setting oldest=latest to that timestamp will return an empty messages array. To get threaded replies: 1. Use this action to get parent messages (which include thread_ts, reply_count, latest_reply fields) 2. Use SLACK_FETCH_MESSAGE_THREAD_FROM_A_CONVERSATION with the parent's thread_ts to fetch all replies in that thread

tools.name: Fetch item reactions
tools.description: Fetches reactions for a Slack message, file, or file comment. Exactly one identifier path must be provided: `channel`+`timestamp`, `file`, or `file_comment`. Mixing identifiers (e.g., providing both `channel`+`timestamp` and `file`) causes errors. If the response omits the `reactions` field, the item has zero reactions.

tools.name: Retrieve conversation replies
tools.description: Retrieves replies to a specific parent message in a Slack conversation, using the channel ID and the parent message's timestamp (`ts`). Note: The parent message in the response contains metadata (reply_count, reply_users, latest_reply) that indicates expected thread activity. If the returned messages array contains fewer replies than reply_count indicates, check: (1) has_more=true means pagination is needed, (2) recently posted replies may have timing delays, (3) some replies may be filtered by permissions or deleted. The composio_execution_message field will warn about any detected mismatches.

tools.name: Fetch team info
tools.description: Fetches comprehensive metadata about the current Slack team, or a specified team if the provided ID is accessible.

tools.name: Find channels
tools.description: Find channels in a Slack workspace by any criteria - name, topic, purpose, or description. Returns channel IDs (C*/G* prefixed) required by most Slack tools — always resolve names to IDs here before passing to other tools. NOTE: This action searches channels and conversations visible to the authenticated user. Empty results may indicate: - No channels match the search query in name, topic, or purpose - The target private channel or DM is not accessible to the authenticated user because they are not a member - The connection lacks required read scopes (channels:read, groups:read, im:read, mpim:read). If empty, retry with exact_match=false or exclude_archived=false to avoid false negatives. In large workspaces, paginate using next_cursor to avoid missing matches. Check 'composio_execution_message' and 'total_channels_searched' in the response for details.

tools.name: Lookup users by email
tools.description: Retrieves the Slack user object for an active user by their registered email address; requires the users:read.email OAuth scope. Fails with 'users_not_found' if the email is unregistered, the user is inactive, the account is a guest, or the email is hidden by workspace privacy settings.

tools.name: Find users
tools.description: Find users in a Slack workspace by any criteria - email, name, display name, or other text. Includes optimized email lookup for exact email matches. Zero results may reflect email visibility restrictions or workspace policies, not global absence. Repeated calls may trigger HTTP 429; honor the Retry-After header.

tools.name: Fetch bot user information
tools.description: Fetches information for a specified, existing Slack bot user; will not work for regular user accounts or other integration types.

tools.name: Retrieve call information
tools.description: Retrieves a point-in-time snapshot of a specific Slack call's information.

tools.name: Get Slack Canvas (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SLACK_RETRIEVE_DETAILED_INFORMATION_ABOUT_A_FILE instead. Retrieves a specific Slack Canvas by its ID, including its content and metadata.

tools.name: Get Slack List item
tools.description: Fetches a single item (row) from a Slack List via `slackLists.items.info`. Returns the row's `column_id`-keyed typed values along with metadata about the parent List. Set `include_is_subscribed` to also report whether the calling user is subscribed to the row. Requires a user token with the `lists:read` scope.

tools.name: Get reminder information
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information for an existing Slack reminder specified by its ID; this is a read-only operation.

tools.name: Get remote file
tools.description: Retrieve information about a remote file added to Slack via the files.remote API. Does not work for standard Slack-hosted file uploads.

tools.name: Retrieve team profile details
tools.description: Retrieves all profile field definitions for a Slack team, optionally filtered by visibility, to understand the team's profile structure.

tools.name: Get unread messages from user
tools.description: Retrieves unread direct messages from a specific user by opening their DM conversation, checking for unread messages, and fetching message history since the last read timestamp. Use this action when you need to check if a specific user has sent unread direct messages to the authenticated user, or when monitoring incoming DMs from particular users. Returns an empty messages array if there are no unread messages from the specified user. Note: This action only works for direct messages (DMs), not channel messages or group conversations.

tools.name: Get team DND status
tools.description: Retrieves a user's current Do Not Disturb status.

tools.name: Retrieve user presence
tools.description: Retrieves a Slack user's current real-time presence (e.g., 'active', 'away') to determine their availability, noting this action does not provide historical data or status reasons.

tools.name: Invite users to a Slack channel
tools.description: Invites users to an existing Slack channel using their valid Slack User IDs. Response is always HTTP 200; inspect `ok`, `error`, and `errors` fields to confirm users were added.

tools.name: Join conversation by channel id
tools.description: Joins an existing Slack conversation (public channel, private channel, or multi-person direct message) by its ID, if the authenticated user has permission. Joining an already-joined channel returns a non-fatal no-op response. Private or restricted channel joins may fail with a permission error.

tools.name: Leave conversation channel
tools.description: Leaves a Slack conversation given its channel ID; fails if leaving as the last member of a private channel or if used on a Slack Connect channel.

tools.name: List all channels
tools.description: Lists conversations available to the user with various filters and search options. Always use resolved `channel_id` (not display names) for downstream operations, as names may be non-unique. The `created` field in results is a Unix epoch timestamp (UTC). Pagination across large workspaces may return HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header; honor the delay and resume from the last successful cursor.

tools.name: List all users
tools.description: Retrieves a paginated list of all users with profile details, status, and team memberships in a Slack workspace; data may not be real-time. Filter response fields `is_bot`, `is_app_user`, and `deleted` to build human-only rosters. Profile fields like `email` and `phone` may be absent depending on OAuth scopes and workspace privacy settings. Guest/restricted accounts may be omitted based on scopes—do not treat results as a complete directory. High-frequency calls risk HTTP 429; honor the `Retry-After` header and throttle to ~1–2 requests/second. Use stable user IDs rather than display names for mapping. Prefer SLACK_FIND_USERS for targeted lookups; cache results to avoid full-workspace fetches.

tools.name: List available workspaces
tools.description: List Slack workspaces where both the connection and target user have access. Returns each workspace's team_id and name. Use this when: (1) the user references a workspace by name, (2) a user-specific tool requires team_id and you don't have one, or (3) a user-specific call fails with a team/workspace access error. Match the user's workspace name to a team_id from the results and pass that team_id to subsequent tools. If the name matches zero or multiple workspaces, ask the user to clarify. Only meaningful for org-level installs; single-workspace connections return the workspace only if the specified user's membership is visible to this token.

tools.name: List Slack Canvases (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use SLACK_LIST_FILES_WITH_FILTERS_IN_SLACK instead (pass types="canvas" for equivalent behavior). Lists Slack Canvases with filtering by channel, user, timestamp, and page-based pagination. Uses Slack's files.list API with types=canvas filter. Only canvases accessible to the authenticated app are returned; missing canvases indicate permissions restrictions, not empty data. Use `paging.pages` in the response to determine total pages; iterate `page` with `count` to retrieve all results. Known limitations: - The 'user' filter may return canvases accessible to the specified user, not just canvases they created. - The 'ts_from' and 'ts_to' timestamp filters may not work reliably for canvas types. Consider client-side filtering on the 'created' field in the response if precise date filtering is required.

tools.name: List conversations
tools.description: List conversations (channels/DMs) accessible to a specified user (or the authenticated user if no user ID is provided), respecting shared membership for non-public channels. Returns conversation IDs (C* for channels, G* for group DMs), not display names. Absence of private channels, DMs, or MPIMs from results indicates token scope or membership limits, not that the conversation is nonexistent.

tools.name: List team custom emojis
tools.description: Retrieves all custom emojis for the Slack workspace (image URLs or aliases), not standard Unicode emojis; does not include usage statistics or creation dates.

tools.name: List Slack files
tools.description: Lists files and their metadata within a Slack workspace, filterable by user, channel, timestamp, or type; returns metadata only, not file content. Results are limited to files visible to the authenticated user — files in private channels or restricted to certain members require appropriate membership and permissions. For large workspaces, check `paging.pages` in the response to determine total pages when paginating.

tools.name: List Slack List items
tools.description: Lists the rows (items) in a Slack List via `slackLists.items.list`. Each row exposes `column_id`-keyed typed values (e.g. `rich_text`, `select`, `user`, `date`, `number`); the legacy `key`/`value` fields are deprecated. Results are cursor-paginated—you must paginate using `response_metadata.next_cursor` until it is empty, or rows are silently truncated to the first page. Set `archived=true` to return archived rows instead of active ones. Requires a user token with the `lists:read` scope.

tools.name: List pinned items in a channel
tools.description: Retrieves all messages and files pinned to a specified channel; the caller must have access to this channel.

tools.name: List reminders
tools.description: Lists all reminders with their details for the authenticated Slack user; returns an empty array if no reminders exist (valid state, not an error). Reminder text is not unique—perform client-side matching on returned objects before extracting a reminder ID for use with SLACK_DELETE_A_SLACK_REMINDER.

tools.name: List remote files
tools.description: Retrieve information about a team's remote files.

tools.name: List unread channel messages
tools.description: Lists all unread messages in a specified Slack channel for the authenticated user. This action fetches messages that have been posted since the user's last read position in the channel. Use this action when you need to retrieve messages the user hasn't seen yet. The action determines the user's read position and returns all messages posted after that timestamp. Note: This only returns messages from the main channel timeline, not threaded replies. For threaded replies, use SLACK_FETCH_MESSAGE_THREAD_FROM_A_CONVERSATION.

tools.name: List all users in a user group
tools.description: Retrieves a list of all user IDs within a specified Slack user group, with an option to include users from disabled groups.

tools.name: List user groups
tools.description: Lists user groups in a Slack workspace, including user-created and default groups; results for large workspaces may be paginated.

tools.name: List user reactions
tools.description: Lists all reactions added by a specific user to messages, files, or file comments in Slack, useful for engagement analysis when the item content itself is not required. Results are paginated; check `response_metadata.next_cursor` and iterate with the `cursor` parameter to retrieve complete reaction history.

tools.name: Lookup Canvas Sections
tools.description: Looks up section IDs in a Slack Canvas for use with targeted edit operations. Section IDs are needed for insert_after, insert_before, delete, and section-specific replace operations.

tools.name: Open DM
tools.description: Opens or resumes a Slack direct message (DM) or multi-person direct message (MPIM) by providing either user IDs or an existing channel ID. Returns `already_open=true` when the DM exists — treat as success and reuse the returned `channel.id` (starts with 'D') for subsequent SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE calls; passing a username, email, or user ID directly to SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE causes `channel_not_found`. Avoid redundant calls when an existing DM channel ID is available.

tools.name: Pin an item to a channel
tools.description: Pins a message to a specified Slack channel; the message must not already be pinned.

tools.name: Remove call participants
tools.description: Registers participants removed from a Slack call.

tools.name: Remove reaction from item
tools.description: Removes an emoji reaction from a message, file, or file comment in Slack. Provide exactly one targeting method: channel+timestamp together, file, or file_comment. Mixing methods or omitting all returns invalid_arguments.

tools.name: Remove remote file
tools.description: Removes the Slack reference to an external file (which must have been previously added via the remote files API), specified by either its `external_id` or `file` ID (one of which is required), without deleting the actual external file.

tools.name: Remove user from conversation
tools.description: Removes a specified user from a Slack conversation (channel); the caller must have permissions to remove users and cannot remove themselves using this action.

tools.name: Rename a conversation
tools.description: Renames a Slack channel, automatically adjusting the new name to meet naming conventions (e.g., converting to lowercase), which may affect integrations using the old name.

tools.name: Reserve Slack file upload
tools.description: Reserve a temporary Slack upload URL without uploading bytes. Upload the exact bytes to the returned URL, then call Slack's files.completeUploadExternal method; Slack aborts reservations that are not completed.

tools.name: Retrieve conversation information
tools.description: Retrieves metadata for a Slack conversation by ID (e.g., name, purpose, creation date, with options for member count/locale), excluding message content. The `channel` parameter is effectively required. Private channels, DMs, or channels where the app lacks membership may return restricted data; check `is_archived` and `is_member` fields in the response to diagnose access issues. Bulk lookups may trigger HTTP 429 rate limiting; honor the `Retry-After` response header.

tools.name: Get conversation members
tools.description: Retrieves a paginated list of active member IDs (not names, emails, or presence) for a specified Slack public channel, private channel, DM, or MPIM. Returns only user IDs; use a user-lookup tool to enrich member data.

tools.name: Retrieve user DND status
tools.description: Retrieves a Slack user's current Do Not Disturb (DND) status to determine their availability before interaction; any specified user ID must be a valid Slack user ID.

tools.name: Retrieve detailed file information
tools.description: Retrieves detailed metadata and paginated comments for a specific Slack file ID; does not download file content.

tools.name: Retrieve detailed user information
tools.description: Retrieves comprehensive information for a valid Slack user ID, excluding message history and channel memberships. Sensitive fields like `email` and `phone` require the `users:read.email` scope and may be silently omitted based on workspace privacy policies.

tools.name: Retrieve user profile information
tools.description: Retrieves profile information for a specified Slack user (defaults to the authenticated user if `user` ID is omitted); a provided `user` ID must be valid. Sensitive fields like email and phone may be silently omitted if required scopes (e.g., `users:read.email`) are not granted or workspace privacy policies restrict access.

tools.name: Revoke a file's public url
tools.description: Revokes a Slack file's public URL, making it private; this is a no-op if not already public and is irreversible.

tools.name: Schedule message
tools.description: Schedules a message to a Slack channel, DM, or private group for a future time (`post_at`), requiring `text`, `blocks`, or `attachments` for content; scheduling is limited to 120 days in advance.

tools.name: Search all content
tools.description: Tool to search all messages and files. Use when you need unified content search across channels and files in one call. Results are scoped to content visible to the authenticated token; missing hits in private or restricted channels reflect permission/membership gaps. Response separates messages and files into distinct sections — explicitly read the files section for document results. Results are index-based and may lag several minutes behind real-time; use SLACK_FETCH_CONVERSATION_HISTORY for near-real-time per-channel coverage. Paginated searches exceeding ~1 req/sec may return HTTP 429 too_many_requests; honor the Retry-After header and resume from the last page.

tools.name: Search Slack files
tools.description: Search files visible to the connected Slack user by text and modifiers.

tools.name: Search messages
tools.description: Workspace‑wide Slack message search with date ranges and filters. Use `query` modifiers (e.g., in:#channel, from:@user, before/after:YYYY-MM-DD), sorting (score/timestamp), and pagination.

tools.name: Send ephemeral message
tools.description: Sends an ephemeral message visible only to the specified `user` in a channel; other channel members cannot see it. Both the bot and the target user must be members of the specified channel.

tools.name: Share a me message in a channel
tools.description: Sends a 'me message' (e.g., '/me is typing') to a Slack channel, where it's displayed as a third-person user action; messages are plain text and the channel must exist and be accessible.

tools.name: Send message
tools.description: Posts a message to a Slack channel, DM, or private group. Provide exactly one visible content mode: `markdown_text` for normal Markdown content, or `blocks` for raw Slack Block Kit layouts. Use `fallback_text` only with `blocks`; it maps to Slack's top-level `text` fallback. Fails with `not_in_channel`, `channel_not_found`, or `channel_is_archived` if the bot lacks access. Rate-limited at ~1 req/sec (HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After`). Not idempotent — duplicate calls post duplicate messages.

tools.name: Set a conversation's purpose
tools.description: Sets the purpose (a short description of its topic/goal, displayed in the header) for a Slack conversation; the calling user must be a member.

tools.name: Set Slack List access
tools.description: Grants or sets sharing access on a Slack List via `slackLists.access.set`. Grant `read`, `write`, or `owner` access to either channels (`channel_ids`) or users (`user_ids`) — exactly one of the two is required. The `owner` level is user-only and subject to additional server-side rules. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Set conversation read cursor
tools.description: Marks a message, specified by its timestamp (`ts`), as the most recently read for the authenticated user in the given `channel`, provided the user is a member of the channel and the message exists within it.

tools.name: Set conversation topic
tools.description: Sets or updates the topic for a specified Slack conversation.

tools.name: Mark user as active
tools.description: Tool to mark a user as active in Slack. Note: This endpoint is deprecated and non-functional - it exists for backwards compatibility but does not perform any action.

tools.name: Set user presence
tools.description: Manually sets a user's Slack presence, overriding automatic detection; this setting persists across connections but can be overridden by user actions or Slack's auto-away (e.g., after 10 mins of inactivity).

tools.name: Share a remote file in channels
tools.description: Shares a remote file, which must already be registered with Slack, into specified Slack channels or direct message conversations.

tools.name: Start call
tools.description: Registers a new call in Slack using `calls.add` for third-party call integration; `created_by` is required if not using a user-specific token.

tools.name: Unarchive channel
tools.description: Reverses conversation archival.

tools.name: Unpin message from channel
tools.description: Unpins a message, identified by its timestamp, from a specified channel if the message is currently pinned there; this operation is destructive.

tools.name: Update call information
tools.description: Updates the title, join URL, or desktop app join URL for an existing Slack call identified by its ID.

tools.name: Update Slack List
tools.description: Updates a Slack List's metadata via `slackLists.update`. Only the List's `name`, `description_blocks`, and `todo_mode` are editable here. The List to update is identified by its `id` (not `list_id`). Descriptions are rich text — a plain string is wrapped into a `rich_text` block automatically. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Update Slack List item
tools.description: Updates one or more cells in an EXISTING Slack List row via `slackLists.items.update`. Each cell is identified by `row_id` (an existing row ID matching `^Rec[A-Z0-9]{8,}$`) and `column_id` and carries a typed value; text columns require Block Kit `rich_text` (a plain string is wrapped automatically), and `select` takes the column's choice values (e.g. `["todo"]`). Use it to UPDATE existing rows; the live API rejects `row_id_to_create` inside a cell (despite Slack's inline example), so to ADD a row use `create_slack_list_item`. Requires a user token with the `lists:write` scope.

tools.name: Update an existing remote file
tools.description: Updates metadata or content details for an existing remote file in Slack; this action cannot upload new files or change the fundamental file type.

tools.name: Update a Slack message
tools.description: Updates a Slack message by timestamp. Provide exactly one visible content mode: `markdown_text` for normal Markdown content, or `blocks` for raw Slack Block Kit layouts. Use `fallback_text` only with `blocks`; it maps to Slack's top-level `text` fallback.

tools.name: Update Slack user group
tools.description: Updates an existing Slack User Group, which must be specified by an existing `usergroup` ID, with new optional details such as its name, description, handle, or default channels.

tools.name: Update user group members
tools.description: Replaces all members of an existing Slack User Group with a new list of valid user IDs.

tools.name: Upload or create a file in Slack
tools.description: Upload files, images, screenshots, documents, or any media to Slack channels or threads. Supports all file types including images (PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF), documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT), code files, and more. Can share files publicly in channels or as thread replies with optional comments. Large files may fail with `upload_too_large`; use SLACK_ADD_A_REMOTE_FILE_FROM_A_SERVICE for large uploads. If the API returns `ok=false` with `method_deprecated`, fall back to SLACK_ADD_A_REMOTE_FILE_FROM_A_SERVICE or SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE with a URL.

triggers.name: New Channel Created Trigger
triggers.description: Triggered when a new channel is created in Slack.

triggers.name: Channel Message Received
triggers.description:
Triggered when a message is posted in a Slack channel
(public, private, or multi-party IM). Does NOT match direct messages.

triggers.name: Direct Message Received
triggers.description:
Triggered when a new direct message (DM) is sent to a user in Slack.
