tools.description: Updates the `idModel` (the monitored Trello entity like a board, list, or card) for an active webhook `idWebhook` to the new model ID `value`; other webhook properties are unaffected.

tools.name: Who Am I
tools.description: Return the identity (username, email) of the connected Trello account.

triggers.name: Attachment Added To Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a file or link is attached to a card.

triggers.name: Attachment Removed From Card
triggers.description:
Triggers when an attachment is removed from a card. Trello drops the
attachment's URL from this event.

triggers.name: Board Added To Workspace
triggers.description:
Triggers when a board enters the watched Workspace — the Trello equivalent
of a new project starting. Covers both a board created inside the Workspace
and an existing board moved into it.

triggers.name: Board Label Created
triggers.description:
Triggers when a label is added to the board's label set. Applying an
existing label to a card is TRELLO_LABEL_ADDED_TO_CARD.

triggers.name: Board Label Deleted
triggers.description:
Triggers when a label is deleted from the board's label set. Trello drops
the label's text and colour from this event.

triggers.name: Board Label Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when a board label changes. `old` carries the previous value of the
field that changed.

triggers.name: Board Member Role Changed
triggers.description:
Triggers when a board member is promoted to admin or demoted to a normal
member. `role` says which they hold now. Changes to and from Trello's
observer role are not covered.

triggers.name: Board Removed From Workspace
triggers.description: Triggers when a board leaves the watched Workspace.

triggers.name: Board Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when the watched board is renamed, its description changes, it is
closed or reopened, or one of its preferences changes — commenting,
self-join, voting or card covers. `old` carries the previous value of the
one field that changed. Board visibility changes emit no Trello event, so
this never fires for a board becoming public or private.

triggers.name: Card Copied
triggers.description:
Triggers when a card is duplicated onto the watched board. The copy is the
card in the payload; `source_card` is the one it came from.

triggers.name: Card Created
triggers.description:
Triggers when a new card is typed onto the watched board. A card that
arrives by being copied, converted from a checklist item, or moved in from
another board has its own trigger.

triggers.name: Card Created From Checklist Item
triggers.description:
Triggers when a checklist item is promoted into a card of its own — a
sub-task becoming tracked work.

triggers.name: Card Deleted
triggers.description:
Triggers when a card is permanently deleted from the watched board. Trello
drops the card's title from this event, so only its ids are available.

triggers.name: Card Moved Between Lists
triggers.description:
Triggers when a card moves from one list to another on the watched board —
the hook for stage-change automations such as 'when a card reaches Done,
close the linked issue'. Moving a card within its own list changes only its
position and emits nothing.

triggers.name: Card Moved In From Another Board
triggers.description:
Triggers when a card is moved onto the watched board from a different one —
a triage board handing work to a sprint board, say.

triggers.name: Card Moved Out To Another Board
triggers.description: Triggers when a card leaves the watched board for a different one.

triggers.name: Card Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when a card's title, description, due date, start date, completion
checkbox or archived state changes. `old` carries the previous value of the
one field that changed and `card` carries the new one. Moving a card to a
different list is TRELLO_CARD_MOVED_BETWEEN_LISTS instead.

triggers.name: Card Vote Changed
triggers.description:
Triggers when a vote is cast on or withdrawn from a card — `voted` says
which. Voting has to be enabled on the board for this to be possible.

triggers.name: Checklist Added To Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a checklist is attached to a card.

triggers.name: Checklist Item Added
triggers.description: Triggers when an item is added to a checklist.

triggers.name: Checklist Item Deleted
triggers.description: Triggers when an item is deleted from a checklist.

triggers.name: Checklist Item State Changed
triggers.description:
Triggers when a checklist item is ticked off or un-ticked.
`check_item.state` says which.

triggers.name: Checklist Item Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when a checklist item changes. `old` carries the previous value of
the field that changed.

triggers.name: Checklist Removed From Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a checklist is deleted from a card.

triggers.name: Checklist Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when a checklist changes. `old` carries the previous value of the
field that changed.

triggers.name: Comment Added To Card
triggers.description:
Triggers when someone comments on a card. Comments carried over by copying a
card are TRELLO_COMMENT_COPIED_TO_CARD, so this never replays history.

triggers.name: Comment Copied To Card
triggers.description:
Triggers when a comment is carried onto a new card by copying the card it
was on. Copying a card with ten comments emits ten of these at once, all of
them historical — mirror them, do not treat them as new activity.

triggers.name: Comment Deleted From Card
triggers.description:
Triggers when a comment is deleted from a card. Trello drops the comment
text from this event.

triggers.name: Comment Edited On Card
triggers.description: Triggers when an existing comment on a card is edited.

triggers.name: Label Added To Card
triggers.description:
Triggers when a label is applied to a card — the hook for triage automations
such as 'when Urgent is applied, page on-call'.

triggers.name: Label Removed From Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a label is taken off a card.

triggers.name: List Created
triggers.description: Triggers when a new list is added to the watched board.

triggers.name: List Moved In From Another Board
triggers.description:
Triggers when a whole list is moved onto the watched board from a different
one.

triggers.name: List Moved Out To Another Board
triggers.description:
Triggers when a whole list is moved off the watched board to a different
one.

triggers.name: List Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when a list is renamed, archived, restored, or moved to a different
position on the board. `old` carries the previous value of the one field
that changed and `list` carries the new one.

triggers.name: Member Added To Board
triggers.description:
Triggers when someone joins the watched board. An invitation to a person who
has not accepted yet is TRELLO_MEMBER_INVITED_TO_BOARD.

triggers.name: Member Added To Workspace
triggers.description: Triggers when someone joins the watched Workspace.

triggers.name: Member Assigned To Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a member is added to a card.

triggers.name: Member Invited To Board
triggers.description:
Triggers when someone is invited to the watched board and has not accepted
yet. Trello does not name the invited person in this event — no email and no
member id — so the payload carries the board and who sent the invitation.
TRELLO_MEMBER_ADDED_TO_BOARD fires when they accept.

triggers.name: Member Removed From Board
triggers.description: Triggers when someone leaves or is removed from the watched board.

triggers.name: Member Removed From Workspace
triggers.description: Triggers when someone leaves or is removed from the watched Workspace.

triggers.name: Member Unassigned From Card
triggers.description: Triggers when a member comes off a card.

triggers.name: Workspace Updated
triggers.description:
Triggers when the watched Workspace's display name or description changes.
`old` carries the previous value of the one field that changed.

required.name: consumer_key

optional.description: Access token injected automatically after OAuth2 authentication flow.

name: Apollo
description: Apollo provides CRM and lead generation capabilities, helping businesses discover contacts, manage outreach, and track sales pipelines for consistent customer relationship development

tools.name: Activate Sequence
tools.description: Activate an inactive Apollo sequence and begin its scheduled outreach. Activation allows Apollo to send emails externally to enrolled contacts according to the sequence's configured steps and schedule. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/approve-sequence

tools.name: Add Contacts to Sequence
tools.description: Adds contacts to a specified Apollo email sequence and returns the contact details. `sequence_id`, `emailer_campaign_id`, and `send_email_from_email_account_id` must be retrieved from Apollo listing/search endpoints before calling this tool — these IDs cannot be inferred from names.

tools.name: Add People to Prospects
tools.description: Save Apollo person IDs returned by APOLLO_PEOPLE_SEARCH as persistent prospect contacts. Unlike APOLLO_CREATE_CONTACT, this converts existing Apollo search results instead of creating a contact from caller-supplied attributes. Requires a paid Apollo plan. Apollo can also create an associated account record, which its API cannot delete; obtain explicit user confirmation before execution.

tools.name: Archive Sequence
tools.description: Archive an Apollo sequence, making it inactive and finishing all enrolled contacts. This lifecycle change can end outreach for every contact currently in the sequence. The caller must own the sequence or have full-access sharing permission. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/archive-sequence

tools.name: Bulk organization enrichment
tools.description: Enriches data for up to 10 organizations simultaneously by providing a list of their base company domains (e.g., 'apollo.io', not 'www.apollo.io'). Charged per domain enriched.

price.description: Estimated $0.02 per organization enriched in the batch

tools.name: Bulk people enrichment
tools.description: Use to enrich multiple person profiles simultaneously with comprehensive data from Apollo's database. Charged per person enriched; avoid re-enriching the same contacts. Responses may include null or missing fields (e.g., email, phone, organization); treat unmatched records as valid 'no match' outcomes, not errors. Heavy use may trigger HTTP 429; respect Retry-After headers.

price.description: $0.02–$0.18 per person enriched; waterfall may cost more.

tools.name: Bulk update account stage
tools.description: Bulk updates the stage for specified existing Apollo.io accounts, moving them to a valid new account stage.

tools.name: Complete Apollo Task
tools.description: Permanently mark an Apollo task as completed and return its resulting state. Apollo provides no undo or reopen route, so confirm the task ID before calling.

tools.name: Create an Apollo account
tools.description: Creates a new account in Apollo.io; a new record is created even if a similar account exists, and provided `owner_id` or `account_stage_id` must be valid existing IDs. The response includes the new account's ID, which can be used directly in subsequent calls.

tools.name: Bulk create Apollo accounts
tools.description: Creates multiple accounts in Apollo.io with a single API call (maximum 100 accounts per request). Use when creating multiple company records at once.

tools.name: Bulk create Apollo contacts
tools.description: Tool to bulk create multiple contacts in Apollo with a single API call. Use when you need to create multiple contacts efficiently. Supports up to 100 contacts per request with optional deduplication.

tools.name: Create call record in Apollo
tools.description: Tool to log call records in Apollo from external systems. Use when recording calls made through outside systems like Orum or Nooks; requires a master API key and cannot dial prospects directly.

tools.name: Create Apollo contact
tools.description: Creates a new contact in Apollo.io; use `account_id` to link to an organization and `contact_stage_id` for sales stage. Apollo does not auto-deduplicate — duplicate records sharing the same email are silently created; always search via APOLLO_SEARCH_CONTACTS before calling this tool. Requires explicit user confirmation before execution.

tools.name: Create custom field
tools.description: Creates a new custom field in Apollo.io for contacts, accounts, or opportunities. Use when you need to define additional data fields beyond Apollo's standard attributes.

tools.name: Create Apollo deal
tools.description: Creates a new sales opportunity (deal) in Apollo.io; all provided IDs (`owner_id`, `account_id`, `opportunity_stage_id`) must be valid existing Apollo identifiers. This action has persistent side effects — obtain explicit user confirmation before invoking.

tools.name: Create Email Draft
tools.description: Create an unsent Apollo outreach draft, or return the existing draft already linked to outreach_task_id.

tools.name: Create Apollo Sequence
tools.description: Create an Apollo outreach sequence, optionally including steps and email variants.

tools.name: Create Apollo Sequence Step
tools.description: Create one step at a specified position in an existing Apollo outreach sequence.

tools.name: Create Apollo Task
tools.description: Tool to create a single task in Apollo.io. Use when you need to add a new task to your team's Apollo account for a specific contact. The task will be assigned to a user and includes details like type, status, priority, due date, and optional notes.

tools.name: Deactivate Sequence
tools.description: Deactivate an active Apollo sequence. Deactivation pauses all enrolled contacts and stops scheduled email sends. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/abort-sequence

tools.name: Export Conversations
tools.description: Start an asynchronous gzipped JSON conversation export and email a team member when it is ready. Each exported conversation with AI insights costs 1 credit; conversations without AI insights are free. Free plans allow one export request per minute and 20 per hour.

tools.name: Get Account by ID
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific account by its Apollo ID. Use when you need to fetch complete account data including company details, contact information, and CRM integration fields.

tools.name: Check Apollo API key status
tools.description: Tool to check whether the provided Apollo API key is valid and accepted by Apollo (health/auth check).

tools.name: Get Apollo Contact
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific contact by its ID. Use this to view contact details including name, email, phone numbers, organization, and custom fields.

tools.name: Get Conversation
tools.description: Retrieve full Apollo conversation details, including transcript, participants, recordings, and opportunities. Charged only when AI insights are present; otherwise free.

tools.name: Get Conversation Export
tools.description: Retrieve the download redirect URL for a previously started Apollo conversation export.

tools.name: Get Current User Profile
tools.description: Return the authenticated Apollo user's identity and optional credit balances.

tools.name: Get Apollo deal
tools.description: Retrieves information about a specific deal by its ID. Use this when you need to view details of a single deal.

tools.name: Get Email Activities
tools.description: Retrieves content, open and click activity, and recipient details for one Apollo sequence email. Requires a master API key; OAuth is unsupported.

tools.name: Get Email Content
tools.description: Retrieve content for up to 10 sent team outreach emails.

tools.name: Get Labels
tools.description: Retrieves all labels from Apollo.io, used for organizing contacts and accounts. Call this before APOLLO_CREATE_CONTACT or APOLLO_UPDATE_ACCOUNT to validate label values against the returned list; mismatched labels cause 400/422 errors.

tools.name: Get opportunity stages
tools.description: Retrieves all configured opportunity (deal) stages from the Apollo.io account.

tools.name: Get Organization by ID
tools.description: Retrieves complete information about a specific organization by its Apollo ID. Use when you need detailed company data including funding, technologies, employee counts, and more.

tools.name: Get Organization Job Postings
tools.description: Retrieves paginated job postings for a specified organization by its ID, optionally filtering by domain; ensure `organization_id` is a valid identifier.

tools.name: Get Apollo Task
tools.description: Retrieves the full details of one Apollo task by ID, including associated records and type-specific data when present.

tools.name: Get typed custom fields
tools.description: Retrieves all typed custom field definitions available in the Apollo.io instance, detailing their types and configurations. Call before constructing payloads for APOLLO_UPDATE_CONTACT or APOLLO_UPDATE_ACCOUNT — mismatched types or invalid enum options cause 400 errors.

tools.name: Get Apollo User
tools.description: Retrieve one teammate in the connected Apollo workspace by Apollo user ID.

tools.name: List Apollo account stages
tools.description: Retrieves the IDs for all available account stages in your team's Apollo account.

tools.name: List apollo contact stages
tools.description: Retrieves all available contact stages from an Apollo account, including their unique IDs and names.

tools.name: List Apollo deals
tools.description: Retrieves a list of deals from Apollo, using Apollo's default sort order if 'sort_by_field' is omitted.

tools.name: List email accounts
tools.description: Retrieves all email accounts and their details for the authenticated user; takes no parameters.

tools.name: List Fields
tools.description: Retrieves all field definitions from Apollo.io, including system fields and custom fields. Use the optional 'source' parameter to filter by field type (system, custom, or crm_synced).

tools.name: List Apollo Notes
tools.description: List notes associated with Apollo records. Supply at least one contact, account, opportunity, calendar-event, or conversation ID field.

tools.name: List Apollo Users
tools.description: Retrieves a list of all users (teammates) associated with the Apollo account, supporting pagination via `page` and `per_page` parameters. Use this to obtain numeric user IDs required by operations like APOLLO_UPDATE_CONTACT_OWNERSHIP — names or email addresses are not accepted in place of these IDs.

tools.name: Enrich organization data
tools.description: Fetches comprehensive organization enrichment data from Apollo.io for a given company domain; results are most meaningful if the company exists in Apollo's database. Charged on every call; may be unavailable on free plans. Returns HTTP 429 under burst usage; use exponential backoff on retries.

tools.name: Search organizations in Apollo
tools.description: Searches Apollo's database for organizations using various filters; charged on every call (unavailable on free plans). Avoid re-running identical queries and surface quota errors rather than retrying. Retrieves a maximum of 50,000 records; uses `page` (1-500) and `per_page` (1-100) for pagination — check `total_pages` in the response to iterate. Overly strict filter combinations can return zero results; start broad and narrow iteratively. Empty results and `org_not_found` are valid outcomes, not errors.

tools.name: Enrich person with Apollo
tools.description: Enriches and retrieves information for a person from Apollo.io. Requires one of: `id`, `email`, `hashed_email`, `linkedin_url`, or (`first_name` and `last_name` with `organization_name` or `domain`) for matching. `webhook_url` must be provided if `reveal_phone_number` is true. Name-only inputs without `organization_name` or `domain` frequently return no matches.

price.description: $0.02–$0.18 per person enriched; waterfall may cost more.

tools.name: Apollo people search
tools.description: Searches Apollo's contact database for people using various filters; results capped at 50,000 records and does not enrich contact data. Combining multiple strict filters (organization_ids, person_titles, person_seniorities) can return zero results — start broad and narrow iteratively. Result records may have null email, phone, or organization fields.

tools.name: Query Analytics Report
tools.description: Query Apollo analytics metrics, dimensions, filters, and date ranges. This operation is free. Apollo rate limits depend on the connected team's plan; use the returned rate_limit metadata as the source of truth. Metric and dimension descriptions include common Apollo identifiers; team-defined custom metrics use custom_metric_{id}.

tools.name: Search Apollo Accounts
tools.description: Searches for accounts within your existing Apollo.io database using various criteria; requires a paid plan and is limited to 50,000 records.

tools.name: Search for Calls
tools.description: Searches for call records in Apollo.io using filters like date range, duration, direction (inbound/outgoing), users, contacts, purposes, outcomes, and keywords. Supports pagination for efficient data retrieval.

tools.name: Search Apollo contacts
tools.description: Searches Apollo contacts using keywords, stage IDs (from 'List Contact Stages' action), or sorting (max 50,000 records; `sort_ascending` requires `sort_by_field`). Search before creating contacts to avoid duplicates.

tools.name: Search Apollo Conversations
tools.description: Search Apollo video meetings and dialer calls using record, participant, date, scorecard, sorting, and visibility filters.

tools.name: Search news articles
tools.description: Tool to search for news articles about companies in Apollo's database. Use when you need to find recent news, announcements, or updates about specific organizations using their Apollo IDs.

tools.name: Search outreach emails
tools.description: Tool to search for outreach emails sent through Apollo sequences. Use when you need to find emails created and sent by your team as part of Apollo email campaigns. This endpoint requires a master API key and has a display limit of 50,000 records (100 records per page, up to 500 pages).

tools.name: Search sequences
tools.description: Searches for sequences (e.g., automated email campaigns) in Apollo.io.

tools.name: Search tasks
tools.description: Searches for tasks in Apollo.io using filters like keywords, date ranges (due, created, updated), priorities, types, assigned users, associated contacts/accounts, supporting sorting and pagination.

tools.name: Send Email Now
tools.description: Queue an Apollo email for external sending; success means queued, not delivered. This action causes Apollo to send an email outside Composio. Apollo processes the send asynchronously, so callers must check send status separately for delivery. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/send-email-now

tools.name: Update an Apollo account
tools.description: Updates specified attributes of an existing account in Apollo.io.

tools.name: Update account ownership
tools.description: Updates the ownership of multiple Apollo accounts to a specified user. Use when bulk assigning account ownership to a team member.

tools.name: Update Apollo call record
tools.description: Tool to update an existing call record in Apollo.io. Use when you need to modify details of a previously logged phone call such as duration, status, notes, or associated contact/account information.

tools.name: Update Apollo contact details
tools.description: Tool to update an existing contact's information in Apollo. Use when you need to modify contact details such as name, email, phone, title, organization, or custom fields. At least one field beyond contact_id must be provided.

tools.name: Update contact ownership
tools.description: Updates the ownership of specified Apollo contacts to a given Apollo user, who must be part of the same team.

tools.name: Bulk update Apollo contacts
tools.description: Tool to bulk update multiple Apollo contacts with a single API call. Use when updating multiple contacts simultaneously - either apply the same updates to all contacts using contact_ids, or apply different updates to each contact using contact_attributes. Automatically processes asynchronously for more than 100 contacts.

tools.name: Update contact stage
tools.description: Updates the stage for one or more existing contacts in Apollo.io to a new valid contact stage, useful for managing sales funnel progression.

tools.name: Update contact status in sequence
tools.description: Updates a contact's status within a designated Apollo sequence, but cannot set the status to 'active'.

tools.name: Update Apollo deal
tools.description: Updates specified fields of an existing Apollo.io deal (opportunity), requiring a valid `opportunity_id`.

tools.name: Update Apollo List
tools.description: Rename an Apollo list and optionally change its Book of Business status. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/update-a-list

tools.name: Update Sequence
tools.description: Update an Apollo sequence's settings, ownership, sharing, steps, and touches. Supplying emailer_steps replaces the ordered step set and can create, update, reorder, or remove steps and their touches based on the IDs supplied. Apollo can require the current complete step list even for a settings-only update. Reference: https://docs.apollo.io/reference/update-sequence

tools.name: Update Apollo Task
tools.description: Update editable details of an existing Apollo task. Supply at least one update field in addition to task_id.

tools.name: View API Usage Stats
tools.description: Fetches Apollo API usage statistics and rate limits for the connected team. Use before large enrichment/search runs to understand current API usage and plan/budget constraints.

tools.name: View Credit Usage Stats
tools.description: Read team balances by credit type for Apollo's current billing cycle. Balance values represent credits except for the ``dialer`` key, which Apollo reports in minutes. This operation is free.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Apollo API key. Create one in Apollo under Settings → Integrations → API Keys (admin access required); turn on 'Set as master key' so all tools work.

name: Semrush
description: Semrush provides legacy v3 SEO, domain, advertising, and PLA reports alongside v4 backlink and keyword metrics, projects, local listings and reviews, Google Business Profile management, and map rank tracking.

tools.name: Check Semrush account units balance
tools.description: Fetch remaining Semrush Standard API units for a legacy v3 connection. This documented balance request is free. Use it before large paid report batches to fail fast when units are exhausted or below a required threshold.

tools.name: Add Semrush review comment
tools.description: Publish an owner comment to a review that supports replies. This mutation creates a public reply. Requires a Semrush v4 API key and a Local Pro or Business, plus a connected publisher account that permits replies.

tools.name: Get ad copies
tools.description: Retrieves unique ad copies Semrush has observed for a specified domain from a regional database, detailing ads seen in Google's paid search results. Results are a sampled subset, not a complete picture of the domain's advertising. Response is returned as a CSV-like string; parse columns (e.g., Tt, Ds) using the pipe or semicolon delimiter.

tools.name: Get anchor texts
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_ANCHORS' instead. Use this action to get a CSV report of anchor texts for backlinks pointing to a specified, publicly accessible domain, root domain, or URL.

tools.name: Get authority score profile
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_AUTHORITY_SCORE_PROFILE' instead. Retrieves the Authority Score (AS) profile for a specified target, showing the count of referring domains that link to the target for each AS value from 0 to 100.

tools.name: Get backlinks
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_BACKLINKS' instead. Fetches backlinks for a specified domain or URL as a semicolon-delimited CSV string (parse with `sep=';'`); allows customization of columns, sorting, and filtering. Consumes Semrush API credits per request. Ensure `display_limit` surpasses `display_offset` when an offset is used, and note the `urlanchor` filter may have limitations for targets with extensive backlinks.

tools.name: Backlinks overview
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_BACKLINKS_OVERVIEW' instead. Provides a semicolon-delimited (sep=';') CSV summary of backlinks, including Authority Score and link type breakdowns, for a specified and publicly accessible domain, root domain, or URL. A result of 'ERROR 50 :: NOTHING FOUND' means the target has no data in the database and is a valid zero-result response.

tools.name: Batch comparison
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_BACKLINKS_COMPARISON' instead. Compares backlink profiles for multiple specified targets (domains, subdomains, or URLs) to analyze and compare link-building efforts.

tools.name: Batch keyword overview
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. Fetches a keyword overview report from a Semrush regional database for up to 100 keywords, providing metrics like search volume, CPC, and keyword difficulty. Response is CSV-like text (not JSON); parse accordingly. Returns literal string 'ERROR 50 :: NOTHING FOUND' for keywords with no data in the selected database — treat as zero results and fall back to SEMRUSH_KEYWORD_OVERVIEW_ONE_DATABASE or SEMRUSH_KEYWORD_OVERVIEW_ALL_DATABASES for those terms.

tools.name: Broad match keyword
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. Fetches broad match keywords for a given phrase. Response is CSV-like text (not JSON); parse by splitting on line breaks and delimiters. `display_sort` and `display_filter` parameters are defined but currently not utilized by the API call.

tools.name: Get categories
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. Retrieves categories and their 0-1 confidence ratings for a specified domain, subdomain, or URL, with results sorted by rating. Response is returned as semicolon-separated text in a single 'data' field requiring parsing before use. Some niche or atypical targets may return no category data.

tools.name: Get categories profile
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. Retrieves a profile of content categories from referring domains for a specified target, analyzing its first 10,000 referring domains and sorting results by domain count.

tools.name: Get competitor data
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_BACKLINK_COMPETITORS' instead. Retrieves a CSV-formatted report of competitors for a specified target (root domain, domain, or URL) based on shared backlinks or referring domains. Output is a CSV string; use display_limit and display_offset to paginate without silent truncation.

tools.name: Get competitors in organic search
tools.description: Use to get a domain's organic search competitors from Semrush as a semicolon-separated string; `display_date` requires 'YYYYMM15' format if used.

tools.name: Get competitors in paid search
tools.description: Retrieves a list of a domain's competitors in paid search results from a specified regional database.

tools.name: Create Semrush GBP post
tools.description: Create a draft, scheduled, or ready-to-send GBP post. Either content or image_urls must be supplied. Requires EDIT or OWNER rights for an active Semrush location with a Google Business Profile connection.

tools.name: Create Listing Management location
tools.description: Create a Semrush Listing Management location. HTTP success starts asynchronous provisioning; poll Get Listing Management location until its status is COMPLETED or FAILED, which may take up to seven days. Supply at least one location body field. Use the validation action to check a payload without creating. Create locations sequentially; Semrush does not support concurrent create requests and may return 429. Requires a v4 key with Read and write permission and Local Pro or Business. This family does not consume Standard API units.

tools.name: Create location image
tools.description: Add a base64-encoded JPEG or PNG image to a Semrush Listing Management location using a read-write v4 key and Local Pro or Business.

tools.name: Manage Semrush GBP suggestion
tools.description: Start accepting or rejecting an open GBP suggestion. Poll List GBP Suggestions until the status becomes ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or FAILED. Accepting a GBP_USER_EDIT may also close a paired GBP_DATA_MISMATCH suggestion for the same field. Requires EDIT or OWNER rights on an active location.

tools.name: Delete Semrush GBP post
tools.description: Permanently delete a DRAFT, SCHEDULED, or TO_SEND GBP post. Requires EDIT or OWNER rights; posts for frozen or canceled locations cannot be deleted.

tools.name: Delete Listing Management location
tools.description: Permanently delete an eligible location using a read-write v4 key and Local plan.

tools.name: Delete location image
tools.description: Permanently delete an image using a read-write v4 key and Local plan.

tools.name: Delete Semrush review comment
tools.description: Permanently remove a public review comment. This destructive mutation cannot be undone. Requires a Semrush v4 API key and Local Pro or Business, plus a connected publisher account that permits comment removal.

tools.name: Disable location listing
tools.description: Stop distribution for a controllable listing; a parent may affect child listings. Requires a read-write v4 key and Local Pro or Business.

tools.name: Get domain ad history
tools.description: Retrieves a domain's 12-month advertising history from Semrush (keywords bid on, ad positions, ad copy) for PPC strategy and competitor analysis; most effective when the domain has ad history in the selected database.

tools.name: Get domain organic pages
tools.description: Fetches a report on a domain's unique organic pages ranking in Google's top 100 search results, with options for specifying database, date, columns, sorting, and filtering. Response is semicolon-separated CSV text in a single `data` field requiring explicit parsing. The literal response `ERROR 50 :: NOTHING FOUND` means zero results for that domain/database combination, not a system error. Traffic metrics (e.g., `Tr`) are modeled estimates incompatible with first-party analytics data.

tools.name: Get domain organic search keywords
tools.description: Retrieves organic search keywords for a domain from a specified Semrush regional database; `display_positions` must be set if `display_daily=1` for daily updates. Response is semicolon-delimited CSV text (parse with sep=';', cast numeric columns before aggregations). A response of 'ERROR 50 :: NOTHING FOUND' indicates no data for the domain in the selected database — treat as a valid zero-result.

tools.name: Get domain organic subdomains
tools.description: Retrieves a report on subdomains of a given domain that rank in Google's top 100 organic search results for a specified regional database.

tools.name: Get domain paid search keywords
tools.description: Fetches keywords driving paid search traffic to a specified, existing domain using a supported Semrush regional database.

tools.name: Get PLA search keywords for a domain
tools.description: Retrieves Product Listing Ad (PLA) search keywords for a specified domain from a Semrush regional database.

tools.name: Compare domains
tools.description: Analyzes keyword rankings by comparing up to five domains to find common, unique, or gap keywords, using specified organic/paid types and comparison logic in the `domains` string.

tools.name: Enable location listing
tools.description: Resume distribution for a controllable disconnected listing. Requires a read-write v4 key and Local Pro or Business.

tools.name: Get Semrush GBP metrics
tools.description: Return GBP metrics for up to five locations. Provide at least one of `aggregated_metrics` or `total_metrics`. Requires a Semrush v4 API key and Local Pro or Business. Each location requires a Google Business Profile connection. Semrush does not document the total_metrics response shape, so that field remains untyped.

tools.name: Get Listing Management location
tools.description: Get one Listing Management location using a v4 key and Local Pro or Business.

tools.name: Get Semrush review auto-reply config
tools.description: Return review auto-reply settings for a location. Requires a Semrush v4 API key, Local Pro or Business, and a GBP connection.

tools.name: Get Semrush review overview
tools.description: Return review counts, rating distribution, and reply statistics. Requires a Semrush v4 API key, Local Pro or Business, and a GBP connection.

tools.name: Get historical data
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_BACKLINKS_HISTORICAL_SUMMARY' instead. Retrieves monthly historical backlink and referring domain data for a specified root domain, returned as a time series string with newest records first.

tools.name: Get indexed pages
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_INDEXED_PAGES' instead. Retrieves a list of indexed pages from Semrush for a specified `target` (root domain, domain, or URL) and `target_type`, ensuring `target` is publicly accessible, Semrush-analyzable, and correctly matches `target_type`. Returns CSV-like text output requiring parsing before structured analysis.

tools.name: Get keyword difficulty
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_KEYWORD_METRICS' instead. Returns CSV-formatted text; parse before programmatic use.

tools.name: Keyword overview all databases
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. Fetches a keyword overview from Semrush for a specified phrase, including metrics like search volume, CPC, and competition. Response is returned as a CSV-like string; parse headers and rows into a structured table before extracting values like Nq, Cp, or Kd.

tools.name: Get keyword overview for one database
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Please use 'SEMRUSH_V4_KEYWORD_METRICS' instead. Fetches a keyword summary for a specified phrase from a chosen regional database. Returns CSV-like text (not JSON) with column headers matching `export_columns` codes (e.g., 'Ph', 'Nq', 'Kd'); parse headers and rows into structured data before use. A plain-text 'ERROR 50 :: NOTHING FOUND' response indicates zero results, not a transport error.

tools.name: Get keywords ads history
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Semrush has deprecated this v3 report; no v4 equivalent exists. tools.name: List Semrush GBP additional-hour types

tools.name: List Semrush GBP attributes
tools.description: Return GBP attributes and allowed values for a category and country. Requires a Semrush v4 API key and Local Pro or Business.

tools.name: List Semrush GBP posts

tools.name: List Semrush GBP suggestions

tools.name: List Listing Management locations
tools.description: List locations using a v4 key and Local Pro or Business; uses no API units.

tools.name: List location categories

tools.name: List location images

required.name: generic_api_key

required.name: generic_id

name: Mem0
description: Mem0 is an universal, self-improving memory layer for LLM applications.

tools.name: Add member to project
tools.description: Adds an existing user to a project (identified by `project_id` within organization `org_id`), assigning a valid system role.

tools.name: Add new memory records
tools.description: Stores new memory records from a list of messages, optionally inferring structured content; requires association via `agent_id`, `user_id`, `app_id`, or `run_id`.

tools.name: Add organization member
tools.description: Adds a new member, who must be a registered user, to an organization, assigning them a specific role.

tools.name: Create a new agent
tools.description: Creates a new agent with a unique `agent_id` and an optional `name`; additional metadata may be assigned by the system.

tools.name: Create a new agent run
tools.description: Creates a new agent run in the mem0.ai system.

tools.name: Create a new application
tools.description: Creates a new application, allowing metadata to be passed in the request body (not an explicit field in this action's request model); ensure `app_id` is unique to avoid potential errors or unintended updates.

tools.name: Create a new organization entry
tools.description: Creates a new organization entry using the provided name and returns its details.

tools.name: Create a new user
tools.description: Creates a new user with the specified unique `user_id` and supports associating `metadata` (not part of the request schema fields).

tools.name: Create memory entry
tools.description: Lists/searches existing memory entries with filtering and pagination; critically, this action retrieves memories and does *not* create new ones, despite its name.

tools.name: Create project
tools.description: Creates a new project with a given name within an organization that must already exist.

tools.name: Create webhook
tools.description: Creates a new webhook for a specific project to receive real-time notifications. Use when you need to set up event-driven integrations that trigger on memory operations.

tools.name: Delete an organization
tools.description: Permanently deletes an existing organization identified by its unique ID.

tools.name: Delete memory by id
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific memory by its unique ID; ensure the `memory_id` exists as this operation is irreversible.

tools.name: Delete entity by type and id
tools.description: Call to permanently and irreversibly hard-delete an existing entity (user, agent, app, or run) and all its associated data, using its type and ID.

tools.name: Delete memories
tools.description: Deletes all memories matching specified filter criteria. IMPORTANT: At least one filter (agent_id, user_id, app_id, or run_id) must be provided to prevent accidental deletion of all memories. Requires delete permissions on the organization/project.

tools.name: Delete memory batch with uuids
tools.description: Deletes a batch of up to 1000 existing memories, identified by their UUIDs, in a single API call.

tools.name: Delete project
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific project and all its associated data from an organization; this action cannot be undone and requires the project to exist within the specified organization.

tools.name: Delete project member
tools.description: Removes an existing member, specified by email address, from a project, immediately revoking their project-specific access; the user is not removed from the organization.

tools.name: Delete webhook
tools.description: Deletes a webhook and stops receiving notifications for the specified webhook ID. Use this when you no longer need webhook notifications or want to remove a specific webhook configuration.

tools.name: Export data based on filters
tools.description: Creates a new memory export job with optional entity filters (user_id, agent_id, app_id, run_id). Returns export job ID and confirmation message. Requires org_id and project_id. Uses default schema for memory structure if not specified.

tools.name: List organizations
tools.description: Retrieves a summary list of organizations for administrative oversight; returns summary data (names, IDs), not exhaustive details, despite 'detailed' in the name.

tools.name: Fetch details of a specific organization
tools.description: Fetches comprehensive details for an organization using its `org_id`; the `org_id` must be valid and for an existing organization.

tools.name: Get list of entity filters
tools.description: Retrieves predefined filter definitions for entities (e.g., by type, creation/modification date); returns definitions only, not filtered entity data.

tools.name: Get entity by id
tools.description: Fetches detailed information for an existing entity (user, agent, app, or run) identified by its type and unique ID.

tools.name: Get event status by event ID
tools.description: Retrieves a single async event by ID to check its current status and results. Use this after operations that return event IDs (e.g., add_new_memory_records) to poll for completion before proceeding with dependent operations.

tools.name: Get memories by entity
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all memories associated with a specific entity (user, agent, app, or run). Use when you need to fetch memories for a known entity type and ID combination.

tools.name: Get memory export
tools.description: Retrieves the status and results of a memory export job by its ID. Use this after creating an export job to fetch the processed memory data. The response structure matches the schema defined during export creation.

tools.name: Get organization members
tools.description: Fetches a list of members for a specified, existing organization.

tools.name: Get project details
tools.description: Fetches comprehensive details for a specified project within an organization.

tools.name: Get project members
tools.description: Retrieves all members for a specified project within an organization.

tools.name: Get projects
tools.description: Retrieves all projects for a given organization `org_id` to which the caller has access.

tools.name: Get project webhooks
tools.description: Retrieves all webhooks configured for a specific project. Use this to list webhook configurations including their event types, URLs, and active status.

tools.name: Get user memory stats
tools.description: Retrieves a summary of the authenticated user's memory activity, including total memories created, search events, and add events. Note: This endpoint is undocumented in the official mem0 API specification but is functional.

tools.name: List entities
tools.description: Retrieves a list of entities, optionally filtered by organization or project (prefer `org_id`/`project_id` over deprecated `org_name`/`project_name`), noting results may be summaries and subject to limits.

tools.name: Perform semantic search on memories
tools.description: Searches memories semantically using a natural language query and metadata filters. IMPORTANT: - At least one of 'user_id', 'agent_id', or 'run_id' MUST be provided - A non-empty 'query' string is REQUIRED for semantic search - To retrieve memories without a search query, use 'retrieve_memory_list' action instead

tools.name: Remove a member from the organization
tools.description: Removes a member, specified by their username, from an existing organization of which they are currently a member.

tools.name: Retrieve all events for the currently logged in user
tools.description: Retrieves a paginated list of events for the authenticated user, filterable and paginable via URL query parameters. This is a read-only operation that does not modify data. Supported Query Parameters (applied directly to the request URL): - `event_type` (str, optional): Filters events by their type (e.g., 'ADD', 'SEARCH'). - `start_date` (str, optional): Filters events on or after this date (format: YYYY-MM-DD). - `end_date` (str, optional): Filters events on or before this date (format: YYYY-MM-DD). - `page` (int, optional): Specifies the page number for paginated results. - `page_size` (int, optional): Number of events per page (default: 50, max: 100).

tools.name: Retrieve list of memory events
tools.description: Retrieves a chronological list of all memory events (e.g., user inputs, AI responses) from the Mem0 platform, providing interaction history and context for AI assistants.

tools.name: Retrieve memory by id
tools.description: Retrieves a complete memory entry by its unique identifier; `memory_id` must be valid and for an existing memory.

tools.name: Retrieve memory history by id
tools.description: Retrieves the complete version history for an existing memory, using its unique `memory_id`, to inspect its evolution or audit changes.

tools.name: Retrieve memory list
tools.description: Retrieves a list of memories, supporting pagination and diverse filtering (e.g., by IDs, metadata, keywords, date ranges); ensure dates are ISO 8601 and `page`/`page_size` (if used) are positive integers. REQUIRED: At least one of agent_id, user_id, app_id, or run_id must be provided.

tools.name: Search memories with filters
tools.description: Semantically searches memories using structured filters with an optional natural language query. If query is omitted, defaults to '*' (wildcard) for filter-only searches. Offers options to rerank results, select specific fields, and adjust similarity threshold; any provided `org_id` or `project_id` must reference a valid existing entity.

tools.name: Update memory batch with uuid
tools.description: Updates text for up to 1000 memories in a single batch, using their UUIDs.

tools.name: Update memory text content
tools.description: Updates the text content of an existing memory, identified by its `memory_id`.

tools.name: Update organization member role
tools.description: Updates the role of an existing member to a new valid role within an existing organization.

tools.name: Update project
tools.description: Updates a project by `project_id` within an `org_id`, modifying only provided fields (name, description, custom_instructions, custom_categories); list fields are fully replaced (cleared by `[]`), other omitted/null fields remain unchanged.

tools.name: Update project member role
tools.description: Updates the role of a specific member within a designated project, ensuring the new role is valid and recognized by the system.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Mem0 API key for authentication. Obtain it from your Mem0 settings.

name: Neon
description: Postgres, on a serverless platform designed to help you build reliable and scalable applications faster

tools.name: Accept project transfer request
tools.description: Accepts a pending transfer request and irreversibly moves the Neon project to the authenticated account or specified organization. This consumes the request and changes project ownership. Confirm the destination before calling, and do not retry an ambiguous failure because the transfer may already have completed.

tools.name: Count project branches
tools.description: Tool to get the total number of branches in a Neon project. Use when you need to count branches without retrieving full branch details. Optionally filter by branch name using the search parameter.

tools.name: Create API key
tools.description: Creates a new personal API key for the authenticated Neon user account. Use this action to generate API keys for programmatic access to Neon services, such as CI/CD pipelines, backend integrations, or development environments. Each key should have a descriptive name to help identify its purpose. IMPORTANT: The returned 'key' value is shown only once - store it securely immediately after creation. To manage organization-level API keys, use the organization API key endpoints instead.

tools.name: Create API Key for Organization
tools.description: Creates a new API key for the specified organization in Neon. The API key is used for authenticating and authorizing access to the Neon API. The `key_name` parameter allows for easy identification and management of multiple API keys within the organization. IMPORTANT: The actual API key value is returned only once in the response and cannot be retrieved later. Store it securely immediately after creation. Organization API keys provide admin-level access to all organization resources, including projects, members, and settings. Only organization admins can create these keys.

tools.name: Create Auth Provider SDK Keys
tools.description: Tool to generate SDK or API keys for authentication providers. Use when setting up authentication for a Neon project with providers like Stack Auth, Better Auth, or for testing with mock provider.

tools.name: Create auth user
tools.description: Tool to create a new user in Neon Auth for a specific project branch. Use when you need to add authentication users to a branch that has Neon Auth enabled with the 'stack' provider. The branch must already have Neon Auth configured before creating users.

tools.name: Create branch database
tools.description: Creates a new database within a specified project and branch in the Neon platform. This endpoint allows users to set up a new database with a custom name and assign an owner role, facilitating the organization and management of databases within the Neon ecosystem. It should be used when initializing a new database for a specific project or when branching requires a separate database instance. The endpoint is particularly useful for developers and database administrators who need to quickly set up new databases as part of their workflow or application deployment process. Note that this operation only creates the database; additional steps may be required to configure specific schemas, tables, or access permissions within the newly created database.

tools.name: Enable Neon Auth for branch
tools.description: Tool to enable Neon Auth integration for a branch. Use when you need to set up authentication for a specific branch in a Neon project.

tools.name: Create Neon Data API
tools.description: Creates a Neon Data API REST endpoint for an existing branch database. Authentication is optional: use neon_auth for Neon's managed authentication, or external with jwks_url for an external JWT provider.

tools.name: Create branch snapshot
tools.description: Creates a snapshot from the specified branch at a specific point in time. Snapshots capture the state of a branch and can be used for database versioning, creating backups, or establishing checkpoints for AI agents. Use when you need to preserve the exact state of your database at a moment in time. This endpoint may initiate an asynchronous operation.

tools.name: Create compute endpoint
tools.description: Creates a compute endpoint for a Neon branch. Each branch supports at most one read_write endpoint and can have multiple read_only endpoints. Use this to make a branch connectable or add a read replica; it does not modify an existing endpoint.

tools.name: Create project branch
tools.description: Creates a new branch in a Neon project. Branches are copy-on-write clones of the parent branch's data, perfect for creating development/staging environments, testing features, or previewing database changes without affecting production. The branch is created from the project's default branch unless a parent_id is specified. By default, the branch copies all data from the parent ('parent-data'). Note: A branch is created without a compute endpoint. To connect to the branch, use the 'create_compute_endpoint' action to add a read_write or read_only endpoint.

tools.name: Create anonymized branch
tools.description: Creates a Beta anonymized branch using PostgreSQL Anonymizer. It can store masking rules and, when start_anonymization is true, immediately applies irreversible masking to the new branch's copied data.

tools.name: Create project branch role
tools.description: Creates a PostgreSQL role in a Neon branch. Existing connections to the branch's active compute endpoint are dropped; an idle endpoint is activated briefly. The branch must already have a compute endpoint. Login roles receive a generated password in the create response. Set no_login for a group or permission-only role that cannot connect.

tools.name: Create project JWKS
tools.description: Adds a new JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) URL to a Neon project for JWT-based authentication. The JWKS URL must point to a valid HTTPS endpoint that returns cryptographic keys used to verify JSON Web Tokens (JWTs). Use this action to configure authentication with identity providers like Google, Microsoft, Apple, Auth0, Clerk, or Stytch. The JWKS can be scoped to specific branches and mapped to database roles. Maximum of 10 role names can be associated with each JWKS configuration.

tools.name: Create project permission
tools.description: Grants the specified email address access to a Neon project. Use this to add a new project collaborator. It creates a project permission; it does not modify an existing permission or select a permission level.

tools.name: Create project transfer request
tools.description: Creates a transfer request for a Neon project. The request expires after its configured validity period. Requires the `urn:neoncloud:orgs:delete` OAuth scope on the connection; it is not in the default scope set.

tools.name: Create project with quota and settings
tools.description: Creates a Neon project and can also enable logical replication in its project settings. Optional configuration includes quotas, network restrictions, autoscaling, maintenance windows, and default branch settings. WARNING: Enabling logical replication is an irreversible project-settings update and suspends all active compute endpoints; the API does not provide a way to disable it afterward.

tools.name: Set VPC endpoint restriction
tools.description: Sets or updates a VPC endpoint restriction for a Neon project. When a VPC endpoint restriction is set, the project only accepts connections from the specified VPC endpoint, providing network-level security isolation. This is useful for Private Networking scenarios where you want to restrict database access to only connections coming through a specific AWS VPC endpoint. The VPC endpoint must first be assigned to the parent organization (using the organization-level VPC endpoint API) before it can be used as a project restriction. The operation is idempotent - repeated calls with the same parameters will not create additional changes. Note: This is a paid feature requiring a Neon Business or Enterprise plan.

tools.name: Assign or Update VPC Endpoint
tools.description: Assigns an existing AWS VPC endpoint to a Neon organization, or updates the label of that assignment. Azure regions are unsupported. The endpoint must already exist in AWS and Private Networking requires an eligible Neon plan.

tools.name: Delete api key by id
tools.description: Deletes a specific API key from the Neon platform. This endpoint should be used when you need to revoke access for a particular API key, such as when an employee leaves the organization or when you suspect the key has been compromised. The operation is irreversible, so use it with caution. Once deleted, any applications or services using this API key will lose access to Neon's API. This endpoint helps maintain the security of your Neon account by allowing you to manage and control API key access effectively.

tools.name: Delete auth domain from project
tools.description: Deprecated project-level endpoint for deleting trusted redirect domains. Use the branch-level delete action for new integrations. This legacy action keeps its original project-only request contract for existing callers. Deletion immediately removes the domains from the redirect URI whitelist.

tools.name: Delete OAuth provider
tools.description: Deletes an OAuth provider configuration from a specific branch in a Neon project. This removes the OAuth authentication integration for the specified provider (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, or Vercel) from the given branch. Use this action when you need to revoke OAuth access or clean up authentication configurations for a particular branch. Note: This operation is permanent and will affect all users authenticating through this provider on this branch. Neon Auth must be enabled on the branch before OAuth providers can be deleted.

tools.name: Delete auth user
tools.description: Deletes an authentication user from a specified branch within a Neon project. Use this endpoint to permanently remove user access from a particular branch. Important notes: - This operation is permanent and cannot be undone - Successful deletion returns a 204 No Content status - The deleted user will no longer be able to authenticate to the specified branch - This operation only affects the specified branch, not other branches in the project

tools.name: Delete branch auth domains
tools.description: Deletes domains from the redirect_uri whitelist for a specific branch's authentication configuration. Use when you need to revoke access for specific domains in your Neon authentication setup.

tools.name: Delete branch data API
tools.description: Deletes the Neon Data API for a specified branch and database. Use this when you need to remove Data API access for a specific database within a branch.

tools.name: Delete database from branch
tools.description: Permanently deletes a database and all of its data from the specified project branch. Databases on other branches are unaffected.

tools.name: Delete organization api key
tools.description: Deletes a specific API key associated with an organization in the Neon platform. This endpoint is used to revoke access for a particular API key, enhancing security by removing unused or compromised keys. It should be used when an API key is no longer needed, when rotating keys for security purposes, or when an API key may have been exposed. Once deleted, the API key cannot be recovered, and any systems using this key will lose access to the Neon API. Ensure you have a backup or replacement key in place before deletion to avoid service interruptions.

tools.name: Delete organization member
tools.description: Removes a specific member from a Neon organization. This action permanently revokes the member's access to all organization resources. Use this when an employee leaves the company, changes roles, or their access needs to be revoked. Important notes: - This action cannot be undone; re-adding requires a new invitation - You cannot delete the last admin member of an organization - The member_id must be a valid UUID (not the user's email) - Requires admin permissions on the organization Use fetch_organization_members_by_id first to get valid member IDs.

tools.name: Delete project branch by id
tools.description: Deletes a branch and idles its compute endpoints, breaking existing client connections. By default, the branch can be recovered within seven days; set hard_delete to true for immediate permanent deletion. A root or default branch, a branch with children, or a project's only branch cannot be deleted.

tools.name: Delete project branch role
tools.description: Deletes a PostgreSQL role from a specific branch within a Neon project. This permanently removes the role and its associated database permissions. Use this endpoint to: - Remove obsolete user accounts from a database branch - Clean up roles after application decommissioning - Revoke access for former team members Important notes: - This operation is permanent and cannot be undone - The deletion triggers an async 'apply_config' operation on the compute endpoint - If the role doesn't exist, returns 204 No Content (idempotent behavior) - If the role exists and is deleted, returns 200 OK with role and operation details - You cannot delete the default owner role created with the database

tools.name: Delete project by id
tools.description: Deletes a Neon PostgreSQL project and all its associated resources. Deleted projects can be recovered within seven days using Neon's recover-project endpoint. After that recovery window, the project and its endpoints, branches, databases, users, and configurations are permanently removed. Use this action when: - A project is no longer needed - Cleaning up test/development resources - Removing unused projects to free up quota Returns the details of the deleted project upon successful deletion. Returns 404 if the project does not exist or is not accessible.

tools.name: Delete project endpoint
tools.description: Deletes a specific endpoint within a Neon project. This operation permanently removes the endpoint and all associated resources, such as configurations and access points. Use this endpoint when you need to decommission or clean up unused endpoints in your project. It's important to note that this action is irreversible, so ensure you have backed up any necessary data or configurations before proceeding. This endpoint should be used with caution, as it will immediately terminate access to the specified endpoint and may impact any systems or applications relying on it.

tools.name: Delete project jwks by id
tools.description: Permanently deletes a JWKS configuration from a Neon project. JWT authentication that depends on the removed configuration may stop working.

tools.name: Delete project permission
tools.description: Revokes project access for the user associated with a permission ID. Obtain the permission ID by listing project access. Returns the revoked permission directly, including its grant and revocation timestamps.

tools.name: Delete project snapshot
tools.description: Deletes a specific snapshot for a project in Neon. Use when you need to remove an old or unnecessary snapshot to free up storage or clean up resources. **Note**: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

tools.name: Delete vpc endpoint by ids
tools.description: Permanently deletes a VPC endpoint from a Neon organization in a specified AWS region. This removes the private network connection between your AWS VPC and Neon's service. IMPORTANT: This operation is irreversible. Once a VPC endpoint is deleted from a Neon organization, it cannot be re-added to the same organization. Use with caution. Requirements: - Organization must be on the Scale plan (VPC/Private Networking is not available on Free plan) - Only AWS regions are supported (not Azure) - The VPC endpoint must exist in the specified organization and region This action is useful when decommissioning private network connections or cleaning up unused VPC endpoints. Deleting a VPC endpoint will disrupt any applications relying on private connectivity through that endpoint.

tools.name: Delete vpc endpoint by project id
tools.description: Removes a VPC endpoint restriction from a Neon project. It does not delete or unassign the VPC endpoint from its organization. Connections through that VPC endpoint are no longer permitted by this project-level restriction.

tools.name: Disable branches auth
tools.description: Tool to disable Neon Auth for a specific branch in a Neon project. Use when you need to remove authentication integration for a branch. This operation can optionally delete the `neon_auth` schema from the database by setting delete_data to true.

tools.name: Finalize branch restore
tools.description: Finalizes the restore operation for a branch created from a snapshot. This updates the branch to function as the original branch it replaced by: reassigning computes from the original branch (which restarts them), renaming the restored branch to the original's name, and renaming the original branch. Only applies to branches created using the restoreSnapshot endpoint.

tools.name: Get account consumption history
tools.description: Retrieves selected consumption metrics for projects in a Neon organization, grouped by project, billing period, and the requested granularity. Omit project_ids to include all projects, and pass a returned cursor unchanged to retrieve the next page. This request does not wake project computes.

tools.name: Get auth
tools.description: Retrieves authentication information about the current API request credentials. Use this action to verify which account and authentication method are being used for API calls, which is helpful for debugging authentication issues or confirming the identity of the calling user or API key.

tools.name: Get auth allow localhost
tools.description: Retrieves the allow localhost configuration for a specific branch in a Neon project. Use when you need to check if localhost connections are permitted for a branch's authentication settings.

tools.name: Get auth email provider
tools.description: Retrieves the email provider configuration for Neon Auth on a specific branch. Returns SMTP configuration details if a custom provider is configured, or just sender information if using the default Neon email provider. Use this action to verify email settings before testing authentication flows or troubleshooting email delivery issues.

tools.name: Get branch database
tools.description: Returns metadata and configuration for one database in a project branch without modifying the database.

tools.name: Get branches anonymized status
tools.description: Retrieves the current status of an anonymized branch, including its state and progress information. This endpoint allows you to monitor the anonymization process from initialization through completion. Only anonymized branches will have status information available. Use this action when you need to: - Monitor the progress of an anonymization process - Check the state of an anonymized branch (created, initialized, anonymizing, anonymized, error) - View details about the most recent anonymization attempt - Identify when an anonymization operation failed Note: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

tools.name: Get branches backup schedule
tools.description: Retrieves the backup schedule configuration for a specified branch within a Neon project. This endpoint provides information about when backups are created and how long they are retained. Use this when you need to verify or audit the backup schedule settings for a branch. Note: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

tools.name: Get Neon Data API for branch
tools.description: Retrieves the Neon Data API information for a specific branch and database. Use when you need to access the Data API URL, deployment status, or configuration settings for a particular database within a branch.

tools.name: Get branches masking rules
tools.description: Retrieves the masking rules for the specified anonymized branch. Masking rules define how sensitive data should be anonymized using PostgreSQL Anonymizer. Use this when you need to view the data anonymization configuration for a branch. Note: This endpoint is currently in Beta.

tools.name: Get current user information
tools.description: Gets account identifiers, plan details, and linked auth accounts for the currently authenticated Neon user. This action requires credentials tied to a user; organization- and project-scoped API keys do not represent a current user. It accepts no parameters and cannot retrieve another user's profile.

tools.name: Get organization
tools.description: Retrieves one Neon organization's identity and account settings, including its name, handle, billing plan, management source, timestamps, and available organization-level flags. It does not list the organization's members or projects; use the corresponding list actions for those resources.

tools.name: Get organization member
tools.description: Returns one organization's member record, including the associated user ID, organization role, and join timestamp.

tools.name: Get project
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific Neon serverless Postgres project. Returns project data including configuration, database settings, compute resources, owner information, and consumption metrics. Use this action when you need to: - Get project configuration details (region, PostgreSQL version, settings) - Check project ownership and organization membership - Review compute and storage consumption metrics - Verify project settings before making updates The action is read-only and safe to call frequently. For listing multiple projects, use the retrieve_projects_list action instead.

tools.name: Get project branch
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific branch within a Neon project. This endpoint allows developers to fetch the current state and configuration of a branch, including its name, creation timestamp, and other relevant metadata. It's particularly useful when you need to verify branch details, check its status, or gather information for further operations on the branch. The endpoint should be used when you require up-to-date information about a single branch in your project's context. Note that this endpoint only provides read access and does not modify any branch data.

tools.name: Get project branch role
tools.description: Returns a specific PostgreSQL role's branch ID, name, protected status, authentication method, creation and update timestamps, and any related Neon operations. It does not return the role's PostgreSQL privileges, grants, or memberships, and it does not return Neon project permission grants.

tools.name: Get project branch schema comparison
tools.description: Compares the database schema of a branch with another branch's schema in a Neon project. Returns the difference as a unified diff format string. Use this when you need to understand what schema changes exist between two branches (e.g., before merging, to review migrations, or to verify schema consistency). The comparison can be done at specific points in time using LSN or timestamp parameters for both branches.

tools.name: Get project connection uri
tools.description: Returns a PostgreSQL connection URI for a database and role in a Neon project. Optionally targets a branch or endpoint and can return a pooled URI.

tools.name: Get project endpoint
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific compute endpoint within a Neon serverless PostgreSQL project. Compute endpoints are the connection points for your Neon databases. Use this action to get information about a specific endpoint including its hostname for connections, autoscaling settings, current state (active/idle/suspended), connection pooling config, and PostgreSQL settings. This is useful for getting the connection hostname, checking endpoint health, verifying compute resources, or troubleshooting connection issues. The endpoint_id can be obtained from the list endpoints action. Note: This is a read-only operation.

tools.name: Get project operation by id
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific operation within a Neon serverless PostgreSQL project. Use this endpoint to check the status and details of operations such as compute start/suspend, branch creation/deletion, configuration changes, or timeline operations. This is useful for monitoring long-running tasks, verifying operation completion, or debugging failures. Requires both a project ID and operation ID. Returns operation details including status ('scheduling', 'running', 'finished', 'failed'), duration, and associated branch/endpoint IDs. This is a read-only endpoint.

tools.name: Get schema for project branch
tools.description: Retrieves the PostgreSQL database schema (DDL) for a specific database on a branch within a Neon project. Returns the schema as SQL statements (similar to pg_dump output), including CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and other DDL statements. This is useful for understanding the database structure, comparing schemas between branches, or for documentation purposes. The schema can be retrieved at the current point in time or at a specific historical point using either an LSN or timestamp parameter. Note: The branch's compute endpoint must be active for this endpoint to work.

tools.name: Get VPC endpoint details
tools.description: Retrieves the current state and configuration details of a specific VPC endpoint assigned to a Neon organization. VPC endpoints enable private connectivity between your AWS VPC and Neon databases using AWS PrivateLink, bypassing the public internet. Prerequisites: - Organization must be on the Scale plan or higher (VPC Private Networking is not available on Free or Launch plans) - VPC endpoint must be previously assigned using 'create_vpc_endpoint_with_label' action Use cases: - Check the operational state of a VPC endpoint (new, accepted, available, pending, rejected) - View which projects are restricted to use this VPC endpoint - Verify endpoint configuration for compliance and security auditing - Troubleshoot private connectivity issues Note: This is a read-only endpoint. To modify VPC endpoint configuration, use 'create_vpc_endpoint_with_label' or 'delete_vpc_endpoint_by_ids' actions.

tools.name: List api keys
tools.description: Lists API keys for the authenticated user's Neon account, including key IDs, names, creators, creation times, and last-use metadata. It does not return secret key values or create, update, or delete keys.

tools.name: List auth domains
tools.description: Lists the domains in the redirect_uri whitelist for the specified project and branch. Use when you need to retrieve or verify the allowed domains for authentication redirects.

tools.name: List auth oauth providers
tools.description: Deprecated project-level endpoint for listing OAuth providers. Use the branch-level list action for new integrations. This legacy action intentionally keeps its project-only request contract so existing calls remain valid.

tools.name: List available preload libraries
tools.description: Retrieves the list of available shared preload libraries for a Neon project. Shared preload libraries are PostgreSQL extensions that can be loaded at server startup using the shared_preload_libraries setting. Use this action when you need to: - Discover which PostgreSQL extensions are available for your project - Check versions of available extensions (TimescaleDB, pg_cron, etc.) - Identify experimental vs. stable extensions before configuration - Review default libraries included in your project configuration Returns details about each library including name, version, description, and whether it's experimental or included by default. Common extensions include timescaledb (time-series data), pg_cron (job scheduling), pg_partman_bgw (partition management), and vector search extensions.

tools.name: List branch auth OAuth providers
tools.description: Lists OAuth providers configured for a specific branch's Neon Auth integration. This is the current branch-level endpoint. The response can contain OAuth client IDs and sensitive client secrets; do not expose or log returned credentials.

tools.name: List branch databases
tools.description: Retrieves a list of databases associated with a specific project and branch in the Neon platform. This endpoint allows developers to view all databases within a particular project and branch context, which is useful for managing different environments (e.g., development, staging, production) or versions of an application's database setup. It should be used when you need to inventory the databases in a specific branch or verify the existence of databases in a particular project environment. The endpoint does not provide detailed information about each database's schema or contents; it's primarily for listing purposes.

tools.name: List branch endpoints
tools.description: Retrieves all compute endpoints associated with a specific branch in a Neon project. Compute endpoints are the connection points for accessing your PostgreSQL database - they provide the hostname and configuration needed to connect to your database.
