tools.name: Project members list
tools.description: List project members.

tools.name: Project members remove
tools.description: Remove a grant from the project. The path id is the principal id: a user by default, or a team with `?type=team`. Notifies the removed user (unless self-removal). The Everyone team's row is refused — workspace access is set through the project's visibility, which is its only control.

tools.name: Project members update role
tools.description: Change a member's role.

tools.name: Project notification pref get
tools.description: Get the caller's notification preference for the project.

tools.name: Project notification pref set
tools.description: Set the caller's notification preference (`level`) for the project.

tools.name: Project templates apply
tools.description: Create a new project from a template. Pass `{name, description}` in the body.

tools.name: Project templates create
tools.description: Create a project template.

tools.name: Project templates delete
tools.description: Delete a project template.

tools.name: Project templates get
tools.description: Get a single project template.

tools.name: Project templates list
tools.description: List project templates in the workspace.

tools.name: Project updates delete
tools.description: Delete a status update. Author or admin only.

tools.name: Project updates edit
tools.description: Edit a status update. Author or admin only.

tools.name: Protect range
tools.description: Protect a range in a spreadsheet. Protected ranges restrict editing to users in editorUserIds. Set warningOnly to true for soft warnings instead of hard blocks.

tools.name: Publish calendar
tools.description: Publish a calendar as a public read-only .ics feed URL (no auth required). Returns a shareable feed URL that anyone can subscribe to from Google/Apple/Outlook Calendar. Anyone holding the URL can read every event on the calendar until it is unpublished or its URL is rotated.

tools.name: Publish form
tools.description: Publish a form so it accepts public responses. Semantic shortcut for PATCH /api/forms/{id} with is_published=true; same validation (every field needs a non-empty label).

tools.name: Query wiki database
tools.description: Query rows from an inline database with optional view, filter, and sort. Returns paginated results.

tools.name: Realtime exchange connection capability
tools.description: Exchange the caller's normal credential (JWT or `ak_` API key) for a short-lived realtime connection capability scoped to exactly the caller's own workspace and credential session. Takes no input — workspace, principal and session are read off the authenticated credential, never a request field, so the endpoint has no field a caller could set to another principal's value. The capability names no resource, channel or operation: object-scoped channels each need their own resource capability, and every durable mutation is independently re-authorized API-side. Refused with 429 + `Retry-After` when the per-principal rate budget or this instance's concurrent database-admission budget is exhausted.

tools.name: Realtime exchange resource capability
tools.description: Exchange the caller's normal credential for a short-lived capability over ONE object-scoped channel. The caller names the channel; it never names its own authority — the granted operations are resolved from the caller's real role on that object through the same `can()` seam the REST surface authorizes with, so the capability and a later durable commit cannot disagree about what this principal may do. `operations` may narrow that set and may never widen it: a request naming an operation the caller does not hold is refused rather than quietly reduced, because a clamped token lets a client believe it may write and discover otherwise only as frames dropped at the edge. An object the caller cannot reach answers 404 exactly as an absent one does.

tools.name: Recalculate lead scores
tools.description: Recalculate lead scores for all contacts in the workspace. Use this after creating or updating scoring rules so existing contacts pick up the new scoring.

tools.name: Register custom domain
tools.description: Register a custom email domain as a pending row; ownership must be verified via DNS TXT before sending is enabled. Requires admin role.

tools.name: Remove access
tools.description: Remove a named grant, pending invitation or link access on a document, spreadsheet, presentation, canvas, Drive item, form, wiki page, or calendar. Give exactly one user_id, team_id, pending_share_id (unaccepted invitation), or link=true (restricts the link tier; unavailable on calendars). To remove broad access while retaining explicit collaborators use set_visibility(visibility=restricted), not Everyone removal.

tools.name: Remove forwarding address
tools.description: Remove a forwarding address

tools.name: Remove pipeline member
tools.description: Remove a user or team from a CRM pipeline. The principalId is the user_id or team_id of the member to remove.

tools.name: Remove role
tools.description: Remove a role from a user. Requires admin role.

tools.name: Remove shared drive member
tools.description: Remove a shared drive member (manager-only; cannot remove last manager).

tools.name: Remove sheet column
tools.description: Remove a column from a sheet tab by column ID. Use `?sheet=` to target a tab other than the first.

tools.name: Remove sheet tab
tools.description: Remove a sheet tab by name. Cannot remove the last remaining tab.

tools.name: Remove slide
tools.description: Remove the slide at the given zero-based index.

tools.name: Remove task attachment
tools.description: Remove a file attachment from a task. Does not delete the Drive file.

tools.name: Rename document version
tools.description: Rename a version snapshot of a document. Useful for labeling meaningful versions (e.g., "Pre-launch draft", "Board approved"). Requires editor permission.

tools.name: Rename sheet tab
tools.description: Rename an existing sheet tab.

tools.name: Reorder mail labels
tools.description: Reorder the mail labels shown in the sidebar.

tools.name: Reorder mail rules
tools.description: Reorder the mail rules to change which runs first.

tools.name: Reorder slides
tools.description: Reorder slides in a presentation. Provide the full list of slide indices in the desired new order. Example: [2, 0, 1, 3] moves the third slide to the front.

tools.name: Replace named range content
tools.description: Replace all content within a named range with new content. Used for template-based document generation — define named ranges as placeholders, then call this to fill each one. The named range must have positional anchors (startNodeId/endNodeId). Content can be Markdown text or PM JSON. Returns 409 if the anchored nodes no longer exist (stale range after CRDT edits).

tools.name: Replace shapes with image
tools.description: Replace text placeholder elements with an image across all slides. Finds text elements whose text matches the search string and replaces them with image elements at the same position and size. Like Google Slides ReplaceAllShapesWithImage — useful for template-based workflows where placeholder shapes like {{logo}} are swapped with actual images.

tools.name: Replace sheet tab
tools.description: Replace a sheet tab's columns and/or rows wholesale. Use for bulk data replacement. Use update_cells for surgical edits.

tools.name: Request access
tools.description: Ask the owner of a document, spreadsheet, presentation, canvas, Drive item, form, wiki page, or calendar, task, project, or CRM pipeline for access at a role higher than any you hold. Documents, Drive items and wiki pages offer viewer, commenter and editor; forms and calendars viewer and editor; projects commenter and editor; tasks editor; pipelines member. Returns 409 while a request is already open.

tools.name: Reschedule scheduled email
tools.description: Change the delivery time of a pending scheduled email without changing its content.

tools.name: Resend forwarding verification
tools.description: Resend verification email

tools.name: Restore file
tools.description: Restore a file from trash. Needs the owner rung (the owner, the owner of a folder above it, or a manager of its shared drive); a caller who can see the file without it gets 403.

tools.name: Restore sheet structure
tools.description: Undo or redo a structural change receipt without overwriting unrelated later edits.

tools.name: Restore task
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted task when the caller has task editor access.

tools.name: Restore wiki synced block
tools.description: Restore a previously deleted synced block. Embedding pages will render the block again instead of showing error chips.

tools.name: Resume coworker
tools.description: Resume a paused coworker.

tools.name: Revert wiki page version
tools.description: Revert a wiki page to a previous version snapshot. This replaces the current content with the version's content and rebuilds the page's collaborative state from it. A snapshot of the current state is automatically created before reverting. This is destructive for the in-progress edit — always confirm with the user first.

tools.name: Revoke api key
tools.description: Revoke an API key. Immediate — any requests using the key will fail. Requires admin role.

tools.name: Revoke identity api key
tools.description: Revoke (permanently delete) one of the calling user's own API keys. 404 if the key doesn't belong to the calling user. Returns 204 No Content on success.

tools.name: Rotate calendar publish url
tools.description: Rotate a published calendar's read-only subscription URL. The previous URL is revoked immediately.

tools.name: Rsvp email invite
tools.description: RSVP to a calendar invite on an email.

tools.name: Rsvp event
tools.description: RSVP to a calendar event that the user is invited to. Use this when the user asks to accept, decline, or mark tentative on an event invitation.

tools.name: Run data connector
tools.description: Execute a data connector: fetch the latest data and write it to the connector's target cells. Returns the connector with updated last-run metadata.

tools.name: Save message
tools.description: Bookmark an EXISTING chat message in the current user's private Later/saved list. Resolve the original message_id with search_chat_messages or get_channel_messages when it is not supplied. Does not post or copy a message, and does not set a timed reminder (use set_reminder for that). Saving an already-saved message is a no-op.

tools.name: Scan business card
tools.description: OCR a photo of a business card and extract structured contact fields (name, title, company, email, phone, website, address, notes). Returns JSON with each field nullable when not present on the card. Use when the user uploads or references a business card image and wants to add the contact to CRM. The image must be passed as a base64 data URL (data:image/jpeg;base64,...) of an image format Gemini Vision supports (JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC). Max 6 MB.

tools.name: Search calendar events
tools.description: Full-text search across all calendar events for the current workspace. Returns matching events with id, title, start/end times, and calendar info. Use this when the user asks to find a specific event by name or description keyword.

tools.name: Search chat messages
tools.description: Find existing chat messages by keyword, phrase, or topic across the caller's accessible channels. Results include the message id and channel context needed to bookmark, remind, react, reply, or edit that message. Use channel_id to restrict the search to a known channel; this read does not post messages.

tools.name: Search mail
tools.description: Full-text + operator search (Gmail-style: from:, to:, cc:, bcc:, subject:, has:attachment, is:read|unread|starred, in:inbox|sent|drafts|trash|archive, label:, after:YYYY-MM-DD, before:YYYY-MM-DD, size:N, larger:N, smaller:N, "phrase"). cc:/bcc: filter by recipient type. size:/larger:/smaller: filter by body byte size.

tools.name: Search palette
tools.description: Cross-module command-palette search — every module including chat messages. `q` is the query string; `limit` caps results (default 30, max 50). Empty query returns an empty response. Module diversity is preserved. `counts` carries the per-module match total before the per-module cap.

tools.name: Search wiki
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search across wiki page titles and Markdown content. Returns only pages the caller can view under the effective page-to-space permission rules, with id, title, space, and content snippets. Use this when the user asks to find information in the wiki, look up documentation, or search the knowledge base. More efficient than reading individual pages.

tools.name: Search workspace
tools.description: Search across every module in the user's workspace (docs, sheets, slides, canvas, tasks, contacts, deals, channels, chat messages, wiki, forms, calendar, users, mail, files, teams, and saved Analytics reports for callers who can read them). Returns a flat list of results with module-aware metadata, plus `counts` — the per-module match total before the per-module cap. Optional module filter narrows the search to one or more modules; `sort` picks relevance or recency. Use this when the user asks to find something but you don't know which module it lives in.

tools.name: Send draft email
tools.description: Send a previously created draft email. The draft transitions from the drafts folder to sent, SES delivery is triggered, and recipient inbox copies are created. Use this when the user wants to send a draft they previously saved. A send is not always a delivery: when the sender is an agent limited to workspace recipients and any To/Cc/Bcc address is external, the WHOLE email is queued for a human decision instead of being sent — the response carries `delivery_status: pending_approval` and `pending_approval.review_id`, and nothing has reached the recipients. Report that state; do not report it as sent, and do not re-send it.

tools.name: Send email
tools.description: Send an email from the current user. The body is written in Markdown and automatically converted to a beautifully formatted HTML email for delivery. Use this when the user asks to send an email, message someone, or share something via email. Supports to, cc, and bcc recipients. Recipients are specified by email address. A send is not always a delivery: when the sender is an agent limited to workspace recipients and any To/Cc/Bcc address is external, the WHOLE email is queued for a human decision instead of being sent — the response carries `delivery_status: pending_approval` and `pending_approval.review_id`, and nothing has reached the recipients. Report that state; do not report it as sent, and do not re-send it.

tools.name: Send message
tools.description: Post a NEW message visible to the chat channel's members, or send a thread reply. Use for requested communication, not for finding, bookmarking, or reminding about an existing message: those actions use search_chat_messages/get_channel_messages then save_message/set_reminder on the returned message id. Content is Markdown with @mentions, code blocks, and links. Use the current channel ID when supplied by page context. To reply, set thread_id to the original parent message's id. To attach a file, upload it with drive_file_upload_proxy (source=chat) and include [name](drive://<file_id>) in content.

tools.name: Send quote
tools.description: Send a CRM quote via email to the contact. Marks the quote as 'sent'. By default, sends to the linked contact's email address.

tools.name: Send scheduled message now
tools.description: Deliver a pending scheduled message immediately instead of waiting for its scheduled time. Flips the message to sent and fans it out to the channel right now. Fails if the message has already been sent or cancelled. Use this when the user wants to send a queued message without waiting.

tools.name: Send test notification email
tools.description: Send a test notification email (useful for checking email rendering and deliverability). Requires admin role.

tools.name: Set channel archived
tools.description: Archive or unarchive a chat channel. Archiving freezes writes for everyone. Requires the same administrative authority as the individual archive and unarchive actions.

tools.name: Set channel muted
tools.description: Mute or unmute a chat channel for yourself, including DMs, temporarily or indefinitely. Muting silences ordinary message, keyword and subscribed-thread alerts and removes the channel-presence badge contribution; direct mentions and broadcasts still reach you. This changes the channel mute setting, not its notification preference or a delivery-suppression rule. muted=true optionally accepts until or duration_ms; omit both for indefinite mute. muted=false cannot include timing fields.

tools.name: Set deck fonts
tools.description: Set the heading and/or body font across a whole presentation: every text box, shape and table on every slide and master, group children and per-run rich-text fonts included. Text at 28px or larger takes the heading font; smaller text and tables take the body font. Fonts are a closed list. The saved deck is re-read before responding: a 409 means some elements still use another font, so the change is incomplete and must not be reported as done.

tools.name: Set default send as
tools.description: Set the user's default send-as address.

tools.name: Set docs page layout default
tools.description: Set the caller's default layout for new Docs (`pageless_default: true` = pageless, `false` = pages). Affects only Docs created afterwards; existing Docs keep their layout.

tools.name: Set document footnotes
tools.description: Set footnote body content on a document. Replaces all existing footnoteBody nodes. Each footnote must have a footnoteId and either a text string (auto-wrapped in a paragraph) or a content array (PM JSON). To add inline footnote references in the body text, use update_document with PM JSON content containing footnoteRef nodes with matching footnoteIds.

tools.name: Set document headers footers
tools.description: Set default, first-page, and even-page headers and footers. Each field accepts a plain text string (auto-wrapped in a paragraph), a ProseMirror JSON node, or null to remove. Omit a field to leave unchanged.

tools.name: Set email archived
tools.description: Archive an email or return it to the inbox. archived=true archives; false unarchives. Existing mailbox access rules apply.

tools.name: Set email signature
tools.description: Set the workspace default email signature. Pass null (or omit markdown) to clear. Requires admin role.

tools.name: Set mail signature
tools.description: Set personal email signature. Pass null to clear.

tools.name: Set mail thread assignee
tools.description: Assign a shared-mailbox conversation to a member, or clear its assignment with user_id=null. Does not change its folder.

tools.name: Set mail thread muted
tools.description: Mute or unmute a mail conversation. muted=true moves it out of the inbox and keeps future replies muted; false restores it. mailbox_id selects a shared mailbox.

tools.name: Set notification keywords
tools.description: Replace the current user's notification keyword list. Keywords are case-insensitive, whole-word, and capped at 20 entries (each up to 50 characters). Duplicates/empties are dropped. Use this when the user says 'alert me whenever someone mentions X' or 'stop notifying me about Y'.

tools.name: Set pinned header rows
tools.description: Set the number of pinned (repeating) header rows on a table in a document. Pinned header rows repeat on every printed page when the table spans multiple pages in exported .docx and .pdf files. Set to 0 to clear the pinned header rows attribute.

tools.name: Set reaction
tools.description: Add or remove your emoji reaction on a chat message or a document, task, wiki, mail-thread or Code comment. The target is resolved from ID. present=true adds; false removes. Existing parent visibility, workspace custom-emoji rules, broadcast-message identity, and missing-reaction errors apply.

tools.name: Set read receipts default
tools.description: Toggle the default for new compose windows

tools.name: Set reminder
tools.description: Remind only the signed-in user about an existing chat message at a future time. A channel named in a personal reminder request locates the source message; it is not an audience or a request to post there. When message_id is unknown, first find the original with search_chat_messages or get_channel_messages; an unknown ID does not mean the message is absent. If the target cannot be identified, ask for clarification instead of publishing a replacement. Automatically bookmarks the original in Later. remind_at is an ISO 8601 datetime and must be in the future.

tools.name: Set resource starred
tools.description: Add or remove favorites (star/unstar) for documents, spreadsheets, presentations, canvases, Drive items, forms, channels or teams. Resource type is resolved from ID; existing starring/access rules apply. Tasks-sidebar view/project pins use tasks_favorites_add/remove instead.

tools.name: Set sheet validation
tools.description: Set a data-validation rule on a spreadsheet cell range in A1 notation. Supports dropdown/range lists, numeric/text/date conditions, checkbox values, and custom formulas. Numeric constraints use JSON numbers, not numeric strings. Strict configures invalid-entry rejection rather than warnings in the editor; API cell writes do not enforce these rules.

tools.name: Set snooze presets
tools.description: Set the user's custom snooze quick-presets (up to 10). Pass an empty array to reset to defaults.

tools.name: Set swipe actions
tools.description: Set the caller's own mail-row swipe actions — one action per direction, chosen from archive, trash, read, star, snooze.

tools.name: Set task archived
tools.description: Archive or unarchive a task. Archive is separate from Trash; archived=false does not restore a trashed task. Existing project and task permissions apply.

tools.name: Set task subscription
tools.description: Subscribe or unsubscribe yourself from a task's notifications. When subscribed=true, user_id may select another subscriber under the existing subscription rules; unsubscribe applies only to yourself. Subscription does not grant task access.

tools.name: Set undo send setting
tools.description: Set undo-send duration (seconds).

tools.name: Set user dnd
tools.description: Enable or disable Do-Not-Disturb for the current user. Pass an ISO-8601 timestamp in the future to snooze notifications until that time, or pass null to disable DND immediately. Use this when the user says 'mute me for an hour', 'DND until 5pm', or 'turn off DND'.

tools.name: Set user status
tools.description: Set the current user's chat status — an emoji, short text (<=100 chars), and optional auto-clear timestamp. All fields are optional; pass null to clear a single field. Use this when the user says things like 'set my status to lunch until 1pm' or 'I'm on vacation'.

tools.name: Set vacation settings
tools.description: Update vacation auto-reply settings.

tools.name: Set visibility
tools.description: Set broad access to a document, spreadsheet, presentation, canvas, Drive item, form, wiki page, or calendar: restricted removes broad tiers but keeps owner and explicit collaborators; workspace covers current/future workspace humans and agents at workspaceRole; link/public use linkPermission, optionally behind linkPassword until linkExpiresAt. Use this for Everyone/workspace access, not individual grants or the Everyone entry. Calendars allow only restricted/workspace; forms publish responder links separately. Unsupported fields are rejected.

tools.name: Shared with me hide
tools.description: Hide one row from the caller's own Shared-with-me list. Revokes nothing — the grant is untouched and the resource stays reachable by its id or link; only the list entry goes. 404 when the caller holds no live grant or the key lacks that resource's read scope. Idempotent.

tools.name: Shared with me list
tools.description: Everything shared with the calling account through a direct grant, a team grant, or a bound external grant, across docs / sheets / slides, Drive, Wiki, Forms and Calendar — and across every workspace and identity the account owns. Excludes what the account owns, and excludes workspace-tier access, which is standing authority rather than a share. An API key sees only resource families within its read scopes. Newest share first. `scope=workspace` narrows discovery to resources in the authenticated current workspace without changing access.

tools.name: Shared with me undo leave
tools.description: Undo a "Remove me": restore the exact grant the caller removed, from the `undo_token` the leave call returned. The token is bound to the caller, single-use, and lasts ten minutes. An outside grant is re-checked against the workspace's current outside-sharing policy. 400 `undo_token_invalid` / `undo_token_expired` / `undo_token_used`; 403 `outside_sharing_off` / `outside_sharing_domain_not_allowed`; 404 when the resource is gone or the key lacks its read scope.

tools.name: Sheet get data
tools.description: Get the spreadsheet as the structured JSON canvas. Returns the `Sheet` envelope: top-level metadata plus the structured sheet body nested under `data` (see `SheetData`). Read the tab list as `response.data.sheets`; columns and rows are under `response.data.sheets[0]`, not at the response root.

tools.name: Sheet update cells
tools.description: Update specific cells in a spreadsheet. Provide an array of cell updates, each specifying the row index (0-based), column ID, and new value. If the user is currently viewing a sheet, use the sheet ID from the page context.

tools.name: Sign add field
tools.description: Add a signature field to a signing document.

tools.name: Sign add signer
tools.description: Add a signer or CC recipient. An agent user can be a CC recipient but never a signer; adding one as a signer is refused.

tools.name: Sign get certificate
tools.description: Download the Certificate of Completion for a completed document.

tools.name: Sign get references
tools.description: List signing documents that use this document as a source.

tools.name: Sign prepare send
tools.description: Validate signers and render the PDF preview (draft → preview_pending).

tools.name: Sign remove field
tools.description: Remove a field from a signing document.

tools.name: Sign remove signer
tools.description: Remove a signer or CC recipient from a draft signing document.

tools.name: Sign reorder signers
tools.description: Atomically set the sequential signing order: the full ordered list of the document's signer-role ids. Draft only.

tools.name: Sign update field
tools.description: Reassign, reposition, resize, or change requiredness for a field on a draft signing document. The field id is stable — updates never re-create the field.

tools.name: Sign verify document
tools.description: Verify the integrity and signature of a completed document.

tools.name: Slide apply template
tools.description: Apply a slide template — built-in or workspace — to the deck or to a single slide.

tools.name: Slide layouts list
tools.description: List the slide-level layouts the editor knows about.

tools.name: Slide save as template
tools.description: Save an existing deck as a reusable workspace template. Deep-copies the deck with fresh element IDs into a new workspace-visible template document; the source deck is left untouched. Returns the new template's ID.

tools.name: Slide star
tools.description: Star a deck. Idempotent — re-starring is a no-op.

tools.name: Slide stars list
tools.description: List IDs of slide decks the current user has starred.

tools.name: Slide templates list
tools.description: List the built-in slide deck templates.

tools.name: Slide unstar
tools.description: Unstar a deck. Idempotent.

tools.name: Slide use template
tools.description: Start a new deck from a template — built-in or workspace. Deep-copies the template deck with fresh element IDs into a new deck, substitutes `{{key}}` placeholders to bracketed prompts (e.g. `{{client_name}}` → `[Client Name]`), and returns the new deck's ID.

tools.name: Snooze email
tools.description: Snooze an email until a datetime.

tools.name: Snooze reminder
tools.description: Re-snooze an existing saved message by updating its remind_at time. Resets reminded to false so the scheduler picks it up again. Accepts ISO 8601 datetime string; must be in the future.

tools.name: Sort sheet
tools.description: Sort a tab's rows by one column, optionally within an exact filter range. Re-anchors formulas, comment anchors, and cell notes so nothing orphans.

tools.name: Start task timer
tools.description: Start a time-tracking timer on a task for the current user. If another timer is already running for this user, it is stopped automatically (only one active timer per user).

tools.name: Stop task timer
tools.description: Stop the current user's active timer. The duration is accumulated onto the task's time_spent_minutes total. Returns null if no timer is active.

tools.name: Submit feedback
tools.description: Tell Ambiguous what happened in your own words. Only description is required; do not choose a report category or supply a goal outcome. Optional context and attachments are welcome, never required. Ambiguous handles classification and triage. Accepts unauthenticated REST calls; valid credentials optionally identify the submitter. Rate-limited per user when authenticated and per IP otherwise. Body shape: `{title?, description, priority?, screenshotDataUrl?, attachments?, context?}` — see `FeedbackInput`. The submission is stored as a task in Ambiguous's own Feedback project and the 200 carries that task's id as the receipt; there is no receipt without a record, so a storage failure is a 500 and the caller should retry. Returns 503 with `{error: "Feedback reporting not available"}` when the intake is not configured (outside the contract error-code enum, surfaced via raw Response).

tools.name: Submit form
tools.description: Submit a response to a published form, identified by its public slug or form ID. Data is a map keyed by field ID with user answers. Use when an agent is filling out a form on behalf of a user or when completing a structured data-entry task.

tools.name: Task asset create
tools.description: Add an image to a task description as one of its own assets and get back the URL its body should store (`/api/assets/{id}/content`). Send the bytes as `content_base64`, `source_file_id` to copy a Drive file the caller can view, or `source_url` to import a public HTTPS image through the SSRF guard; neither source is referenced afterwards. The type is decided from the bytes and only images are accepted (415 otherwise); SVG uploads are sanitized before storage and refused with 415 when malformed. Stored SVG is sanitized on every read and served inline as image/svg+xml under a restrictive Content-Security-Policy; malformed stored SVG is refused with 404. Drive SVG downloads remain attachments. The bytes count against the container owner's storage (413 past it). The same image added to the same container again returns the asset already held. The asset is never visible in Drive and is readable exactly when the container is.

tools.name: Task collaborators add
tools.description: Share a task with one workspace member: grants `editor` on this task and its subtasks (never on its project) and subscribes them. A projectless task is shared by its creator or assignee; a project task by an editor on that project.

tools.name: Task collaborators list
tools.description: List the collaborators on a task — the people holding `editor` on it (and its subtasks) without a role on its project.

tools.name: Task collaborators remove
tools.description: Revoke a task collaborator's grant. The add-time subscription is left in place — it grants no access on its own.

tools.name: Tasks activity
tools.description: List audit-log activity entries for a task (status changes, assignments, comments, label edits, etc.). Paginated via `limit`/`offset`.

tools.name: Tasks batch
tools.description: Batch-fetch up to 50 tasks by ID. Powers LinkedTaskItem hydration in Docs/Wiki.

tools.name: Tasks by key
tools.description: Resolve a workspace-scoped task key (e.g. `WS-123`) to its task ID. Used by deep links and integrations.

tools.name: Tasks delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a task. Only the creator can delete.

tools.name: Tasks export
tools.description: Export authorized tasks matching the selected filters as CSV (default) or JSON. CSV includes human-readable columns and a task_json column containing the complete public task representation. Owned description images are embedded; an unavailable or malformed owned image refuses the export with its task reference.

tools.name: Tasks favorites add
tools.description: Pin a saved task view or project in your Tasks sidebar. For document, Drive, channel or team favorites, use set_resource_starred.

tools.name: Tasks favorites list
tools.description: List your Tasks-sidebar pins: saved views and projects, not starred documents, Drive items, channels or teams.

tools.name: Tasks favorites remove
tools.description: Unpin a saved task view or project from your Tasks sidebar, matching resource_type and resource_id. For other resource favorites, use set_resource_starred.

tools.name: Tasks favorites reorder
tools.description: Reorder your Tasks-sidebar view/project pins using ordered_ids (favorite-row IDs, top-to-bottom), not resource IDs.

tools.name: Tasks inbox count
tools.description: Count of triage-bucket tasks (untriaged + projects in 'triage' status). Powers the sidebar inbox badge.

tools.name: Tasks labels assign
tools.description: Assign a label to a task. Returns the task's full label list.

tools.name: Tasks labels create
tools.description: Create a workspace task label. Returns 409 if a label with the same name already exists in the group.

tools.name: Tasks labels delete
tools.description: Delete a task label. Existing assignments are removed.

tools.name: Tasks labels list
tools.description: List task labels visible in the workspace, grouped by `group_name`. Without `project_id`, returns workspace-level labels only. With `project_id`, returns workspace-level labels plus labels scoped to that project.

tools.name: Tasks labels remove
tools.description: Remove a label assignment from a task. Returns the task's remaining label list.

tools.name: Tasks labels update
tools.description: Update a task label.

tools.name: Tasks pr links
tools.description: List GitHub pull requests linked to a task (via the integration-links service).

tools.name: Tasks relations batch
tools.description: Batch-fetch every relation type for up to 200 tasks. Powers relation overlays and sweeps.

tools.name: Tasks relations create
tools.description: Create a relation between two tasks. `blocking`/`blocked_by` auto-creates the inverse edge. With `type=duplicate, mark_as_duplicate=true` the source task is cancelled with a system comment.

tools.name: Tasks relations delete
tools.description: Delete a task relation edge. Auto-deletes the inverse edge for blocking/blocked_by pairs.

tools.name: Tasks relations list
tools.description: List edges in the task-relations graph for a task (related, blocking, blocked_by, duplicate).

tools.name: Tasks remove subscriber
tools.description: Remove another user's subscription from a task. Requires task access.

tools.name: Tasks sla dashboard
tools.description: Aggregate SLA metrics for the workspace (compliance rates, avg times, counts per status). Optionally scope to a project.

tools.name: Tasks sla thresholds
tools.description: Get the workspace's SLA thresholds (response + resolution times per priority). Auth-only.

tools.name: Tasks subscribed
tools.description: List task IDs the caller is subscribed to (manual + auto-subscribed via creator/assignee/comment).

tools.name: Tasks subscriptions list
tools.description: List all users subscribed to a task (with the reason each is subscribed).

tools.name: Tasks subscription status
tools.description: Check whether the current user is subscribed to a task (and the reason if so).

tools.name: Tasks subtasks
tools.description: List immediate subtasks of a task (`parent_task_id = :id`).

tools.name: Tasks templates delete
tools.description: Delete a task template. Workspace admins or project admins only.

tools.name: Tasks templates get
tools.description: Get a single task template by ID.

tools.name: Tasks templates update
tools.description: Update a task template. Workspace admins or project admins only.

tools.name: Tasks views create
tools.description: Create a saved task view (filter + layout). Setting `is_shared: true` exposes it to the workspace.

tools.name: Tasks views delete
tools.description: Delete a saved task view.

tools.name: Tasks views layout get
tools.description: Get the caller's layout preferences for a view, or fall back to the view's defaults. `source` indicates which.

tools.name: Tasks views layout update
tools.description: Upsert the caller's layout preferences for a view (per-project scope optional).

tools.name: Tasks views list
tools.description: List task views accessible to the caller (own + shared + system defaults).

tools.name: Tasks views update
tools.description: Update a saved task view (rename, change filters or layout defaults, toggle sharing).

tools.name: Teams cancel join request
tools.description: Cancel your own pending join request for this team.

tools.name: Teams get subscription
tools.description: Get the caller's email-delivery preference for the team. Returns `{team_id, user_id, email_delivery}`.

tools.name: Teams join
tools.description: Join a team. Open teams grant instant membership; request teams create a pending join request; invite teams reject.

tools.name: Teams leave
tools.description: Leave a team. Cannot leave if you're the last admin.

tools.name: Teams members list
tools.description: Paginated member list. Private teams visible only to members or admins.

tools.name: Teams members remove
tools.description: Remove a member. Admin only. Cannot remove the last admin.

tools.name: Teams members update role
tools.description: Change a member's role. Admin only. Cannot demote the last admin.

tools.name: Teams requests approve
tools.description: Approve a join request — adds the user as a member.

tools.name: Teams requests deny
tools.description: Deny a join request.

tools.name: Teams requests list
tools.description: List pending join requests. Admin only.

tools.name: Teams searchable
tools.description: Search teams visible to the caller for the share dialog. Returns the union of public teams and private teams where the caller is a member. Supports case-insensitive name filtering via `q` and a configurable `limit`.

tools.name: Teams update subscription
tools.description: Update the caller's email-delivery preference for the team. Body: `{email_delivery: 'each' | 'daily_digest' | 'weekly_digest' | 'none'}`. `none` is refused on the workspace-wide all-members list, which has no opt-out.

tools.name: Transfer ownership
tools.description: Make another principal owner of a document, spreadsheet, presentation, canvas, Drive item or form. The new owner needs a live explicit share: check list_access and do not re-grant an existing share. The previous owner keeps editor. Wiki and calendars cannot transfer ownership.

tools.name: Trash mail thread
tools.description: Trash all messages in a thread atomically. Moves every message in the thread to the trash folder.

tools.name: Unblock sender
tools.description: Unblock by id or pattern.

tools.name: Undo send email
tools.description: Undo an in-flight send within the undo-send window.

tools.name: Unenroll contact from sequence
tools.description: Permanently remove a contact from a CRM sequence (terminal — sets status to 'unenrolled'). The contact will not receive any further sequence steps. Returns 409 if already in a terminal status. Provide the enrollment ID (not the contact ID — find it via list_sequence_enrollments).

tools.name: Unfurl link
tools.description: Fetch OpenGraph / link-preview metadata for a URL (title, description, image, site name, favicon). Useful for generating rich previews of shared links, or inspecting what a URL would look like when shared in chat. Only http(s) URLs are allowed, and internal/private addresses are blocked.

tools.name: Ungroup slide elements
tools.description: Dissolve a group element on a slide back into independent top-level elements. Children positions are converted from group-relative to absolute coordinates. The group element is removed and its former children become top-level elements on the slide.

tools.name: Unprotect range
tools.description: Remove a protected range from a spreadsheet by its ID. Returns 200 on success, 404 if the range does not exist.

tools.name: Unpublish calendar
tools.description: Revoke the public .ics feed for a calendar, making it private again.

tools.name: Unpublish form
tools.description: Unpublish a form so it stops accepting public responses. Semantic shortcut for PATCH /api/forms/{id} with is_published=false.

tools.name: Unsave message
tools.description: Remove a saved (bookmarked) message from the user's saved list. The message itself is untouched; only the personal bookmark is deleted.

tools.name: Untrash email
tools.description: Restore a trashed email to inbox

tools.name: Untrash mail thread
tools.description: Restore all trashed messages in a thread to inbox. Only affects messages currently in trash.

tools.name: Update access
tools.description: Change an existing named user/team grant on a document, spreadsheet, presentation, canvas, Drive item, form, wiki page, or calendar. id names the resource; exactly one user_id or team_id names the recipient. For the workspace tier use set_visibility and workspaceRole, not the Everyone entry. role and expires_at are set exactly, including shorter expiry.

tools.name: Update api key
tools.description: Update an API key's name, scopes, or rate limit. Requires admin role.

tools.name: Update canvas
tools.description: Update canvas-level metadata (title, preview cover). Use to rename a canvas or set its preview; never touches elements — use the element ops for board content. Coordinates: board units, top-left origin, +x right / +y down. Example: update_canvas({ id: "<boardId>", title: "Renamed board" }).

tools.name: Update canvas timer
tools.description: Control a board's shared brainstorm countdown. Use to time-box a round: start (with duration_ms), pause (banks remaining time), resume (from banked time), or reset (clear). The server stamps `ends_at` from its own clock, so every participant renders the same countdown regardless of local clocks; the timer touches no elements. Coordinates: board units, top-left origin, +x right / +y down (unaffected by the timer). Example: update_canvas_timer({ id: "<boardId>", action: "start", duration_ms: 300000 }) starts a 5-minute countdown.

tools.name: Update channel member role
tools.description: Change a channel member's role to 'admin' or 'member'. Requires channel admin privileges. Use this when the user asks to promote or demote a member in a channel.

tools.name: Update chart
tools.description: Patch a chart's config — type, title, data range, overlay position, or series styling. Only the fields you send are updated; the rest of the chart config is preserved.

tools.name: Update conditional format
tools.description: Update a conditional formatting rule by ID. Partial update: ranges or one canonical rule payload; replacing the kind clears the previous kind.

tools.name: Update contact
tools.description: Update an existing CRM contact's fields. Provide only the fields you want to change. For interrupted sync recovery, read the contact and send expected_updated_at with only remaining changes. A 409 means the contact changed: read again and reconcile; never replay an earlier snapshot over newer values. If the user is currently viewing a contact, use the contact ID from the page context.

tools.name: Update contact group
tools.description: Update an existing contact group's name, color, or sort order. Group name must remain unique within the workspace.

tools.name: Update coworker
tools.description: Update coworker metadata (persona, focus areas, display name, avatar).

tools.name: Update crm property definition
tools.description: Update a custom-property definition's label or select options.

tools.name: Update crm view
tools.description: Update a saved CRM view (rename, change filters, toggle default/shared).

tools.name: Update data connector
tools.description: Update a data connector's name, config, target cells, or refresh schedule.

tools.name: Update deal
tools.description: Update an existing CRM deal's fields. Provide only the fields you want to change. Use this to move a deal to a new stage, update the amount, mark as won/lost, etc. If the user is currently viewing a deal, use the deal ID from the page context.

tools.name: Update deal line item
tools.description: Update a deal line item (quantity, price, discount, name/description). Amount auto-recomputed. If sync_deal_amount defaults true, the deal's total is also refreshed.

tools.name: Update deal template
tools.description: Update a deal template. Providing `line_items` replaces the entire line-item list.

tools.name: Update deck settings
tools.description: Update deck-level settings: theme, aspect ratio, default background. Changing aspect ratio rescales every slide's elements proportionally; changing default background updates slides currently using the old default.

tools.name: Update document
tools.description: Edit an existing document inline. Read the document first (get_document), modify the content, then pass the full updated text — content replaces the entire body. Do NOT create a new document to edit; version history preserves prior states. Accepts Markdown or ProseMirror JSON (HTML tolerated but lossy — drops listed in `import_warnings`). Provide only the fields you want to change.

tools.name: Update document page style
tools.description: Set page-level formatting for a document: margins (PT), page size (letter/A4/legal or {width, height} in PT), orientation (portrait/landscape). 72 PT = 1 inch. These settings control export output (.docx, .pdf). Pass an empty object to reset to defaults.

tools.name: Update draft email
tools.description: Update an existing draft email. Only works on drafts (not sent messages). Use this to refine recipients, subject, or body of a draft across multiple iterations before sending.

tools.name: Update event
tools.description: Update an existing calendar event. Provide only the fields you want to change. Use this to reschedule, change attendees, update the description, or cancel an event. If the user is currently viewing an event, use the event ID from the page context.

tools.name: Update form
tools.description: Update an existing form's title, description, fields, settings, or publish status. Use this when the user asks to edit a form, add/remove fields, publish/unpublish, or change form settings. If the user is currently viewing a form, use the resource ID from page context.

tools.name: Update form variant
tools.description: Update an A/B test variant's name, traffic weight, or active status. Use when the user asks to rename a variant, adjust the traffic split, or pause/resume an experiment.

tools.name: Update identity api key
tools.description: Update name, scopes, or `rate_limit` on the calling user's own API key. Returns the updated key. 404 if the key doesn't belong to the calling user.

tools.name: Update mail label
tools.description: Update a mail label's name, color or sidebar order.

tools.name: Update mail rule
tools.description: Update a mail rule's conditions or actions.

tools.name: Update mail template
tools.description: Update a saved mail template's subject or body.

tools.name: Update named range
tools.description: Update a named range or named expression with either an A1 range or an exact literal Excel expression; optionally rename it with newName. Names are matched case-insensitively. External-workbook expressions are preserved verbatim and remain unresolved.

tools.name: Update pipeline
tools.description: Update a pipeline's name or stages. Providing `stages` replaces the entire stage list — include every stage you want to keep. Reordering is done by the order in the array.

tools.name: Update pivot table

tools.name: Create group types
tools.description:
Create one or more group types in a project, OR add already-ingested group types with status "unexpected" to the tracking plan.

A group type is a category of group that users can belong to (for example "Company", "Account", "Team", "Workspace", "Organization"). The Amplitude Accounts add-on lets you analyse product usage at the group level rather than per individual user. NOTE: group TYPES are the categories themselves — use create_properties with propertyType "group" to add attributes (e.g. company name, plan tier) to an existing group type.

When a user says "create a group type" without further qualification, or "add to plan" for an unexpected group type, use this tool. Specify whether each item is unexpected with `isUnexpected`. If `isUnexpected` is true, the group type must already exist in the project as observed-but-unexpected and will be added to the tracking plan. If false (default), a brand-new entry is created.

INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use get_context to get available project IDs first.
- Use get_group_types to check which group types already exist before creating new ones.
- If the user has not specified a project, prompt the user to decide. Don't decide for them.

EXAMPLES:
- Minimal: {"projectId": "123456", "groupTypes": [{"name": "Company"}]}
- With description: {"projectId": "123456", "groupTypes": [{"name": "Team", "description": "Engineering teams within a company"}]}
- Mixed batch (one fresh, one add-to-plan, on a feature branch): {"projectId": "123456", "branchName": "marketing-edits", "groupTypes": [{"name": "Account"}, {"name": "Workspace", "isUnexpected": true}]}

# Response
Each input item is reported individually in `groupTypes[]` with a `result` of `"created"`, `"addedToPlan"`, or `"failed"` (with a `reason`). Partial successes are preserved: a failure on one item never discards the results of others in the same batch.

PERMISSIONS:
- This tool requires the "Update Tracking Plan" permission and may fail with a 403. Don't pre-warn the user; if it fails, surface the error and note that an admin may need to grant access.

# Workspace warnings
Be sure you have information on the workspace settings and environments from get_workspace_context before using this tool. If the workspace has more than one environment, warn the user that the change will apply across multiple environments. If the main branch is protected (workspace setting approvalWF is "Required"), let the user know that changes cannot be made on the default branch and they will have to first create a new branch and make changes on that.

NOTES:
- A group type with the same name cannot already exist on the targeted branch — that item will be marked as failed.
- Branch targeting: unless specified, the default branch is used. Pass either branchId or branchName, not both.
- `description` is only allowed on brand-new group types (isUnexpected: false). Unexpected items added to the plan cannot include metadata at the same time — add them first, then use a follow-up tool call to set the description.

USER-INTERFACING LANGUAGE:
When relaying results to the user, do not surface internal mechanics.
- Refer to the default branch as "main", not "default branch".
- Say "unexpected group types" not "isUnexpected group types".
- Say "added to the tracking plan" rather than using field names like "addedToPlan".
- Say "branch approval setting" not "approvalWF".
- Do not mention "mutations", "versionId", "stagingVersionId", "propertyPath", branch IDs, or GraphQL details to the user.

tools.name: Create properties
tools.description:
Create one or more properties in a project's tracking plan. Use propertyType to select which kind of properties to create.

PROPERTY TYPES:
| propertyType | What it creates | Key params |
|---|---|---|
| event | Event properties (global or event-scoped) | properties[].eventType (omit for global) |
| user | User-level properties | properties[].type, regex, enumValues |
| group | Group properties (e.g., company_name, plan_tier) for a group type | groupType, properties[] |

INSTRUCTIONS:
- If a user says "create a property" without specifying a type, ask them to clarify which type they mean: event, user, or group.
- If a user says "create a property on an event," assume they mean an event property — propertyType "event" is the default for that phrasing.
- Derived properties, profile properties, lookup properties, computed properties, and persisted properties are NOT supported via MCP tools. If the user asks to create one of these, let them know that this property type is not currently supported through MCP tools.
- If the user has not specified a project, prompt them to decide. Don't decide for them.

PERMISSIONS:
- This tool requires the "Update Tracking Plan" permission and may fail with a 403. Don't pre-warn the user; if it fails, surface the error and note that an admin may need to grant access.

# Workspace warnings
Be sure you have information on the workspace settings and environments from get_workspace_context before using this tool. If the workspace has more than one environment, warn the user that the change will apply across multiple environments. If the main branch is protected (workspace setting approvalWF is "Required"), let the user know that changes cannot be made on the default branch and they will have to first create a new branch and make changes on that.

NOTES BY PROPERTY TYPE:
- group: Group properties describe attributes of a group type (e.g., company name, plan tier). Accepts a group type name (e.g., "org id", "Company") — the tool resolves it to the correct ID internally. If no branch is specified, defaults to the main branch.

EXAMPLES:
- Event property (global): { "propertyType": "event", "projectId": "123", "properties": [{ "name": "page_url", "type": "string" }] }
- Event property (event-scoped): { "propertyType": "event", "projectId": "123", "properties": [{ "name": "button_name", "eventType": "Button Clicked", "type": "string" }] }
- Event properties (mixed: one fresh, one add-to-plan, on a feature branch): { "propertyType": "event", "projectId": "123", "branchName": "marketing-edits", "properties": [{ "name": "page_url", "type": "string" }, { "name": "button_name", "eventType": "Button Clicked", "isUnexpected": true }] }
- User property: { "propertyType": "user", "projectId": "123", "properties": [{ "name": "plan_type", "type": "string" }] }
- Group properties: { "propertyType": "group", "projectId": "123", "groupType": "Company", "properties": [{ "name": "plan_tier", "type": "string" }] }

USER-INTERFACING LANGUAGE:
When relaying results to the user, do not surface internal mechanics.
- Refer to the default branch as "main", not "default branch".
- Say "event property", "user property", or "group property" not "propertyType".
- Say "unexpected" or "unplanned" not "isUnexpected" when describing properties not yet in the plan.
- Say "array type" not "isArrayType", "hidden" not "isHidden", "enum values" not "enumValues", and "classification" not "classifications".
- Say "branch approval setting" not "approvalWF".
- Do not mention "mutations", "versionId", "stagingVersionId", branch IDs, or GraphQL details to the user.

tools.name: Delete event properties
tools.description:
Delete one or more event properties in a project.

Each requested property is routed by whether eventType is provided:
- eventType provided → per-event delete (scoped to that one event):
  - live on this event → marked as deleted on this event (restorable).
  - planned on this event → the property-event link is removed on this event only (does NOT affect other events).
  - unexpected on this event → added to the plan as deleted on this event.
- eventType omitted → plan-wide delete (across all events):
  - live → marked as deleted (restorable).
  - planned → removed entirely (NOT restorable; you'd have to recreate). Affects all events that used the property.
  - unexpected → added to the plan as deleted.

A single call may mix both — each entry is routed independently. Amplitude-owned properties cannot be deleted.

# Before deleting
Before an event-property delete, pass includeDeleted: true when looking up which events are using the property so deleted attachments are also included.

# Warning
Marking an ingested event property as deleted stops ingestion until restored (immediately on main; after merge on other branches). A delete on a non-main tracking-plan branch does not drop live ingest until that branch is merged into main. Removing a planned property does not stop ingestion — it was never ingested. Always surface this to the user before they confirm.

# Confirmation
This is a destructive taxonomy mutation. Mark as deleted and remove both use the same confirmation gate — never skip it. The first call returns a confirmation_required response showing the bucketed actions, project, and branch; relay that and its warning field to the user. Only call again with confirmed: true after the user explicitly acknowledges. Do not pass confirmed: true on the first call.

# Branch targeting
Unless specified, the default branch is used. To apply changes to a non-default branch, pass either branchId or branchName. If the user references a branch by name (e.g. "my-edits-branch"), use branchName. Pass only one.

# Permissions
This tool requires the "Update Tracking Plan" permission and may fail with a 403. Don't pre-warn the user; if it fails, surface the error and note that an admin may need to grant access.

tools.name: Delete user properties
tools.description:
Delete one or more user properties in a project.

Properties that are planned and ingested are marked as deleted (restorable). Properties that are planned but never ingested are removed. Properties ingested but not in the plan are added to the plan as deleted. When a name exists as both customer and Amplitude, only the customer property is targeted.

# Warning
Marking ingested properties as deleted (toMarkAsDeleted) stops ingestion until restored (immediately on main; after merge on other branches). A delete on a non-main tracking-plan branch does not drop live ingest until that branch is merged into main. Removing planned properties (toRemove) does not stop ingestion — they were never ingested and cannot be restored. Always surface both buckets and this warning to the user before they confirm.

This tool only deletes customer-defined user properties. Amplitude-owned user properties cannot be deleted and are always skipped — tell the user if any were requested.

# Confirmation
This is a destructive taxonomy mutation. Mark as deleted and remove both use the same confirmation gate — never skip it. The first call returns a confirmation_required response listing the bucketed properties, project, and branch; relay that and its warning field to the user. Only call again with confirmed: true after they explicitly acknowledge. Do not pass confirmed: true on the first call.

# Branch targeting
Unless specified, the default branch is used. To apply changes to a non-default branch, pass either branchId or branchName. If the user references a branch by name (e.g. "my-edits-branch"), use branchName. Pass only one.

# Permissions
This tool requires the "Update Tracking Plan" permission and may fail with a 403. Don't pre-warn the user; if it fails, surface the error and note that an admin may need to grant access.

tools.name: Get agent results
tools.description:
Retrieve results from AI agents that have analyzed your dashboards or session replays.

This is NOT for searching dashboards, charts, or notebooks — use 'search' for that.
This is specifically for retrieving the AI-generated insights and analyses that agents produced.

This tool handles both searching for agent analyses and fetching full results in a single call.

MODES:
1. **Search mode** (no session_id): Search agent analyses with filters. Returns preview summaries.
2. **Direct fetch mode** (session_id provided): Fetch full artifact data for a specific session.
3. **Auto-expand**: If search returns exactly 1 session, full artifacts are included automatically.

SEARCH STRATEGY (important — follow this order):
1. If you have a specific session_id, use direct fetch mode.
2. For dashboard analyses, pass agent_params with dashboard_id (cheap exact-match).
3. For session replay insights, use agent_params with category and/or impact (cheap exact-match).
4. Use "query" ONLY for natural language / fuzzy search when exact filters aren't sufficient.

WHEN TO USE:
- "What are my dashboard agents?" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer
- "Show my agent results" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer (or session_replay_explorer)
- "What agents have I run?" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer
- "What analyses exist for dashboard xyz?" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer, agent_params: { dashboard_id: "xyz" }
- "Show me high-impact session replay insights" → agent_type: session_replay_explorer, agent_params: { impact: "High" }
- "Friction hotspots in the checkout flow" → agent_type: session_replay_explorer, agent_params: { category: "Friction Hotspots" }, query: "checkout flow"
- "What did the AI find about rage clicks?" → agent_type: session_replay_explorer, query: "rage clicks"
- "Any dashboard insights about revenue?" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer, query: "revenue"
- "Show me insights from last week" → agent_type: session_replay_explorer, created_after: "2026-03-16T00:00:00Z"
- "What did I analyze recently?" → agent_type: dashboard_explorer

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Finding or listing dashboards, charts, or notebooks → use 'search' instead
- Running new analyses or queries → use 'query_dataset' or 'query_charts' instead
- Creating dashboards → use 'create_dashboard' instead

RETURNS:
- Search mode: List of analysis sessions with preview summaries, URLs, and pagination info
- Direct fetch mode: Full artifact data for the session
- Links to view each session in the Amplitude UI are included

tools.name: Get amplitude agent analytics info
tools.description:
Single read entry point for Amplitude Agent Analytics (AI/LLM session investigation).

NOT FOR: Customer product feedback (use use_amplitude_ai_feedback) or browser Session Replay.

Set `view` to choose the read route (each view has its own parameters in the tool schema):
- `schema` — fields, rubrics, taxonomy, filter_options. Use only when an exact filter identifier is not already known; request only the needed filterOptionTypes.
- `sessions` — filtered session lists and groupBy aggregations (replaces metrics/timeseries tools).
- `conversation` — full transcript; sessionId is required.
- `spans` — per-operation trace; sessionId or traceId is required (no org-wide scans).
- `tool_reliability` — metrics enum is only tool_stats | tool_definitions.

REMOVED (use sessions filters instead):
- search_agent_analytics_conversations (ILIKE scans)
- query_agent_analytics_metrics quality/cost/topics/timeseries enums

EXAMPLES:
- Agent names: { "view": "schema", "projectId": "12345", "include": ["filter_options"], "filterOptionTypes": ["agent_names"] }
- Failed sessions: { "view": "sessions", "projectId": "12345", "hasTechnicalFailure": true, "agentNames": ["global-chat"] }
- Transcript: { "view": "conversation", "projectId": "12345", "sessionId": "abc-123" }
- Tool reliability: { "view": "tool_reliability", "projectId": "12345", "metrics": ["tool_stats","tool_definitions"], "agentNames": ["global-chat"] }

tools.name: Get amplitude charts
tools.description:
Read saved Amplitude charts by ID, or look up the chart-type schema. One tool with five output modes selected by `include` (default `link`).

OUTPUT MODES:
- `link` (default) → 'get_chart_link': validates each id exists, then returns the chart's URL(s). Does not run the chart — cheap id lookup only.
- `typed` → 'lower_chart': returns the chart as typed UI-shaped parameters (`kind` + events/where/group_by/…) — the same shape `query_amplitude_data`'s `chart` parameter accepts. Prefer this when creating a variant of an existing chart or preparing a modification: edit the typed object, then call `query_amplitude_data` with `chart` (+ `chartId` to fork/modify the saved chart).
- `definition` → 'get_charts': returns the full raw Amplitude definition object(s). Use when `typed` cannot lower the chart (advanced features) or you need fields the typed model does not cover.
- `data` → 'query_charts': runs the chart(s) and returns the result data. Use when you need the numbers.
- `guide` → 'get_chart_definition_params': no ids needed. Pass `chartType` to get that type's parameter schema, valid enum values, and a working example definition — use BEFORE calling `query_amplitude_data` if you are unsure of the shape, or to look up valid enum values (e.g. funnel modes, segmentation metrics). Omit `chartType` to list all supported chart types. NOTE: This schema describes chart STRUCTURE only (params, enums, example) — it does NOT validate event or property names against your project's taxonomy. An unrecognized event/property key will NOT error; it silently returns a chart with empty data. Before building, confirm exact spelling via 'search', 'get_properties' (propertyType="event"), or get_amplitude_charts include='definition' on a similar existing chart — never guess a key name.

PREREQUISITES (required):
- For `link` / `typed` / `definition` / `data`: you MUST have at least one concrete `chartIds` or `chartEditIds` entry. Do not call speculatively. Resolve ids FIRST via `search` (by name), `get_from_url` (from a chart link), or `query_amplitude_data` (for ad-hoc analysis, which returns a chart edit id).
- For `guide`: no ids required; `chartType` is optional (omit to list all supported types).

INSTRUCTIONS:
- Create a new chart: `search` (taxonomy) → build typed `chart` → `query_amplitude_data`.
- Modify / fork a saved chart: `search` (find chart) → `get_amplitude_charts include='typed'` → edit the returned `chart` → `query_amplitude_data` with that `chart` and `chartId` set to the saved chart id.
- Saved charts → `chartIds`. Chart edits (links ending in /chart/new/<edit_id> or /chart/<chart_id>/edit/<edit_id>) → `chartEditIds`.
- `typed` and `definition` modes support `chartIds` only. For a chart edit's data use `data` mode.
- `data` mode accepts up to 3 ids/edits combined.
- The data params (`groupByLimit`, `excludeIncompleteDatapoints`, `timeSeriesLimit`) only apply when `include = 'data'`. `chartType` only applies when `include = 'guide'`.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Ad-hoc analysis without a saved chart → use 'query_amplitude_data'.
- Finding charts by name → use 'search'.

tools.name: Get amplitude context
tools.description:
Unified entry point for Amplitude context. Routes to one of two underlying tools based on whether a `projectId` is provided.

ROUTES:
- No `projectId` → 'get_context' route: returns the current user, organization (including org-level AI context), and the LIST of accessible projects as `{ appId, appName }`. Use this to discover which projects exist and their ids.
- `projectId` provided → 'get_project_context' route: returns that single project's details — description, timezone, currency, session definition, source projects, and project-level AI context.

WHEN TO USE:
- Session start, "what projects do I have access to?", "show me my org details", "what is my role?" → call with no arguments.
- "what timezone / currency / session settings does project X use?", "describe project X" → pass `projectId`.

CONTEXT DOCUMENTS (uploaded files):
- `org.aiContext` / project `aiContext` are short text fields only. Customers also upload context files (CSV data dictionaries, PDFs, process docs) in Settings → AI Controls; those are indexed for search and never returned in full — only titles (opt-in) or search snippets.
- `listContextDocuments: true` adds `contextDocuments` — document titles and ids only, no file contents. Use it when `aiContext` references an uploaded file by name (e.g. "always check <file> before answering").
- `searchContextDocuments` runs semantic search over the uploaded documents' contents and adds `contextDocumentSearch` with matching text snippets. Use specific terms from the user's question (event names, property names, column names).
- Scope for both: without `projectId`, org-level documents only; with `projectId`, org-level plus that project's documents.

EXAMPLES:
- Session start: {}
- Project settings: {"projectId": 12345}
- aiContext says "check the event dictionary file" → {"projectId": 12345, "listContextDocuments": true}
- Look up a term from uploaded docs: {"projectId": 12345, "searchContextDocuments": "envelope_event_type_id"}

NOTES:
- `projectId` is optional on purpose. Omit it to get the project list first, then call again with a real id from that list — do NOT guess project ids.
- The two layers are meant to be loaded together: call once without `projectId` at session start for org context, then with a `projectId` to drill into a project. On conflict, project-level context overrides org-level.
- Omit `listContextDocuments` and `searchContextDocuments` at session start — they add latency and are only useful once you know what to look for.

DO NOT USE FOR:
- Running analytics queries → use 'query_dataset'.
- Finding charts/dashboards/cohorts → use 'search'.

tools.name: Get amp session replay info
tools.description:
Unified entry point for session replay data: find replays and inspect what happened in them. Replaces get_session_replays, list_session_replays, get_session_replay_events, and get_session_replay_timeline.

ACTIONS:
- `search` (default): find replays by event / user-property / cohort filters, by Amplitude user (`userId`), by ID (`sessionReplayIds`), or sample recent sessions with no filters (random slice from the last 24 hours).
- `list`: simple paginated time-range listing via the public Session Replay API (`start_time`/`end_time`/`page_size`/`page_token`). Use `search` instead when filtering by events or user properties.
- `events`: processed rrweb interaction timeline for one replay (`sessionReplayId`) — page navigations, clicks, inputs, scrolls.
- `timeline`: full analytics event timeline for one replay (`sessionReplayId`) — every event the user fired during and around the session. PREFER THIS over user-timeline tools when you have a replay ID.

REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP — render_amp_session_replay:
- After `search`/`list` return replay IDs, you MUST call `render_amp_session_replay` in the SAME turn whenever the user's request implies viewing the replays ("show me", "let me see", "pull up", "watch", "play", "open", or any phrasing where seeing the replays is the deliverable). A list of IDs alone is not the answer the user wants.
- ONLY skip the render call for raw data extraction ("just count them", "export the IDs"). When in doubt, render.

INSTRUCTIONS:
- Provide `projectId` for every action.
- Replay IDs use the "<device_id>/<session_id>" format — pass them verbatim between actions.
- search: filters are ANDed; reference real event names (call get_events first if unsure). `userId` and `sessionReplayIds` are mutually exclusive with each other and with filters.
- list: use the returned next_page_token to fetch subsequent pages; keep sort_order consistent across pages. The list response's start/end times describe the analytics session window, NOT the recorded replay length.
- events vs timeline: `events` shows what the user DID in the recording (clicks/inputs/navigation from rrweb); `timeline` shows which analytics EVENTS fired (with properties). For "walk me through this session" prefer `timeline`.

EXAMPLES:
- Sample recent sessions: { "projectId": "12345" }
- Users who hit checkout errors: { "action": "search", "projectId": "12345", "events": [{ "name": "Checkout", "withProperty": { "name": "error_type", "exists": true } }] }
- Replays for a user yesterday: { "action": "search", "projectId": "12345", "userId": "98765", "since": "yesterday" }
- Paginated listing: { "action": "list", "projectId": "12345", "page_size": 50, "sort_order": "desc" }
- What the user did in a replay: { "action": "events", "projectId": "12345", "sessionReplayId": "device-abc/1773235450374" }
- Events fired during a replay: { "action": "timeline", "projectId": "12345", "sessionReplayId": "device-abc/1773235450374", "includeEventProperties": true }

NOTES:
- search defaults: 10 results; 30-day window for filtered queries, 24 hours otherwise. If a filtered search is empty, widen the window or relax filters instead of retrying unchanged.
- list defaults to the last 48 hours when no time range is provided.
- Cohort filters take numeric IDs only — resolve names with get_cohorts first.

tools.name: Get amp taxonomy
tools.description:
Read a project's tracking plan: the events it defines, the properties on them, what a branch changes relative to main, and who changed what when.

# WHEN TO USE — answer questions like:
- "What events exist in project 12345?" → { action: "events", projectId: "12345" }
- "List the custom events" → { action: "events", kind: "custom", projectId }
- "Show custom and labeled events together" → { action: "events", kind: "all", projectId }
- "Which properties are on the Purchase event?" → { action: "properties", propertyType: "event", eventType: "Purchase", projectId }
- "Which events use button_name?" → { action: "properties", propertyType: "event", names: ["button_name"], projectId }
- "What user properties are tracked?" → { action: "properties", propertyType: "user", projectId }
- "What does branch feature/v2 change?" / "review this branch before merging" → { action: "branch_changes", branchName: "feature/v2", projectId }
- "What changed in the tracking plan last week?" / "who deleted that event?" → { action: "activity", since: "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", projectId }
- Discovering valid event or property names before building a query_dataset filter or group_by

This is a fast schema lookup. Do NOT run query_dataset to discover which events or properties exist.

# DO NOT USE FOR:
- Metrics, counts, trends, funnels, retention → use 'query_dataset'
- Creating, updating or deleting taxonomy → use 'manage_amp_events' / 'manage_amp_properties'

ACTIONS:
| action | What it returns | Key params |
|---|---|---|
| events | Events in the tracking plan, with status and metadata. `kind` picks the surface: `event` (default, raw), `custom`, `labeled`, or `all` (custom + labeled together). | kind; raw: eventTypes, fields, includeDeleted, branchId/branchName; custom/labeled: customEventNames, customEventIds; both: limit, cursor |
| properties | Properties by surface. propertyType selects which: event, user, group, derived, lookup, channel, persisted. | propertyType, eventType, name, sources, groupTypes, names, fields, includeDeleted, includeHidden, includeBlocked, includeTransformations, branchId/branchName |
| branch_changes | What a branch adds, removes or updates vs main — events, properties, templates, group types. Use before approving or merging: review_branch reports only a count. `detail` adds per-field before/after; `detailFor` expands only the entities you name. | branchId/branchName, includeMainDrift, detail, detailFor |
| activity | Change history: who changed which taxonomy entity and when, newest first. Use for activity logs, "what changed since X", and per-person attribution. `detail` adds stored before/after values. | since, until, entityTypes, changeActions, loginIds, detail, limit, cursor, branchId/branchName |

INSTRUCTIONS:
- Use get_amplitude_context first to get project IDs. If the user has not specified a project, prompt them to decide.
- Raw events and custom/labeled events take different identifiers: `eventTypes` for raw, `customEventNames` / `customEventIds` for custom and labeled. Passing the wrong one is rejected rather than ignored.
- Only raw-event reads are branch-aware and take `fields`; custom and labeled events are neither branch-scoped nor field-projected.
- Where branch-aware, omit branchId/branchName for the default branch; otherwise pass exactly one selector.
- Event and property semantics are unchanged from the tools this replaces — same statuses, same transformation folding, same field projection via fields.
- activity reports current state nowhere: use it for "what changed", and events/properties for "what exists now".
- activity is NOT a complete audit of everything that changed — say so rather than implying it is. Custom, labeled and autotrack event edits deliberately write no activity record; transformations live in a separate service with no activity log; derived and computed properties are not tracking-plan entities; and newly ingested unexpected events and properties never appear (read `firstSeen` from an events or properties read instead). Passing entityTypes or changeActions narrows further, dropping changes whose activity type has no mapping — sources, tags, group types, and edits made through the API — so an unfiltered query is the only complete view.
- activity history belongs to the Data workspace, not the project, so every project sharing that workspace (its dev, staging and EU environments) returns the same rows. The response echoes workspaceId and branch — state that scope.
- branch_changes requires exactly one branch selector, and always reports a `comparison` field. "3-way" compares against the point the branch was cut and also returns `mainDrift` and `conflicts`; "2-way" is used when no review is open, may include changes main made after the branch was cut, and cannot report drift or conflicts. Relay that caveat rather than presenting a 2-way result as the branch's own edits.

tools.name: Get amp user data
tools.description:
Look up Amplitude users. One tool with modes selected by `include` (default `profile`).

TWO KINDS OF "USER":
- Product users (default): people in project analytics data — use amplitudeId / userId / email / deviceId.
- Org teammates (`include='org'`): people with Amplitude login accounts in your org — emails for sharing charts/dashboards/notebooks.

PRODUCT LOOKUPS — identify with exactly one of:
- `amplitudeId` → exact lookup (fastest, no resolution step).
- `userId` → your product's user id; resolved to an amplitudeId first.
- `email` → resolved to an amplitudeId (most projects use the email as the user id; a fallback search covers the rest).
- `deviceId` → resolved via device-id match (anonymous / pre-login users).
- `amplitudeIds` → batch form (max 10); profile mode only.

OUTPUT MODES (`include`):
- `id` → 'resolve_user_id': resolve identifier to amplitudeId only.
- `profile` (default) → 'get_user_profile': identity, properties, groups, usage stats.
- `timeline` → 'get_user_timeline': recent event stream.
- `both` → profile + timeline.
- `org` → 'get_org_users': list org login emails/names for sharing. No product identifier or projectId needed. Pass returned `loginId` values to share tools.

INSTRUCTIONS:
- `projectId` is required for product modes (id/profile/timeline/both); omit it for `include='org'`.
