tools.name: Abort-actor-run
tools.description:
Abort an Actor run that is currently starting or running.
For runs with status SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTING, ABORTED, or TIMED-OUT, this call has no effect.
The results will include the updated run details after the abort request.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to stop a run that is taking too long or misconfigured.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Abort run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Gracefully abort run y2h7sK3Wc

tools.name: Apify--rag-web-browser
tools.description:
This tool calls the Actor "apify/rag-web-browser" and retrieves its output results.
Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
Actor description: Web search and fetch tool for AI agents and RAG pipelines. It queries Google Search, scrapes the top N pages using a full web browser, and returns their content as clean Markdown for further processing by an LLM. Can also fetch individual URLs.

Use this tool when user wants to GET or RETRIEVE actual data immediately (one-time data retrieval).
This tool scrapes the data itself - it does NOT just find tools.

Examples of when to use:
- User wants current/immediate data (e.g., "Get flight prices for tomorrow", "What's the weather today?")
- User needs to fetch specific content now (e.g., "Fetch news articles from CNN", "Get product info from Amazon")
- User has time indicators like "today", "current", "latest", "recent", "now"

This is for general web scraping and immediate data needs. For repeated/scheduled scraping of specific platforms (e-commerce, social media), consider suggesting a specialized Actor from the Store for better performance and reliability.
When the user provides one specific URL and wants that page's full or verbatim content, prefer the dedicated apify/web-fetch tool when it is available - this tool is for searching and scraping by query.
If a scraped page comes back blocked or empty (e.g. the crawl reports a 403 or the page text is missing), do not give up: retry that URL with the apify/web-fetch tool when it is available - its anti-bot fetching gets through blocks this tool cannot.

tools.name: Apify--web-fetch
tools.description:
This tool calls the Actor "apify/web-fetch" and retrieves its output results.
Use this tool instead of the "call-actor" if user requests this specific Actor.
Actor description: Download any web page by URL and convert it to clean Markdown, plain text, HTML, and other formats. Automatically renders JavaScript and works around bot blocking. The Actor provides a real-time API for quick response times.

Use this tool to fetch a specific http(s) URL and return its complete content (one URL per call; http and https only).
It renders JavaScript and bypasses anti-bot protection, so it also retrieves pages where a plain HTTP fetch gets blocked, fails with an error such as 403 or 429, or returns incomplete content.
The page comes back verbatim - full content, no summarization - as Markdown, plain text, HTML, the raw response body, or the list of links on the page.

Examples of when to use:
- User provides a URL and wants its content, its data or links, or an answer that requires reading that page
- A previous attempt to fetch a page was blocked, returned an error or CAPTCHA, or came back incomplete because the page needs JavaScript rendering
- Verbatim page content is needed, e.g. for quoting, extraction, or archiving

This tool does not search the web - it needs a URL. To find pages by query, use a web search tool instead.
If the exact URL cannot be fetched (e.g. a non-http(s) scheme), say so rather than silently substituting a different URL.

tools.name: Call-actor
tools.description:
Call any Actor from the Apify Store.

WORKFLOW:
1. Use fetch-actor-details to get the Actor's input schema
2. Call this tool with the actor name and proper input based on the schema

If the actor name is not in "username/name" format, use search-actors to resolve the correct Actor first.

For MCP server Actors:
- Use fetch-actor-details with output={ mcpTools: true } to list available tools
- Call using format: "actorName:toolName" (e.g., "apify/actors-mcp-server:fetch-apify-docs")

IMPORTANT:
- Waits up to waitSecs (default 30s) for completion; returns run status and storage IDs, and with waitSecs > 0 also reports dataset field metadata
- Use get-dataset-items with the datasetId to fetch results; non-terminal runs include a nextStep with polling instructions
- Use dedicated Actor tools when available for better experience

There are two ways to run Actors:
1. Dedicated Actor tools (e.g., apify--rag-web-browser): These are pre-configured tools, offering a simpler and more direct experience.
2. Generic call-actor tool (call-actor): Use this when a dedicated tool is not available or when you want to run any Actor dynamically. This tool is especially useful if you do not want to add specific tools or your client does not support dynamic tool registration.

USAGE:
- Always use dedicated tools when available (e.g., apify--rag-web-browser)
- Use the generic call-actor tool only if a dedicated tool does not exist for your Actor.

- Use `waitSecs` (0–45) to control how long to wait. Default 30s returns results for fast actors. Use `waitSecs: 0` to start and return immediately for long-running actors.

EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get instagram posts using apify/instagram-scraper

tools.name: Fetch-actor-details
tools.description:
Get detailed information about an Actor by its ID or full name (format: "username/name", e.g., "apify/rag-web-browser").

Requires the exact ID or full name — do not construct a plausible-looking name and call this tool with it. If you only have a description, a partial name, or a name you have not seen in this conversation, find it with search-actors first.

Use 'output' parameter with boolean flags to control returned information:
- Default: All fields true except mcpTools
- Selective: Set desired fields to true (e.g., output: { inputSchema: true })
- Common patterns: inputSchema only, description + readme, mcpTools for MCP Actors

The 'readme' field returns the summary when available, full README otherwise.
Use when querying Actor details, documentation, input requirements, or MCP tools.

EXAMPLES:
- What does apify/rag-web-browser do?
- What is the input schema for apify/web-scraper?
- What tools does apify/actors-mcp-server provide?

tools.name: Fetch-apify-docs
tools.description:
Fetch the full content of an Apify or Crawlee documentation page by its URL.
Use this after finding a relevant page with the search-apify-docs tool.

USAGE:
- Use when you need the complete content of a specific docs page for detailed answers.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/platform/actors/running#builds
- user_input: Fetch https://docs.apify.com/academy
- user_input: Fetch https://crawlee.dev/docs/guides/basic-concepts

tools.name: Get-actor-run
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Actor run.

Returns run result: status, storages (datasets/keyValueStores alias map), stats, summary, nextStep.
- summary describes the past (e.g. "SUCCEEDED in 22s. 47 items; 3 fields available.").
- nextStep prescribes one primary follow-up action with identifiers interpolated (e.g. "Use get-dataset-items with datasetId=...").
- waitSecs (0–45, default 30) waits up to that many seconds for terminal status before returning.

USAGE:
- Use to check the status of a run started by any Actor-running tool.
- Pass waitSecs > 0 to block until terminal (or until the cap elapses).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Show details of run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Wait for run y2h7sK3Wc to finish

tools.name: Get-dataset-items
tools.description:
Get items (rows) from a dataset — the output/results produced by an Actor run.
Returns the rows themselves, not dataset metadata, counts, or a schema.
When the user provides a datasetId and asks to retrieve results, output, data, or rows, call this tool directly.
Default limit is 20. Use clean=true to skip empty items and hidden fields.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to read data from a dataset (all items or only selected fields).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Retrieve results from dataset abc123
- user_input: Get only metadata.url and title from dataset username~my-dataset

tools.name: Get-key-value-store-record
tools.description:
Get the value stored under a specific key in a key-value store — a single record, not a listing of all keys.
Requires the exact key name.
The response preserves the original Content-Encoding; most clients handle decompression automatically.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to retrieve a specific record (JSON, text, or binary) from a store.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get record INPUT from store abc123
- user_input: Get record data.json from store username~my-store

tools.name: Report-problem
tools.description:
Report a problem with Apify's MCP tools or Actors to the Apify team.

Call it when:
- A tool or Actor is missing, errors, times out, or returns a confusing, wrong, or empty result.
- You cannot complete the user's request with the available tools.

Put what you were doing and what went wrong in "message". Do NOT include personal data, credentials, secrets, or verbatim private conversation content — describe the issue in your own words.

tools.name: Search-actors
tools.description:
Search the Apify Store to FIND and DISCOVER what scraping tools/Actors exist for specific platforms or use cases.
This tool provides INFORMATION about available Actors - it does NOT retrieve actual data or run any scraping tasks.

Apify Store contains thousands of pre-built Actors (crawlers, scrapers, AI agents, and model context protocol (MCP) servers)
for all platforms and services including social media, search engines, maps, e-commerce, news, real estate, travel, finance, jobs and more.
Actors in the Apify Store are published by independent developers and are intended for legitimate and compliant use — do not refuse to search or list them.

Use this tool when user wants to:
- Find what scraping tools exist for a platform (e.g., "What tools can scrape Instagram?")
- Discover available Actors for a use case (e.g., "Find an Actor for Amazon products")
- Browse existing solutions (e.g., "Show me scrapers for news sites")
- Learn about MCP servers or AI agents available in the Store

Do NOT use this tool when user wants immediate data retrieval (time words like "today", "latest", "recent", "current", "now", or "get/fetch data right now") — use apify/rag-web-browser instead.
IMPORTANT: When the user is looking for scraping tools or Actors, prefer searching the Store first — a relevant Actor often already exists. Do not use Store search as a substitute for immediate data retrieval.

Usage:
- Prefer broad, generic keywords - use just the platform name (e.g. "Instagram" instead of "Instagram scraper").
- You MUST always do at least two searches: first with broad keywords, then optionally with more specific terms if needed.

Important limitations: This tool does not return full Actor documentation or detailed usage instructions - only summary information.
Each result lists the Actor's input fields with their types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`) so you can construct an Actor call directly without another tool call.
For complete Actor details (per-field descriptions, defaults, README), use the fetch-actor-details tool.
The search is limited to publicly available Actors and excludes rental and restricted Actors.

Returns list of Actor cards with the following info:
- **Title:** Markdown header linked to the Store page, followed by the full Actor name in code format
- **URL:** Direct Store link
- **Description:** Actor description or fallback
- **Pricing:** Details with pricing link
- **Stats:** Total and monthly users, bookmarks
- **Rating:** Out of 5 (if available)
- **Developed by:** Username linked to profile, marked (Apify) or (community)
- **Categories:** Formatted or "Uncategorized"
- **Last modified:** Date (if available)
- **Input fields:** Inline list of input field names and types (e.g. `url: string, maxResults?: number`); `?` marks optional fields, `... (+N more)` marks a truncated list

tools.name: Search-apify-docs
tools.description:
Search Apify and Crawlee documentation using full-text search.
Do not also search the Apify Store unless the user asks to find Actors.

You must explicitly select which documentation source to search using the docSource parameter:

• docSource="apify" - Apify:
  Apify Platform documentation including: Platform features, SDKs (JS, Python), CLI, REST API, Academy (web scraping fundamentals), Actor development and deployment

• docSource="crawlee-js" - Crawlee (JavaScript):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for JavaScript. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

• docSource="crawlee-py" - Crawlee (Python):
  Crawlee is a web scraping library for Python. It handles blocking, crawling, proxies, and browsers for you.

The results will include the URL of the documentation page (which may include an anchor),
and a limited piece of content that matches the search query.

Fetch the full content of the document using the fetch-apify-docs tool by providing the URL.

When results contain both platform documentation (`docs.apify.com/platform`) and Academy content (`docs.apify.com/academy`) on the same topic, prefer the platform documentation.

tools.name: Get Detailed Models

tools.name: Get query history

tools.name: Get state

tools.name: List AI Models

tools.name: List Vector Collections
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of all vector collections under your account. Use when you need to view available collections before performing vector operations like querying, upserting, or deleting vectors.

tools.name: Parse Document

tools.name: Update State Settings

tools.name: Upload File

description: APIVerve offers a comprehensive suite of APIs designed to simplify integration processes, providing developers with scalable and reliable solutions for various applications.

tools.name: Advice Generator

tools.name: Age Calculator

tools.name: Get Airline Info by Name
tools.description: Look up airline information by name. Returns airline details including IATA code (2-letter), ICAO code (3-letter), radio callsign, and country of operation. Supports partial name matching, so searching 'American' returns all airlines containing 'American' in their name.

tools.name: Get airport distance by IATA
tools.description: Tool to get distance between two airports by their IATA codes. Use when you have valid airport IATA codes and need the flight distance.

tools.name: Get Airport Info by ICAO Code

tools.name: Air Quality

tools.name: Find antonyms for a word

tools.name: Currency Converter
tools.description: Tool to convert currency rates. Use when you need to convert an amount between two currencies with the latest exchange rate.

tools.name: Get Word Definition
tools.description: Tool to get the definition of a word. Use when you need to find the meaning of a specific word. E.g., "Define the word apple."

tools.name: Weather by City

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your unique API key for authenticating requests to APIVerve.

name: Appcircle
description: Appcircle is an enterprise-grade mobile CI/CD platform that enables developers to build, test, and publish mobile applications efficiently, offering both cloud-based and self-hosted deployment options.

tools.name: Standard Repo Webhook Callback
tools.description: Trigger Appcircle builds via Git provider webhook callbacks. This action forwards webhook payloads from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps to Appcircle's build webhook endpoint to automatically trigger builds when code is pushed. Use this action when: - Simulating or testing webhook-triggered builds - Programmatically triggering builds using webhook payloads - Integrating custom CI/CD workflows that need to trigger Appcircle builds - Replaying or debugging webhook events Requirements: - The organization must exist and have webhook integration configured in Appcircle - Build profiles must be set up with repository connections - The webhook URL pattern is: https://api.appcircle.io/build/v1/callback/hooks/{provider}/{org_id}/V7 Note: The action returns the raw HTTP response including status code and response body, allowing you to handle success, validation errors, or authentication issues appropriately.

tools.name: Custom Integration Webhook Callback
tools.description: Triggers Appcircle builds via custom integration webhook endpoint by forwarding Git provider webhook payloads. This action is designed to receive and forward webhook payloads from Git providers (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps) to Appcircle's build system. The webhook URL format and parameters (organization_id, integration_id, version) are provided by Appcircle when you configure custom integrations for repositories connected via SSH or public URL in the build profile settings. Use this action when: - You need to programmatically trigger Appcircle builds from Git provider webhook events - Testing webhook integrations with different payload structures - Implementing custom CI/CD workflows that forward webhook events to Appcircle Note: The organization_id and integration_id values must correspond to actual configurations in Appcircle. Test payloads will typically return 400/404 errors indicating no valid configuration exists for the provided IDs.

tools.name: List Distribution Profiles
tools.description: List all distribution profiles for the authenticated organization. Distribution profiles are used to manage and distribute app builds to testers. This endpoint supports pagination, sorting, and filtering by profile name. Use this when you need to retrieve available distribution profiles.

tools.name: Get Distribution Sent Profiles
tools.description: Get distinct profile names for App Sharing Report filter. Returns a list of unique profile names that can be used to filter app sharing reports within the specified date range and organization. Use this to discover available profile names before querying detailed sharing reports.

tools.name: Get Publish Activity Report
tools.description: Retrieve the publish activity report for your organization. Returns paginated list of publish activities with filtering options by date range, platform, action type, and organization. Use this to monitor and audit publish operations across profiles.

tools.name: List Build Profiles
tools.description: List all build profiles for the authenticated organization. Build profiles define the configuration for building mobile applications. Use this to discover available build profiles and their IDs before triggering builds or configuring webhooks.

tools.name: List Bundle Identifiers
tools.description: List all bundle identifiers in Appcircle. Returns all bundle identifiers configured in your organization, including their platforms, capabilities, and associated credentials. Use this to discover available bundle identifiers before managing signing identities or app configurations.

tools.name: List Organizations
tools.description: List organizations accessible to the authenticated user. Returns a paginated list of organizations with their details including ID, name, logo URL, and SSO status. Supports search filtering and pagination controls. Use this to discover available organizations before performing organization-specific operations like managing builds, distributions, or webhooks.

tools.name: List Store Profiles
tools.description: List all Enterprise App Store profiles for the authenticated organization. Enterprise App Store profiles are used to distribute apps internally. Use this to discover available store profiles and their IDs before listing app versions or managing store content.

tools.name: Rename Variable Group
tools.description: Tool to rename an environment group (variable group) in Appcircle. Use when you need to update the name of an existing variable group to better reflect its purpose or environment.

tools.name: Obtain In-App Update Auth Token
tools.description: Tool to fetch an access token for Enterprise App Store in-app updates. Use when you have the enterprise store profileId and secret and need to obtain a bearer token for subsequent update requests.

tools.name: Download In-App Update Version with User
tools.description: Tool to download a specific in-app store version and attribute the download to a user for reporting. Use when triggering an in-app update download after obtaining an access token.

tools.name: List Enterprise App Store App Versions
tools.description: Tool to list available app versions for the Enterprise App Store profile. Use when fetching available in-app update versions.

tools.name: List Store Profile App Versions V2
tools.description: Tool to list app versions under a given store profile. Use when you need to fetch all versions for a specific Enterprise App Store profile after obtaining its ID.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The Personal API Token generated from the Appcircle dashboard.

name: Appointo

tools.name: Authenticate Appointo API Token
tools.description: Tool to authenticate with the Appointo API by validating the APPOINTO-TOKEN header. Use when verifying the token before subsequent API calls.

tools.name: Cancel Booking
tools.description: Tool to cancel a booking or selected customers. Use when you need to revoke an entire booking or individual attendees after verifying booking details. Use after retrieving booking information.

tools.name: Create Booking
tools.description: Tool to create a new booking. Use when scheduling a customer booking after confirming appointment availability.

tools.name: Get Appointment Availability
tools.description: Tool to get calendar availability for a specific appointment. Use when you need to fetch available time slots for an appointment within a date range.

tools.name: List Appointments
tools.description: Tool to list appointments. Use when fetching appointments with optional filters and pagination after confirming a valid API token.

tools.name: List Bookings

tools.name: List Products
tools.description: Tool to fetch all available products. Use when browsing products with optional paging and search. Call after authenticating with Appointo API.

tools.name: List Subscription Contracts
tools.description: Tool to list subscription contracts. Use when retrieving contracts with optional search after confirming a valid API token.

tools.name: Reschedule Booking
tools.description: Tool to reschedule an existing booking to a new timeslot. Use after confirming new timeslot availability.

tools.name: Update Booking Buffers
tools.description: Tool to update buffer times for an existing booking. Use after confirming new buffer durations.

tools.name: Upsert Appointment Configuration
tools.description: Tool to upsert availability config for an appointment. Use when setting or updating appointment availability settings.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API token used for authenticating requests to the Appointo API.

name: ApptiveGrid
description: ApptiveGrid is a collaborative no-code database and app platform for managing spaces, grids, forms, and structured records.

tools.name: Create Record
tools.description: Create one record in a grid from a provider-native object keyed by that grid's field IDs or field keys; inspect the grid first to construct valid values.

tools.name: Get Current User
tools.description: Return the connected ApptiveGrid user's ID, plan, seat availability, and resource links; use it to identify the user before listing spaces.

tools.name: Get Grid
tools.description: Return a grid's metadata and dynamic field definitions; use it before listing, reading, or creating records.

tools.name: Get Record
tools.description: Return one record from a grid by record ID, optionally rendered with a provider layout.

tools.name: Get Space
tools.description: Return a space and its grid summaries or grid links; use it to discover grid IDs before reading records.

tools.name: List Records
tools.description: Return one 1-based page of records from a grid, optionally using the provider's layout, filter, and sorting definitions.

tools.name: List Spaces
tools.description: Return one 1-based page of spaces available to a user, including IDs needed to inspect a space.

description: AppVeyor is a hosted continuous integration service for building and deploying applications.

tools.name: Download Build Log
tools.description: Tool to download the build log for a specific job. Use when you need to retrieve the log output from a completed or running build job.

tools.description: Tool to get the list of artifacts for a specific build job. Use when you need to retrieve artifacts after a job completes.

tools.name: Get Build By Version

tools.name: Get Project Branch Status Badge
tools.description: Tool to get a project branch status badge image. Returns a PNG or SVG badge image showing the build status for a specific project branch.

tools.description: Tool to get a list of all projects for the authenticated account. Use after authentication to enumerate available projects.

tools.name: Get Project Status Badge
tools.description: Tool to get project status badge image. Use when you need to retrieve the status badge for displaying project build status.

tools.name: Get Public Project Status Badge
tools.description: Tool to get status badge image for a project with a public repository. Use when you need to retrieve a build status badge for display or documentation purposes.

tools.name: Get Role
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific role. Use when you need to inspect permissions and metadata of a role by ID.

tools.name: Get User Invitations
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all pending user invitations in the account. Use when you need to list all outstanding invitations sent to potential team members.

tools.name: Get Users
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all users in the account. Use when you need to list all team users in your AppVeyor account.

tools.name: List Collaborators

name: Archive.org
description: Search and access Internet Archive content, inspect analytics, Wayback captures, IIIF images, and account tasks, and manage item files, metadata, derivation, and the connected user's reviews.

tools.name: Advanced Search Archive.org Items
tools.description: Search Archive.org metadata with exact Advanced Search page semantics. Use Search Archive.org Items instead when cursor-based deep paging is needed.

tools.name: Check Identifier Availability
tools.description: Check whether an Archive.org item identifier is available before attempting to create an item.

tools.name: Check Archive.org Upload Limit
tools.description: Check whether Archive.org's ingest queue is likely to accept an upload or delete, using only the connection's LOW Authorization header.

tools.name: Copy Item File
tools.description: Copy one Archive.org file server-side to a named path in an existing destination item. This creates the destination file when absent and overwrites it when present while preserving the prior destination under history/files. The source remains unchanged. This action never queues derivation; use DERIVE_ITEM for that separate irreversible effect. Catalog visibility may lag after IA-S3 accepts the copy.

tools.name: Delete Item File
tools.description: Submit asynchronous deletion of one named file from an Archive.org item through IA-S3. An accepted response does not verify file absence; read item metadata later to verify it. This action cannot delete an item/bucket. Cascade deletion is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled.

tools.name: Delete My Archive.org Review
tools.description: Permanently delete the connected Archive.org user's public review from one item. Archive.org queues the deletion and rejects the request if no such review exists.

tools.name: Derive Archive.org Item
tools.description: Queue Archive.org's fixed derive.php task for an item owned or editable by the connected account. The task transforms source content into derived files asynchronously and may replace prior derivatives; this action never requests the untested remove_derived option.

tools.name: Download Item File
tools.description: Download one public file from an Archive.org item and return a temporary downloadable file reference.

tools.name: Find Wayback Snapshots
tools.description: Find the closest archived Wayback Machine snapshot for each requested URL, using one before, after, or either direction for the batch.

tools.name: Get Connected Archive.org User
tools.description: Return the authenticated Archive.org user's identity and privileges without returning either IA-S3 credential.

tools.name: Get Detailed Archive.org Views
tools.description: Get bounded geographic view analytics and, for items, top referrers over a recent window or date range. Collections support both timeframes; contributors support date ranges only and do not include referrers.

tools.name: Get IIIF Image Info
tools.description: Get normalized IIIF Image API capabilities through Archive.org's fixed-host single-image convenience route or a live-proven versioned file route.

tools.name: Get IIIF Manifest
tools.description: Get a compact IIIF Presentation manifest for an Archive.org item or one page of an Archive.org collection.

tools.name: Get Item Metadata
tools.description: Get an Archive.org item's full record, including metadata, file inventory, public reviews, and catalog tasks, or return one selected metadata field or array slice.

tools.name: Get Item View Counts
tools.description: Get all-time, last-30-day, and last-7-day view counts for one or more Archive.org item or collection identifiers from the current or legacy counting pipeline.

tools.name: Get Item View History
tools.description: Get a bounded daily view history for one Archive.org item or collection, split by robot classification.

tools.name: Get My Review
tools.description: Get the connected Archive.org user's review for one item, if that user has reviewed it.

tools.name: Get Archive.org Task Log
tools.description: Download a plain-text log for a task visible to the connected account. Optionally return only the first or last requested number of lines.

tools.name: Get Task Rate Limits
tools.description: Report the connected account's current task capacity and in-flight counts for one Archive.org catalog command.

tools.name: List Archive.org Tasks
tools.description: Return any documented combination of the connected account's task summary, active catalog, and resource-authorized history, one page at a time.

tools.name: List Wayback Captures
tools.description: Return one bounded structured CDX page of Wayback captures for a URL or host.

tools.name: Render IIIF Image
tools.description: Render a bounded crop, resize, rotation, quality, and format from a fixed Archive.org IIIF image route.

tools.name: Search Archive.org Items
tools.description: Search Archive.org item metadata with a Lucene-style query and return one deep-pagination page of matching items.

tools.name: Update Item Metadata
tools.description: Apply JSON Patch changes to one Archive.org item owned or editable by the connected account, limited to ordinary item metadata and metadata records for named files. Remove permanently deletes the selected metadata value; move removes a value from its source path and adds it elsewhere within the same target. File bytes are never moved or removed. Archive.org validates the whole request under an item lock, and multiple target changes are atomic. SimpleLists, reviews, and custom user JSON targets are deferred.

tools.name: Upload Item File
tools.description: Create or replace one file through Archive.org IA-S3, explicitly choosing a new-item or existing-item upload. New-item uploads alone send item creation metadata. Overwrites preserve the prior file under history/files, and this action never queues derivation; use DERIVE_ITEM for that separate irreversible effect. Input buffering is limited by the platform-configured maximum file download size. Acceptance does not mean catalog ingest is complete.

tools.name: Upsert My Archive.org Review
tools.description: Create or overwrite the connected Archive.org user's single public review for an eligible item. The title, body, and optional rating become publicly visible on the item.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Archive.org IA-S3 access key. Sign in to Archive.org, open https://archive.org/account/s3.php, and copy the access key shown under S3 API Keys.

required.name: generic_secret
required.description: The secret key paired with your Archive.org IA-S3 access key. Sign in and copy it from https://archive.org/account/s3.php. Keep it private; Archive.org uses this pair for programmatic account operations.

name: Are.na
description: Are.na is a platform for collecting, organizing, and connecting ideas, images, links, and other creative research.

tools.name: Add To Channels
tools.description: Add an existing Are.na block or channel to one or more target channels without duplicating the underlying resource.

tools.name: Create Channel
tools.description: Create a user-owned Are.na channel, closed by default, and return its stable numeric ID and generated slug.

tools.name: Delete Channel
tools.description: Permanently delete one Are.na channel the authenticated user is allowed to destroy. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: Get Block
tools.description: Get the details of one Are.na block by ID, including its subtype, content, source, creator, and metadata.

tools.name: Get Channel
tools.description: Get an Are.na channel by numeric ID or slug, including visibility, counts, owner, and the current user's permissions.

tools.name: Get Current User
tools.description: Return the identity and account details for the authenticated Are.na user.

tools.name: Get My Feed
tools.description: Return one page of the authenticated user's personalized Are.na activity feed, newest first. Call again with next_cursor only when another page is needed.

tools.name: List Channel Contents
tools.description: Return one page of blocks and nested channels from an Are.na channel, with optional sorting and contributor filtering.

tools.name: Remove From Channel
tools.description: Remove one block or nested channel placement from an Are.na channel. This deletes only the connection; the underlying block or channel remains intact and may still exist in other channels.

tools.name: Update Channel
tools.description: Update selected fields of an Are.na channel the authenticated user can edit. Fields omitted from the request remain unchanged.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create a Personal Access Token with write permission at https://www.are.na/settings/personal-access-tokens, then paste the token here. Write permission enables both read and write operations in the Are.na V3 API. Keep this token secret.

name: Arize AX

tools.name: Create Prompt

tools.name: Get Dataset

tools.name: Get Experiment

tools.name: Get Prompt

tools.name: List Projects

tools.name: List Prompts
tools.description: List one page of Arize prompts, optionally filtered by space or prompt name.

tools.name: List Prompt Versions

tools.name: Update Prompt
tools.description: Update or clear an Arize prompt's description.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create a user or service API key in Arize AX under Settings > API Keys, then copy the full key when it is shown. Arize displays the full key only once. Service keys are recommended for durable automations; grant the key access to the organizations and spaces the automation needs.

name: Artificial Analysis
description: Artificial Analysis provides independent benchmarks and analysis of AI models and API providers — intelligence, coding and math indices, pricing, latency and throughput performance, plus arena rankings for image, video, speech and music models.

tools.name: List Image-Editing Models (Arena)
tools.description: List image-editing models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. Use to find the best-rated image-editing model. Returns all models in one call (unpaginated).

tools.name: List Image-to-Video-with-Audio Models (Arena)
tools.description: List image-to-video-with-audio models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. Returns all models unpaginated in one call. No legacy sibling exists for this modality.

tools.name: List Image-to-Video Models (Arena)

tools.name: List Language Models (Intelligence & Pricing)
tools.description: List LLMs from the Artificial Analysis leaderboard with intelligence, coding and agentic indices, pricing, and performance (speed and latency). tools.name: List Instrumental Music Models (Arena)
tools.description: List instrumental music-generation models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. Returns all models in one call (unpaginated). Note: music items have no slug field.

tools.name: List Music-with-Vocals Models (Arena)
tools.description: List music-with-vocals generation models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. Use to find the best-rated music-with-vocals model. Returns all models in one call (unpaginated).

tools.name: List Speech-to-Speech Models
tools.description: List speech-to-speech models with Big Bench Audio (bba_score), Full Duplex Bench (fdb_score), and Tau-Voice (tau_voice_score) quality scores. tools.name: List Speech-to-Text Models (WER)

tools.name: List Text-to-Image Models (Arena)

tools.name: List Text-to-Speech Models (Arena)

tools.name: List Text-to-Video-with-Audio Models (Arena)
tools.description: List text-to-video-with-audio models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. No legacy sibling exists for this modality.

tools.name: List Text-to-Video Models (Arena)
tools.description: List text-to-video models ranked by the Artificial Analysis arena, with Elo score and 95% confidence interval. Use to find the best-rated text-to-video model. Returns all models in one call (unpaginated).

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Artificial Analysis Data API key. Create a free account on the Artificial Analysis Insights Platform (https://artificialanalysis.ai/), then open "API key management" from your account menu and generate a key. Sent in the 'x-api-key' request header. Keep it secret and server-side — regenerating a key immediately revokes the previous value. tools.name: Addconfluencecontentpermissions
tools.description:
Adds one or more content-level permission grants to a single Confluence
content entity. Existing grants for other principals are preserved; to
replace the full set, use replaceConfluenceContentPermissions instead.

These are Specific access grants: operation `read` = Can view; `update` =
Can edit and already includes view. A principal has exactly ONE level, so
assigning `read` to a principal who currently has `update` is a downgrade
to view-only. Never include the same principal under both operations.
Adding a grant does NOT restrict others, make content private, or change
General access; use setConfluenceContentRestrictionState for that baseline.
Private creation already gives the creator `update`. Do not add `read` for
that creator, because update already includes view. Existing-state and
self-lockout rules are enforced by the Confluence monolith.

Each grant pairs an operation with a list of principals. Pass the grants via
the `permissions` input, an array of objects shaped exactly like:
  [
    {
      "operation": "read",
      "principals": [
        { "principalType": "user",  "principalId": "<atlassian-account-id>" },
        { "principalType": "group", "principalId": "<group-id>" }
      ]
    }
  ]
Enums: operation is one of read | update; principalType is one of
user | group. For a user, principalId is the Atlassian account ID; for a
group, principalId is the group ID.

A new worklog is always logged as the calling user; an edit keeps its original author. Jira reduces the issue's remaining estimate by the time logged (by the difference on an edit). To change the estimate itself, use editJiraIssue. Returns the worklog's id, needed to edit it later, with the stored timeSpent and started.

tools.name: Approvejsmrequestresolverplans
tools.description: Approve the current Request Resolver plans for explicitly selected JSM issue keys after the user has reviewed their plans with getJsmRequestResolverPlans and confirmed approval. Approval applies to each request's current plan at execution time, which may have changed since retrieval. The caller must be the request's human assignee or delegator. Returns one result per input in order; approved means approval was accepted, not that execution is complete. Output fields include requests[].issueKey, requests[].status, and approver.displayName; use these paths when selecting responseFields. Duplicate keys for the same request are submitted once per call. This is not idempotent across calls. For an unknown outcome, refresh the plan before any further approval; never automatically retry approval. Use getJsmRequestResolverPlans to check subsequent execution status. Does not decide customer-portal approvals.

tools.name: Convertjiraissuehierarchy
tools.description: Convert an existing Jira issue across hierarchy levels: a standard issue (Task, Bug, Story) into a sub-task under a parent, or a sub-task back into a standard issue. Mirrors Jira's Move / Convert-to-sub-task wizard: preview destination compatibility (mode=preview_step1), preview field retain/remap/drop (mode=preview_step2), then execute (mode=confirm). Do not use this for same-level type edits such as Bug → Story — use editJiraIssue for those. Task → Sub-task: always ask the user for parentIssueKey before calling. Do not search for, infer, or pick a parent. If they did not name a parent, ask them instead of calling this tool. The parent must be a standard issue. If this result has CHILD_ISSUES_WILL_REPARENT, those children will get the same new parent — ask the user to accept that, then confirm with acknowledgeChildReparent=true. If this result has SOURCE_HAS_SUBTASKS, the convert is blocked; tell the user that. If this result has MOVE_PERMISSION_REQUIRED, the user lacks Jira Bulk change or Move permission — tell them to convert in the Jira UI. Do not retry. Do not mention another project style. If preview execution.method is bulk-move, or confirm returns MOVE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, this is Jira's Move wizard: list the destination project, statusMapping, and fieldPlan.dropped to the user and ask them to accept that status change and that those fields will be dropped. Do not convert until they accept, then retry with mode=confirm and acknowledgeMove=true. If they decline, stop. Sub-task → Task: no parent needed; confirm clears the parent. After convert, reply with this issue's key, new type, and parent. If appliedChanges.dropped is present, also name those dropped fields. If appliedChanges.status is present, also name that status change. Do not mention bulk-move permissions or project-style notes unless this result has MOVE_PERMISSION_REQUIRED.

tools.name: Createartifactthumbnailupload

Overwriting, replacing, or regenerating an existing thumbnail is not supported. For HTML and PDF, use a static 672-by-400 PNG (1.68:1), capturing rendered HTML and a representative animation frame, or the first PDF page. Returns a pre-signed URL and instructions for uploading the image. No publishArtifact call is needed.

tools.name: Createcapacityplannonprojectwork
tools.description:
Create a non-project work item in Individual Capacity Planning. "Non-project work" is a bucket of time that is not a Jira issue or an Atlas project, such as Leave, Run the Business (RtB), on-call, or training.
USE WHEN the user asks to create a new non-project work item, or a category of work that does not already exist as a Jira issue or Atlas project. Search first with listCapacityPlanNonProjectWork to avoid creating a duplicate - the match is on name and is case-insensitive.
Non-project work is owned by Capacity Planning and exists nowhere else in Atlassian, so it can only be created through this tool. A contributor must be supplied: the new work item is created together with a work association for that person, so it is immediately allocatable to them. Allocate additional people or set the effort per period afterwards with updateCapacityPlanAllocations, using the ARI returned here as workId.
On success, nonProjectWork contains the created item's name and ari - use that ari as workId for updateCapacityPlanAllocations rather than fabricating one.

tools.name: Createconfluenceattachment
tools.description: Prepare a Confluence attachment upload and return a local curl command

tools.name: Createconfluencecomment
tools.description: Create or reply to a comment on a Confluence page or blog post

tools.name: Createconfluencecontent
tools.description:
Create a new Confluence page, blog post, live doc, whiteboard, database,
embed, smart link, or folder.

Before choosing body.format or authoring a body, call getContentFormatGuide through execute with
name=getContentFormatGuide and inputs={toolName}. Use createConfluencePage
for pages, blog posts, and live docs; createConfluenceWhiteboard for
whiteboards; or createConfluenceDatabase for databases.

Space instructions describe how to author content in a Confluence space.
Apply relevant guidance to the content you create or update. Follow this
decision rule:
1. Before authoring, call getConfluenceSpace for the target space unless
   getConfluenceContent returned metadata.hasSpaceInstructions=false for
   content in that space. If getConfluenceSpace already returned for the
   same cloudId and space during the current task, reuse its
   spaceInstructions and do not call it again.
2. When the value is true or unknown and instructions have not been
   loaded, you must call getConfluenceSpace once before authoring through
   execute with name=getConfluenceSpace, top-level cloudId, and
   inputs={spaceIdOrKey}.
3. Apply any returned spaceInstructions. If a successful response omits
   them, no instructions are configured; author with defaults and do not
   block.

After a successful getConfluenceSpace call, do not make a separate
getConfluenceSpaceInstructions call.

tools.name: Createconfluenceinfographicforpage
tools.description: Create an infographic in a page workflow. Use only when a Confluence page creation or editing skill or guided workflow selects it; never as a standalone tool. Returns a media reference for embedding, which may sync later. Before prompting, reuse the shared Remix guide (headed `## Remix embeds`) if its text is in your current context. Only if missing, call getContentFormatGuide with toolName=createConfluenceInfographicForPage and follow its Remix guidance. Generation and billing finish asynchronously; typical cost is 15–30 Rovo credits. Download detailed billing data for final usage; match any returned correlationId and usageUniqueId.

tools.name: Createconfluencemauiapp
tools.description: Create a Maui app in a page workflow. Use only when a Confluence page creation or editing skill or guided workflow selects it; never as a standalone tool. Returns a reserved app ID and embed URL for the owning page. Before prompting, reuse the shared Remix guide (headed `## Remix embeds`) if its text is in your current context. Only if missing, call getContentFormatGuide with toolName=createConfluenceMauiApp and follow its Remix guidance. Generation and billing finish asynchronously; typical cost is 15–30 Rovo credits. Download detailed billing data for final usage; match any returned correlationId and usageUniqueId.

tools.name: Createconfluencespace
tools.description: Create a Confluence space. Successful responses include id, key, and homepageId (the homepage / sidebar root content ID).

tools.name: Createfocusarea
tools.description: Create a new Focus area in a workspace. Call getFocusAreaTypes first and use an enabled type UUID for focusAreaTypeId — do not fabricate it. Optionally set parentFocusAreaIdentifier (UUID, ARI, or Focus page URL); if set, the parent's type must be a higher hierarchy level than the type being created. Optionally set startDate and targetDate as { date, confidence } where date is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm (e.g. 2026-08-10T00:00; bare dates are not accepted) and confidence is DAY, MONTH, or QUARTER. Omit owner to default to the creating user. Returns the created focus area (identifiers, type, owner, parent, dates, status, health, timestamps). Use getFocusArea for expansions such as aboutContent, statusUpdates, or subFocusAreas. When passing both cloudId and a parent ARI, they must refer to the same site.

tools.name: Createfocusareastatusupdate
tools.description: Create a status update on a focus area, or save it as a draft. A status update is a change to one or more of status, health, summary, target date. Changing status needs an id discovered first with getFocusArea and include.statusTransitions; health does not. Passing only focusAreaIdentifier still posts a visible, empty update when publishing, so never call this tool speculatively. Field-level behavior for status, health, summary, target date, and draft constraints is documented on the inputs.

tools.name: Creategoal
tools.description: Create an Atlassian Goal or Success Measure using an enabled Goal Type.

tools.name: Creategoalupdate

tools.name: Createjiraboard
tools.description: Create a new company-managed Jira Software board (scrum or kanban) from an existing filter. Requires a filter ID the user can view. When location is omitted, the board is filed in the single company-managed project from the filter's JQL. Team-managed (TMP) locations are always rejected: TMP projects are 1:1 project to board (one built-in board at project creation, no way to add another). User locations are also rejected. The response includes a url that opens the board. The filter decides which issues the board shows; location only decides where the board is filed in navigation.

tools.name: Createjiraissue
