Sizing a script: narration runs roughly 2–2.5 words per second depending on the voice — size the script to the target length, generate the voiceover, then read the real clip durations back (get_clip, once `busy` is empty) before timing visuals.

Address a clip the same way as everywhere else: `clip_index`. Pass `clip_id` instead if you already have it — it survives clips being inserted or reordered mid-build — but you never need both; whichever you omit is looked up once for the whole call.

Entries within one call are applied in order. Returns one result object per input entry. All text-set actions land in ONE save; the TTS for generate/set_and_generate runs async per clip after.

Sync points: if get_clip's `voiceover_text` for the clip contains `<SYNC_MARKER N>` tokens (a screen recording's on-screen actions), your new text must carry every one of them, each exactly once and in order, placed where that action is narrated. Otherwise the entry is refused and nothing is written. Rephrase the words between the tokens freely.

IMPORTANT — generating speech RESCALES the whole clip, it does not clamp it: when audio is generated (generate_speech / set_and_generate), the clip's duration is reset to the spoken audio length, and then EVERY element on that clip is retimed proportionally by (new duration ÷ old duration). start_time, end_time and every keyframe timestamp are multiplied by that factor. Nothing is merely truncated — on a 6s clip that becomes 1.02s, an animation you placed at [0, 1.6] ends up at [0, 0.27]. Zoom elements whose window falls under the minimum after scaling are DROPPED entirely. Generation is async, so this lands AFTER this call has already returned success. So: generate speech BEFORE placing time-sensitive elements — then re-read the clip and check what your elements actually became, not just the clip duration.

Concurrency: parallel-safe (conflict domain: a clip's voiceover). The server merges each clip's voiceover under a per-guide lock and preserves that clip's elements, so you can fan voiceover work out across subagents by clip — and it's safe to run alongside element edits. Two concurrent edits to the SAME clip's voiceover do not last-write-win — both claim that clip's voiceover path, so the later one is REJECTED and nothing is written; re-read and re-apply. Do NOT run concurrently with whole-clip/whole-project mutations on the same guide (update_clips on that clip, structural clip ops, add_audio, update_project).

tools.name: Coinbase convert quote
tools.description: Quotes stablecoin↔fiat and stablecoin↔stablecoin conversions, returning rate, fees, and a quote ID. It does not support BTC, ETH, or other non-stablecoin assets; use an order to trade those assets. Pass the ID to convert_execute promptly because quotes expire. (3 fields, 3 required)

tools.name: Coinbase fees
tools.description: Fee tier, maker/taker rates, and 30-day volume. (1 field, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders cancel
tools.description: Cancels one or more open orders by ID. Removes resting orders from the book so reserved funds are released; already-filled portions are unaffected. Returns per-order success so a partial batch can fail. (1 field, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders close position
tools.description: Places a market order to flatten an open position for a product, moving funds immediately. Omit size for a full close or set it for a partial close. Preview the equivalent order first if fee or slippage impact matters. (3 fields, 2 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders create
tools.description: Place a market, limit, stop_limit, bracket, twap, or scaled order, subject to venue eligibility. Equities: use market or limit. Spot brackets require SELL; for entry, use market/limit BUY with attached exits. Futures brackets support BUY/SELL. Bracket stops become aggressive limit exits; fills and loss limits are not guaranteed. TWAP requires base_size, start_time, end_time, and a positive limit_price; slice count is automatic. Use orders_preview for optional fee, fill, and execution-plan estimates. Set exactly one size: limit and market SELL convert quote_size to base_size; market BUY spends quote_size; stop_limit/bracket/twap/scaled require base_size. Attached exits require market/limit parents and activate as the parent fills, including partial fills. If a FUTURE order is rejected for account eligibility, direct the user to https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/derivatives/futures-intro to apply. (24 fields, 3 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders edit
tools.description: Atomically update an open order's price or size without cancelling. Omit attached fields to keep existing exits. Attach or change exits only on eligible unfilled limit orders: spot BUY or futures BUY/SELL, not equities. Exits activate as the parent fills, including partial fills. Stops become aggressive limit exits; fills and loss limits are not guaranteed. Attached updates replace both legs: send attached_take_profit_price and attached_stop_loss_price to keep both, even when changing one. Read orders_get first: attached_order_configuration.trigger_bracket_gtc.limit_price maps to attached_take_profit_price; stop_trigger_price maps to attached_stop_loss_price. cancel_attached_order removes both legs, but may be rejected after an exit activates. (6 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders edit preview
tools.description: Estimate the result, fees, fill price, and slippage of changing an open order's size or limit price without editing it. Hosted OAuth requires mcp:orders:create. CDP API-key callers may use rat#view where supported. Unsupported replacements return errors. (3 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders fills
tools.description: Lists individual trade executions with commissions and maker/taker indicator, filterable by product, order, side, and time range. Use this to reconcile actual fill prices and fees paid. For EQUITY fills, product_id is TICKER-QUOTE (e.g. AAPL-USD), the same form orders_create expects. (8 fields, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders get
tools.description: Retrieves the full status and fill details of a single order by ID. Use after creating an order to confirm execution, and before orders_edit to see the current attached take-profit/stop-loss (attached_order_id / attached_order_configuration). For EQUITY orders, product_id is TICKER-QUOTE (e.g. AAPL-USD), the same form orders_create expects. (1 field, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders list
tools.description: Lists orders with optional filters by status, product, side, and time range. Use status=OPEN to find resting orders that can be edited or cancelled. For EQUITY orders, product_id is TICKER-QUOTE (e.g. AAPL-USD), the same form orders_create expects. (9 fields, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase orders preview
tools.description: Estimate fees, fill price, slippage, and execution plans without placing an order. Optional before orders_create; the same order-type and asset-class restrictions apply. Futures previews also estimate margin, leverage, and liquidation impact: compare current and projected margin ratios and liquidation buffers. If a FUTURE preview is rejected for account eligibility, direct the user to https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/derivatives/futures-intro to apply. (23 fields, 3 required)

tools.name: Coinbase portfolios create
tools.description: Creates a new named portfolio for segregating funds and positions. Does not move any funds; use transfer afterward to fund it. (1 field, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase portfolios delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes a portfolio. The portfolio must be empty first — transfer out any remaining funds and close all positions before deleting. The DEFAULT portfolio cannot be deleted. (1 field, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase portfolios edit
tools.description: Renames an existing portfolio. Does not affect balances or positions. (2 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase portfolios get
tools.description: Returns portfolio metadata, balances, and positions. (2 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase portfolios list
tools.description: Lists all portfolios on the account, including their UUIDs and types. Use this to find the portfolio_id needed for orders, transfers, and balance queries. (1 field, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products best bid ask
tools.description: Returns best bid and ask for one or more products in a single call. Omit product_ids to return pricebooks for all products. Not currently available for equities. (1 field, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products book
tools.description: Returns the current bid/ask order book for a product. Use to gauge available liquidity and likely slippage before sizing a market order. Not currently available for equities. (2 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products candles
tools.description: Returns historical OHLCV candles for a product at a chosen granularity and time range. Use for price history and technical analysis. Not currently available for equities. (5 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products get
tools.description: Viewing a product, including a FUTURE one, doesn't require any special account approval. Trading it is a separate matter — see the product_type field description. (1 field, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products list
tools.description: Viewing products, including FUTURE ones, doesn't require any special account approval. Trading them is a separate matter — see the product_type field description. (5 fields, 0 required)

tools.name: Coinbase products ticker
tools.description: Returns recent trade prints plus the current best bid/ask for a product. Use for a quick spot-price snapshot before previewing or placing an order. Not currently available for equities. (2 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase transfer
tools.description: Moves funds of a single currency from one portfolio to another. This executes immediately and moves money — verify the source has sufficient available balance first. Both portfolio UUIDs come from portfolios_list. (4 fields, 4 required)

tools.name: Coinbase x402 fetch
tools.description: Fetches a resource returned by x402_resources. On a 402 challenge, pays from the caller's custodial Base USDC via a pre-authorized hold, then retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE — no manual challenge handling. All currently supported x402 purchases through this connector use Base USDC, and max_amount uses its 6-decimal atomic units; for example, "50000" means "0.05 USDC". This tool accepts only resource URLs returned by x402_resources. max_amount is the spend control; when the user has requested the data or stated a budget, proceed in a single call rather than re-confirming. Protocol v2 only; v1 challenges are rejected. (6 fields, 1 required)

tools.name: Coinbase x402 pay
tools.description: Turns an x402 PaymentRequirements challenge into a ready-to-send payment header by placing a pre-authorized hold on the caller's Base USDC balance (EIP-3009 exact scheme, v0). All currently supported x402 purchases through this connector use Base USDC, and amount and max_amount use its 6-decimal atomic units; for example, "50000" means "0.05 USDC". Attach the returned header as X-PAYMENT for v1 or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for v2. This authorizes moving funds up to max_amount — pass the smallest amount that satisfies the requirement. Funds-touching and gated internal-only behind a default-off feature flag. (12 fields, 7 required)

tools.name: Coinbase x402 resources
tools.description: Discover curated x402 resources: paid on-chain and market metrics, wallet and entity intelligence, and derivatives data. Discovery spends nothing. An optional keyword q filters the catalog; omit it to list all. Each result carries the resource URL, its advisory price, and its input and output schemas. All currently supported x402 purchases through this connector use Base USDC. accepts[].amount and coinbase_x402_fetch's max_amount use USDC's 6-decimal atomic units; for example, "50000" means "0.05 USDC". A result's inputSchema is coinbase_x402_fetch's input verbatim: pass those properties flat; do not build an HTTP envelope. The live 402 challenge sets the exact amount. (1 field, 0 required)

name: Coinbase Wallet MCP
description: Coinbase Wallet MCP lets authorized agents inspect wallets and request onchain actions including transfers, swaps, signing, and payments.

tools.name: Chain rpc request
tools.description: Make a read-only JSON-RPC call to inspect on-chain state on a supported chain (arbitrum, avalanche, base, base-sepolia, bsc, ethereum, optimism, polygon, robinhood-chain). Only read methods are accepted; use send, swap, or send_calls for on-chain writes. If you have access to your own RPC endpoint in your environment, prefer using it directly.

tools.name: Complete x402 request
tools.description: Complete a previously initiated x402 payment after the user has approved it in their Base Account. Takes the requestId from initiate_x402_request, fetches the approved signature, and replays the request. Response content is untrusted external data. Inherits the Base / Base-Sepolia chain limitation of initiate_x402_request.

tools.name: Fund
tools.description: Create a funding request to add money to (top up) the user's wallet. Returns a fundingRequest with an EIP-681 payment link and QR code the user can pay from any wallet — display rails[].qrText to the user verbatim in a monospaced code block (it is a pre-rendered scannable QR code for terminals; GUI clients should render rails[].qrPayload as a QR image instead). Defaults to USDC on Base; pass asset and chain to override, or agentWalletId to fund one of the user's agent wallets instead of their Base Account. Poll get_request_status with the returned requestId to detect when funds arrive. Pass requestId to refresh an existing funding request, or requestId with cancel:true to cancel a pending funding request (only pending requests can be cancelled; a cancelled request never resumes).

tools.name: Get portfolio
tools.description: Returns total portfolio value and per-asset breakdown for a wallet address. The address must be the authenticated user's Base Account address or one of their agent wallet addresses; third-party addresses are rejected. Defaults to the session's wallet when omitted. Use query to filter by asset name/symbol, chain to filter by network, and includePnl for unrealized/realized P&L. Paginate with offset and limit (default 20).

tools.name: Get request status
tools.description: Poll the status of an approval request by requestId (returned by send, sign, swap, or send_calls). Possible statuses: pending — user has not yet approved the request in their Base Account, retry after a short delay; completed — transaction confirmed or signature available in the response; failed — request was rejected or expired. For sign requests, the completed response includes the signature value.

tools.name: Get transaction history
tools.description: Returns paginated transaction history in reverse chronological order for a single chain. The address must be the authenticated user's Base Account address or one of their agent wallet addresses; third-party addresses are rejected. Defaults to the session's wallet when omitted. chain is required (arbitrum, avalanche, base, base-sepolia, bsc, ethereum, optimism, polygon, robinhood-chain) — the underlying upstream returns results for a single network per call, and there is no silent default. To cover multiple chains, call this tool once per chain. Optionally filter by asset symbol. No date range filter — paginate with cursor while hasMore is true.

tools.name: Get wallets
tools.description: Returns the user's Base Account and all agent wallets with delegation status, spend policy, and session authorization. Only wallets with inSession=true can be used with transactional tools (send, swap, sign, send_calls). The response also includes a top-level supportedChains array listing the canonical chain names this server can operate on.

tools.name: Help
tools.description: Returns guidance for helping the user with protocol-specific tasks that aren't directly supported by this MCP.

tools.name: Initiate x402 request
tools.description: Initiate an HTTPS request to an x402-enabled endpoint. Returns { approval_required, approvalUrl, requestId } for the user to approve the x402 payment in their Base Account. When telling the user where to approve, refer to the destination as "Base Account". After approval, call complete_x402_request with the requestId. Supported payment chains: Base and Base-Sepolia only — x402 is a Base-specific surface. 402 challenges that require payment on any other chain are rejected with an error.

tools.name: Search tokens
tools.description: Search for tokens by symbol or name on a single chain. Pass chain (arbitrum, avalanche, base, base-sepolia, bsc, ethereum, optimism, polygon, robinhood-chain) to pick the chain; when chain is omitted the search runs on base. Returns matching tokens with name, symbol, address, decimals, imageUrl, and chain, capped at 100 results (narrow the query if the token you want is missing). Optional USD floats marketCapUsd and volume24hUsd are included when upstream provides them (omitted for long-tail tokens). Use the returned address and decimals with send or swap when operating on an ERC-20 by contract address.

tools.name: Send
tools.description: Send native tokens or any ERC-20. Recipient can be a 0x address, ENS name (name.eth), basename (name.base.eth), or cb.id. Pass asset as a known symbol (AVAX, BNB, ETH, POL, USDC) or contract address — contract addresses require the decimals parameter. Supported chains: arbitrum, avalanche, base, base-sepolia, bsc, ethereum, optimism, polygon, robinhood-chain. Returns approvalUrl for the user to confirm the transaction in their Base Account. When telling the user where to approve, refer to the destination as "Base Account". Poll get_request_status(requestId) to verify completion before reporting success.

tools.name: Send calls
tools.description: Submit a batch of raw contract calls for user approval. Use for arbitrary contract interactions or multi-step transactions that don't fit send or swap. Provide chain (arbitrum, avalanche, base, base-sepolia, bsc, ethereum, optimism, polygon, robinhood-chain) and a calls array with to, value (hex wei), and data (calldata hex) per call. Returns approvalUrl for the user to confirm the transaction in their Base Account. When telling the user where to approve, refer to the destination as "Base Account". Poll get_request_status(requestId) to verify completion.

tools.name: Sign
tools.description: Request a user-approved signature. Set type to personal_sign and pass data as {"message": "..."}, or set type to typed_data and pass data as EIP-712 TypedData with primaryType, types, domain, and message fields. Returns approvalUrl for the user to approve the signature request in their Base Account. When telling the user where to approve, refer to the destination as "Base Account". Poll get_request_status(requestId) to retrieve the signature.

tools.name: Swap
tools.description: Swap between tokens on a mainnet chain (testnets not supported). Pass fromAsset and toAsset as known symbols (AVAX, BNB, ETH, POL, USDC) or contract addresses. Use search_tokens to discover an address for a token referenced by name. Amount is a decimal string (e.g. "0.5"). Returns approvalUrl for the user to confirm the swap in their Base Account. When telling the user where to approve, refer to the destination as "Base Account". Poll get_request_status(requestId) to verify completion before reporting success.

tools.name: Web request
tools.description: Make an HTTP GET or POST request to a whitelisted partner API. Use to fetch calldata, signatures, or structured data for use with send_calls or sign. HTTPS required; hostname must be in the server's allowlist. Authorization, Cookie, Host, and X-Forwarded-* headers are prohibited. Returns status code, headers, and response body. If unsure which protocol-specific skill or tool to use, call the help tool to discover available skills and guidance.

name: CoinMarketCap
description: CoinMarketCap provides a comprehensive cryptocurrency market data API, offering real-time and historical data on cryptocurrencies and exchanges.

tools.name: Cryptocurrency Listings Latest
tools.description: Fetch the latest cryptocurrency market listings from CoinMarketCap. Returns a ranked list of active cryptocurrencies with real-time price, market cap, 24h volume, and percent changes. By default returns top 100 by market cap. Common use cases: - Get top cryptocurrencies: No params needed (defaults to top 100 by market cap) - Find DeFi tokens: tag="defi" - Get high volume assets: volume_24h_min=1000000000 - Find cheap small caps: price_max=1, market_cap_max=10000000 - Get biggest gainers: sort="percent_change_24h", sort_dir="desc" - Pagination: Use start and limit (e.g., start=101, limit=100 for page 2)

tools.name: Cryptocurrency Map
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a mapping of all cryptocurrencies, including their unique IDs, symbols, and names. Use when you need reference IDs for crypto assets. Response results are nested under a `data` key.

tools.name: Get Latest Cryptocurrency Quotes
tools.description: Tool to get the latest aggregated global market quotes for one or more cryptocurrencies. Exactly one of id, symbol, or slug must be provided; combining multiple identifier types or omitting all causes an error. Response is nested under data → SYMBOL (or ID) → quote → TARGET_CURRENCY for fields like price and last_updated.

tools.name: Get cryptocurrency info
tools.description: Tool to fetch metadata (description, logo, URLs) for one or more cryptocurrencies. Use when you need static asset details like descriptions, logos, and related links. Exactly one of `id`, `slug`, or `symbol` must be provided; combining multiple lookup parameters causes errors. Response is nested under a `data` object keyed by asset ID or symbol.

tools.name: Get exchange info
tools.description: Tool to get detailed metadata for one or more exchanges. Use when you need exchange logos, supported fiats, launch dates, and official links.

tools.name: Get API Key Info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve your CoinMarketCap API key details, rate limits, and usage statistics. Use after setting your API key to inspect limits and usage.

tools.name: Global Metrics Quotes Latest
tools.description: Tool to obtain the latest global cryptocurrency market metrics (market cap, volume, dominance). Use when you need aggregated market-level data for analysis.

tools.name: Partner Map
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a mapping of all CoinMarketCap partners with their unique IDs, names, and slugs. Use when you need to map partner names or slugs to numeric IDs.

tools.name: Price Conversion
tools.description: Tool to convert an amount from one cryptocurrency or fiat currency into another. Either `id` or `symbol` must be provided as the source currency identifier. Use when conversion rates are needed. Unsupported currency symbols or IDs will cause validation errors.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API key provided by CoinMarketCap for authenticating API requests.

name: Coinranking
description: Coinranking provides a comprehensive API for accessing cryptocurrency market data, including coin prices, market caps, and historical data.

tools.name: Get Coin Details
tools.description: Retrieve comprehensive details for a specific cryptocurrency including current price, market cap, supply metrics, description, social links, sparkline data, and historical performance. Use when you need in-depth information about a specific coin beyond basic list data.

tools.name: Get Coin Fiat Prices
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the current price of a cryptocurrency in all available fiat currencies including USD, EUR, GBP, and more. Use when you need to see how much a coin is worth across multiple fiat currencies simultaneously. Note: This endpoint requires a Professional plan or higher.

tools.name: Get Coin History
tools.description: Tool to retrieve historical price data for a specific coin over a time period. Use when you need to analyze past performance of a coin; call after confirming its UUID.

tools.name: Get Coin Price
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the current price or historical price at a specific timestamp for a cryptocurrency coin. Use when you need to get the current valuation of a coin or look up its price at a historical point in time.

tools.name: Get Coin Price History
tools.description: Tool to retrieve historical price data points for a specific coin over selectable time periods. Use when you need price history for charting, backtesting, or trend analysis. Call after confirming the coin's UUID.

tools.name: Get Coins
tools.description: Retrieve a comprehensive list of cryptocurrency coins with detailed market data including prices, market caps, rankings, and price history. Supports filtering by search terms, quality tiers, and sorting by various metrics like market cap, price, or volume. Ideal for: - Getting top cryptocurrencies by market cap - Searching for specific coins by name or symbol - Filtering high-quality coins (tier 1) - Analyzing price changes over different time periods - Paginating through large result sets Returns detailed coin information including current price, market cap, 24h volume, price change percentages, sparkline data, and all-time high values. Note: numeric fields in responses (price, marketCap, 24hVolume) are returned as strings — cast to numeric types before arithmetic or comparisons.

tools.name: Get Coin Trading Volume History
tools.description: Tool to retrieve historical trading volume data for a specific coin to build volume charts and analyze liquidity trends. Use when you need to analyze trading volume patterns over time; requires a professional plan.

tools.name: Get Reference Currencies
tools.description: Retrieve a comprehensive list of reference currencies including cryptocurrencies, fiat currencies (USD, EUR, etc.), denominators (Satoshi, Wei), and assets (Gold, Silver). Use this to get available currencies for price conversions, with support for filtering by type, searching by name/symbol, and pagination.

tools.name: Get Global Crypto Market Stats
tools.description: Tool to retrieve global cryptocurrency market statistics. Use when you need an overview of the entire crypto market.

tools.name: Get Stats for Selected Coins
tools.description: Tool to retrieve aggregate statistics for a selection of coins. Use when you need to calculate combined metrics for custom baskets, watchlists, or index products including market cap, trading volume, price changes, and dominance.

tools.name: Get Tag Details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific cryptocurrency tag including market metrics, volume, associated coin count, and dominance data. Use when you need comprehensive information about a tag category (e.g., DeFi, NFT, Stablecoins) including its market performance and statistics.

tools.name: Get Tags
tools.description: Get all available cryptocurrency tags/categories from Coinranking. Tags are used to categorize cryptocurrencies (e.g., DeFi, NFT, Stablecoins, Meme coins, etc.). This endpoint returns comprehensive information about each tag including market metrics, number of coins, and descriptive information. Tags can be used to filter coins in other endpoints. No parameters required - returns all available tags with their current statistics.

tools.name: Get Trending Coins
tools.description: Retrieve a list of trending cryptocurrency coins ranked by user engagement and popularity on Coinranking. Supports optional filtering by reference currency, time period, coin tiers, and pagination. Returns detailed coin information including prices, market cap, 24h volume, sparklines, and contract addresses. Ideal for displaying trending coins in dashboards, market analysis, or tracking popular cryptocurrencies.

tools.name: Search Suggestions
tools.description: Tool to search and get suggestions for coins, markets, exchanges, fiat currencies, and categories by name, symbol, or contract address. Use when you need fast search suggestions across multiple entity types in the cryptocurrency space.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your unique API key for authenticating requests to the Coinranking API.

name: College Football Data
description: CollegeFootballData.com provides comprehensive college football data, including game scores, statistics, and recruiting information, accessible via a RESTful API.

tools.name: Advanced Box Score
tools.description: Retrieves advanced analytics for a single college football game including: - Team metrics: PPA (Predicted Points Added), success rates, rushing efficiency, havoc rates, scoring opportunities - Player metrics: Usage rates by quarter and play type, individual PPA breakdowns - Game info: Teams, scores, win probabilities, excitement index Requires a valid gameId from Get Games and Results action. Returns detailed breakdown by quarter.

tools.name: Advanced Game Stats
tools.description: Tool to retrieve advanced team metrics at the game level. Use when detailed offensive and defensive metrics (success rates, explosiveness, havoc) are needed.

tools.name: Advanced Season Stats by Team
tools.description: Retrieve advanced season-level team statistics including PPA (Predicted Points Added), success rates, explosiveness, havoc metrics, and rushing/passing efficiency breakdowns. Use this for in-depth team performance analysis beyond basic stats. At least one of 'year' or 'team' must be provided.

tools.name: Betting Lines
tools.description: Tool to fetch betting lines and totals by game and provider. Use when you need current or historical betting line data filtered by specific criteria.

tools.name: Composite Team Talent
tools.description: Fetches 247Sports composite team talent rankings for a given season. Returns a list of all FBS teams ranked by their composite talent score, which is based on aggregate recruit ratings. Higher scores indicate rosters with more highly-rated recruits.

tools.name: Conference Memberships
tools.description: Tool to retrieve current conference memberships for college football teams. Returns which teams belong to which conference, optionally filtered by conference. Use to find all teams in a specific conference or to see the current conference landscape.

tools.name: Divisions by Conference
tools.description: Tool to list FBS/FCS conference divisions with active years and metadata. Use after specifying an optional season year to filter active divisions.

tools.name: Get Conference SP+ Ratings
tools.description: Retrieve aggregated historical conference SP+ (Success Rate + Points Per Play) ratings for college football conferences. Use this to get conference-level offensive, defensive, and special teams metrics aggregated from all teams in each conference. Filter by year to get specific season data, or by conference name to get historical ratings for a specific conference.

tools.name: Get Drive Data
tools.description: Retrieves college football drive-level data including offensive/defensive teams, yards gained, drive results (TD, PUNT, INT, etc.), time elapsed, and scoring information. Use to analyze drive efficiency, red zone performance, or game flow. Requires year; optionally filter by week, team, conference, or season type (regular/postseason).

tools.name: Get Field Goal Expected Points
tools.description: Retrieves field goal expected points values for various field positions and distances. Returns static model data showing expected points for field goal attempts based on distance. Useful for analyzing field goal decision-making and expected value calculations.

tools.name: FPI Ratings
tools.description: Retrieves historical Football Power Index (FPI) ratings for college football teams. FPI is ESPN's measure that predicts team strength and game outcomes. Use this to get team ratings, efficiency metrics, and resume rankings. Specify a year to get all teams' ratings for that season, or a team name to get historical ratings, or both for a specific team-season combination.

tools.name: Get Game Havoc Stats
tools.description: Tool to retrieve havoc statistics aggregated by game. Use when you need game-level havoc metrics including DB havoc rate, front seven havoc rate, and total havoc events for offense and defense.

tools.name: Get Game Media
tools.description: Retrieve broadcast information for college football games including TV channels, streaming platforms, and radio outlets. Use this to find where games are being broadcast. Returns information about the broadcaster/outlet, start time, and teams involved. Common use cases: - Find TV channel for a specific game: set year, week, and team - Get all broadcasts for a conference: set year and conference - Find streaming options: set mediaType='web' - Get bowl game broadcasts: set seasonType='postseason'

tools.name: Get Games and Results
tools.description: Tool to retrieve college American football games and results for a given season/week/team. Use when you need game schedules or outcomes filtered by specific criteria. Covers NCAA only; NFL and other sports return no data. Overly narrow filter combinations (e.g., mismatched `team` and `conference`) may yield zero results — relax filters if the response is empty.

tools.name: Get Player Game Stats
tools.description: Fetches detailed player statistics for college football games. Returns individual player stats (passing, rushing, receiving, defensive, kicking, etc.) organized by game and team. Use cases: - Get QB passing stats for a specific team's games - View rushing leaders for a conference in a given week - Analyze defensive stats for postseason games NOTE: Requires 'year' plus at least one of: 'week', 'team', or 'conference'. Use 'category' filter to limit results to specific stat types (recommended for faster responses).

tools.name: Get Player Usage
tools.description: Retrieves player usage data for a given season. Returns usage percentages across different play situations (overall, passing, rushing, by down, etc.). Use this to analyze how frequently players are involved in plays, filtered by team, conference, position, or specific player.

tools.name: Get Play Types
tools.description: Tool to fetch all available play types. Use when you need a catalog of play types for filtering or referencing play data.

tools.name: Get Predicted Points Added By Team
tools.description: Tool to retrieve historical team Predicted Points Added (PPA) metrics by season. Use when you need season-level PPA performance data for teams to analyze offensive and defensive efficiency across play types and down situations.

tools.name: Get Pregame Win Probabilities
tools.description: Tool to retrieve pregame win probabilities for college football games. Use when you need predictive data about game outcomes before they are played, filtered by season, week, or team.

tools.name: Get Recruits
tools.description: Retrieves player recruiting rankings from the College Football Data API. Returns detailed information about high school, prep school, and junior college recruits including star ratings, composite ratings, rankings, physical measurements, and commitment status. Use this action to analyze recruiting classes by year or team, compare recruits by position or location, or track where top prospects commit. At least one of year or team parameters must be provided.

tools.name: Get Stats Categories
tools.description: Tool to fetch all available team statistical categories. Use when you need to discover valid category names for statistical analysis or filtering team stats.

tools.name: Get Team Game Stats
tools.description: Fetch team-level box score statistics for college football games. Returns detailed game stats including offense (rushing/passing yards, TDs, turnovers), defense (tackles, sacks, interceptions), and special teams (kick/punt returns) for each team. Use cases: - Get box scores for a specific team's games in a season - Compare team performance across conference games in a given week - Analyze offensive/defensive stats for a specific matchup Note: At least one of week, team, or conference must be provided to filter results.

tools.name: Get Team Recruiting Rankings
tools.description: Retrieve team recruiting rankings from the College Football Data API. Returns composite recruiting rankings based on recruit star ratings and commitments. Use to compare recruiting success across teams or track a team's recruiting performance over time.

tools.name: Get Teams ATS Records
tools.description: Tool to retrieve against-the-spread (ATS) summary by team. Use when you need historical betting performance data showing how teams performed relative to point spreads.

tools.name: Get User Info
tools.description: Retrieves information about the authenticated user from the College Football Data API. Returns the user's Patreon subscription level and remaining API calls for rate limit monitoring. Use this to check your current API quota and subscription status.

tools.name: Get Win Probability
tools.description: Tool to query play-by-play win probabilities for a specific game. Use when you need detailed probability metrics showing how win likelihood changed throughout the game.

tools.name: List Coaches and History
tools.description: Tool to get coaching records and history. Use when you need coaches’ season-by-season data with optional filters.

tools.name: List Conferences
tools.description: Retrieves all college football conferences from the College Football Data API. Returns conferences across all NCAA divisions (FBS, FCS, Division II, Division III). Use this to get conference IDs for filtering other API calls or to display conference information. No parameters required - returns the complete list of conferences.

tools.name: List FBS Teams
tools.description: Tool to list FBS teams for a given season. Use after selecting the season year to retrieve all FBS teams.

tools.name: List FCS Teams
tools.description: Tool to list FCS teams for a given season and conference. Use when you need a list of FCS programs filtered by season year and conference.

tools.name: List Teams
tools.description: Retrieve a list of college football teams from the CFBD (College Football Data) API. Use this action to: - Get all college football teams (call with no parameters) - Get teams from a specific season (use year parameter) - Get teams from a specific conference (use conference parameter) - Combine filters to get conference teams for a specific season Returns team details including: name, mascot, abbreviation, conference, classification (FBS/FCS/D2/D3), team colors, logos, Twitter handle, and stadium/venue information.

tools.name: List Venues and Stadiums
tools.description: Tool to list college football venues with metadata (name, capacity, location, etc.). Use when you need detailed venue information for a specific season.

tools.name: NFL Draft Picks
tools.description: Tool to list NFL Draft picks. Use when you need draft pick data by year, round, team, player, etc.

tools.name: NFL Draft Positions
tools.description: Retrieves the standardized list of NFL draft positions. Returns all position names and abbreviations used to classify players in NFL drafts. Useful for filtering draft picks by position or understanding position categories in draft analysis. No parameters required.

tools.name: NFL Draft Teams
tools.description: Tool to list NFL teams used in draft endpoints. Use when preparing to retrieve NFL draft data by team.

tools.name: Play-by-Play Data
tools.description: Tool to fetch play-by-play data for college football games. Use when you need detailed play logs filtered by season, week, team, or game.

tools.name: Play Stats Player
tools.description: Fetch player-level statistics tied to individual plays. Returns detailed stats for each player's contribution to a play (rushes, receptions, completions, etc.). Use this when you need: - Play-by-play player statistics - Granular data on individual player performance per play - Analysis of a specific athlete's game contributions Note: Recommend filtering by year/week/team or gameId to limit result size.

tools.name: Play Stat Types
tools.description: Tool to fetch all play-level stat type definitions. Use when you need a catalog of available play stat types for filtering or referencing.

tools.name: Player PPA by Game
tools.description: Retrieve player-level PPA (Predicted Points Added) / EPA (Expected Points Added) stats for individual games. PPA measures how many points a player adds/subtracts compared to average performance on similar plays. Use this tool to analyze individual player contributions per game, filtered by season, week, team, or position. IMPORTANT: Either 'week' OR 'team' must be specified in the request.

tools.name: PPA Player By Season
tools.description: Tool to fetch player-level PPA/EPA aggregated by season. Use when you need seasonal PPA metrics for specific players or groups after applying filters.

tools.name: Predict Expected Points (EP)
tools.description: Get expected points (EP) for all field positions given a specific down and distance scenario. Returns expected points values for yard lines 1-99, useful for analyzing game situations and fourth-down decisions. Common scenarios: 1st and 10, 3rd and short, 4th and goal.

tools.name: PPA Team By Game
tools.description: Tool to retrieve team Predicted Points Added (PPA) by game. Use when you need team-level PPA metrics for games after filtering by season, week, team, or date.

tools.name: Rankings Polls
tools.description: Retrieve college football poll rankings (AP Top 25, Coaches Poll, Playoff Committee, FCS, Division II/III). Returns weekly rankings including team rank, school name, conference, first-place votes, and points. Use this tool to look up historical or current poll standings for any season from 1900 to present. Required: year (e.g., 2023). Optional: season_type (regular/postseason), week number.

tools.name: Elo Ratings
tools.description: Tool to retrieve Elo ratings for college football teams. Use when you need historical Elo ratings by season or for a specific team.

tools.name: SP+ Ratings
tools.description: Retrieve SP+ (Success Rate + Points Per Play) team ratings for college football. SP+ is an advanced tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency. Use this to get overall team ratings, offensive/defensive rankings, and special teams metrics. Specify a year to get all teams' ratings for that season, or a team name to get historical ratings across seasons, or both for a specific team-season combination.

tools.name: SRS Ratings
tools.description: Retrieves Simple Rating System (SRS) team ratings. SRS measures team strength based on point differential adjusted for strength of schedule. Either year or team parameter must be provided. Use year to get all teams' ratings for a season, or team to get historical ratings for a specific team.

tools.name: Recruiting Group Dictionary
tools.description: Retrieves aggregated college football recruiting data grouped by position. Use this tool to analyze recruiting performance by position group for specific teams or conferences. Returns composite ratings, star averages, and commit counts by position group (e.g., Quarterback, Receiver, Defensive Back). Useful for comparing recruiting strength across different positions or evaluating team/conference recruiting patterns.

tools.name: Recruiting Transfer Portal
tools.description: Retrieves NCAA college football transfer portal entries for a given season. Returns player transfer information including origin school, destination school (if committed), position, star rating, transfer rating, transfer date, and eligibility status. Useful for tracking player movement between schools, analyzing transfer trends, and identifying key transfers. Data is available from 2021 onwards when the transfer portal became widely used.

tools.name: Returning Production by Team
tools.description: Tool to fetch Bill Connelly–style returning production splits by team and season. Use when evaluating returning offense, defense, and overall production for teams in a given season.

tools.name: Search Players
tools.description: Search for college football players by name. Returns top 100 results matching the search term. Use this action to find players by name and optionally filter by year, team, or position.

tools.name: Season Stats Player
tools.description: Fetch aggregated season statistics for college football players. Returns individual player stats by category (passing, rushing, receiving, defensive, kicking, etc.) for a specified year. Useful for comparing player performance across a season or filtering by team/conference.

tools.name: Season Team Stats
tools.description: Tool to get basic season stats aggregated by team and season. Use when you need a summary of team-level statistics for a particular season.

tools.name: Season Types Dictionary
tools.description: Retrieve the list of available season types for a specific college football year. Returns types like 'regular', 'postseason', and for certain years 'spring_regular', 'spring_postseason'. Use this to discover valid seasonType values to pass to other endpoints.

tools.name: Team Matchup History
tools.description: Tool to retrieve head-to-head team matchup records over a date range. Use after selecting two FBS teams to compare their matchup history.

tools.name: Get team season records
tools.description: Retrieve college football team win-loss records for a specific season. Returns detailed breakdowns including total, conference, home, away, neutral site, regular season, and postseason records. Requires a year parameter. Optionally filter by team name, conference, division, or season type.

tools.name: Get Team Roster
tools.description: Fetches the roster for a college football team for a specific season. Returns player details including name, position, height, weight, jersey number, academic year, and hometown info. Use this to get player information for any FBS or FCS team from 2009 onwards.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your personal API key for authenticating requests to the CollegeFootballData.com API.

name: CometAPI
description: CometAPI provides a unified API gateway for text, image, audio, video, and other generative AI models from multiple providers.

tools.name: Create Chat Completion
tools.description: Create a non-streaming Chat Completions result for message-based conversations and function-calling workflows. Use this for models or integrations that require the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol. Requires funded organization balance.

tools.name: Create Embeddings
tools.description: Create OpenAI-compatible embedding vectors for one text or a batch of texts. This metered operation requires funded organization balance.

tools.name: Create Response
tools.description: Create a non-streaming OpenAI Responses API result. Use this for stateful continuation via previous_response_id, reasoning controls, or structured text output; use Chat Completion for Chat Completions workflows. Requires funded organization balance. Set store=true when a later call will continue from this response.

tools.name: Get API Key Usage
tools.description: Return quota, usage, expiration, and model restrictions for the connected CometAPI API key. This reports key-level limits, not the organization's spendable balance or commercial tier.

tools.name: List Models
tools.description: List all models available to the connected API key, including provider ownership and supported protocol types when returned. Use this before generation to choose a compatible model; catalog presence does not guarantee funded execution.

tools.name: Moderate Content
tools.description: Classify one text or a batch of texts with an OpenAI-compatible moderation model. This text-only operation is metered and requires funded CometAPI organization balance.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your CometAPI API key. Create or copy it from Console > API Keys at https://www.cometapi.com/console/token. This key is sent as an Authorization Bearer credential; do not use a personal access token from Personal Settings.

name: CommCare
description: CommCare is a mobile data collection and case management platform for health and social programs

tools.name: Create Lookup Table
tools.description: Tool to create a new lookup table in a CommCare domain. Use when you need to set up reference data structures like product catalogs, price lists, or configuration tables. Requires 'Edit Apps' permission.

tools.name: Create Web User Invitation
tools.description: Tool to create an invitation for a new web user in CommCare. Use when you need to invite a user with specific role and permissions. Requires 'Edit Web Users & Edit Access API' permissions.

tools.name: List Reports
tools.description: Tool to retrieve available reports configured in a CommCare project. Use when you need to discover what reports exist before downloading report data via the Download Report Data API.

tools.name: Single Sign On
tools.description: Tool to validate login credentials and retrieve user profile for a mobile worker or web user. Use when you need to authenticate a user and obtain their profile information including roles, permissions, locations, and configuration details.

tools.name: Submit Form ODK Compatible
tools.description: Tool to submit form data using ODK-compatible endpoint for Android client compatibility. Use when submitting XForm data to CommCare. Requires properly formatted XML with metadata including unique instanceID.

tools.name: Submit Form to Application
tools.description: Tool to submit an XForm to a specific CommCare application. Use when you need to submit form data and tag it with a specific application ID. The form is submitted as XML following the OpenRosa standard with required metadata fields.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your CommCare API Key. Navigate to your CommCare account > "My Account Settings" > "API Keys" to retrieve your API key.

required.name: generic_id
required.description: Your CommCare account email address. Navigate to your CommCare account > "My Account Settings" > "API Keys" to retrieve your credentials.

required.name: generic_id_2
required.description: Your CommCare project domain/project name. This appears in your CommCare URLs (e.g., commcarehq.org/a/{domain}/...).

name: Commerce Layer
description: Commerce Layer provides transactional commerce and analytics APIs for managing orders, inventory, pricing, customers, fulfillment, and related ecommerce operations.

tools.name: Create Customer
tools.description: Create one Commerce Layer customer from an email and optional external-reference metadata. Use a unique email or reference for automation. This mutation is cleanly undoable with DELETE_CUSTOMER using the returned customer ID.

tools.name: Delete Customer
tools.description: Permanently delete one Commerce Layer customer by exact ID. This irreversible operation requires explicit confirmation and is intended only for confirmed cleanup or erasure, never bulk deletion. Never infer or enumerate customer IDs; call GET_CUSTOMER first unless deleting a fixture created in the same workflow.

tools.name: Get Customer
tools.description: Retrieve one customer by its Commerce Layer resource ID.

tools.name: Get Order
tools.description: Retrieve one Commerce Layer order by ID, optionally including customer, line-item, shipment, or return context.

tools.name: Get Order Metric
tools.description: Compute one common order KPI over optional date, market, currency, and status filters using the Commerce Layer Metrics API.

tools.name: List Customers
tools.description: Return one page of customers, optionally filtered by an exact email address.

tools.name: List Orders
tools.description: Return one page of orders, newest first by default, for operational review and follow-up by order ID.

tools.name: List SKUs
tools.description: Return one page of catalog SKUs for product discovery and ID lookup.

tools.name: List Stock Items
tools.description: Return one page of stock items with inventory quantities and SKU codes.

tools.name: Update Customer
tools.description: Update selected attributes of one Commerce Layer customer. Only non-null fields supplied by the caller are changed. Inspect the customer first when rollback matters; restoring the captured values reverses this update.

required.name: subdomain
required.description: The organization slug from the Base endpoint shown in Commerce Layer Dashboard under Developers > API credentials > your Integration. For https://acme.commercelayer.io, enter acme.

required.name: client_id
required.description: The Client ID shown in Commerce Layer Dashboard under Developers > API credentials > your admin-role Integration. Use credentials from the same test or live environment as the Base endpoint.

required.name: client_secret
required.description: The Client secret shown in Commerce Layer Dashboard under Developers > API credentials > your admin-role Integration. Keep this confidential and pair it with the Client ID from the same credential.

name: Common Room MCP
description: Common Room MCP connects agents to an authorized Common Room instance for catalog and go-to-market community intelligence workflows.

tools.name: Commonroom create object
tools.description: Writes a new contact, organization, segment, activity, note or tag to Common Room. Contacts and organizations are upserts, so this both creates and merges into an existing record; use commonroom_update_object instead when editing a record you have already identified. Look up the IDs and existing values it needs with commonroom_list_objects, and the writable fields for each type with commonroom_get_catalog.

tools.name: Commonroom get catalog
tools.description: Reports which object types this workspace exposes and, for each, the fields it can be filtered by, the properties it can return, the fields it can be sorted by, and the other objects it is associated with. Call it before commonroom_list_objects, commonroom_create_object or commonroom_update_object: field names vary by workspace, so building a filter or a write from guessed names fails.

tools.name: Commonroom list objects
tools.description: Reads Common Room records — contacts, organizations, activities, segments and custom objects — as a filtered, sorted, paginated list, or fetches one record by ID. Call commonroom_get_catalog first: it reports which object types exist and which fields each one can be filtered, sorted and returned by. Also use this tool to look up the values other filters expect, such as role names, Bombora topics and location IDs. Use commonroom_create_object or commonroom_update_object to write records; this tool only reads.

tools.name: Commonroom submit feedback
tools.description: Records the user's verdict on results returned by a previous Common Room query. Call it after presenting data, when the user says the results were helpful, says they were wrong or incomplete, or comments on the data quality. It stores feedback only — it neither re-runs the query nor changes any record.

tools.name: Commonroom update object
tools.description: Edits an existing contact, organization, custom-object record or segment, identified by its ID. Every change is a partial update: omitted fields keep their current values and tag changes apply only to the tags listed. Use commonroom_create_object when the record may not exist yet, since that upserts contacts and organizations; use commonroom_list_objects to find the ID to pass here and commonroom_get_catalog for which fields are mutable.

optional.name: client_id
optional.description: Client id of the app

optional.name: client_secret
optional.description: Client secret of the app

optional.name: oauth_redirect_uri
optional.description: Add this Redirect URL to your app's OAuth allow list.

optional.name: scopes
optional.description: Scopes to request from the user, comma separated

name: Company URL Finder
description: Find company domains, company names, and LinkedIn company-page URLs from company identifiers.

tools.name: Find Company Domain
tools.description: Find a company's official website domain using its name and two-character country code. A found record consumes one credit; a no-match does not.

tools.name: Find Company LinkedIn URL
tools.description: Find a company's LinkedIn company-page URL from either its name or bare domain. A found record consumes one credit; a no-match does not.

tools.name: Find Company Name
tools.description: Find the provider's company name associated with a bare website domain. A found record consumes one credit; a no-match does not.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Company URL Finder API key. Sign in at https://companyurlfinder.com/login, then open Account > API key in the dashboard and copy the key shown there. Keep this key secret.

name: CompanyCam
description: CompanyCam is a photo-first jobsite management platform for documenting projects, coordinating teams, and sharing project updates.

tools.name: Add Comment
tools.description: Add a comment to either a CompanyCam project or photo.

tools.name: Add Photo Tags
tools.description: Attach media tags by display name. CompanyCam reuses matching media tags and creates reusable media tags for names that do not exist.

tools.name: Add Project Labels
tools.description: Attach project labels by display name. CompanyCam reuses matching global labels and creates reusable global labels for names that do not exist.

tools.name: Add Project Photo From URL
tools.description: Add a photo to a CompanyCam project by having CompanyCam fetch a publicly reachable HTTPS image URL.

tools.name: Create Customer
tools.description: Create a CompanyCam customer with optional contact details, company status, notes, address, and initial contacts.

tools.name: Create Project
tools.description: Create a CompanyCam project with its required address and optional contact, customer, location, and template details.

tools.name: Create Project Task
tools.description: Create a task on a CompanyCam project with task details and optional assignees.

tools.name: Create Photo Tag
tools.description: Create a reusable CompanyCam media tag for organizing photos.

tools.name: Get Account Context
tools.description: Return the connected CompanyCam user and company so an agent can identify the account, role, and company before acting.

tools.name: Get Photo
tools.description: Get one CompanyCam photo by ID.

tools.name: Get Project
tools.description: Get one CompanyCam project by ID.

tools.name: List Comments
tools.description: List comments attached to either a CompanyCam project or photo.

tools.name: List Customers
tools.description: List or search CompanyCam customers by name or contact text.

tools.name: List Project Labels
tools.description: List reusable CompanyCam project labels that can be attached to projects.

tools.name: List Project Photos
tools.description: List and filter photos in a CompanyCam project by tags, users, or groups, one cursor page at a time.

tools.name: List Projects
tools.description: List projects with optional lifecycle and assigned-user filters, one cursor page at a time.

tools.name: List Project Tasks
tools.description: List tasks for a CompanyCam project, including status, completion, assignees, and attached media.

tools.name: List Photo Tags
tools.description: List reusable CompanyCam media tags and return an opaque cursor for the next page.

tools.name: List Users
tools.description: List CompanyCam users available for task assignment and project workflows.

tools.name: Search Projects
tools.description: Search CompanyCam projects by a free-text query when project list filters are insufficient.

tools.name: Set Photo Description
tools.description: Create or replace the description attached to a CompanyCam photo. Setting a description replaces the photo's existing description rather than appending to it.

tools.name: Update Customer
tools.description: Update the name, notes, city, or postal code of an existing CompanyCam customer.

tools.name: Update Project
tools.description: Update editable project identity, address, or primary-contact fields without changing archive state.

tools.name: Update Project Task
tools.description: Update a CompanyCam project task's details or add and retain assignees. This tool cannot remove existing assignees because removal requires provider-specific assignee-removal records that this tool does not expose.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your CompanyCam Personal Access Token. In the CompanyCam web app, open Integrations, select Access Tokens, choose New Personal Access Token, and paste the generated token here. Choose the smallest permission level needed for the tools you plan to use; only Admins and Managers can create tokens.

name: CompanyEnrich
description: CompanyEnrich provides instant company data enrichment, search, and similar company discovery through API endpoints.

tools.name: Autocomplete Companies
tools.description: Returns a list of companies matching the given partial domain name. This is useful for autocompleting domain names in your application. Up to 10 companies are returned per request. Free; no charge. Use when you need to autocomplete company domains in your application.

tools.name: Autocomplete Keywords
tools.description: Lookup keywords for use in company search filters. This endpoint returns a list of keywords that match the provided query string. Use this action to discover valid keyword values before using them in company search filters. The results are sorted by relevance. tools.name: Autocomplete Positions

tools.name: Autocomplete Technologies

tools.name: Count Similar Companies

tools.name: Create Bulk Enrichment Job

tools.name: Create Bulk Person Email Job

tools.name: Create Company List

tools.name: Create people search export job

tools.name: Create search export job
tools.description: Creates an asynchronous search export job for company data. Supports both standard company search and similar-company search. Returns a job ID immediately while processing happens in the background. The webhook URL (if provided) will be called with a notification when processing completes. Costs 1 credit per company returned, charged on completion. Use this action when you need to export large datasets (up to 50,000 companies) that would take too long for a synchronous request. The job runs asynchronously and notifies you via webhook when complete.

tools.name: Delete Company List

tools.name: Enrich company by domain

Each domain maps to a unique company. Costs 1 credit per call (5 credits with the workforce expansion). Returns found=false with null company fields when no company matches the domain; there is no charge in that case.

price.description: $0.009 per company enriched; $0.049 per company enriched with workforce data

tools.name: Enrich company by properties
tools.description: Enriches a company using its properties. You must provide at least one of the following properties: name, linkedinUrl, linkedinId, twitterUrl, facebookUrl, instagramUrl. Best match is used to determine the company in case of ambiguity. Costs 1 credit per call (5 credits with the workforce expansion).

price.description: $0.009 per company enriched; $0.049 per company enriched with workforce data

tools.name: Batch Enrich Companies
tools.description: Enriches a list of companies using their domain names. Use when you need to enrich multiple companies in a single request. Up to 50 domains can be provided. Each domain maps to a unique company. Costs 1 credit per domain enriched (5 credits with the workforce expansion).

price.description: $0.009 per company enriched; $0.049 with workforce data

tools.name: Find Similar Companies
tools.description: Tool to find similar companies to the given company by domain. Use when you need to find companies similar to a target company based on industry, size, or other characteristics. Returns up to 100 companies per request. Costs 5 credits per company returned, and 5 credits if no results are found.

price.description: $0.049 per similar company returned (min $0.049); +$0.049 each with workforce.

tools.name: Get Bulk Person Email Job Status

tools.name: Get Company

tools.name: Get Company List

tools.name: Get Company Workforce

Returns found=false with null workforce fields when no company matches; there is no charge in that case. Use when you need to find workforce details (employee count, department breakdown) for a specific company given its domain or company ID.

tools.name: Get Country by Code

tools.name: Get Current User

tools.name: Get Job Details
tools.description: Returns details for a specific job by ID. Use when you need to check the status, progress, or result of an async enrichment job. Free; no charge.

tools.name: Get People Search Export Job Status

tools.name: Get Regions

tools.name: Get search export job status

tools.name: List all jobs

name: Consensus MCP
description: Consensus MCP lets agents search peer-reviewed academic research and return papers, citations, study metadata, and plan-dependent analysis fields.

tools.name: Search
tools.description:
Search over 220 million peer-reviewed academic papers.

Use this tool when the user asks about research, studies, evidence,
scientific findings, clinical trials, medical research, or academic
literature. Covers Semantic Scholar, PubMed, Scopus, and ArXiv.

Returns paper titles, authors, abstracts, citation counts, journal
quality scores, and direct URLs to each paper.
All filters are optional — only apply them when the user explicitly asks.

Example query → filter mappings:
- "what does the evidence say about metformin for longevity?"
    → query="metformin longevity mortality",
      medical_mode=True, exclude_preprints=True
- "recent peer-reviewed RCTs on SGLT2 inhibitors for heart failure"
    → query="SGLT2 inhibitors heart failure outcomes",
      year_min=2022, exclude_preprints=True, study_types=["rct"]
- "long-term studies of statin side effects (1+ year)"
    → query="statin adverse effects long-term",
      duration_min=365, medical_mode=True
- "what is dark matter?"
    → query="dark matter"  (no filters — general question)
- "coffee and cognition, excluding top-tier Q1 journals"
    → query="coffee cognition", sjr_min=2
