tools.description: Retrieves paginated list of all course progress for a specific user by email. Use to track user progress across all enrolled courses, including active and completed posts. Rate limited to 4 requests per second.

tools.name: List Users
tools.description: List all users in your Memberspot school with optional filtering and pagination. Use this tool to: - Retrieve all users in your membership platform - Filter users by offer access, course enrollment, or active status - Paginate through large user lists using the nextPage token Returns user details including email, name, creation date, progress, and custom properties. Note: API rate limit is 4 requests per second.

tools.name: Set offer expiration
tools.description: Tool to set or remove the expiration date for an offer for a user. Use when you need to grant time-limited access to an offer or remove time limits from an existing offer. When no value is provided for expiresAt, the offer expiration will be removed.

tools.name: Set order state
tools.description: Manages order-based offer access for a user in Memberspot. Use this to activate (grant access), deactivate (revoke access), or delete an order-based offer association. Order IDs typically come from payment providers (Stripe, Copecart, Digistore) after a purchase.

tools.name: Set user offer state
tools.description: Tool to revoke or set the state of a specific offer for a user. Use after confirming whether the user should gain or lose access.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API key for authenticating requests to the Memberspot API. Obtain it from your Memberspot account settings under 'Integrations' > 'API Keys'.

name: Memberstack
description: Memberstack is a platform that enables developers to add user authentication, payments, and member management to their websites without writing backend code.

tools.name: Create Member
tools.description: Tool to create a new member in your application. Use after gathering email, password, optional plans, custom fields, metadata, and redirect.

tools.name: Delete Member
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete a member from your application. Use after confirming you no longer need the member's data and have the member ID.

tools.name: Get Member
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific member by ID or email. Use when you need to fetch member profile details for a given identifier (ID or email). Example: "Get member mem_sb_12345".

tools.name: List Data Tables
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all data tables in your Memberstack application. Returns table metadata including keys, field definitions, and access control rules.

tools.name: List Members
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a paginated list of all members in your application. Use when you need to iterate through members with cursor-based pagination.

tools.name: List Plans
tools.description: Tool to list all available membership plans. Use when you need to retrieve plan IDs and details before assigning or comparing plans.

tools.name: Remove Free Plan
tools.description: Tool to remove a free plan from an existing member. Use after confirming the member's subscription status. Example: "Remove free plan pln_sb_67890 from member mem_sb_12345".

tools.name: Update Member
tools.description: Tool to update an existing member's information. Use when you have a member ID and need to modify their email, customFields, metaData, JSON data, or loginRedirect.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your Memberstack secret API key, used for authenticating API requests. Secret keys carry administrative privileges and should be kept secure and used only in server-side environments.

name: Membervault
description: MemberVault is a Relationship Marketing Platform that allows users to host courses, memberships, and other digital products in one place.

tools.name: Add User to Course
tools.description: Tool to add a user to a specified product. Use when enrolling a user into a course without duplication.

tools.name: Delete User
tools.description: Tool to completely delete a user from the account, including all data, progress, and quiz answers (irreversible). Use when you need to permanently remove a user. Example: "Delete user with email user@example.com"

tools.name: Get Courses
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all courses (products) in the MemberVault account. Use when you need to list available courses after setting up authentication.

tools.name: Remove User from Course
tools.description: Tool to remove a user's access to a product (course). This simply removes access to the product without deleting the user from the account. Use when revoking course access.

required.name: subdomain
required.description: The subdomain of your MemberVault account, used to construct the base URL for API requests.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API key for authenticating requests to the MemberVault API.

name: Memelord
description: Memelord generates and edits image and video memes from prompts, with hosted results and asynchronous video rendering.

tools.name: Check Video Status
tools.description: Read one current Memelord Tools API video job. Poll every few seconds until its provider-defined status becomes completed or failed; completed jobs include the MP4 download URL.

tools.name: Edit Image Meme
tools.description: Create a paid edited image-meme render from a prior generation result. Pass its template ID and template data unchanged; the returned URL is temporary.

tools.name: Edit Meme
tools.description: Create a paid text edit of an image meme using its edit handle and return a fresh signed URL, updated caption slots, and a new edit handle.

tools.name: Edit Video Meme
tools.description: Start a paid asynchronous render that edits a prior video meme's caption and can replace its audio with an overlay, which mutes the base audio. Poll the returned job with Get Video Render Status unless using a webhook.

tools.name: Fulfill Meme Request With Jester
tools.description: Run Memelord's paid Jester agent for a natural-language meme request that does not map cleanly to a specific tool. It may return images immediately and video job IDs that require separate polling.

tools.name: Generate AI Meme
tools.description: Create paid AI-remixed image memes by editing a template picture to fit the joke, optionally using reference images. Returns signed image URLs, caption slots, and edit handles.

tools.name: Generate Caption Meme
tools.description: Create paid classic image memes by writing new captions on unchanged templates. Returns signed image URLs, caption slots, and edit handles.

tools.name: Generate or Edit Video With Gemini Omni
tools.description: Start a paid Gemini Omni video job to edit an existing clip, animate a still image, or generate a short clip from a prompt. Poll the returned job ID for completion.

tools.name: Generate Image Memes
tools.description: Generate 1-10 hosted image memes from a prompt. Each requested meme consumes paid usage, and returned URLs are temporary.

tools.name: Generate Video Meme
tools.description: Start paid video-meme render jobs through the current Memelord Tools API. Returns provider-defined job objects immediately; poll each job ID with Check Video Status until it completes.

tools.name: Generate Video Memes
tools.description: Start 1-5 paid asynchronous video-meme renders from a prompt and return job IDs. Poll each job with Get Video Render Status unless using a webhook.

tools.name: Get Account
tools.description: Get the authenticated Memelord account, usage balance, billable-tool availability, credit URL, authentication mode, and reported end-user ID.

tools.name: Get Meme Template
tools.description: Fetch one Memelord template asset by ID to inspect its media, metadata, dimensions, tags, and text-slot count before generation.

tools.name: Get Video Render Status
tools.description: Get the current state of one asynchronous video render job and, when completed, its temporary MP4 URL. Performs one status read and does not poll.

tools.name: List Image Tools
tools.description: List one-shot image tools available to the connected Memelord account, including each tool's ID, required inputs, and extra parameters.

tools.name: List Trending Memes
tools.description: List the newest curated trending meme templates with cultural context, optionally restricted to images or videos. NSFW drops are excluded.

tools.name: List Video Models
tools.description: List the pro AI video models this Memelord account can run, including each model's required inputs, optional inputs, rules, parameter options, ranges, and defaults. Call this before Run Video Model. This operation is free.

tools.name: Run Image Tool
tools.description: Run one paid Memelord image tool by its catalog tool ID. Supply the image, prompt, and scalar tool-specific parameters required by that tool.

tools.name: Run Video Model
tools.description: Start paid AI video generation using a model and valid parameters from List Video Models. Media inputs must be public URIs supplied by the user. Returns a job ID when processing starts; invalid_request and needs_input results do not start a job or incur a charge.

tools.name: Search Memes
tools.description: Search Memelord's meme, video-clip, and sticker template library by meaning, text, misspelling, or similar media. Returns one provider-managed page.

tools.name: Start Video Meme Edit
tools.description: Start a paid asynchronous caption rewrite and video re-render. Provide a prior generation's template ID and caption, then poll the returned job ID with Check Video Status. Unlike Edit Video Meme, this action does not accept webhooks or audio overlays.

tools.name: Swap Video Subject With Genjutsu
tools.description: Start a paid Genjutsu job that transposes people or characters, or swaps an object or creature, in an existing video while retaining its motion, camera, timing, and audio. Poll the returned job ID for completion.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create or copy your Memelord API key from Developer Settings at https://www.memelord.com/settings/developer. The key begins with mlord_live_ and grants access to Memelord's image and video meme API, so keep it secret.

name: Memelord MCP
description: Search meme templates, generate and edit image and video memes, upload media, and use Jester through Memelord’s hosted MCP server. Generation and editing tools spend the connected account’s usage balance; discovery, uploads, job status, and account information are free.

tools.name: Check video status
tools.description: Check one video job from any video-producing tool. Returns status (pending / processing → completed | failed) and the MP4 download URL once complete. Free — poll every few seconds after a tool returns a job_id.

tools.name: Create media upload url
tools.description: Start a direct upload for a file too large to send inline (over 3 MB), typically a video. Returns an upload_url and upload_id: PUT the raw file bytes to upload_url with the returned Content-Type header (for example curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" --data-binary @clip.mp4 "<upload_url>"), then call upload_media with upload_id to get the file's url. The upload_url expires after 2 hours. Accepts image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm; images up to 10 MB, videos up to 100 MB. Free.

tools.name: Edit meme
tools.description: Change the text of an image meme you already generated. Pass the edit_handle from a generate_caption_meme / generate_ai_meme (or previous edit_meme) result together with a plain-language instruction; use the slot numbers from that result's caption_slots as target_index to change just one box. Re-renders the image and returns a fresh URL, the updated caption_slots, and a new edit_handle (earlier handles stay valid, so you can branch from any version). Handles only work for the account that created them. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Edit video meme
tools.description: Rewrite the caption of a video meme and re-render it. Provide the template_id and the current caption from a previous generate_video_meme job plus a plain-language instruction. Starts a new render job — poll check_video_status for the MP4. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Generate ai meme
tools.description: AI-remixed image memes: Jester picks a meme template (or uses template_id), AI-edits the picture itself to fit the joke — swapping subjects, adding objects, or painting in people and products from reference_image_urls — then captions it. Use generate_caption_meme instead when you only want new text on an unchanged classic template. Returns signed image URLs plus template_id, caption_slots, and an edit_handle for edit_meme. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Generate caption meme
tools.description: Classic caption memes: Jester picks a real meme template from the library (or uses template_id), writes new text for its caption slots, and renders that text on the unchanged template image. The picture is never AI-edited or repainted — use generate_ai_meme for that. Returns signed image URLs plus template_id, caption_slots, and an edit_handle you can hand to edit_meme to change the wording. Use search_memes or get_trending_memes first if you want to pick the template yourself. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Generate video meme
tools.description: Generate AI-captioned video memes from a topic. Jester picks video templates (or uses template_id), writes the caption text, and starts render jobs. Rendering is asynchronous: this returns job_ids immediately — poll check_video_status (or list_video_jobs) until status is "completed" to get the MP4 URL. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Get account
tools.description: Return the authenticated Memelord account: user id, display name, email, usage balance (USD, rounded to cents), whether billable tools can run, where to add credits, and how this MCP session is authenticated (OAuth or API key). Call this to confirm who you are acting as or to check whether billable tools will succeed. Free.

tools.name: Get meme template
tools.description: Fetch one template asset by id: name, type (meme | video | sticker), media URL, description, tags, dimensions, and how many text slots its layout has. Use it to inspect a search result before generating with template_id. Free.

tools.name: Get trending memes
tools.description: What's trending right now: the most recent curated trending templates with a short cultural-context blurb explaining the format. Use it to pick timely templates for generate_caption_meme / generate_ai_meme / generate_video_meme, or to answer "what memes are hot this week". NSFW drops are never included. Free.

tools.name: List image tools
tools.description: Catalog of one-shot image tools you can run with run_image_tool: celebrity face swaps (Trump, Elon, Zuck, Vance, …), filters (Bust Down, Wojakify, GigaChad, Looksmaxxing, mugshot, Windows 95), and text-to-image generators (mascots, logos, Pokémon-style cards). Each entry lists its tool_id, whether it needs an image and/or a prompt, and any extra params. Free.

tools.name: List video jobs
tools.description: List your recent video jobs from every video tool, newest first, with status and MP4 URLs. Use it to recover job_ids after a reconnect or to find finished videos without polling each job. Statuses are as last recorded; call check_video_status on an in-progress job to refresh it. Free.

tools.name: List video models
tools.description: List the pro AI video models this account can run — Kling 3.0, Kling O3, Seedance, Wan 3.0, Cinema Studio 4.0 (run with run_video_model) — and Genjutsu character transpose (run with run_genjutsu). Each entry lists required and optional inputs, rules, and params (options, ranges, defaults). Call this before run_video_model to pick a model and valid params. Free.

tools.name: Run agent
tools.description: Hand a natural-language request to Jester, Memelord's full meme agent — the same brain behind the Memelord chat. Jester decides what to do: search templates, caption a meme, remix a format, edit or generate an image, face-swap, make or caption a video, add text-to-speech or lipsync, convert to GIF, and more. Use this when a request does not map cleanly onto a specific tool ("turn this photo into a 3-panel meme about my cat", "make a video meme with the drake format about Mondays", "put my face on Elon"). Pass thread_id from a previous result to continue the conversation. Returns the assistant's message plus any images; videos come back as job_ids to poll with check_video_status. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Run genjutsu
tools.description: Genjutsu character transpose: put a person or character into an existing video clip while keeping its motion, choreography, camera, timing, and audio ("put me in this music video", "swap the dancer for my character"). Needs the source clip (video_url, or video_job_id of a finished video on this account) and 1-8 photos of who to put in (character_image_urls). Both must be real media the user provided — never invent, guess, or substitute URLs. When the user gives you local photos or a local clip, upload each with upload_media first (clips over 3 MB via create_media_upload_url) and pass the returned urls. If anything is missing the call returns status "needs_input" listing everything still needed, with nothing started or charged: ask the user once, then call again. To generate new footage use run_video_model; for meme-template video clips use generate_video_meme. Returns a job_id; poll check_video_status until completed. Billed against your usage balance per second of the source clip, only once the job starts.

tools.name: Run image tool
tools.description: Run one specific image tool from list_image_tools by tool_id — e.g. "donald-trump-face-swapper" with a face photo, "bust-down-filter" on a portrait, or "mascot-generator" with a prompt. Provide image_url for image-to-image tools, prompt for text-to-image tools, and params for any extra inputs the tool lists. Returns the resulting image URL(s). Prefer this over run_agent when you already know exactly which tool you want. Billed against your usage balance.

tools.name: Run video model
tools.description: Generate new AI video footage with one model from list_video_models: from a prompt alone, a start frame (image_url, optional end_image_url), or reference images / clips / audio. Use this for original footage ("a cinematic drone shot over Tokyo at night", "animate this photo"). For a meme template turned into a captioned video clip use generate_video_meme; for still images use run_image_tool or generate_ai_meme; to put a person into an existing clip use run_genjutsu. Media must be public URLs the user provided — never invent or guess them; if the user gave you local files, upload them with upload_media and pass the returned url. Invalid requests come back as status "invalid_request" listing every problem, with nothing charged. Returns a job_id; poll check_video_status until completed (usually a few minutes). Billed against your usage balance per generated second, only once the job starts.

tools.name: Search memes
tools.description: Search Memelord's template library of memes, video clips, and stickers. Default method "semantic_context" matches what a meme MEANS or depicts (natural-language queries like "when the deploy works on the first try"). Use "fulltext" for exact names and proper nouns ("drake", "spongebob"), "fuzzy" for misspellings, "semantic_combined" when visual identity matters, or "semantic_media" with media_url to find templates that look like a given image. Results come best match first and include ids you can pass as template_id to generate_caption_meme / generate_ai_meme / generate_video_meme / get_meme_template. Paging: each response has has_more and next_offset; to get the next page, repeat the exact same call (same query, method, filters, limit, min_score) with offset set to next_offset, and stop when has_more is false (next_offset is null). Pass ids you already have in exclude_ids only when starting a fresh search, not while paging, or the pages shift. Free.

tools.name: Upload media
tools.description: Upload the user's own photo or video into their Memelord Uploads and get back an https url to pass to generate_ai_meme reference_image_urls, run_image_tool image_url, run_agent image_urls, run_genjutsu character_image_urls / video_url, or run_video_model image and reference fields. Use it whenever the user gives you a local file or an attachment instead of a public link — never invent or guess media URLs. Send exactly one of: data_base64 (file bytes, up to 3 MB decoded), source_url (an https link to download), file (a host-provided file), or upload_id (after PUTting a larger file to the upload_url from create_media_upload_url). Accepts image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm; images up to 10 MB, videos up to 100 MB. Genjutsu uses 4-30 s of a source clip (longer clips are trimmed to 30 s) and clear, front-facing photos work best for character_image_urls. The url is valid for 7 days; calling upload_media again with the same upload_id returns a fresh one. Free, and limited to 50 uploads per hour.

name: MerchantPro

tools.name: Get Inventory Unit

tools.name: Get Product

tools.name: Get Shop Taxonomy

tools.name: List Catalog Partners
tools.description: List brands or suppliers used by the product catalog; choose one resource type per call.

tools.name: List Categories

tools.name: List Customers

tools.name: Getaccount

tools.name: Getaccountcards

tools.name: Getaccounts

tools.name: Getaccountstatements

tools.name: Getattachment

tools.name: Gettransaction

    - These categories are custom and different from the values for "mercuryCategory".

tools.name: Listcredit

tools.name: Listcustomers

tools.name: Listsendmoneyapprovalrequests
tools.description: Retrieve a paginated list of send money approval requests for the authenticated organization. Supports filtering by account and status.

tools.name: Listtransactions
tools.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all transactions across all accounts. Supports advanced filtering by date ranges, status, categories, and cursor-based pagination.

    
    CRITICAL TRUNCATION RULE - READ THIS FIRST:
    ================================================================================
    IF YOU SEE "Result too long" IN THE RESPONSE:
    1. IMMEDIATELY STOP - Do not analyze or use the truncated data
    2. The data is INCOMPLETE and any analysis will be WRONG
    3. Start over with a smaller limit (reduce by 50%)
    4. Paginate through ALL pages until you have complete data
    5. NEVER provide answers based on truncated results
    ================================================================================

    MANDATORY PAGINATION FOR COMPLETE RESULTS:
    When a user asks ANY question requiring complete data (totals, balances, aggregates, 
    "most/least", "all transactions", comparisons, or any calculation across transactions):

    CRITICAL: Incomplete pagination will produce WRONG ANSWERS for questions about totals, 
    spending categories, balances, minimums, maximums, or "most/least". You must fetch everything 
    before calculating or answering.

    1. Start with a limit of 300 transactions.
    2. You MUST automatically paginate through ALL pages WITHOUT asking the user
    3. Continue calling listTransactions using the page.nextPage value from each response
    4. Keep fetching until page.nextPage is not present
    5. If pagination would take more than 3 tool calls, ask the user to narrow down to a smaller time period
    6. It is a CRITICAL ERROR to answer before having fetched ALL pages

    FILTERING:
    - IMPORTANT: WHEN FILTERING BY DATE, ALWAYS CHECK THE CURRENT DATE FIRST and ensure you're using the current year for current year queries
    - Unless specified otherwise or queried for "all transactions", ONLY include transactions with "status: sent"
    - To get transactions for a specific account, use the accountId parameter to filter by accountId

    PAGINATION MECHANICS:
    - Use the limit parameter to control page size
    - If page.nextPage is returned, use it as the start_after parameter in your next call
    - Keep fetching until page.nextPage is null/undefined
    - The page.nextPage value is a transaction ID to start after (exclusive)

    COMPUTATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
    - For any query requiring:
      - Sums, totals, averages, medians, modes, ranges, most/least, or other aggregations across accounts/transactions
      - Calculations involving currency amounts
      - Comparisons of financial metrics
    - You MUST:
      - Create an artifact that processes the data programmatically
      - Parse the JSON response and use JavaScript/Python to calculate
      - Display intermediate steps for verification
      - Never rely on mental arithmetic for financial calculations
    - Example: "What's my total balance?"
      - CORRECT: Create artifact that parses accounts, maps to balances, uses reduce() to sum
      - INCORRECT: Manually adding up balance values

    For queries about 'last two months' or 'this year', calculate dates based on the actual current date
    Use the getCurrentDate tool to get the current date.

    Use the getTransaction tool to get more details about a specific transaction.
