name: Microsoft Entra ID
description: Manage Microsoft Entra ID directory resources through Microsoft Graph v1.0, including users, groups, applications, roles, devices, policies, and audit data.

tools.name: Add Administrative Unit Member
tools.description: Add one existing user, group, or device to an assigned-membership Microsoft Entra administrative unit, bringing that object into the unit's delegated administration scope. Dynamic administrative units are managed only by their membership rule and reject manual changes. In a restricted-management unit, a group must be a nonunified, security-enabled, non-mail-enabled group that is not synchronized from on-premises. For delegated access, Privileged Role Administrator is the least-privileged supported role. App-only callers that need directory reads also require a supported directory-reader role or an application permission such as Directory.Read.All.

tools.name: Add Application Owner
tools.description: Add an existing user or service principal as an owner of an application registration, granting authority to administer it. For delegated access, the signed-in user must also hold Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, or a supported custom Microsoft Entra role.

tools.name: Add Directory Role Member
tools.description: Assign a principal to an activated Microsoft Entra directory role, granting that role's tenant-wide administrative access. This is an access-elevation operation. For delegated access, the signed-in user must be a Privileged Role Administrator (the least-privileged supported role) or hold a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation. Prefer unified role assignments when scoped access is required.

tools.name: Add Group Member
tools.description: Add an existing directory object as a direct member of an assigned-membership Microsoft Entra group. Dynamic group membership cannot be changed manually. Role-assignable groups additionally require RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory and an eligible Entra role. Adding a device, service principal, or organizational contact can require an additional permission for that member type.

tools.name: Add Group Owner
tools.description: Add an existing user or service principal as an owner of a Microsoft 365 or security group, granting authority to modify the group. Delegated callers must also be a group owner or hold a supported Microsoft Entra role; some roles can add only user owners or are limited to particular group types.

tools.name: Add Service Principal Owner
tools.description: Add an existing user or service principal as an owner of an enterprise application/service principal, granting authority to administer it. For delegated access, the signed-in user must also hold Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, or a supported custom Microsoft Entra role. With app-only Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy access, the calling application must already own the target service principal.

tools.name: Assign User Licenses
tools.description: Add and remove Microsoft product licenses for one Entra user in a single request. Both add and remove lists are required and either can be empty. Removing a license revokes the user's entitlement to that product's services and can immediately prevent access; data retention depends on the affected Microsoft product.

tools.name: Create Administrative Unit
tools.description: Create an assigned or dynamic Microsoft Entra administrative unit for scoping directory administration. Restricted member management can be set only during creation and is immutable afterward.

tools.name: Create Application
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Entra application registration with allowlisted platform, role, and API permission settings, without creating or accepting password or key credentials.

tools.name: Create App Role Assignment
tools.description: Assign an application role to a user, group, or client service principal. This grants the principal the application access represented by that role; for client service principals, the grant is an application permission.

tools.name: Create Group
tools.description: Create a Microsoft 365, assigned security, or dynamic-membership group. Optionally bind up to 20 total initial owners and members by directory object ID; dynamic groups cannot have initial members.

tools.name: Create Role Assignment
tools.description: Grant a user, role-assignable group, or service principal a Microsoft Entra directory role, conferring the role's administrative access at the explicit tenant, administrative-unit, resource-application, or app-specific scope. This is an access-elevation operation. For delegated access, the signed-in user must be a Privileged Role Administrator (the least-privileged supported role) or hold a custom role that grants the required permissions.

tools.name: Create Service Principal
tools.description: Create an enterprise application (service principal) for an existing application ID without accepting or creating password or key credentials. Delegated callers also need a supported Microsoft Entra role. With app-only Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, the calling application must own the backing application.

tools.name: Create User
tools.description: Create a Microsoft Entra tenant user with the required sign-in profile and an initial password. This action only sets the password required during creation; it does not reset passwords or modify authentication methods.

tools.name: Delete Administrative Unit
tools.description: Delete a Microsoft Entra administrative unit and remove its administrative scope. This is irreversible from this toolkit because restoration is not supported here.

tools.name: Delete Application
tools.description: Delete a Microsoft Entra application registration by its directory Object ID. This is irreversible from this toolkit because restoration is not supported here. Deleting the registration can break dependent user or workload sign-in and integrations that rely on its Application (client) ID, permissions, roles, or redirect configuration.

tools.name: Delete Group
tools.description: Delete a Microsoft Entra group and its associated group resources. This is irreversible from this toolkit: Microsoft 365 and security groups can be restored for 30 days only through recovery outside this toolkit, while distribution groups are permanently deleted immediately.

tools.name: Delete Service Principal
tools.description: Delete a Microsoft Entra enterprise application/service principal. This is irreversible from this toolkit because restoration is not supported here. Deletion removes the enterprise application's tenant identity and can break sign-in, resource access, and app-role assignments that depend on it.

tools.name: Delete User
tools.description: Delete a tenant user and remove the directory identity. This deletion is irreversible from this toolkit; restoration is outside this toolkit.

tools.name: Disable User
tools.description: Disable a Microsoft Entra user without deleting the directory object. This sets accountEnabled=false and blocks future sign-ins; already-issued access tokens or sessions can remain usable until they expire or are separately revoked.

tools.name: Get Administrative Unit
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra administrative unit by directory object ID.

tools.name: Get Application
tools.description: Get one application registration by its directory Object ID, not its Application (client) ID, returning only credential-safe properties.

tools.name: Get Conditional Access Policy
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy by object ID. This is a read-only paid-tier capability; delegated callers also need a supported Entra role such as Security Reader, Global Reader, or Conditional Access Administrator.

tools.name: Get Device
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra device by its directory Object ID, not its distinct Device Registration Service deviceId value.

tools.name: Get Directory Audit
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra directory audit event by its event ID.

tools.name: Get Directory Role
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra directory role that is activated in the tenant by its activated role object ID. Inactive role definitions are not available.

tools.name: Get Domain
tools.description: Get one tenant domain by its fully qualified domain name.

tools.name: Get Group
tools.description: Get one tenant group by directory object ID.

tools.name: Get Organization
tools.description: Get the connected Microsoft Entra tenant's organization record by tenant organization ID. The keyed Graph route returns one organization entity.

tools.name: Get Role Assignment
tools.description: Get one unified Microsoft Entra directory role assignment by its assignment ID, including its principal, role definition, and directory or application scope identifiers.

tools.name: Get Service Principal
tools.description: Get one Microsoft Entra enterprise application/service principal by its directory Object ID, not its Application (client) ID, returning only credential-safe properties.

tools.name: Get Sign In
tools.description: Get one retained Microsoft Entra sign-in event by event ID. Availability is limited by the tenant's sign-in data retention policy; downloading sign-in logs requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and delegated callers need a supported Entra role such as Reports Reader or Security Reader. P2-only risk details can be hidden.

tools.name: Get Subscribed SKU
tools.description: Get one commercial product subscription acquired by the Microsoft Entra tenant using its subscribed-SKU object ID.

tools.name: Get User
tools.description: Get one tenant user by directory object ID or user principal name.

tools.name: Get User Manager
tools.description: Get the directory object recorded as a user's manager. Returns not found when no manager is assigned.

tools.name: List Administrative Unit Members
tools.description: List users, groups, and devices directly assigned to a Microsoft Entra administrative unit. Hidden membership requires the additional Member.Read.Hidden grant, so hidden members can otherwise be omitted. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read a member's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Administrative Units
tools.description: List Microsoft Entra administrative units with optional OData filtering, search, field selection, relationship expansion, and cursor pagination.

tools.name: List Administrative Unit Scoped Role Members
tools.description: List the legacy scoped-role memberships that grant users administrative access within one Microsoft Entra administrative unit. This action is read-only; create new scoped grants with unified role assignments instead.

tools.name: List Application Owners
tools.description: List the users and service principals that own an application registration. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read an owner's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Applications
tools.description: List Microsoft Entra application registrations with OData filtering, search, ordering, and cursor pagination. Selection and output schemas structurally exclude password and key credential collections.

tools.name: List App Role Assignments
tools.description: List users, groups, and client service principals granted application roles on a resource service principal, with OData filtering, field selection, and cursor pagination. Recently added or removed assignments can be delayed by Microsoft Entra replication.

tools.name: List Conditional Access Policies
tools.description: List read-only Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy definitions, including conditions, grant controls, and session controls, with OData queries and cursor pagination. Conditional Access is license-dependent; delegated callers also need a supported Microsoft Entra role.

tools.name: List Devices
tools.description: List devices registered in the Microsoft Entra tenant with optional advanced OData queries and cursor pagination. Results distinguish each device's directory object ID from its registration-service deviceId.

tools.name: List Directory Audits
tools.description: List retained Microsoft Entra directory audit events with documented OData filtering, activity-time ordering, and opaque cursor pagination. Availability is limited by the tenant's Microsoft Entra data-retention policy. For delegated access, the signed-in user must have Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator, or a supported custom role.

tools.name: List Directory Role Members
tools.description: List principals currently assigned to one activated Microsoft Entra directory role. Microsoft Graph returns up to 1,000 objects by default and this operation does not support $top pagination, so the result is a single bounded collection. Concrete-type properties can be null when the connection has limited permission.

tools.name: List Directory Roles
tools.description: List Microsoft Entra directory roles that are activated in the tenant. Inactive built-in roles and other available role definitions are not returned.

tools.name: List Domains
tools.description: List verified and unverified domains configured for the Microsoft Entra tenant, with documented OData query controls and cursor pagination.

tools.name: List Group Members
tools.description: List a group's direct members; transitive members are not included. Hidden membership requires the additional Member.Read.Hidden grant and, for delegated access, an eligible Entra role, so hidden members can otherwise be omitted. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read a member's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Group Owners
tools.description: List the users and service principals that own a group. Microsoft Graph can omit service-principal owners during its staged v1.0 rollout. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read an owner's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Groups
tools.description: List tenant groups with general OData options, or list only dynamic-membership groups with a fixed safe filter and membership-rule fields.

tools.name: List Group Transitive Members
tools.description: Return one cursor-paginated flat page of direct and nested members of a Microsoft Entra group. Hidden members can be omitted unless the connection also has Member.Read.Hidden. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read a member's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Organizations
tools.description: Return the connected Microsoft Entra tenant's organization record. Microsoft Graph exposes it as a collection containing exactly one organization.

tools.name: List Role Assignments
tools.description: List unified Microsoft Entra directory role assignments, including the assigned principal, role definition, and directory or application scope.

tools.name: List Service Principal Owners
tools.description: List directory objects that own an enterprise application/service principal. Properties other than id and type can be null when the connection lacks permission to read an owner's concrete object type.

tools.name: List Service Principals
tools.description: List Microsoft Entra enterprise applications and service principals with OData filtering, search, ordering, and cursor pagination. Selection and output schemas structurally exclude password credentials, key credentials, and token-encryption key identifiers.

tools.name: List Sign Ins
tools.description: List retained Microsoft Entra sign-in events, newest first. Prefer a createdDateTime range filter to avoid timeouts. Results are limited by the tenant's retention policy; downloading sign-in logs requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, and delegated callers need a supported Entra role such as Reports Reader or Security Reader. P2-only risk details can be hidden.

tools.name: List Subscribed SKUs
tools.description: List commercial product subscriptions acquired by the Microsoft Entra tenant, including assigned-license counts, prepaid-unit availability, and included service plans.

tools.name: List User Direct Reports
tools.description: List directory objects that directly report to one user, with optional OData filtering, search, ordering, field selection, and safe cursor pagination.

tools.name: List User License Details
tools.description: List one tenant user's assigned product licenses and the provisioning state of their included service plans.

tools.name: List User Memberships
tools.description: List groups, directory roles, and administrative units a user directly belongs to. This is not transitive. Hidden memberships require the additional Member.Read.Hidden grant and otherwise might be omitted. Advanced OData queries use an eventually consistent index, so recent membership changes might not appear immediately.

tools.name: List Users
tools.description: List tenant users with optional OData filtering, search, ordering, field selection, and a safe continuation cursor.

tools.name: Remove Administrative Unit Member
tools.description: Remove a user, group, or device from a Microsoft Entra administrative unit, ending administration scoped through that membership. This is irreversible from this toolkit because the prior membership is not restored automatically. The request retains the mandatory /$ref suffix, so it removes only the membership reference and never deletes the member directory object.

tools.name: Remove Application Owner
tools.description: Remove an owner from a Microsoft Entra application registration, revoking that principal's authority to administer the application. This is irreversible from this toolkit because prior ownership and administration access are not restored automatically. Microsoft recommends retaining at least two owners; verify that another valid owner will retain access before removal. The request preserves the required /$ref suffix, so it removes only the ownership reference and never deletes the owner directory object. With app-only authentication, the target application must be owned by the calling application when using Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy.

tools.name: Remove App Role Assignment
tools.description: Remove an app-role assignment from a Microsoft Entra resource service principal. This revokes the user, group, or client service principal's application access granted by that role. The removal is irreversible from this toolkit because the prior assignment is not restored automatically.

tools.name: Remove Directory Role Member
tools.description: Remove a principal from an activated Microsoft Entra directory role, revoking the role's tenant-wide administrative access. This is irreversible from this toolkit because the prior role membership is not restored automatically. The request retains the mandatory /$ref suffix, so it removes only the membership reference and never deletes the principal directory object.

tools.name: Remove Group Member
tools.description: Remove a direct member from an assigned-membership Microsoft Entra group, revoking access inherited through that membership. This is irreversible from this toolkit because the prior membership is not restored automatically. Dynamic groups do not support manual membership changes. Role-assignable groups additionally require RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory and a supported Microsoft Entra role. The request retains the required /$ref suffix so it removes only the membership reference and never deletes the member object.

tools.name: Remove Group Owner
tools.description: Remove a user or service principal as an owner of a Microsoft Entra group, revoking that principal's authority to administer the group. This is irreversible from this toolkit because prior ownership is not restored automatically. Verify that another valid owner remains before removing the current owner; removing the last owner can leave ownership-dependent groups without an administrator. The owner directory object itself is not deleted.

tools.name: Remove Role Assignment
tools.description: Remove a unified Microsoft Entra directory role assignment and revoke the principal's administrative access at that assignment's scope. This is irreversible from this toolkit because the prior assignment is not restored automatically.

tools.name: Remove Service Principal Owner
tools.description: Remove an owner from a Microsoft Entra enterprise application/service principal, revoking that principal's authority to administer it. This is irreversible from this toolkit because prior ownership and administration access are not restored automatically. Microsoft recommends retaining at least two owners; verify that another valid owner will retain access before removal. The request preserves the required /$ref suffix, so it removes only the ownership reference and never deletes the owner directory object. With app-only authentication, the target service principal must be owned by the calling application when using Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy.

tools.name: Update Administrative Unit
tools.description: Update explicitly supplied profile or dynamic-membership properties of one Microsoft Entra administrative unit. The immutable restricted-member-management property is not accepted.

tools.name: Update Application
tools.description: Update explicitly supplied, allowlisted settings of one Microsoft Entra application registration. Password credentials, key credentials, and token encryption key selection are structurally unavailable. With app-only OAuth, the least-privilege grant can update only applications owned by the calling app.

tools.name: Update Group
tools.description: Update explicitly supplied, allowlisted properties of one Microsoft Entra group, including its dynamic membership rule or processing state. Properties that require separate permissions or delegated-only support are unavailable.

tools.name: Update Service Principal
tools.description: Update explicitly supplied, allowlisted settings of one Microsoft Entra enterprise application/service principal. Password credentials, key credentials, and token-encryption-key selection are structurally unavailable. With app-only OAuth, the least-privilege grant applies only to service principals owned by the calling application.

tools.name: Update User
tools.description: Update allowlisted, non-credential profile properties for one Microsoft Entra user. Only explicitly supplied fields are changed; use null only on fields whose description permits clearing. Account status, passwords, authentication methods, identities, phone properties, lifecycle data, and custom security attributes are intentionally unavailable.

name: Microsoft OneNote
description: Digital notebook for capturing and organizing notes, drawings, and information

tools.name: Copy notebook in group
tools.description: Copies a OneNote notebook to the Notebooks folder in the destination Documents library. The notebook is copied asynchronously. This action initiates the copy operation and returns a 202 Accepted response with an Operation-Location header. Use the OnenoteOperationGet action to poll the Operation-Location endpoint to check the status of the copy operation until it completes. Use this action when you need to duplicate a notebook within a Microsoft 365 group, or copy it to a different group's documents library. The copied notebook's folder is created in the destination Documents library if it doesn't exist.

tools.name: Copy notebook in site
tools.description: Copies a OneNote notebook within a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to duplicate a notebook within a SharePoint site. This is an asynchronous operation. Poll the returned operation URL to check whether the copy has completed.

tools.name: Copy section to notebook (site context)
tools.description: Copy a site-hosted OneNote section to a notebook natively.

tools.name: Copy section to notebook (user)
tools.description: Copies a OneNote section to a specific notebook for a specified user. Use this action when you need to duplicate an existing OneNote section into a different notebook under a specific user's account. The operation is asynchronous and returns an Operation-Location header that should be polled to get the final result. The copy is additive and does not remove the source section. Poll the returned Operation-Location value to determine the final outcome.

tools.name: Copy group section to section group
tools.description: Copies a OneNote section from a Microsoft 365 group's notebook into another section group. Use this action when you need to duplicate an existing OneNote section that lives in a Microsoft 365 group's notebook into a different section group. The operation is asynchronous and returns an Operation-Location header that should be polled to get the final result. The copy is additive and does not remove the source section. Poll the returned Operation-Location value to determine the final outcome.

tools.name: Copy section to section group (user)
tools.description: Copies a OneNote section to a specific section group for a specified user. Use this action when you need to duplicate an existing OneNote section into a different section group under a specific user's account. The operation is asynchronous and returns an Operation-Location header that should be polled to get the final result. The copy is additive and does not remove the source section. Poll the returned Operation-Location value to determine the final outcome.

tools.name: Copy site page to section
tools.description: Copy a site-hosted OneNote page to a section natively.

tools.name: Copy user notebook
tools.description: Start an asynchronous copy of a user OneNote notebook.

tools.name: Copy user page to section
tools.description: Copy a OneNote page from a user's notebook to a specified section. Use this action when you need to duplicate a OneNote page into a different section within a user's Microsoft 365 account. This is an asynchronous operation that returns a 202 Accepted response with an Operation-Location header. Poll that endpoint to determine when the copy completes and get the result of the operation. The page is identified by its full path through the notebook's hierarchy.

tools.name: Count user section group sections
tools.description: Gets the provider-reported count of OneNote sections directly within a user's section group. Use this action when you need to quickly determine the number of sections in a section group without retrieving the full list of section objects. This is a read-only operation.

tools.name: Count site section group sections
tools.description: Gets the provider-reported count of sections directly within a SharePoint site's OneNote section group. Use this action when you need to quickly determine the number of sections in a section group without retrieving the full list of section objects. Microsoft Graph requires the `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` header when using the `$count=true` query parameter on OneNote endpoints.

tools.name: Create group nested section group
tools.description: Create a section group inside another group OneNote section group.

tools.name: Create group notebook
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote notebook within a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to create a new notebook for storing notes within a specific Microsoft 365 group. The notebook will be owned by the specified group and accessible to all members of that group with appropriate permissions. Required permissions: Notes.Create (least privileged), Notes.ReadWrite, or Notes.ReadWrite.All for the group.

tools.name: Create group OneNote page
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote page in the default section of the default notebook for a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to programmatically create a new page in a group's OneNote notebook. The page content must be provided as HTML. The page will be created in the default section of the default notebook unless a specific section name is provided via the sectionName query parameter.

tools.name: Create section in section group
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote section within a specified section group of a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to add a new section to organize OneNote pages within a section group's hierarchy within a group. The section name must be unique within the same hierarchy level, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot contain the characters: ?*/:<>|&#''%~. Repeating the call with the same display name may create duplicate sections depending on the API's handling of unique-name constraints.

tools.name: Create user notebook
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote notebook for the signed-in user. Use this action when you need to create a new personal notebook to organize notes. The notebook will be created in the user's default OneDrive for Business location. Notebook names must be unique, cannot exceed 128 characters, and cannot contain ? * / : < > | ' or ". Ampersands are allowed. Returns the full created notebook object including the server-assigned ID and URLs for accessing sections.

tools.name: Create section in user's section group
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote section within a specified section group of a notebook for the signed-in user. Use this action when you need to add a new section to organize OneNote pages within a user's section group hierarchy. The section name must be unique within the same hierarchy level, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot contain the characters: ?*/:<>|&#''%~. Repeating the call with the same display name may create duplicate sections depending on the API's handling of unique-name constraints.

tools.name: Create OneNote page in section
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote page in a specific section for the signed-in user. Use this action when you need to create a new page within a specific section of the user's OneNote notebook. The page content must be provided as HTML. The action constructs a complete HTML document including the title and optional creation timestamp in the meta tag. To include images or attachments, provide the full HTML with external image URLs, or use a multipart request approach. Repeated calls create separate pages, even when the title and content match.

tools.name: Create section group in group notebook
tools.description: Creates a new section group within a OneNote notebook that belongs to a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to organize sections inside a group notebook by creating a new top-level section group to hold related sections together. The displayName must be 50 characters or fewer and cannot contain the characters ? * / : < > | & # ' % ~. Section group names must be unique within the same hierarchy level in the notebook.

tools.name: Create site nested section group
tools.description: Create a section group inside another site OneNote section group.

tools.name: Create site notebook
tools.description: Create a OneNote notebook in a SharePoint site.

tools.name: Create section in site notebook
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote section within a specified notebook in a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to add a new section to organize OneNote pages within a notebook that belongs to a SharePoint site. The section name must be unique within the same hierarchy level, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot contain the characters: ?*/:<>|&#''%~. This action is available in the following national cloud deployments: Global service only. Required permissions: Notes.Create (delegated/personal account), Notes.ReadWrite.All (application).

tools.name: Create user nested section group
tools.description: Create a section group inside another user OneNote section group.

tools.name: Create section in user notebook
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote section within a specified notebook for a specific user. Use this action when you need to add a new section to organize OneNote pages within a notebook that belongs to a specific user. The section name must be unique within the same hierarchy level, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot contain the characters: ?*/:<>|&#''%~. Returns the full created section object including the server-assigned ID.

tools.name: Create user OneNote page
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote page in the default section of the default notebook for a specific user. Use this action when you need to programmatically create a new page in a user's OneNote notebook. The page content must be provided as HTML. The page will be created in the default section of the default notebook unless a specific section name is provided via the sectionName query parameter.

tools.name: Create section in user section group
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote section within a specified section group for a specific user. Use this action when you need to add a new section to organize OneNote pages within a section group's hierarchy for a specific user's notebook. The section name must be unique within the same hierarchy level, cannot exceed 50 characters, and cannot contain the characters: ?*/:<>|&#''%~. Repeating the call with the same display name may create duplicate sections depending on the API's handling of unique-name constraints.

tools.name: Create user section page
tools.description: Creates a new OneNote page in a specific section of a user's notebook. Use this action when you need to create a new page directly in a section within a user's OneNote notebook. The page content must be provided as valid HTML with proper structure (html, head, and body tags). Calling this action multiple times creates separate pages.

tools.name: Delete group section page
tools.description: Deletes a OneNote page within a Microsoft 365 group's OneNote workspace. Canonical action for this group page deletion route. Microsoft Graph returns 204 No Content after accepting the deletion; OneNote retention policies may still apply.

tools.name: Delete OneNote page from section
tools.description: Delete a specific OneNote page from a section within a notebook in a group. Compatibility alias for deleting a group OneNote page. Prefer DeleteOnenoteGroupSectionGroupPageContent for new calls. Microsoft Graph returns 204 No Content after accepting the deletion; OneNote retention policies may apply.

tools.name: Delete OneNote page from site
tools.description: Deletes a OneNote page from a SharePoint site. Use this action to delete a OneNote page from a SharePoint site's OneNote workspace. Microsoft Graph returns 204 No Content after accepting the deletion; OneNote retention policies may still apply.

tools.name: Delete user OneNote page from section
tools.description: Deletes a OneNote page from a section within a section group in a user's notebook. Compatibility alias for deleting a user OneNote page. Prefer DeleteUserPages for new calls. Microsoft Graph returns 204 No Content after accepting the deletion; OneNote retention policies may still apply. Use this action when you need to remove an unwanted page from a section in a user's OneNote notebook.

tools.name: Delete OneNote page for user
tools.description: Deletes a OneNote page from a user's OneNote workspace. Canonical action for this user page deletion route. Microsoft Graph returns 204 No Content after accepting the deletion; OneNote retention policies may still apply. Use this action when you need to remove an unwanted OneNote page from a user's notebook that has been shared with the current user.

tools.name: Get a OneNote section from a group
tools.description: Retrieves a specific OneNote section from a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to fetch metadata or details for a single OneNote section by specifying the group ID and section ID. This action supports OData query parameters for selecting specific properties and expanding relationships like parentNotebook or parentSectionGroup.

tools.name: Get OneNote resource content by ID
tools.description: Retrieves the binary content of a specific OneNote resource using its ID. Use this action when you need to fetch the raw binary content of an image, file attachment, or other embedded resource from a OneNote page in the signed-in user's notebooks. The resource is identified by its unique resource_id, which can be obtained from page content URLs. Note: Binary content is returned as-is; images and files may need additional processing (e.g., base64 decoding or writing to a file) depending on your use case.

tools.name: Get OneNote page content from section
tools.description: Retrieves the HTML content of a specific OneNote page from a section for the signed-in user. Use this action when you need to fetch the full HTML content of a OneNote page within a specific section. This endpoint provides access to page content for processing, rendering, or exporting page data. The returned HTML includes text, images, and other embedded content references. This action is read-only and does not modify any data.

tools.name: Get notebook from web URL
tools.description: Retrieves a OneNote notebook by using its web URL path. Use this action when you have the SharePoint or OneDrive URL of a notebook and need to retrieve its properties and metadata. The webUrl parameter accepts both standard HTTPS URLs and OneNote protocol URLs with the 'onenote:' prefix. This API is available in the following national cloud deployments: Global service only. Required permissions: Notes.Create (delegated) or Notes.Read.All (application).

tools.name: Get notebook section group
tools.description: Retrieves a specific section group from a OneNote notebook within a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to get details about a specific section group, including its name, creation/modification timestamps, and links to its sections and nested section groups.

tools.name: Get group OneNote operation status
tools.description: Retrieves the status of a long-running OneNote operation for a group. Use this action when you need to check whether a copy or sync operation (e.g., CopyNotebook, CopyToNotebook, CopyToSectionGroup, CopyToSection) has completed, failed, or is still in progress.

tools.name: Get a OneNote page from a group
tools.description: Retrieves OneNote page metadata directly by page ID in a Microsoft 365 group. Legacy notebook, section group, and section IDs do not affect the Graph route.

tools.name: Get site OneNote operation status
tools.description: Retrieves the status of a long-running OneNote operation for a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to check whether a copy or sync operation (e.g., CopyNotebook, CopyToNotebook, CopyToSectionGroup, CopyToSection) has completed, failed, or is still in progress for a site.

tools.name: Get OneNote page content for user
tools.description: Gets the HTML content of a specific OneNote page for a user. Use this action when you need to retrieve the actual HTML content of a specific OneNote page for reading, processing, or displaying page content. The action supports the includeIDs query parameter to include element IDs in the HTML, which is useful when preparing content for page updates via the PATCH endpoint.

tools.name: Get a OneNote page
tools.description: Retrieves metadata and properties of a specific OneNote page from the authenticated user's notebooks. Use this action when you need to fetch details about a OneNote page by its ID without navigating the full notebook/section hierarchy. This returns page metadata including title, creation date, modification date, and optional expanded parent relationships. For retrieving the HTML content of a page, use the dedicated page content endpoint instead.

tools.name: Get recent notebooks
tools.description: Retrieves a list of recently accessed OneNote notebooks for the signed-in user. Use this action when you need to display recently accessed notebooks, provide quick access to notebooks the user has been working with, or build a recent notebooks feature. The notebooks are returned in order of most recent access. Set includePersonalNotebooks to true to include notebooks owned by the user, or false to exclude them.

tools.name: Get a OneNote section by ID
tools.description: Retrieves a specific OneNote section by its ID from the current user's OneNote. Use this action when you need to fetch metadata or details for a single OneNote section by specifying only the section ID, without requiring additional context like group, user, or site IDs. This action supports OData query parameters for selecting specific properties and expanding relationships like parentNotebook or parentSectionGroup.

tools.name: Get OneNote page from site
tools.description: Retrieves a specific OneNote page from a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to fetch metadata or details for a single OneNote page by its page identifier within a SharePoint site. This action supports optional OData query parameters to select specific properties or expand related entities like parentSection and parentNotebook. Note: This action is read-only and does not modify any data. It is the canonical action for the site page metadata route.

tools.name: Get site notebook page preview
tools.description: Retrieves a text preview of a specific OneNote page from a SharePoint site or the signed-in user's OneNote. Use this action when you need to quickly get the content preview of a OneNote page from a site-hosted notebook without fetching the full page content. The preview returns a text snippet of the page's content. This action is read-only and does not modify any data.

tools.name: Get a OneNote section from a site
tools.description: Retrieves a specific OneNote section from a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to fetch metadata or details for a single OneNote section by specifying the site ID and section ID. This action supports OData query parameters for selecting specific properties and expanding relationships like parentNotebook or parentSectionGroup.

tools.name: Get OneNote page from site (compatibility alias)
tools.description: Compatibility alias for retrieving OneNote page metadata directly by page ID in a SharePoint site. Prefer GetSiteOnenotePages for new calls. Legacy notebook, section group, and section IDs do not affect the Graph route.

tools.name: Get user notebook
tools.description: Retrieves the properties and relationships of a OneNote notebook by ID for a specific user. Use this action when you need to fetch details about a specific notebook belonging to a user, including its display name, sharing status, section URLs, and the user's role on the notebook. Supports OData $select and $expand query parameters to customize the response.

tools.name: Get user OneNote operation
tools.description: Poll the status of a user's asynchronous OneNote operation.

tools.name: Get a OneNote page from user
tools.description: Retrieves a specific OneNote page from a user's OneNote notebooks. Use this action when you need to fetch metadata or details for a single OneNote page directly by page ID and user ID. This is useful for retrieving page information without navigating through the full notebook/section hierarchy. The default response expands the parentSection relationship and selects its id, name, and self properties.

tools.name: Get parent section group from user section
tools.description: Retrieves the parent section group of a OneNote section within a user's notebook. Use this action when you need to navigate up the OneNote hierarchy from a section to its parent section group, for example to determine which section group contains a specific section.

tools.name: List group notebooks
tools.description: List OneNote notebooks owned by a Microsoft 365 group or Teams team. Use this with a group or team ID, including IDs returned by List joined teams.

tools.name: List notebook section groups
tools.description: Retrieves a list of section groups from the specified notebook within a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action to retrieve a page of section groups in a group-owned OneNote notebook to understand its structure or find a specific section group.

tools.name: List pages from a group notebook section
tools.description: Compatibility alias for listing a page of OneNote pages from a specific section within a notebook in a Microsoft 365 group. Prefer the canonical ListOnenoteGroupSectionsPages4 action for new calls. Use this action when you need to retrieve a page of pages from a known section in a group notebook. This action accesses pages directly through the section path without going through section groups.

tools.name: List group root section groups
tools.description: List section groups at the root of a Microsoft 365 group's OneNote hierarchy.

tools.name: List group root sections
tools.description: List sections at the root of a Microsoft 365 group's OneNote hierarchy.

tools.name: List section group sections
tools.description: Lists a paginated collection of OneNote sections from a section group within a Microsoft 365 group's OneNote. Use this action when you need to retrieve the sections contained within a section group in a group-owned OneNote notebook. Supports pagination and filtering via OData query parameters. This is a read-only operation that retrieves existing sections without modifying any data.

tools.name: List joined teams
tools.description: List Microsoft Teams that a user is a direct member of. Use this to get team IDs, which are also Microsoft 365 group IDs, before listing group-owned OneNote notebooks.

tools.name: List pages in section
tools.description: Retrieves a list of OneNote pages from a specific section for the current user. Use this action when you need to retrieve a page of pages from a specific section in the current user's OneNote notebook. This action supports pagination, filtering, sorting, and relationship expansion via OData query parameters. The default query returns up to 10 pages. Note: This action is read-only and does not modify any data.

tools.name: List group OneNote pages
tools.description: Lists a paginated collection of OneNote pages from a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action to retrieve a page of OneNote pages within a Microsoft 365 group. Supports pagination via page_size. The default page size is 10 and maximum is 100. Results are ordered by lastModifiedDateTime descending by default.

tools.name: List group section group section groups
tools.description: Lists a paginated collection of nested section groups from a specified parent section group within a Microsoft 365 group's OneNote notebook. Use this action when you need to retrieve the nested section groups within a section group in a group context to navigate the OneNote notebook hierarchy. This action supports OData query parameters for filtering, sorting, pagination, and expanding related entities.

tools.name: List pages from a group section
tools.description: Canonical action for listing a paginated collection of OneNote pages from a specific section in a Microsoft 365 group. Use this action when you need to retrieve a page of pages from a known section in a group notebook without specifying the notebook ID. This action supports pagination, filtering, sorting, and relationship expansion via OData query parameters. Note: This action is read-only and does not modify any data.

tools.name: List site notebooks
tools.description: List OneNote notebooks stored in a SharePoint site. Use this after resolving a SharePoint site ID from a site name or URL when the user asks for notebooks in a SharePoint site.

tools.name: List site notebook section groups
tools.description: Retrieves a list of section groups from the specified notebook within a SharePoint site. Use this action to retrieve a page of section groups in a SharePoint site-owned OneNote notebook to understand its structure or to find a specific section group. The default sort order is name ascending. The default query expands parentNotebook and selects its id, displayName, and self properties.

tools.name: Get OneNote page content from SharePoint site
tools.description: Retrieves the HTML content of a specific OneNote page within a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to fetch the full HTML content of a OneNote page from a SharePoint site for processing, rendering, or exporting page data. This endpoint provides direct access to page content without requiring notebook or section context. Returns the raw HTML content of the page, including text, images, and other embedded content references. Note: This action is read-only and does not modify any data.

tools.name: List site root section groups
tools.description: List section groups at the root of a SharePoint site's OneNote hierarchy.

tools.name: List site section pages
tools.description: List one result page of OneNote pages in a known SharePoint site section; pass next_cursor back as cursor to continue.

tools.name: List site sections
tools.description: Retrieves a list of OneNote sections from a SharePoint site. Use this action to retrieve a page of OneNote sections within a SharePoint site's OneNote notebook to understand its structure or to find a specific section. This is a read-only operation that retrieves existing sections without modifying any data. Supports OData query parameters for filtering, sorting, pagination, and property expansion. The default sort order is name ascending. The default query expands parentNotebook and selects its id, displayName, and self properties.

tools.name: List user notebooks
tools.description: Lists a paginated collection of OneNote notebooks accessible by a specific user. Use this action when you need to retrieve the available notebooks for a user, display notebook listings, or browse notebooks that are owned by or shared with a specific user. Supports OData query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination. Note: The user_id can be a GUID or a user principal name (UPN). Use 'me' to reference the signed-in user.

tools.name: List user notebook sections
tools.description: Lists a paginated collection of OneNote sections from a specified user notebook. Use this action when you need to retrieve a page of sections within a notebook that is owned by or accessible to a specific user. Supports OData query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination. Note: The user_id can be a GUID or user principal name (UPN). Use 'me' to reference the signed-in user. The default sort order is by display name ascending. This is a read-only operation.

tools.name: List user pages
tools.description: List OneNote pages owned by a user, defaulting to the signed-in user.

tools.name: List user root section groups
tools.description: List root OneNote section groups for a user, defaulting to the signed-in user.

tools.name: List user sections
tools.description: List root OneNote sections for a user, defaulting to the signed-in user.

tools.name: Resolve SharePoint site by URL
tools.description: Resolve a SharePoint site URL or hostname and path to a Microsoft Graph site resource. Use this when the user provides a SharePoint URL and a site ID is needed for OneNote notebook discovery.

tools.name: Search SharePoint sites
tools.description: Search SharePoint sites available through Microsoft Graph. Use this to find a site ID from a site name or keyword before listing site-hosted OneNote notebooks. Microsoft Graph site search does not support $count; page only with returned @odata.nextLink URLs.

tools.name: Update my OneNote page content
tools.description: Update the content of a OneNote page for the signed-in user. Sends a PATCH request with patch content commands to modify the HTML structure of a OneNote page. Supports appending children, inserting siblings, replacing elements, and prepending content. Use this action when you need to update or modify the content of an existing OneNote page owned by the signed-in user, such as adding new paragraphs, inserting images, modifying lists, or replacing existing elements. Repeating append, prepend, or insert commands can add duplicate content.

tools.name: Update my OneNote section
tools.description: Updates the navigation property sections in me. Use when you need to modify properties of an existing OneNote section, such as renaming it, within the current user's notebooks. This action uses a PATCH request to update the section entity at the specified path. Use this action when you need to update a specific OneNote section owned by the authenticated user, such as changing its display name. This operation modifies the specified properties while preserving all other existing values. Note: Only the displayName property can be updated via this endpoint. Other properties like isDefault, createdDateTime, etc. are read-only. This PATCH operation is provider-undocumented; its behavior is live-observed.

tools.name: Update OneNote page content
tools.description: Update the content of a OneNote page within a Microsoft 365 group using HTML patch commands. Use this action when you need to modify the content of an existing OneNote page, such as replacing text, inserting new content, or appending elements. The action supports multiple patch commands in a single request. The API returns 204 No Content on success, meaning no JSON response body is returned.

tools.name: Update section in site notebook
tools.description: Canonical action for updating a OneNote section in a SharePoint site. Use this action when you need to modify properties of an existing section, such as renaming it. This action uses a PATCH request to update the section entity at the specified path within the site's notebook hierarchy. Note: Only the displayName property of a section can be updated via this endpoint. Other properties like createdDateTime, isDefault, etc. are read-only. This PATCH operation is provider-undocumented; its behavior is live-observed.

tools.name: Update site OneNote page content
tools.description: Update the content of a OneNote page within a SharePoint site. Sends a PATCH request with patch content commands to modify the HTML structure of a OneNote page. Supports appending children, inserting siblings, replacing elements, and prepending content. Use this action when you need to update or modify the content of an existing OneNote page within a SharePoint site, such as adding new paragraphs, inserting images, modifying lists, or replacing existing elements. Repeating append, prepend, or insert commands can add duplicate content.

tools.name: Update site section group section
tools.description: Compatibility alias for updating a OneNote section in a SharePoint site. Prefer UpdateSiteNotebooksSections for new site calls. Legacy notebook and section-group context does not affect the Graph route. Use this action when you need to modify properties of an existing OneNote section, such as updating its display name. This action uses a PATCH request to update the section entity at the specified path within the SharePoint site's notebook hierarchy. Note: Only the displayName property can be updated via this endpoint. Other properties are read-only. This PATCH operation is provider-undocumented; its behavior is live-observed.

tools.name: Update section in user notebook
tools.description: Updates a OneNote section within a user's notebook. Use this action when you need to modify properties of an existing OneNote section, such as renaming it, for a specific user identified by their Microsoft Graph user ID. This action uses a PATCH request to update the section entity at the specified path within the user's notebook hierarchy. Note: Only the displayName property can be updated via this endpoint. Other properties like isDefault, createdDateTime, etc. are read-only. This PATCH operation is provider-undocumented; its behavior is live-observed.

tools.name: Validate OneNote credentials
tools.description: Validates OneNote API credentials by attempting to access the user's notebooks. Use this action when you need to verify that the provided authentication token has valid permissions to access Microsoft OneNote. This action makes a lightweight API call to confirm the credentials work before performing other operations.

required.name: client_id
required.description: Client id of the app

required.name: client_secret
required.description: Client secret of the app

optional.name: oauth_redirect_uri
optional.description: Add this Redirect URL to your app's OAuth allow list.

optional.name: scopes
optional.description: Scopes to request from the user, comma separated

optional.name: microsoft_cloud
optional.description: Microsoft cloud containing the Entra app registration. Use "global" for commercial Microsoft 365 or "gcc_high" for Microsoft 365 US Government GCC High.

optional.name: issuer
optional.description: Optional Microsoft Entra tenant alias, tenant ID, or tenant domain used to target a specific tenant instead of /common.

name: Microsoft Power Bi
description: Microsoft Power BI is a business analytics service that provides interactive visualizations and business intelligence capabilities with an interface simple enough for end users to create their own reports and dashboards.

tools.name: Add Dashboard to Workspace
tools.description: Creates a new empty dashboard in the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to create a new dashboard in a Power BI workspace. The API call can be called by a service principal profile. Requires the Workspace.ReadWrite.All scope. Note: The created dashboard will be empty and can be populated with tiles afterward using other APIs.

tools.name: Get Reports From App
tools.description: Returns a list of reports from the specified app. Use this action when you need to retrieve all reports that belong to a specific Power BI app. This is useful for exploring app contents, finding specific reports within apps, or managing app resources. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All Limitations: Service principal authentication isn't supported.

tools.name: Assign Workspace to Capacity
tools.description: Assigns the specified workspace to the specified capacity. Use this action when you need to assign a Power BI workspace to a dedicated capacity or unassign My workspace from a capacity by providing an empty GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). This operation is typically performed by Fabric administrators to manage workspace capacity assignments. Note: The user must have appropriate permissions (Capacity.ReadWrite.All or workspace admin rights).

tools.name: Cancel Dataset Refresh in Workspace
tools.description: Cancels the specified refresh operation for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to cancel an in-progress dataset refresh operation within a specific Power BI workspace. This is useful for stopping long-running refreshes that are no longer needed or that appear to be stuck. Note that only refresh operations with status of Unknown or Queued can be canceled. Once a refresh has started processing, it cannot be cancelled. This action is irreversible - once a refresh is successfully cancelled, it cannot be resumed and must be triggered again manually. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Clone Report
tools.description: Clones the specified report from My workspace. If the dataset for a cloned report resides in two different workspaces or in My workspace, then a shared dataset is created. Use when you need to duplicate a report within My workspace or to another workspace. This is useful for creating backup copies of reports, testing modifications without affecting the original, or preparing reports for different audiences. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Clone Report in Workspace
tools.description: Clones the specified report from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to duplicate a Power BI report within the same workspace or to a different workspace. If the dataset for a cloned report resides in two different workspaces or in My workspace, then a share is required. The API returns the cloned report with a new ID. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Create Goal Value Check-in
tools.description: Creates a new goal value check-in for a Power BI scorecard goal. Use this action when you need to record a new value check-in for a specific goal within a Power BI scorecard. This action allows you to update the current value, target, status, trend, and forecast of a goal. The timestamp is required and represents the UTC time of the check-in. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Create Workspace
tools.description: Creates a new workspace in Power BI. Use this action when you need to create a new Power BI workspace to organize reports, dashboards, datasets, and other Power BI content. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Requires the Workspace.ReadWrite.All scope. Note: The created workspace will be empty and may require additional configuration such as assigning capacity or adding members.

tools.name: Create Push Dataset
tools.description: Creates a new dataset on My workspace in Power BI. Use this action when you need to create a new push dataset to store and manage data that can be pushed programmatically via the Power BI REST API. This API call only supports push datasets (Push, Streaming, or PushStreaming mode). This action is irreversible once the dataset is created. The dataset name must be unique within the workspace.

tools.name: Create Scorecard
tools.description: Creates a new scorecard in the specified Power BI workspace. Use this action when you need to create a new scorecard to track business objectives and key results in a specific Power BI workspace. Scorecards help organizations monitor progress toward goals with customizable metrics, status rules, and reporting. Requires the Dataset.ReadWrite.All scope. This action is irreversible once the scorecard is created. The scorecard name must be unique within the workspace.

tools.name: Create Temporary Upload Location
tools.description: Creates a temporary blob storage upload location for importing large Power BI .pbix files that are between 1 GB and 10 GB in size. Use this action when you need to upload a large Power BI .pbix file (between 1 GB and 10 GB) to the organization. The temporary upload location provides a shared access signature (SAS) URL where the file can be uploaded before being imported into Power BI. After uploading to the temporary location, you would use the regular import API to complete the import process. This action creates an upload location at the organization level (myorg), not a specific workspace. To upload to a specific workspace, use CreateTemporaryUploadLocationInGroup instead. Required Scope: Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Create Temporary Upload Location
tools.description: Creates a temporary blob storage upload location for importing large Power BI .pbix files that are between 1 GB and 10 GB in size. Use this action when you need to upload a large Power BI .pbix file (between 1 GB and 10 GB) to a workspace. The temporary upload location provides a shared access signature (SAS) URL where the file can be uploaded before being imported into Power BI. After uploading to the temporary location, you would use the regular import API to complete the import process. Required Scope: Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Dashboard
tools.description: Deletes the specified dashboard from My workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a dashboard from a user's Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the dashboard and all its content cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dashboard.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Dataflow
tools.description: Deletes the specified dataflow from Power BI data prep storage, including its definition file and model. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a dataflow from a Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the dataflow and all its associated data cannot be recovered. Permissions: The user must have administrator rights or the caller must be a service principal.

tools.name: Delete Dataset
tools.description: Deletes the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a dataset from a user's Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the dataset and all its associated data cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Dataset from Workspace
tools.description: Deletes the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a dataset from a specific Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the dataset and all its associated data cannot be recovered. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Goal
tools.description: Deletes a goal from a scorecard by goal ID. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a goal from a Power BI scorecard. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the goal and its associated data cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Goal Note by ID
tools.description: Deletes a goal value check-in note by its unique identifier. Use this action when you need to remove a specific check-in note from a goal value in Power BI goals. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the note cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Goal Status Rules
tools.description: Removes status rule definitions from a goal. Use this action when you need to remove all status rules from a specific goal within a Power BI scorecard. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the status rules and their configuration cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Pipeline User
tools.description: Removes user permissions from the specified deployment pipeline. Use this action when you need to revoke a user's access to a deployment pipeline. This action is irreversible — once removed, the user loses access to the pipeline. Required Scope: Pipeline.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Report from Workspace
tools.description: Deletes the specified report from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a report from a specific Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the report and all its content cannot be recovered. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Rows from Dataset Table
tools.description: Deletes all rows from the specified table within the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to clear all data from a specific table within a Power BI push dataset. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the rows cannot be recovered. This operation is commonly used to reset test data or prepare a table for fresh data ingestion. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Rows from Dataset Table in Workspace
tools.description: Deletes all rows from the specified table within the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to clear all data from a specific table within a Power BI push dataset in a specific workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the rows cannot be recovered. This operation is commonly used to reset test data or prepare a table for fresh data ingestion in a workspace context. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Scorecard By ID
tools.description: Deletes a scorecard by its ID from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a scorecard from a Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the scorecard and all its data cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Delete Workspace
tools.description: Deletes the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to permanently remove a Power BI workspace. This action is irreversible — once deleted, the workspace and all its content (reports, dashboards, datasets) cannot be recovered. Required Scope: Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Discover Gateways for Dataset
tools.description: Returns a list of gateways that the specified dataset from the specified workspace can be bound to. Use this action when you need to discover which on-premises data gateways are available to bind a dataset to for refresh and data source connections. This API call is only relevant for datasets that have at least one binding to an on-premises data source. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Execute DAX Queries
tools.description: Executes Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) queries against the provided dataset in My workspace. Use this action when you need to run DAX queries to retrieve or analyze data from a Power BI dataset. This endpoint supports complex DAX queries with multiple EVALUATE statements and includes features for Row-Level Security (RLS), culture-specific formatting, and custom data injection. The response is returned in Apache Arrow format and contains the query results in a columnar format. Use pyarrow or similar libraries to parse the response. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All Important: This API is only available for datasets hosted on a capacity. Datasets with live connections to Azure Analysis Services or on-premises models are not supported. There's a limit of 120 query requests per minute per user.

tools.name: Execute DAX Queries on Dataset
tools.description: Executes Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) queries against the specified Power BI dataset. Use this action when you need to run DAX queries to retrieve data, perform calculations, or analyze data directly from a Power BI dataset. DAX query errors (such as syntax errors or invalid references) will result in an error response. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Execute Subscription
tools.description: Executes the Subscription specified by the Id. Use this action when you need to manually trigger a Power BI email subscription to run immediately instead of waiting for its scheduled frequency. This is useful for testing subscriptions, generating reports on-demand, or forcing an unscheduled distribution of a report. Note: The API returns 204 No Content on success with an empty body.

tools.name: Generate Dashboard Embed Token
tools.description: Generates an embed token to view or edit the specified dashboard from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to generate an embed token to embed a Power BI dashboard in your application. The token allows you to embed the dashboard with the specified access level. You can also configure row-level security (RLS) by providing identities. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Generate Embed Token for Power BI
tools.description: Generates an embed token for multiple reports, datasets, and target workspaces. Use this action when you need to generate an embed token to embed Power BI reports, dashboards, or visuals in your application. Reports and datasets do not have to be related. The token can include identities for row-level security (RLS) and single sign-on (SSO) data sources.

tools.name: Generate Report Embed Token in Group
tools.description: Generates an embed token to view or edit the specified report from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to generate an embed token to embed a Power BI report in your application. The token allows you to control the access level (View, Edit, or Create) for the embedded report. You can also configure row-level security (RLS) by providing identities, customize the token lifetime, and enable the allowSaveAs option for saving embedded reports as new reports. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Generate Dataset Embed Token in Group
tools.description: Generates an embed token based on the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to generate an embed token to embed Power BI reports or dashboards using a specific dataset from a workspace in your application. The token allows you to control the access level (View, Edit, or Create) for the embedded content. You can also configure row-level security (RLS) by providing identities, and customize the token lifetime. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Available Feature By Name
tools.description: Returns the specified available feature for the user by name. Use this action when you need to check the availability and status of a specific Power BI feature, such as embedTrial. This API call doesn't require any scopes. Note: The featureName path parameter should be URL-encoded if it contains special characters.

tools.name: Get Capacities
tools.description: Returns a list of Power BI capacities that the authenticated user has access to. Use this action to retrieve information about all available capacities in the organization, including their state, SKU, region, and access permissions. This is useful for admin operations and capacity management tasks. Permissions: Requires one of the following scopes: Capacity.Read.All or Capacity.ReadWrite.All. This API call can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Dashboard from My Workspace
tools.description: Returns the specified dashboard from My workspace. Use when you need to retrieve details about a specific dashboard from the current user's personal workspace in Power BI. This is useful for getting dashboard metadata, embed URLs, or user permissions. Required Scope: Dashboard.ReadWrite.All or Dashboard.Read.All

tools.name: Get Dashboards
tools.description: Returns a list of dashboards from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all dashboards within a Power BI workspace. This is useful for exploring workspace contents, finding specific dashboard IDs, or managing dashboard resources. Permissions: This API call can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Dataflows
tools.description: Returns a list of all dataflows from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all dataflows within a specific Power BI workspace. This is useful for inventory, monitoring, or managing dataflows within a workspace. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataflow.Read.All or Dataflow.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Dataset
tools.description: Returns the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI dataset in your workspace, including its configuration, permissions, and relationships to other artifacts like dataflows and tables. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Dataset in Workspace
tools.description: Returns the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI dataset in a workspace, including its configuration, permissions, and relationships to other artifacts like dataflows and tables. Permissions: This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get DataSet Data
tools.description: Gets the query results for the specified DataSet. Use when you need to retrieve the actual data values from a Power BI DataSet, such as for exporting data, generating reports outside of Power BI, or performing data analysis on dataset contents. This action executes a query against the dataset and returns the column definitions and row data. Use the optional parameters to filter or customize the query results.

tools.name: Get Datasets from My Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of datasets from My workspace. Use when you need to retrieve all datasets available in the authenticated user's personal workspace, including their configuration and metadata. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get DataSets from Power BI
tools.description: Gets an array of DataSet CatalogItems from Power BI. Use when you need to retrieve all available datasets from the Power BI service, including their metadata such as creation date, modified date, owner, and dataset-specific properties like query timeout and parameters. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Dataset to Dataflows Links
tools.description: Returns a list of upstream dataflows for datasets from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve the relationships between datasets and their upstream dataflows in a Power BI workspace for dependency analysis or lineage tracking. This API call can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Dataset Users
tools.description: Returns a list of principals that have access to the specified dataset. Use this action when you need to retrieve the list of users or service principals who have been granted access to a specific Power BI dataset. This is useful for auditing dataset permissions, managing access control, or understanding who can view or modify the dataset. Note: When user permissions to a dataset have been recently updated, the new permissions might not be immediately available.

tools.name: Get Dataset Users In Group
tools.description: Returns a list of principals that have access to the specified dataset within a workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve the list of users or service principals who have been granted access to a specific Power BI dataset within a workspace. This is useful for auditing dataset permissions, managing access control, or understanding who can view or modify the dataset in a group context. Note: When user permissions to a dataset have been recently updated, the new permissions might not be immediately available.

tools.name: Get Datasources for Dataset
tools.description: Returns a list of data sources for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use when you need to retrieve all data source connections configured for a specific Power BI dataset, such as when auditing data sources, troubleshooting refresh issues, or understanding dataset dependencies. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Datasources for Dataset in Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of data sources for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use when you need to retrieve all data source connections configured for a specific Power BI dataset within a workspace, such as when auditing data sources, troubleshooting refresh issues, or understanding dataset dependencies. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Gateway
tools.description: Returns the specified gateway. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI gateway, including its status, type, and public key for encryption. Permissions: The user must have gateway admin permissions. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Gateway Datasources in Group
tools.description: Returns a list of gateway data sources for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all gateway data source connections configured for a specific Power BI dataset within a workspace.
