This is useful for auditing data source configurations, troubleshooting refresh issues, or understanding dataset dependencies. This API is deprecated - use Get Datasources In Group instead.

tools.name: Get Gateways
tools.description: Returns a list of gateways for which the user is an admin. Use this action when you need to retrieve all Power BI gateways that you have administrative permissions for. This is useful for monitoring gateway status, managing data sources, or administering on-premises data gateway configurations. Gateway admin permissions are required to access this endpoint.

tools.name: Get Goals from Scorecard
tools.description: Returns a list of goals from a scorecard. Use this action when you need to retrieve all goals defined within a Power BI scorecard. This is useful for understanding the organizational objectives and key results (OKRs) tracked in Power BI, finding specific goal IDs, or monitoring progress against targets. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Goals Refresh History
tools.description: Reads refresh history of a connected goal. Use this action when you need to retrieve the refresh history for a specific Power BI goal to monitor refresh performance, identify failed refreshes, or audit refresh operations on goals. This endpoint is part of the Power BI Goals (Preview) API. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All Note: This is a preview API and may be subject to changes.

tools.name: Get Goals Status Rules
tools.description: Returns status rules of a goal. Use this action when you need to retrieve the status rules configuration for a specific Power BI goal within a scorecard. Status rules determine how goal status is calculated based on conditions (e.g., if actual value > 50% of target, status is "On track"). This action supports reading both simple expression-based conditions and complex field comparison conditions. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Goal Value By ID
tools.description: Reads a goal value check-in by a UTC date timestamp. Use this action when you need to retrieve a specific goal value check-in from a Power BI scorecard. This is useful for tracking historical goal values, reviewing notes on goal progress, or analyzing trends. The timestamp must be provided in UTC format (e.g., 2024-05-12T00:00:00Z). Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Groups
tools.description: Returns a list of workspaces the user has access to. Use this action when you need to retrieve all Power BI workspaces (groups) that the authenticated user has access to. This is useful for listing available workspaces, finding specific workspace IDs, or managing workspace resources. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Workspace.Read.All or Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Groups Capacity Assignment Status
tools.description: Gets the status of the assignment-to-capacity operation for the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to check the current status of a workspace assignment operation to a capacity. This is useful for monitoring long-running workspace migrations or diagnosing failed assignments. Required Scope: Workspace.Read.All or Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Group Users
tools.description: Returns a list of users that have access to the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve the list of users or service principals who have been granted access to a specific Power BI workspace. This is useful for auditing workspace permissions, managing access control, or understanding who can view or modify the workspace contents. Permissions: This API call can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Import
tools.description: Returns the specified import from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific import in your Power BI workspace, including its status, associated datasets, and reports. This is useful for tracking import operations, checking whether an import succeeded or failed, and identifying related artifacts. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Imports from My Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of imports from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all imports in the authenticated user's personal workspace, including their status, associated datasets, and reports. This is useful for monitoring import operations, checking import completion status, or listing imported content in your workspace. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Imports in Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of imports from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all imports in a Power BI workspace to monitor import status, list imported datasets and reports, or check for failed imports. This API can be called by a service principal profile with appropriate workspace permissions.

tools.name: Get Linked Report History Snapshot
tools.description: Gets requested HistorySnapshot item specified by HistoryId of the LinkedReport specified by Id. Use this action when you need to retrieve a specific history snapshot for a Power BI LinkedReport. History snapshots capture the state of a report at a particular point in time and can be used for auditing, versioning, or recovery purposes. This is a read-only operation that returns snapshot metadata including creation date, snapshot ID, and size information.

tools.name: Get Report Page
tools.description: Returns the specified page within the specified report from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific page within a Power BI report. This is useful for exploring report structure, getting page metadata, or identifying the order of pages in a report. Permissions: This API call can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Pages from Report
tools.description: Returns a list of pages within the specified report from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all pages in a Power BI report to understand the report structure, navigate between pages, or manage report content. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Get Pages from Report in My Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of pages within the specified report from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all pages in a Power BI report that belongs to your personal workspace. This is useful for understanding the report structure, navigating between pages, or managing report content. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Get Dataset Parameters
tools.description: Returns a list of parameters for the specified dataset from **My workspace**. Use this action when you need to retrieve all parameter definitions and their current values for a Power BI dataset, including whether each parameter is required, its data type, and any suggested values. This is useful for auditing dataset configuration, understanding data source connections, or preparing to update parameter values. Required Scope: Dataset.Read

tools.name: Get Dataset Parameters in Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of parameters for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all parameter definitions and their current values for a Power BI dataset within a specific workspace, including whether each parameter is required, its data type, and any suggested values. This is useful for auditing dataset configuration, understanding data source connections, or preparing to update parameter values in a workspace context. This API call can be called by a service principal profile with appropriate workspace permissions. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Query Scale Out Sync Status
tools.description: Returns the query scale-out sync status for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to check the synchronization status of read-only replicas for a dataset that supports query scale-out. This includes information about commit versions, active read timestamps, and the current sync status. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Refreshable For Capacity
tools.description: Returns the specified refreshable for the specified capacity that the user has access to. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific refreshable item (dataset) within a capacity, including refresh history, schedules, and status. Power BI retains a seven-day refresh history for each dataset, up to a maximum of sixty refreshes. Required Scope: Capacity.Read.All or Capacity.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get refreshables for all capacities
tools.description: Returns a list of refreshables for all capacities that the user has access to. Use when you need to retrieve information about datasets and dataflows that have refresh schedules or refresh history across all Power BI capacities. Power BI retains a seven-day refresh history for each dataset, up to a maximum of sixty refreshes. This action is useful for monitoring refresh performance, identifying failed refreshes, and auditing refresh schedules across the organization.

tools.name: Get Refresh Execution Details In Group
tools.description: Returns execution details of a refresh operation for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve detailed information about a dataset refresh operation within a workspace, including timing, status, errors, and any retry attempts. This is useful for monitoring refresh operations, troubleshooting failed refreshes, and auditing refresh history. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Refresh History for Dataset
tools.description: Returns the refresh history for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use when you need to retrieve the refresh history of a specific Power BI dataset to monitor refresh performance, identify failed refreshes, or audit refresh operations. Power BI retains between 20-60 available refresh history entries depending on the number of refreshes in the last 3 days. The most recent 60 entries are kept if they are all less than 3 days old. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All Note: OneDrive refresh history isn't returned by this endpoint.

tools.name: Get Dataset Refresh Schedule
tools.description: Returns the refresh schedule for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use when you need to retrieve the current refresh schedule configuration for a dataset, including the days, times, and notification settings. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Refresh Schedule In Group 2
tools.description: Returns the refresh schedule for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve the current refresh schedule configuration for a dataset within a specific Power BI workspace, including the days, times, and notification settings. This action is read-only and idempotent. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All Note: This API can be called by a service principal profile.

tools.name: Get Report from My Workspace
tools.description: Returns the specified report from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI report from your personal workspace, including its metadata, embed URL, ownership information, and associated dataset. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Get Report Page From My Workspace
tools.description: Returns the specified page within the specified report from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific page within a Power BI report in your personal workspace. This is useful for exploring report structure, getting page metadata, or identifying the order of pages in a report. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Get Reports
tools.description: Gets an array of Report CatalogItems from Power BI. Use this action when you need to retrieve all reports available in the Power BI service. This is useful for browsing the report catalog, finding specific reports, or auditing available resources. The endpoint supports OData query parameters for filtering, sorting, and pagination. Required Scope: Report.Read.All or Report.ReadWrite.All Note: This endpoint uses the v2.0 Power BI Report Server API path.

tools.name: Get Reports From My Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of reports from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all reports from your personal Power BI workspace. This also returns shared reports and reports from shared apps. This is useful for exploring your personal workspace contents, finding specific report IDs, or managing report resources. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All Note: Service principal authentication isn't supported.

tools.name: Get Resources
tools.description: Gets an array of Resource catalog items. Use this action when you need to retrieve all Power BI resources from the catalog. This is useful for exploring available resources, finding specific resource IDs, or managing resource content. Note: This endpoint uses the Power BI REST API (cloud service).

tools.name: Get Scorecard By ID
tools.description: Returns a scorecard with the specified ID. Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI scorecard within a workspace, including its goals, metrics, and configuration. This action supports optional OData expansion for including related data like goals, goal values, aggregations, and notes in the response. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Scorecards
tools.description: Returns a list of scorecards from a workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all scorecards within a Power BI workspace. This is useful for exploring workspace goals, finding specific scorecard IDs, or managing scorecard resources. Required Scope: Dataset.Read.All or Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Tables in Dataset
tools.description: Returns a list of tables within the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve the schema, columns, measures, and other structural metadata of tables within a Power BI dataset. This is useful for understanding the data model, exploring available fields, or preparing to write DAX expressions. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All

tools.name: Get Tables in Dataset within Workspace
tools.description: Returns a list of tables within the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use when you need to retrieve the schema, columns, measures, and other structural metadata of tables within a Power BI dataset in a specific workspace. This is useful for understanding the data model, exploring available fields, or preparing to write DAX expressions. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All or Dataset.Read.All Note: This API only supports push datasets.

tools.name: Get Tiles from My Workspace Dashboard
tools.description: Returns a list of tiles within the specified dashboard from My workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all tiles (visualizations) from a specific dashboard in My workspace. Supported tiles include datasets and live tiles that contain an entire report page. This is useful for understanding what content exists in a dashboard or for enumerating dashboard elements. Required Scope: Dashboard.Read.All or Dashboard.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Tiles from Workspace Dashboard
tools.description: Returns a list of tiles within the specified dashboard from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to retrieve all tiles (visualizations) from a specific dashboard within a Power BI workspace. Supported tiles include datasets and live tiles that contain an entire report page. This is useful for understanding what content exists in a dashboard or for enumerating dashboard elements. Required Scope: Dashboard.Read.All or Dashboard.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Get Workspace
tools.description: Returns a specified workspace (group). Use this action when you need to retrieve details about a specific Power BI workspace, including its name, capacity configuration, storage settings, and Log Analytics workspace integration. Permissions: This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Workspace.Read.All or Workspace.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Trigger Query Scale Out Sync in Workspace
tools.description: Triggers a query scale-out sync of read-only replicas for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to manually synchronize read-only replicas for a dataset in a specific Power BI workspace. This is typically used for maintenance or to ensure all replicas are synchronized before performing administrative operations. The sync operation ensures that read-only replicas have the latest data from the primary dataset. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Move Power BI Scorecard Goals
tools.description: Moves goals within the scorecard. Changes their ranks and parents. Use when you need to reorganize the goal hierarchy in a Power BI scorecard, such as reordering goals within the same parent, moving a goal to a different parent, or repositioning a goal among its siblings. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Patch Goal Note
tools.description: Updates a goal value check-in note by ID. Use this action when you need to update the content of an existing goal check-in note in Power BI goals. This action modifies the note body while preserving other note metadata like timestamps and IDs. This is useful for correcting errors, adding additional context, or updating progress notes on goals. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Patch Goal Value By ID
tools.description: Updates a goal value check-in by a UTC date timestamp. Use this action when you need to update the value, status, target, or other properties of a specific goal value check-in within a Power BI scorecard. This allows you to record progress updates for goals at specific timestamps. Requires the Dataset.ReadWrite.All scope. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Patch Scorecard By ID
tools.description: Updates a scorecard by its ID. Use this action when you need to modify properties of an existing Power BI scorecard, such as updating its name, description, permissions, or associated settings. This action requires the Dataset.ReadWrite.All scope. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Create Push Dataset in Workspace
tools.description: Creates a new push dataset in the specified Power BI workspace. Use this action when you need to create a new push dataset in a specific workspace to store and manage data that can be pushed programmatically via the Power BI REST API. This API call only supports push datasets (Push, Streaming, or PushStreaming mode). This action is irreversible once the dataset is created. The dataset name must be unique within the workspace.

tools.name: Grant Dataset User Permissions
tools.description: Grants the specified user's permissions to the specified dataset. Use this action when you need to assign access rights to a Power BI dataset for a specific user, group, or app. This is useful for managing dataset permissions and controlling who can access or interact with the dataset. Note: When user permissions to a dataset have been recently updated, the new permissions might not be immediately available.

tools.name: Grant Dataset User Permissions In Group
tools.description: Grants the specified user's permissions to the specified dataset in a workspace. Use this action when you need to assign access rights to a Power BI dataset for a specific user, group, or app within a workspace context. This is useful for managing dataset permissions and controlling who can access or interact with the dataset. Note: When user permissions to a dataset have been recently updated, the new permissions might not be immediately available. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Post Goal
tools.description: Adds a new goal to a Power BI scorecard. Use this action when you need to create a new goal within an existing scorecard to track objectives, KPIs, or other metrics. Goals can be organized in a parent-child hierarchy and support various formatting options for dates and values. Requires the Dataset.ReadWrite.All scope. Note: The goal will be created with default values that may need to be updated via additional API calls for detailed configuration.

tools.name: Post Goal Note
tools.description: Adds a new note to a goal value check-in for a Power BI scorecard goal. Use this action when you need to add a note or comment to a specific goal value check-in within a Power BI scorecard. This allows you to provide additional context or explanations for goal progress updates. The timestamp parameter identifies the specific goal value check-in to attach the note to. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Add Rows to Dataset Table in Workspace
tools.description: Adds new data rows to the specified table within the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to push new data rows into a Power BI push dataset table. This action is idempotent — pushing the same rows multiple times will add duplicate data. The dataset must be a push dataset (Push, Streaming, or PushStreaming mode) with the Add Rows API enabled. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Post Goal Status Rules
tools.description: Creates or updates status rules of a goal in Power BI. Use this action when you need to define custom status rules that automatically set a goal's status based on conditions such as current value, threshold comparisons, or state values. The defaultOutput is used when no rule conditions are met. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Table Schema
tools.description: Updates the metadata and schema for the specified table within the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to modify the schema or metadata of an existing table in a Power BI push dataset. This includes updating columns, adding measures, or changing table properties. The table must already exist in the dataset. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Table Schema in Workspace
tools.description: Updates the metadata and schema for the specified table within the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to modify the schema or metadata of an existing table in a Power BI push dataset within a workspace. This includes updating columns, adding measures, or changing table properties. The table must already exist in the dataset. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Rebind Report to Dataset
tools.description: Rebinds the specified report from the specified workspace to the specified dataset. Use this action when you need to change which dataset a Power BI report uses. This is useful for migrating reports to different datasets, connecting reports to updated data sources, or consolidating multiple reports under a single dataset. If the target dataset resides in a different workspace than the report, a shared dataset will be automatically created in the report's workspace. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Trigger Dataset Refresh in Workspace
tools.description: Triggers a refresh for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to manually trigger a dataset refresh in a Power BI workspace. An enhanced refresh is triggered only if a request payload other than notifyOption is set (e.g., when specifying specific tables, commit mode, or timeout). Note: This action is asynchronous - it initiates the refresh and returns immediately. Use GetRefreshHistory or GetRefreshExecutionDetails to monitor the refresh status. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All This action is not destructive - it initiates a refresh operation that can be monitored and cancelled if needed.

tools.name: Generate Report Embed Token for Create in Group
tools.description: Generates an embed token to allow report creation in the specified workspace based on the specified dataset. Use this action when you need to generate an embed token to create a new Power BI report within a specific workspace. The token is based on a dataset and allows programmatic report creation through the Power BI API. You can configure row-level security (RLS) by providing identities, and customize the token lifetime. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All or Report.Read.All

tools.name: Set Linked Report Cache Options
tools.description: Replaces the CacheOption's content for a given LinkedReport using the provided definition. Use this action when you need to configure or update the cache settings for a Power BI linked report. This includes setting the execution type (Live, Cache, or Snapshot) and optionally configuring cache expiration. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Take Over Dataset
tools.description: Transfers ownership over the specified dataset to the current authorized user. Use this action when you need to take over ownership of a dataset in a Power BI workspace. This is useful when the original owner has left the organization or is unavailable, and another user needs to manage the dataset. This API call can be called by a service principal profile. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Take Over Paginated Report Ownership
tools.description: Transfers ownership of the data sources for the specified paginated report (RDL) to the current authorized user. Use this action when you need to take ownership of a paginated report's data sources in a Power BI workspace. This is useful when the previous owner is no longer available or you need administrative control over the report's data connections. This operation affects all data sources associated with the report. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Trigger Query Scale Out Sync
tools.description: Triggers a query scale-out sync of read-only replicas for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to manually synchronize read-only replicas for a dataset that supports query scale-out. This is typically used for maintenance or to ensure all replicas are synchronized before performing administrative operations. The sync operation ensures that read-only replicas have the latest data from the primary dataset. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Dataset
tools.description: Updates the properties for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to modify dataset settings such as query scale-out configuration or storage mode. The user must be the dataset owner to perform this operation. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Dataset In Workspace
tools.description: Updates the properties for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to modify dataset settings in a workspace, such as configuring query scale-out settings or changing the storage mode. The user must be the dataset owner to perform this operation. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Paginated Report Data Sources
tools.description: Updates the data sources of the specified paginated report (RDL) from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to update the connection details (server, database) for one or more data sources in a Power BI paginated report within a specific workspace. This is useful for migrating paginated reports between environments (e.g., from development to production) or updating connection strings without republishing the report. [!IMPORTANT] Both the original data source and the new data source must have the exact same schema. Important notes: - Only supports paginated reports (RDL). - Both the original and new data sources must have the exact same schema. - Changing the data source type is not supported. - Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) data sources are not supported. - The user must be the data source owner. Required scope: Reports.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Patch Goal By ID
tools.description: Updates a goal by its ID within a Power BI scorecard. Use this action when you need to modify properties of an existing goal in a Power BI scorecard, such as updating its name, description, dates, permissions, or associated settings. This action requires the Dataset.ReadWrite.All scope. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Dataset Parameters in Workspace
tools.description: Updates the parameters values for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to change one or more parameter values in a Power BI dataset that resides in a specific workspace. This is commonly used after updating underlying data sources or to modify dataset configuration without redeploying. [!NOTE] We recommend using enhanced dataset metadata with this API call.

tools.name: Update Refresh Schedule
tools.description: Updates the refresh schedule for the specified dataset from My workspace. Use this action when you need to configure or modify the automatic refresh schedule for a Power BI dataset, such as enabling/disabling scheduled refresh, setting refresh days and times, or configuring failure notifications. A request that disables the refresh schedule should contain no other changes. This action is idempotent. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Refresh Schedule In Group
tools.description: Updates the refresh schedule for the specified dataset from the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to configure or modify the automatic refresh schedule for a Power BI dataset within a workspace, such as enabling/disabling scheduled refresh, setting refresh days and times, or configuring failure notifications. A request that disables the refresh schedule should contain no other changes. This action is idempotent. Required Scope: Dataset.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Report Content
tools.description: Updates the content of the specified report from **My workspace** with the content of a specified source report. Use this action when you need to replace the content of a report in My workspace with content from another report. The target report must be in My workspace. The source report can be from My workspace or another workspace (in which case a share is required). This operation overwrites the target report's content while keeping its ID, name, and other properties. Required Scope: Report.ReadWrite.All

tools.name: Update Workspace
tools.description: Updates the properties for the specified workspace. Use this action when you need to modify workspace settings such as renaming the workspace or changing the default dataset storage format. This action can be called by a service principal profile with appropriate permissions. This action is idempotent - calling it multiple times with the same parameters will have the same effect. Required Scope: Workspace.ReadWrite.All

name: Microsoft PowerPoint
description: Create, find, inspect, fill, edit, format, share, preview, version, copy, upload, download, organize, and delete Microsoft PowerPoint files through Microsoft Graph and OneDrive, including slide, shape, chart, comment, and geometry workflows.

tools.name: Check In Presentation
tools.description: Check in a checked-out PowerPoint DriveItem and make its version available according to the SharePoint/document-library configuration. Microsoft Graph documents no atomic If-Match/eTag option for this operation.

tools.name: Check Out Presentation
tools.description: Check out a PowerPoint DriveItem where its SharePoint/document-library configuration supports checkout, preventing others from editing and hiding changes until check-in. Microsoft Graph documents no atomic If-Match/eTag option for this operation.

tools.name: Copy Presentation
tools.description: Start an asynchronous Microsoft Graph copy of a PowerPoint presentation. A successful result means only that Graph accepted the submission; it does not mean the copy completed or ultimately succeeded. The action never returns the bearer-equivalent Location monitor URL. Discover the result by destination and filename with FIND_PRESENTATIONS. conflict_behavior is unsupported on OneDrive Personal. To preserve all versions, omit name and rename the copy after discovery.

tools.name: Copy Presentation and Wait
tools.description: Submit a PowerPoint presentation copy with a required unique filename, then boundedly search the resolved destination folder for an exact-name candidate. Search results cannot be correlated to the copy request, so a discovered candidate is returned as discovered_unverified and may belong to another writer. The bearer-equivalent Graph monitor URL is never returned or read. An exact-name search result is returned only as an uncorrelated candidate, never as confirmed completion, because Graph's secret monitor URL is not exposed or consumed. A timeout or indeterminate result is not proof of failure: verify the destination before retrying. All-version-history copies require the asynchronous COPY_PRESENTATION workflow because Graph does not safely combine that option with a discovery name.

tools.name: Create Folder
tools.description: Create a folder for PowerPoint files in the current or an explicitly selected accessible drive.

tools.name: Create Presentation
tools.description: Create a bounded macro-free PPTX from one to 50 structured slides containing titles, plain text, nested bullets, rectangular tables, uploaded PNG images, and optional speaker notes. The generated Open XML package, relationships, and semantic readback are validated locally before exactly one Microsoft Graph upload. Limits include 500 content blocks, 500,000 text characters, 10,000 line breaks, 2,000 table cells, and 20 PNGs (10 MiB each, 25 MiB compressed and decoded in aggregate); the final package is limited to 50 MiB.

tools.name: Create Presentation Sharing Link
tools.description: Create or return a view or edit sharing link for a PowerPoint presentation in the current or an explicitly selected drive.

tools.name: Delete Folder
tools.description: Move a folder to the Microsoft Graph recycle bin after a metadata preflight proves the DriveItem has a folder facet. Recycling a nonempty folder removes the entire descendant tree from its current location. Files are rejected. The preflight eTag is used for a concurrency-safe delete when available.

tools.name: Delete Presentation
tools.description: Move a PowerPoint presentation to the Microsoft Graph recycle bin. This action does not permanently erase the file. It can require a matching eTag or cTag and can send Microsoft's documented shared-lock or checkout bypass preferences.

tools.name: Download Presentation
tools.description: Download a PowerPoint file in its original format or export it as PDF or JPG. Export conversion is not presentation editing and accepts source files up to 2 MB.

tools.name: Download Presentation Version
tools.description: Verify that the selected DriveItem is a PPTX, then download one retained previous version as a bounded PPTX file. Non-PPTX items are rejected before content download. Use LIST_PRESENTATION_VERSIONS to obtain a version ID, but do not use its first newest/current entry: Microsoft Graph refuses current-version content here. Use DOWNLOAD_PRESENTATION for the current version.

tools.name: Fill PowerPoint Template
tools.description: Create one presentation from an existing designed PPTX template by replacing unique literal {{tokens}} simultaneously across reachable slides and speaker notes. The template is downloaded and its eTag is rechecked before one create upload; no intermediate provider copy is created. Every requested token must match.

tools.name: Find Presentations
tools.description: List a folder or search a drive and return only PowerPoint files. Omit search_text to browse folder_id; provide it to search the full drive. A page can contain no matching files while has_more remains true.

tools.name: Get Current Drive
tools.description: Return the signed-in user's default OneDrive ID and basic owner, type, and quota details. Use the drive ID to target other accessible-drive actions explicitly.

tools.name: Get Presentation
tools.description: Return metadata for one PowerPoint file by item ID, including its current eTag for concurrency-safe updates.

tools.name: Get Presentation Content
tools.description: Read bounded, text-first semantic content from a current macro-free PPTX, including slides, shapes, text, safe hyperlinks, alt text, image metadata, tables, and speaker notes. Default budgets are 100 slides, 200 shapes per slide, 100 paragraphs per shape, 100 runs per paragraph, 20,000 characters per shape, 100,000 total characters, 5,000 structural elements, and 100 comments per slide. Maxima are respectively 500, 1,000, 500, 500, 100,000, 500,000, 20,000, and 200. For ordinary reads, use slide_numbers for only the needed slides and lower budgets instead of reading a whole large deck. Formatting, geometry, supported chart data, and modern comments are opt-ins. Uses eTag consistency and never returns layouts, package bytes, raw XML, unsafe external targets, or preauthenticated URLs.

tools.name: Get Presentation Layouts
tools.description: Download and validate the current macro-free PPTX, then return its complete bounded slide-layout catalog. Each layout has a unique opaque selector accepted by UPDATE_PRESENTATION_CONTENT add_slide, plus exact human-facing name and matchingName values and safe type/placeholder summaries for duplicate-name disambiguation. Never returns package paths, raw OOXML, package bytes, or download URLs.

tools.name: Get Presentation Preview
tools.description: Deprecated: return short-lived, human-embeddable UI preview material for a SharePoint or OneDrive presentation, including personal OneDrive. It does not return agent-readable slide content. Agents should use GET_PRESENTATION_CONTENT to inspect content, or DOWNLOAD_PRESENTATION with PDF/JPG output for a rendered artifact. The returned URL is caller-only and bearer-equivalent: never share, log, cache, or persist it.

tools.name: Get Presentation Thumbnails
tools.description: List generated thumbnail metadata for a PowerPoint presentation. Microsoft Graph represents only the first slide and can return an empty set; it does not provide per-slide thumbnails. Returned URLs are short-lived bearer-equivalent capabilities for the caller only and must not be shared, logged, cached, or persisted.

tools.name: Get Presentation Version
tools.description: Retrieve compact metadata for one retained or current version of a PowerPoint file. Use List Presentation Versions to discover retained version IDs.

tools.name: Invite People to Presentation
tools.description: Grant named people read or write access to a PowerPoint presentation. By default, send_invitation=true also causes Microsoft to send external invitation emails; set it false to grant permission without notifications. A 207 response preserves recipient-level errors and is never reported as complete success.

tools.name: List Presentation Versions
tools.description: List retained versions of a PowerPoint file in Microsoft Graph's newest-first order, one provider page at a time. Continue while has_more is true before treating the final version as the oldest retained version. The first entry is current: its metadata is readable, but Graph refuses its content through DOWNLOAD_PRESENTATION_VERSION. Choose a later entry for version download/restore, or use DOWNLOAD_PRESENTATION for current content. Version retention depends on the drive's configuration.

tools.name: Replace Presentation File
tools.description: Replace the bytes of an existing PowerPoint DriveItem with a valid, non-macro-enabled PPTX package no larger than 250 MiB, optionally requiring a matching eTag.

tools.name: Restore Presentation Version
tools.description: Restore a retained previous version of a PowerPoint presentation as a new current version while preserving its version history.

tools.name: Transform Presentation Text and Properties
tools.description: Transform text, slide order, or embedded core document properties inside a macro-free PPTX, then conditionally replace the same file. Supports literal, run-normalized text and {{placeholder}} replacement within DrawingML paragraphs, complete slide reordering, and core document-property updates. Provide at least one non-empty text_replacements, slide_order, or core_properties transformation. Rules run sequentially; a find string crosses a line break only when it includes a newline. Use UPDATE_PRESENTATION_METADATA instead to rename or move the DriveItem or change its filesystem metadata. It does not add or delete slides or edit layouts, themes, animations, charts, tables, or images.

tools.name: Update Presentation Content
tools.description: Atomically update one macro-free PPTX under an exact eTag and one conditional upload. Supports slide lifecycle, shape and run edits, comments, native bar/line/pie charts, text boxes, PNG images, speaker notes, and tables. The delete_slide mode permanently removes a slide and eligible private dependencies; delete_shape permanently removes a top-level shape and unreferenced relationships; delete_comment permanently removes a root comment and its replies. Because this compatibility action exposes destructive modes, every call carries the static irreversible-update hint and requires irreversible-update approval, even when its submitted operations do not delete content; inspect targets before approval. Validates the package graph and semantic result. Limits include 50 MiB packages, 100 operations, 500,000 text characters, 20 uploaded PNGs, and 10,000 generated line breaks. Unsupported, shared, external, macro, combo, pivot, grouped, field, or ambiguous mutation targets are rejected before upload.

tools.name: Update Presentation Content Destructively
tools.description: Atomically update one macro-free PPTX with at least one irreversible delete operation, under an exact eTag and one conditional upload. delete_slide permanently removes a slide and eligible private dependencies; delete_shape permanently removes a top-level shape and unreferenced relationships; delete_comment permanently removes a root comment and its replies. Supporting non-delete operations may be included in the same transaction, but every call must contain delete_slide, delete_shape, or delete_comment and requires irreversible-update approval. Validates the package graph and semantic result. Limits include 50 MiB packages, 100 operations, 500,000 text characters, 20 uploaded PNGs, and 10,000 generated line breaks.

tools.name: Update Presentation Content Safely
tools.description: Atomically update one macro-free PPTX without delete operations, under an exact eTag and one conditional upload. Allowed operations are add_text_box, add_image, replace_image, set_existing_speaker_notes, add_table, add_slide, duplicate_slide, set_slide_hidden, set_shape_text, format_text_run, set_shape_bounds, set_shape_alt_text, set_shape_hyperlink, set_text_run_hyperlink, add_comment, reply_comment, add_chart, and replace_chart_data. delete_slide, delete_shape, and delete_comment are rejected during request validation before any network request. Validates the package graph and semantic result. Limits include 50 MiB packages, 100 operations, 500,000 text characters, 20 uploaded PNGs, and 10,000 generated line breaks.

tools.name: Update Presentation Metadata
tools.description: Update Microsoft Graph DriveItem metadata or path only: rename a PowerPoint presentation, move it within its current drive, or set supported filesystem metadata. This action does not edit slide text, slide order, document properties inside the PPTX package, or other presentation content. Optionally require a matching eTag. Provide at least one of name, parent_folder_id, description, created_datetime, or last_modified_datetime. OneDrive may accept a description without persisting it; the response reports that limitation.

tools.name: Upload New Presentation
tools.description: Create a new PPTX in a Microsoft Graph drive folder, with configurable filename-conflict behavior. The file must be a valid, non-macro-enabled PPTX package no larger than 250 MiB.

name: Microsoft To Do
description: Microsoft To Do is a cloud-based task management application that lets users create, organize, and track task lists, tasks, checklist items, and reminders across devices via Microsoft Graph

tools.name: Complete Task
tools.description: Mark a Microsoft To Do task as completed. Convenience wrapper that always PATCHes status='completed'; the server auto-sets completedDateTime. Use Update Task to reopen a task (status='notStarted') or to change other fields.

tools.name: Create Checklist Item
tools.description: Add a checklist item (subtask) to a Microsoft To Do task. Only display_name is required; the created item is returned with a GUID id, displayName, isChecked, and createdDateTime.

tools.name: Create Linked Resource
tools.description: Attach a partner-application link to an existing Microsoft To Do task.

tools.name: Create Task
tools.description: Create a task in a Microsoft To Do task list. Only title is required. Dates are passed as flat ISO-8601 strings plus a shared timezone; the tool builds the Graph dateTimeTimeZone objects. Notes are passed as body_content (+ body_content_type). NOTE: To Do treats due dates as whole days — the time component of due_date_time is normalized to midnight on save.

tools.name: Create Task List
tools.description: Create a new Microsoft To Do task list.

tools.name: Delete Checklist Item
tools.description: Delete a checklist item (subtask) from a Microsoft To Do task. This permanently removes the checklist item (this cannot be undone).

tools.name: Delete Task
tools.description: Delete a task from a Microsoft To Do task list. WARNING: this also permanently removes the task's checklist items and linked resources.

tools.name: Delete Task Attachment
tools.description: Permanently delete a file attachment from a Microsoft To Do task. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: Delete Task List
tools.description: Delete a Microsoft To Do task list. WARNING: this cascades — all tasks in the list and their checklist items are permanently deleted.

tools.name: Download Task Attachment
tools.description: Download one file attached to a Microsoft To Do task. The file is offloaded to storage and returned as a downloadable reference rather than inline base64.

tools.name: Get Checklist Item
tools.description: Get a single Microsoft To Do checklist item (subtask) by its id, within a task in a task list.

tools.name: Get Current User
tools.description: Return the profile of the Microsoft account connected to this toolkit (whoami / connection verification). Useful to confirm which mailbox the To Do tasks belong to before other operations.

tools.name: Get Task
tools.description: Get a single Microsoft To Do task by its id, within a task list. Set include_checklist_items=true to expand its checklist items inline.

tools.name: Get Task Attachment
tools.description: Get metadata for one file attached to a Microsoft To Do task. Use Download Task Attachment to retrieve the file contents.

tools.name: Get Task List
tools.description: Get a single Microsoft To Do task list by its id.

tools.name: List Checklist Items
tools.description: List the checklist items (subtasks) of a To Do task. Auto-paginates so all subtasks are returned at once as {items: [...]}.

tools.name: List Linked Resources
tools.description: List external resources linked to a Microsoft To Do task. Auto-paginates the task's small linked-resource collection and returns all items at once.

tools.name: List Task Attachments
tools.description: List the files attached to a Microsoft To Do task. Returns attachment metadata without file contents, one page at a time, plus a next_cursor.

tools.name: List Task Lists
tools.description: List the To Do task lists owned by the connected user. The built-in default list has wellknown_list_name='defaultList'; user-created lists have wellknown_list_name='none'. Always returns at least the default list. Select the default list by id or wellknown_list_name, never by the localized display_name.

tools.name: List Tasks
tools.description: List the tasks in a To Do task list. Checklist items (subtasks) are NOT returned by default; set include_checklist_items=true to expand them inline. Returns one page of tasks plus a next_cursor for the next page.

tools.name: Sync Task Lists
tools.description: Read one page of Microsoft To Do task-list changes. Continue the current round with next_cursor, or store the terminal delta_token to retrieve only changes from a later round. Removed task lists retain their removal marker.

tools.name: Update Checklist Item
tools.description: Update a checklist item (subtask) of a Microsoft To Do task: rename it (display_name) and/or check/uncheck it (is_checked). Partial update: only the fields you pass are changed; at least one is required. Setting is_checked=true marks the subtask done.

tools.name: Update Task
tools.description: Update fields of an existing Microsoft To Do task (title, notes, importance, status, due/start/reminder dates, categories). Partial update: only the fields you pass are changed; unset fields are left untouched. To mark a task done set status='completed' (or use the dedicated Complete Task tool).

tools.name: Update Task List
tools.description: Rename a Microsoft To Do task list (updates its displayName).

tools.name: Upload Task Attachment
tools.description: Attach a file up to 25 MB to a Microsoft To Do task. The tool automatically uses a single request for files under 3 MB and a chunked upload session for larger files.

name: Microsoft Word
description: Microsoft Word tools for finding, downloading, updating, and managing DOCX files in OneDrive and SharePoint through Microsoft Graph

tools.name: Add Comment
tools.description: Add a Word comment to one exact paragraph selected by text or a READ_DOCX locator.

tools.name: Append Content
tools.description: Append plain text or supported Markdown paragraphs, headings, formatted runs, lists, rectangular tables, safe http/https/mailto links, and Courier New inline or fenced code to a DOCX body.

tools.name: Copy DOCX
tools.description: Copy a Graph item identified as a DOCX by its filename or MIME type to a OneDrive or SharePoint folder, wait boundedly for the asynchronous operation, and return verified destination metadata. The source package bytes are not inspected. If waiting times out, the server-side copy may continue; inspect the destination before retrying to avoid creating another copy.

tools.name: Create DOCX
tools.description: Create a safe DOCX containing styled paragraphs and formatted runs, bullet or decimal lists, rectangular tables, or constrained HTML/Markdown source with safe external links and inline or fenced code rendered in Courier New, plus validated inline PNG/JPEG images, page breaks, and default/first/even headers and footers. Literal content is escaped and raw XML or image URLs are never accepted. The create-only default fails on a filename conflict. overwrite_existing remains available for backward compatibility; prefer UPSERT_DOCX when replacement is intended.

tools.name: Create DOCX sharing link
tools.description: Create a view, edit, or embed sharing link for a verified DOCX. When link_scope is omitted, Graph uses the drive's default scope, which can be anonymous. Returns Graph's capability-bearing URL; treat it as a secret. Sharing can change the document eTag, so call READ_DOCX again before editing. Setting retain_inherited_permissions=false removes all existing permissions when the item is shared for the first time.

tools.name: Delete DOCX
tools.description: Move one DOCX to the provider recycle bin only when its current eTag matches. This action does not bypass shared locks or checked-out state. A successful result does not guarantee permanent erasure.

tools.name: Edit DOCX
tools.description: Atomically edit literal text, paragraphs, independent Latin/non-complex and complex-script run formatting, lists, rectangular tables including plain cells and rows outside merged regions, uploaded inline PNG/JPEG images, semantic comments, tracked text changes, revision acceptance or rejection, safe external hyperlinks, paired footnotes, section headers or footers, and explicit page breaks in a DOCX. Targets are semantic locators from READ_DOCX and remain valid only for its eTag. The complete package is validated before one guarded replacement upload.

tools.name: Export DOCX to PDF
tools.description: Convert a DOCX of at most 2 MB to PDF through Microsoft Graph and return a temporary file reference. The provider's preauthenticated redirect URL is followed internally and is never returned.

tools.name: Fill Template
tools.description: Fill run-spanning placeholders in main-document paragraphs of a validated DOCX template snapshot, then create and return a new document. Strict mode creates only after every requested placeholder is found; non-strict mode can create a partial fill and reports found, filled, and unfilled keys. If post-upload validation fails, the error identifies the retained destination item and gives guarded cleanup guidance.

tools.name: Find DOCX files
tools.description: Browse one folder or search a drive for DOCX files. Browse pages also return folders for navigation. Search results can be eventually consistent; use a direct read action when authoritative current state is required.

tools.name: Find SharePoint sites
tools.description: Find accessible SharePoint sites by keyword, or resolve one known hostname and site path to its site ID.

tools.name: Get Microsoft Word account context
tools.description: Return the signed-in Microsoft identity and primary OneDrive identifiers needed to start OneDrive DOCX work. Microsoft Graph documents that GET /me/drive automatically provisions OneDrive when the delegated user is licensed but does not yet have a drive.

tools.name: Invite DOCX recipients
tools.description: Grant read or write access to required named recipients. send_invitation and require_sign_in are required; emailing an invitation is an irreversible external side effect. Partial success is reported per recipient. Sharing can change the document eTag, so call READ_DOCX again before editing. Setting retain_inherited_permissions=false removes all existing permissions when the item is shared for the first time.

tools.name: List DOCX versions
tools.description: Validate the selected drive item as a DOCX, then return one page of retained versions in Microsoft Graph's newest-first order. Provider download URLs and raw identity objects are omitted.

tools.name: List OneDrive drives
tools.description: Return one page of drives available to the signed-in user as the Microsoft Word toolkit's OneDrive-drive selector for DOCX workflows. Unlike GET_ACCOUNT_CONTEXT, this lists drives without returning identity context or selecting only the primary drive. Use LIST_SHAREPOINT_LIBRARIES for a specific SharePoint site's document libraries; general OneDrive file automation may use ONE_DRIVE_LIST_DRIVES instead.

tools.name: List SharePoint document libraries
tools.description: Return one page of document libraries and available root folder item IDs for a SharePoint site ID.

tools.name: Move or rename DOCX
tools.description: Rename a DOCX, move it within the same drive, or do both, guarded by its current eTag. At least one of new_name or destination_folder_id is required.

tools.name: Read DOCX
tools.description: Safely inspect a DOCX as bounded rich OOXML: paragraphs and editable text segments, directly formatted runs, tables and merged-cell metadata, internal images, hyperlinks with withheld targets, paired footnotes, semantic comment threads, pending revisions, page breaks, sections with header/footer references, and the style catalog. Existing image framing is inspected without pixel decoding and image records share a 100-megapixel aggregate safety bound. Returns the current eTag required by every locator and never exposes download URLs, external relationship targets, or document bytes.

tools.name: Replace Text
tools.description: Replace literal text across Word run boundaries in a DOCX, optionally as tracked revisions. Uses an optional eTag guard and retries one definite stale unpinned write.

tools.name: Resolve Tracked Changes
tools.description: Accept or reject all pending tracked revisions, or selected revision locators returned by READ_DOCX.

tools.name: Restore DOCX version
tools.description: Restore a retained DOCX version as a new current version, preserving version history, then observe the item's current metadata in a post-operation read. That metadata does not independently prove which version supplied the current content. A required eTag check rejects already-stale callers before mutation, but Graph does not document an atomic If-Match precondition for this operation.

tools.name: Share DOCX
tools.description: Backward-compatible wrapper for sharing a verified DOCX. Prefer CREATE_DOCX_SHARING_LINK for links and INVITE_DOCX_RECIPIENTS for named recipients. mode defaults to create_link. Invite mode requires recipients, roles, send_invitation, and require_sign_in. create_link returns Graph's intended sharing capability URL so it can be delivered to the intended audience; treat that URL as a secret. Other capability tokens, raw identity data, and raw provider error details are omitted; a bounded provider reason may be returned for a failed request. Partial invite success is reported per recipient. Sharing can change the document eTag and invalidate READ_DOCX locators; call READ_DOCX again before editing. Password protection depends on tenant sharing policy and plan; personal OneDrive may require Microsoft 365 Personal or Family. Setting retain_inherited_permissions=false removes all existing permissions when the item is shared for the first time.

tools.name: Upsert DOCX
tools.description: Create or replace a same-name DOCX containing the same validated content supported by CREATE_DOCX. Replacement is always enabled; use CREATE_DOCX for create-only conflict behavior.

name: Midpage MCP
description: Midpage MCP gives agents authorized legal-research tools for searching, retrieving, analyzing, and citing cases, statutes, regulations, and related legal materials.

tools.name: Analyzedocketfiling
tools.description:
Analyze one docket filing selected from analyzeDocketReport and answer a focused question using passages from that filing.

Use this when the user needs to understand what a specific filing says. This tool answers from the filing text, not from the docket entry description.

INPUT:
- caseId: The caseId returned by analyzeDocketReport case.caseId.
- entryNumber: The docket entry number returned by analyzeDocketReport relevantEntries[].entryNumber.
- attachmentNumber: Optional attachment number returned by analyzeDocketReport relevantEntries[].attachmentNumber. Omit for the main filing on the docket entry.
- question: The question to answer about this specific filing.

RETURNS:
- status: "ok" or a specific resolution/analysis error.
- filing: Resolved filing metadata, including entryNumber, optional attachmentNumber, dateFiled, suggestedFileName, and a downloadable Midpage file URL for the filing.
- answer: Direct answer based only on the filing text.
- supportingPassages: Passages from the filing that support the answer, with passage and relevance.
- doesNotAddress: Specific parts of the question that the filing text does not answer. Check this before relying on the answer.

CITATION RULES:
- When using filing content in an answer, cite the filing with the format below.
- Every citation must be a markdown hyperlink to filing.url.
- The ECF No. suffix is important and should be included in filing citations.
- Use a descriptive filing name, then any real page/pin/paragraph if available, followed by this suffix: ECF No. {filing.entryNumber} ({filing.dateFiled formatted as "Mar. 3, 2020"}).
- Example: [Pl.'s Mot. for Summ. J. 5, ECF No. 30 (Mar. 3, 2020)]({filing.url})
- If filing.dateFiled is unavailable, omit the parenthetical date rather than inventing one.
- Never use short cites such as "id." or "supra"; repeat the full linked filing citation.

DOWNLOAD GUIDELINES:
- If the user asks to download or save the filing, use filing.suggestedFileName as the filename.

tools.name: Analyzedocketreport
tools.description:
Analyze a federal docket report and answer a docket-level question.

Use this for case snapshots, recent activity, procedural posture, service, complaint history, motion history, deadlines, and identifying relevant filings. This tool answers from the docket sheet only; use analyzeDocketFiling when the text of a specific filing is needed.

INPUT:
- court: Federal court. Prefer Bluebook-style abbreviations such as "N.D. Cal.", "S.D.N.Y.", "D. Del.", "Bankr. D. Del.", "9th Cir.", or "Fed. Cir."; full federal court names are also accepted.
- docketNumber: Federal case docket number. Prefer full district/bankruptcy numbers with office or division prefix when known, such as "4:24-cv-04722"; appellate numbers look like "24-1234".
- caseName: Optional case caption/name, such as "Musk v. Altman". Include it when available, especially if the docket number is incomplete.
- forceFetch: Optional. Set true only when the user explicitly needs the latest official PACER docket instead of available cached or RECAP data.
- question: The docket-level question to answer.

RETURNS:
- status: "ok" or a specific resolution/analysis error.
- case: Resolved case metadata, including caseId for analyzeDocketFiling.
- docketReport: Docket report metadata, including suggested filename and a downloadable Midpage file URL when one is available.
- answer: Direct answer based only on the docket sheet.
- relevantEntries: Docket entries or attachments supporting or relevant to the answer. Use case.caseId plus relevantEntries[].entryNumber and optional relevantEntries[].attachmentNumber with analyzeDocketFiling when the filing text is needed.
- doesNotAddress: Specific parts of the question that the docket entries do not answer. Check this before relying on the answer.
- warnings: Important source or parsing limitations, when present.

DOWNLOAD GUIDELINES:
- If the user asks to download or save the docket report, use docketReport.suggestedFileName as the filename.

tools.name: Analyzelaw
tools.description:
Analyze a statute, regulation, constitutional provision, or agency guidance document against a legal question. Returns verified passages with deep links. REQUIRED before citing or quoting any statute or regulation.

AUTO-USE: whenever an answer depends on the wording, requirements, exceptions, scope, procedures, or current status of a primary-law provision. Never answer from memory or web snippets instead.

LINK RULE: every statute/regulation citation or subsection relied on in the final answer must be a Markdown link: a passage-specific proposition or quote to its deeplinkUrl, a general reference to url. Never invent path segments.

LOOKUP: exactly ONE of citation, path, registerCitation, or id, plus question. Subsection pinpoints ("18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(C)") and popular names ("First Step Act of 2018") are not citation keys: searchLaws with the user's wording, then analyze the chosen result by id, keeping the pinpoint in question. Never guess or silently truncate a citation. Raw text is never returned.

RETURNS: citation, title, number, state, collectionType; analysis {summary, passages [{point, quote, deeplinkUrl}], doesNotAddress: CHECK BEFORE CITING}; isCurrent (in force today), isHistorical (superseded; both false = not yet effective), effectiveDate, publicationDate, sourceAsOf (source edition date); url (this exact version), sourceUrl (official source); children: for containers, up to 250 of childrenTotal child provisions (no text; analyze a child by id, or searchLaws for the section when the list is capped), parentId; versions (analyze another by id with includeHistorical: true); ambiguousMatches (retry by id); error (unresolvable or unsafe to analyze; source-file-only leaves return metadata and url to open, never quote them).

HOW TO USE: quote only returned passages; for a container (nodeType PARENT) drill into the relevant child; check isCurrent before asserting current law; for state comparisons, analyze each provision with the same question and compare propositions, qualifiers, and doesNotAddress.

tools.name: Analyzeopinion
tools.description:
Analyze a legal opinion against a specific question. Returns the propositions the case ACTUALLY supports, each with a verified quote, scope limits, and a deep link, plus what it does NOT address. REQUIRED before citing any case.

DOCUMENT: exactly ONE of opinionId (preferred, from search results), reporterCitation (never WL/LEXIS), or docket; no placeholder values. question: the legal question, specific about the legal element.

RETURNS: citation (exact Bluebook string); url (the whole case); supportedPropositions[]: proposition (cite-ready text: USE IT when citing), quote (verbatim), scope (limits), centrality (core_holding > supporting_analysis > secondary_matter > background), opinionSection (any non-majority opinion, e.g. "Jackson, Concurring"), deeplinkURL (opens the case at that passage); doesNotAddress (CHECK BEFORE CITING); summary; disposition; jurisdiction; treatment (citator status, cited-by count).

CITATION FORMAT: every citation is a markdown hyperlink built from the returned fields.
Specific proposition or quote: [{citation}]({deeplinkURL})
Case generally: [{citation}]({url})
Example: [International Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310 (1945)](https://app.midpage.ai/document/1234567?lines=10-12)
Cite after every legal proposition and quote with the exact citation string returned: never abbreviate, no short cites (id., supra), no LEXIS/WL, no invented reporter pin cites (deeplinkURL is the pinpoint). Add parentheticals and scope limits when relevant.

HOW TO USE: if your intended use appears in doesNotAddress, do NOT cite the case for it (a fact noted in passing is not a rule). Cite the proposition text or a close paraphrase with its qualifiers; prefer core_holding and supporting_analysis. Never present non-majority text as the holding; name its opinionSection.

WRITING: attorney-style paragraphs: topic sentences, crisp rule statements with hyperlinked citations, direct concise answers, verbatim quotes woven into prose. Sparse lists; no block quotes, repetition, or emojis.

tools.name: Findinopinion
tools.description:
Find quotable passages within a single opinion by keyword search. Fast, free, no AI.

USE after a search to check whether a result is actually relevant (like double-clicking into it) and to decide which cases deserve the AI cost of analyzeOpinion: only the most relevant. Also usable directly when the user gives a citation. Optional but recommended.

DO NOT use this tool alone: a case you intend to cite must still go through analyzeOpinion. Default to search unless the user provided a specific citation.

DOCUMENT: exactly ONE of opinionId (preferred, from search results), reporterCitation ("556 U.S. 662"; never WL/LEXIS), or docket {courtAbbreviation, docketNumber}. Omit fields you don't have; never pass placeholder values.

QUERY: key terms to match, NOT a question. GOOD: "personal jurisdiction minimum contacts purposeful availment". BAD: "Does this case establish personal jurisdiction?"

RETURNS: snippets, verbatim passages from the opinion that can be quoted as written.

LIMITS: keyword-only, so passages with different wording are missed; a snippet is easy to take out of context; it does NOT say whether the case supports or contradicts your proposition and does NOT surface qualifiers or exceptions.

NEXT: analyzeOpinion on promising cases for analysis, qualifiers, and verified quotes before citing.

tools.name: Search
tools.description:
Search US case law across federal and state courts. Returns matching opinions with Bluebook metadata, highlights, and citator treatment. This is the default first step of legal research: follow it with findInOpinion and/or analyzeOpinion. NEVER cite a case until you have run analyzeOpinion on it.

USE whenever a response needs legal analysis; do not presume to know the answer. If the user gives a specific citation, you may go straight to analyzeOpinion.

RETURNS per case: documentId (pass to findInOpinion/analyzeOpinion), metadata (Bluebook citation: parties, court, date, reporter or docket), highlights (why it matched; NOT for quoting, use findInOpinion), treatment (positive/negative/caution/neutral, citation counts).

QUERIES: hybrid semantic + keyword matching. Use key terms ("personal jurisdiction minimum contacts purposeful availment"), natural-language propositions or questions, or exact identifiers verbatim ("556 U.S. 662", "patent no 7,479,949"). Run up to 4 queries per call, in parallel, for different issues; each returns up to 10 results. Narrow with the filter fields; omit publishStatus unless the user explicitly asks to restrict by publication status.

PAGINATION: each queryOutcomes entry reports resultCount and pagination. For one query's next page call search({ queries: [{ cursor: "<pagination.nextCursor>" }] }) with cursor only (no query or filters); continuations mix with new queries. Pages hold 10 cases, up to 100 distinct per query; duplicates across queries are merged and totalResults counts the merged set. Stop when nextCursor is absent: search is not exhaustive, refine instead. Cursors expire 30 minutes after the initial search (pagination.expiresAt); reuse returns the same page; if expired or invalid, rerun the query. paginationError: first page usable but not continuable; a failed query never discards the others.

NEXT: review highlights and treatment, findInOpinion on 3-5 candidates for quotable passages, then analyzeOpinion on every case you will rely on (REQUIRED before citing).

tools.name: Searchlaws
tools.description:
Search Midpage's US primary-law corpus: statutes, regulations, constitutions, and agency guidance for federal law, all 50 states, and DC. BM25 keyword search (not semantic) over text, headings, and citations.

AUTO-USE: call this whenever a user asks what a statute, code section, regulation, administrative rule, or constitutional provision says, requires, permits, or prohibits, or whether it applies. Do not wait for words like "research" or "Midpage", and do not default to web search for primary-law text. FIND the governing provision here, then analyzeLaw with its id for verified text before citing.

RESOLUTION: subsection pinpoints ("18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(C)") and popular/source-law names ("First Step Act of 2018", "ERISA § 514") go through search first: search the user's full wording, choose the intended provision, analyzeLaw by id. Never guess a codified citation or silently truncate a pinpoint.

Results are the law in force TODAY unless currentOnly is false (not superseded, not future-effective, no in-force successor).

RETURNS:
- results: id (pass to analyzeLaw), citation, title, number, state, collectionId/collectionType, path, nodeType, effectiveDate, snippets (matched fragments, <em> marks the hit), isCurrent/isHistorical (both false = not yet effective), url (Midpage page for that exact version)
- total: estimate; the authoritative currency check may drop index-stale rows, so a page can hold fewer than pageSize results (continue normally)
- stateCounts: estimated per-state hits for the WHOLE query, not this page: scope surveys with them, verify each state with a filtered search; not proof of coverage
- error: replaces results when a filter could not be resolved (did-you-mean suggestions included) or the page window was exceeded; says how to fix the call

HOW TO USE: search broad, then narrow with the filter fields. NEVER cite from snippets; quote from analyzeLaw. N-state surveys: one unfiltered query, read stateCounts, per-state filtered queries, then analyzeLaw the top provisions.

name: Mighty Networks
description: Manage members, spaces, content, events, plans, and other administrative resources in a Mighty Network through its GA Admin REST API.

tools.name: Add Member to Space
tools.description: Add an existing member of the connected Mighty Network to a space, granting that member access to the space.

tools.name: Create Event
tools.description: Create a one-time or recurring visible event in a Mighty Networks space. By default, the event is also posted to the activity feed; set post_in_feed=false to suppress that additional feed side effect.

tools.name: Create Invite
tools.description: Create an invitation to the connected Mighty Network. This operation immediately sends an invitation email to the recipient; there is no option to suppress or delay the email.

tools.name: Create Member
tools.description: Create a full Network member or a limited member assigned to specified spaces. This creates a real member account. By default Mighty Networks also sends the new member a welcome email; set send_welcome_email=false to suppress that email.

tools.name: Create Post
tools.description: Create and publish a visible post or article in a Mighty Networks space. This immediately creates community-visible content and can notify the Network; set notify=false to suppress notifications.

tools.name: Get Event
tools.description: Return details for one Mighty Networks event by ID.

tools.name: Get Member
tools.description: Return one member in the connected Mighty Network by member ID or exact email address. Provide exactly one lookup value.

tools.name: Get Network
tools.description: Return identity and profile details for the Network connected to this Admin API key.

tools.name: Get Post
tools.description: Return details for one Mighty Networks post or article by ID.

tools.name: Get Space
tools.description: Return details for one space in the connected Mighty Network by ID.

tools.name: List Abuse Reports
tools.description: Return one page of abuse reports for moderation review.

tools.name: List Collections
tools.description: Return one page of collections that organize spaces in the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Event RSVPs
tools.description: Return one page of RSVP records for an event in the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Events
tools.description: Return one page of events in the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Invites
tools.description: Return one page of Network invitations, optionally filtered by recipient email.

tools.name: List Members
tools.description: Return one page of members in the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Plans
tools.description: Return one page of access and payment plans configured for the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Posts
tools.description: Return one page of posts across the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: List Spaces
tools.description: Return one page of spaces in the connected Mighty Network.

tools.name: Remove Member from Space
tools.description: Remove an existing member from a space without deleting the member's Network account. This revokes the member's access to the selected space.

tools.name: Revoke Invite
tools.description: Revoke an unaccepted invitation to the connected Mighty Network. An invite that has already been accepted cannot be revoked with this action.

tools.name: Set Event RSVP
tools.description: Create or update a Mighty Networks member's RSVP for an event. This changes the member's attendance state to yes, maybe, or no.

tools.name: Update Member
tools.description: Update selected profile or Network role fields for an existing member. Provide at least one of role, email, first_name, or last_name. Changing the role to host or moderator grants elevated community permissions.

tools.name: Update Post
tools.description: Update the title and/or body of an existing Mighty Networks post or article; provide at least one of title or description. This changes content visible to the community and can notify the Network; set notify=false to suppress notifications.

required.name: suffix.one
required.description: The ID of the Mighty Network that owns this API key. Find it in Network Admin, or copy it from an Admin API URL such as /admin/v1/networks/{network_id}/me. The Network ID must match the Network where the key was generated.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Generate an API key in your Mighty Network at Admin > Settings > API Keys, configure the permissions needed for your intended operations, and copy it when it is shown. Mighty Networks displays the full token only once.

tools.name: Get Call Analytics
tools.description: Return authoritative aggregate call counts, duration, outcomes, handling, and cost for a required half-open time window.

tools.name: Get Task
tools.description: Retrieve one existing asynchronous task when its UUID is already known from another Mihu AI response.

tools.name: Get Workspace
tools.description: Return the connected Mihu AI workspace identity, locale, timezone, and wallet balance.

tools.name: List Agents

tools.name: List Appointments
tools.description: List appointments filtered by schedule, contact, status, or date range.

tools.name: List Calls
tools.description: List calls filtered by agent, call status, or inbound/outbound/web direction.

tools.name: List Campaigns

tools.name: List Contacts

name: Mindbody
description: Mindbody provides scheduling, client management, commerce, and business operations software for fitness, wellness, and beauty businesses.

tools.name: Add Client to Class
tools.description: Validate or book a client into a class or waitlist. Check MINDBODY_LIST_CLASSES first. Defaults validate only, send no email, and require no payment; a real booking returns the visit ID needed for exact removal.

tools.name: Create Client
tools.description: Create one Mindbody client, or reactivate a matching inactive client when reactivate_inactive_client=true. Uses typed standard, emergency-contact, location, and custom-field inputs.
