name: OpenAI
description: Toolkit for OpenAI APIs: manage Assistants, Threads/Messages; upload/list/delete Files; list/retrieve Models (including vision/multimodal); and view fine-tune listings and events.

tools.name: Add Upload Part
tools.description: Tool to add a part (chunk of bytes) to an Upload object. Use when uploading large files in chunks, with each part up to 64 MB.

tools.name: Cancel batch
tools.description: Tool to cancel an in-progress batch. Use when you need to stop a batch that is currently processing. The batch will be in status 'cancelling' for up to 10 minutes before changing to 'cancelled', where partial results (if any) will be available.

tools.name: Cancel evaluation run
tools.description: Tool to cancel an ongoing evaluation run. Use when you need to stop an evaluation run that is currently in progress.

tools.name: Cancel Response
tools.description: Tool to cancel a background model response by its ID. Use when you need to stop a response that was created with the 'background' parameter set to true. Only background responses can be cancelled; attempting to cancel a non-background response will fail.

tools.name: Cancel Run
tools.description: Tool to cancel a run that is currently in progress. Use when you need to stop an assistant run that is taking too long or is no longer needed. The run's status will transition to 'cancelling' and then 'cancelled'.

tools.name: Cancel upload
tools.description: Tool to cancel an upload. Use when you need to stop an upload that is in progress. No parts may be added after cancellation.

tools.name: Compact Response
tools.description: Tool to compact a conversation or response to reduce token usage. Use when you need to reduce the size of long conversations while preserving important context. Either provide an array of input messages or reference a previous response ID to compact.

tools.name: Complete Upload
tools.description: Complete a multipart Upload and create its usable File object.

tools.name: Create Audio Transcription
tools.description: Tool to transcribe audio files to text via OpenAI Audio Transcriptions API. Use when you need to convert speech in audio files to written text, optionally with timestamps or speaker diarization.

tools.name: Create Audio Translation
tools.description: Tool to translate audio files to English text via OpenAI Audio Translations API. Use when you need to convert speech in audio files (any language) to English text.

tools.name: Create Batch
tools.description: Tool to create and execute a batch from an uploaded file of requests. Use after uploading a JSONL file with purpose 'batch' to process multiple API requests in a single batch operation.

tools.name: Create Chat Completion
tools.description: Tool to create a chat completion response from OpenAI models. Use for conversational AI, text generation, function calling, multimodal tasks with vision/audio, and structured JSON outputs. Supports advanced features like reasoning models, tool use, and streaming responses.

tools.name: Create Completion (Legacy)
tools.description: Tool to generate text completions using OpenAI's legacy Completions API. Use for single-turn text generation with models like gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct. Note: This endpoint is legacy; prefer Chat Completions for newer models.

tools.name: Create Container
tools.description: Tool to create a new container with configurable memory, expiration, file access, and network policies. Use when you need to provision an isolated execution environment.

tools.name: Create Container File
tools.description: Tool to create a file in a container. Use when adding files to an existing container either by referencing an uploaded file ID or by uploading raw file content directly.

tools.name: Create Conversation
tools.description: Tool to create a new conversation for multi-turn interactions. Use when initializing a persistent conversation with optional starter messages.

tools.name: Create Conversation Items
tools.description: Tool to create items in a conversation with the given ID. Use when adding messages or other items to an existing conversation.

tools.name: Create Decision
tools.description: Evaluate evidence with typed predicate, choice, and score questions. Each call costs at most $2.

price.description: $0.10 per 1M input tokens ($0.20 long context); cache and output free; $2 max.

tools.name: Create Embeddings
tools.description: Tool to generate text embeddings via the OpenAI embeddings endpoint. Use for search, clustering, recommendations, and vector database storage workflows.

tools.name: Create Eval
tools.description: Tool to create an evaluation structure for testing a model's performance. An evaluation is a set of testing criteria and data source config that dictates the schema of data used in the evaluation. Use when setting up automated testing for model outputs with graders like label_model, string_check, or text_similarity.

tools.name: Create Evaluation Run
tools.description: Tool to create a new evaluation run for testing model configurations. Use when you need to kick off an evaluation with a specific data source and model configuration to test.

tools.name: Create fine-tuning job
tools.description: Tool to create a fine-tuning job which begins the process of creating a new model from a given dataset. Use when you need to start fine-tuning a model with your training data. Response includes details of the enqueued job including job status and the name of the fine-tuned models once complete.

tools.name: Generate Image
tools.description: Tool to generate an image via the OpenAI Images API and return hosted image asset URL and metadata. Use when you need to create images from text descriptions for single-shot image generation.

tools.name: Edit Image
tools.description: Tool to create edited or extended images via OpenAI Images Edit API. Use when you need to modify existing images based on a text prompt, with optional mask support for targeted edits.

tools.name: Create Image Variation
tools.description: Tool to create a variation of a given image using the OpenAI Images API. Use when you need to generate alternative versions of an existing image. Only supports dall-e-2 model.

tools.name: Create Message
tools.description: Tool to create a new message in a specific thread. Appends the message only — does not trigger a model response; create a separate run to obtain assistant replies. Use when adding messages to an existing conversation after confirming the thread ID.

tools.name: Create Moderation
tools.description: Tool to classify text and/or image inputs for potentially harmful content via the OpenAI Moderation API. Use for content safety checks, filtering user-generated content, or monitoring for policy violations across 13 harm categories including harassment, hate, violence, sexual content, self-harm, and illicit activities.

tools.name: Create Realtime Call
tools.description: Tool to create a Realtime API call over WebRTC and receive the SDP answer needed to complete the peer connection. Use when initiating a bidirectional audio/data WebRTC session with OpenAI's Realtime API. Returns the SDP answer and call ID for connection establishment.

tools.name: Create Realtime Client Secret
tools.description: Tool to create an ephemeral client secret for authenticating Realtime API connections. Use when you need to establish a WebSocket connection to OpenAI's Realtime API for voice or streaming interactions.

tools.name: Create Realtime Session
tools.description: Tool to create an ephemeral API token for client-side Realtime API applications. Use when setting up browser-based real-time audio/text interactions.

tools.name: Create Realtime Transcription Session
tools.description: Tool to create an ephemeral API token for realtime transcriptions via the Realtime API. Use when you need to authenticate browser clients for realtime audio transcription sessions. Returns a session object with a client_secret containing a usable ephemeral API token.

tools.name: Create Response
tools.description: Tool to generate a one-shot model response via the Responses API. Use for multimodal analysis (image + text), OCR/text extraction from images, or structured JSON outputs. For structured outputs, configure text.format with type='json_schema' and your schema. Returns the full Response object including id, output array, and aggregated output_text for parsing structured data.

tools.name: Create Run
tools.description: Tool to create a run on a thread with an assistant. Use when you need to execute an assistant to generate responses. Creating a message alone does not cause the assistant to respond; a run is the execution primitive. After creating the run, typically poll the run status until it reaches a terminal state (completed, failed, cancelled, expired), then read the assistant's messages from the thread.

tools.name: Create Skill
tools.description: Tool to create a skill from uploaded files. Use when you need to create a new skill with SKILL.md and supporting files.

tools.name: Create Speech (TTS)
tools.description: Tool to generate text-to-speech audio using OpenAI's Audio API. Use when you need to convert text to natural-sounding speech with a choice of voices and models. Returns a hosted audio file URL with metadata, not raw bytes.

tools.name: Create Thread
tools.description: Tool to create a new thread. Use when initializing a conversation with optional starter messages. Returns a thread_id that must be persisted and passed to all subsequent calls (e.g., OPENAI_CREATE_MESSAGE, OPENAI_RETRIEVE_THREAD). Create a fresh thread for each independent conversation or unrelated task.

tools.name: Create Thread And Run
tools.description: Tool to create a thread and run it in one request. Use when you need to start a new conversation and immediately execute the assistant to generate a response. This is more efficient than calling create_thread and create_run separately.

tools.name: Create Upload
tools.description: Tool to create an intermediate Upload object for large file uploads. Use when uploading files larger than the direct upload limit by adding Parts to the Upload. The Upload accepts up to 8 GB total and expires after one hour if not completed.

tools.name: Create Vector Store
tools.description: Tool to create a new vector store. Use when you need to create a collection of processed files for file_search tools.

tools.name: Create Vector Store File
tools.description: Tool to create a vector store file by attaching a File to a vector store. Use when you need to add files to a vector store for file search capabilities.

tools.name: Create vector store file batch
tools.description: Tool to create a vector store file batch. Use when attaching multiple files to a vector store for file search capabilities.

tools.name: Create Video
tools.description: Tool to create a video using Sora models via the OpenAI Videos API. Use when you need to generate videos from text descriptions. The response includes a job ID and status for tracking the asynchronous video generation process.

tools.name: Create Video Remix
tools.description: Tool to create a video remix from an existing generated video using OpenAI's Video API. Use when you need to transform or modify a previously generated video based on a new prompt. The remix operation creates a new video job that applies the new prompt to the original video content.

tools.name: Delete assistant
tools.description: Tool to delete a specific assistant by its ID. Use when you need to remove an assistant after confirming its ID. Deletion is irreversible and permanently removes all assistant configuration.

tools.name: Delete chat completion
tools.description: Tool to delete a stored chat completion by its ID. Use when you need to remove a chat completion that was created with store=true.

tools.name: Delete container
tools.description: Tool to delete a specific container by its ID. Use when you need to remove a container after confirming its ID.

tools.name: Delete container file
tools.description: Tool to delete a file from a container. Use when you need to remove a file from a specific container by providing both container ID and file ID.

tools.name: Delete conversation
tools.description: Tool to delete a conversation by its ID. Items in the conversation will not be deleted. Use when you need to remove a conversation.

tools.name: Delete conversation item
tools.description: Tool to delete an item from a conversation with the given IDs. Use when you need to remove a specific message or item from a conversation.

tools.name: Delete evaluation
tools.description: Tool to delete a specific evaluation by its ID. Use when you need to remove an evaluation after confirming its ID.

tools.name: Delete evaluation run
tools.description: Tool to delete an evaluation run. Use when you need to permanently remove a specific run from an evaluation.

tools.name: Delete file
tools.description: Tool to delete a file by its ID after confirming the target. Files persist indefinitely and count against storage quotas; periodically list and remove unneeded files to avoid hitting file-count or size caps.

tools.name: Delete message
tools.description: Tool to delete a message from a thread. Use when you need to remove a specific message by its ID after confirming both the thread and message IDs.

tools.name: Delete response
tools.description: Tool to delete a model response with the given ID. Use when you need to remove a stored response from the Responses API.

tools.name: Delete skill
tools.description: Tool to delete a specific skill by its ID. Use when you need to remove a skill after confirming its ID.

tools.name: Delete thread
tools.description: Tool to delete a thread by its ID. Use when you need to remove a conversation thread after confirming the target ID.

tools.name: Delete Vector Store
tools.description: Tool to delete a vector store. Use when you need to permanently remove a vector store by its ID.

tools.name: Delete Vector Store File
tools.description: Tool to delete a vector store file. This removes the file from the vector store but does not delete the file itself. Use when you need to remove a file from a vector store's search index.

tools.name: Delete video
tools.description: Tool to delete a video by its ID. Use when you need to remove a video after confirming its identifier.

tools.name: Download file
tools.description: Tool to download the contents of a specified file by its ID. Use when you need to retrieve file content from OpenAI.

tools.name: Download Video Content
tools.description: Tool to download video content (MP4) or preview assets from OpenAI Videos API. Use when you need to retrieve the actual video file, thumbnail, or spritesheet for a generated video.

tools.name: Get Chat Completion
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a stored chat completion. Use when you need to fetch a previously created chat completion that was stored with store=true.

tools.name: Get Chat Completion Messages
tools.description: Tool to retrieve messages from a stored chat completion. Use when you need to fetch the conversation history of a previously created chat completion. Only works with completions that were created with the store parameter set to true.

tools.name: Get ChatKit thread
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a ChatKit thread by its ID. Use when you need to fetch details about a specific ChatKit thread including its status, title, and owner.

tools.name: Get Conversation Item
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a single item from a conversation. Use when you need to fetch details of a specific message or item within a conversation.

tools.name: Get Eval
tools.description: Tool to retrieve an evaluation by ID. Use when you need to inspect an existing evaluation's configuration, data source settings, or testing criteria.

tools.name: Get Evaluation Run
tools.description: Tool to retrieve an evaluation run by ID to check status and results. Use when you need to monitor an evaluation run's progress or retrieve its final results after creation.

tools.name: Get Eval Run Output Item
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific output item from an evaluation run by its ID. Use when you need detailed results for a particular test case within an evaluation run.

tools.name: Get eval run output items
tools.description: Tool to get a list of output items for an evaluation run. Use when you need to retrieve the detailed results of an eval run, including grading outcomes, input/output samples, and token usage.

tools.name: Get Evaluation Runs
tools.description: Tool to get a paginated list of runs for an evaluation. Use when you need to retrieve all runs or check the status of multiple runs for a specific evaluation.

tools.name: Get Input Token Counts
tools.description: Tool to calculate input token counts for OpenAI API requests. Use when you need to estimate token usage before making an API call, validate content fits within model limits, or optimize prompts for token efficiency.

tools.name: Get Message
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific message from a thread by its ID. Use when you need to fetch details of a particular message in an Assistants thread.

tools.name: Get Response
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a model response by ID. Use when you need to check the status, output, or metadata of a previously created response.

tools.name: Get Run Step
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific run step from an Assistants API run to inspect detailed execution progress, view tool calls, or check message creation. Use when you need details about a specific step in a run's execution.

tools.name: Get Vector Store
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a vector store by its ID. Use when you need to get details of an existing vector store for file_search operations.

tools.name: Get Vector Store File
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a file from a vector store. Use when you need to check the status or details of a file attached to a vector store.

tools.name: Get Vector Store File Batch
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a vector store file batch. Use when you need to check the status of a batch file processing operation.

tools.name: Get Video
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a video generation job by its unique identifier. Use when you need to check the status, progress, or details of a video generation task.

tools.name: List Assistants
tools.description: Tool to list assistants to discover the correct assistant_id by name or metadata. Use when assistant_id is unknown to avoid 404 errors.

tools.name: List Batches
tools.description: Tool to list your organization's batches. Use when you need to view all batches, check batch statuses, or find a specific batch by listing them.

tools.name: List Chat Completions
tools.description: Tool to list stored chat completions that were created with the `store` parameter set to true. Use to retrieve previously stored completions for review, analysis, or audit purposes.

tools.name: List ChatKit thread items
tools.description: Tool to list ChatKit thread items. Use when you need to retrieve all items from a ChatKit thread, including messages, tool calls, and tasks.

tools.name: List container files
tools.description: Tool to list files in a container. Use when you need to view all files uploaded to a specific container.

tools.name: List Containers
tools.description: Tool to list containers. Use when you need to view all containers in your organization or filter by name.

tools.name: List Conversation Items
tools.description: Tool to list all items for a conversation with the given ID. Use when you need to retrieve the items in a conversation for review or processing.

tools.name: List engines
tools.description: Tool to list available engines and their basic information. Use when you need to discover which engines are available.

tools.name: List Evals
tools.description: Tool to list evaluations for a project. Use when you need to view all evaluations, check their configurations, or find a specific evaluation by listing them.

tools.name: List files
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of files uploaded to your organization/project context. Cursor-paginated: continue requesting pages until next_cursor is null to retrieve all files. Files from other project environments are not visible. Cached file_ids may become stale if files are deleted; re-query before referencing file_ids in downstream workflows.

tools.name: List Files in Vector Store Batch
tools.description: Tool to list vector store files in a batch. Use when you need to retrieve all files that were added to a vector store as part of a specific batch operation.

tools.name: List fine-tunes
tools.description: Tool to list your organization's fine-tuning jobs. Use when you need to review all fine-tune runs. Results are scoped to the authenticated organization; an empty list means no fine-tunes exist for that org specifically.

tools.name: List fine-tuning job events
tools.description: Tool to get status updates for a fine-tuning job. Use when you need to monitor the progress of a fine-tuning job or retrieve event logs.

tools.name: List fine-tuning job checkpoints
tools.description: Tool to list checkpoints for a fine-tuning job. Use when you need to retrieve model checkpoints created during the fine-tuning process. Checkpoints are created at various steps during training and can be used to evaluate model performance at different stages.

tools.name: List Input Items
tools.description: Tool to retrieve input items for a given response from the OpenAI Responses API. Use when you need to inspect the inputs that were used to generate a specific response.

tools.name: List Messages
tools.description: Tool to list messages in an Assistants thread to fetch the assistant's generated outputs after a run completes. Use after polling a run to completion to retrieve assistant responses.

tools.name: List models
tools.description: Tool to list available models scoped to the current account/organization — some public models may be absent due to permissions. Use when you need to discover which models you can call. Results may include deprecated or assistant-incompatible models; confirm a specific model's status via OPENAI_RETRIEVE_MODEL before using it in OPENAI_CREATE_ASSISTANT or other calls. Use model IDs exactly as returned — misspelled or unsupported IDs cause validation errors. Models vary in capability (vision, file-based features, context size); inspect metadata before assuming support. Filter results by id, owned_by, or status to handle large result sets efficiently.

tools.name: List Runs
tools.description: Tool to list runs belonging to a thread. Use when you need to view all runs that have been executed on a specific thread, for example to find a run by status or to track execution history.

tools.name: List Run Steps
tools.description: Tool to list run steps for an Assistants API run to track detailed execution progress, inspect tool calls, and view message creation events. Use after creating a run to monitor its step-by-step execution or to retrieve tool call details after completion. When polling to monitor active runs, use reasonable intervals to avoid rate-limit errors.

tools.name: List Skills
tools.description: Tool to list skills. Use when you need to discover available skills or retrieve skill IDs by name or description.

tools.name: List ChatKit Threads
tools.description: Tool to list ChatKit threads with pagination and filtering. Use when you need to retrieve threads for a specific user or browse all available threads.

tools.name: List Vector Store Files
tools.description: Tool to list files in a vector store. Use when you need to retrieve all files attached to a specific vector store.

tools.name: List Vector Stores
tools.description: Tool to list vector stores to discover available vector stores by name or metadata. Use when you need to view all vector stores in your organization.

tools.name: List Videos
tools.description: Tool to list all video generation jobs. Use when you need to view all videos that have been created or check the status of multiple video generation tasks.

tools.name: Modify Assistant
tools.description: Tool to modify an existing assistant. Use when you need to update an assistant's configuration, model, instructions, tools, or metadata.

tools.name: Modify Message
tools.description: Tool to modify an existing message's metadata in a thread. Use when you need to update metadata associated with a specific message.

tools.name: Modify Run
tools.description: Tool to modify a run's metadata. Use when you need to update metadata information for a specific run.

tools.name: Modify thread
tools.description: Tool to modify an existing thread's metadata. Use after obtaining the thread ID when you need to update metadata.

tools.name: Modify Vector Store
tools.description: Tool to modify an existing vector store. Use when you need to update the name, expiration policy, or metadata of a vector store.

tools.name: Retrieve assistant
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific assistant. Use when you need to confirm assistant metadata before performing further operations. Prefer this over repeated OPENAI_CREATE_ASSISTANT calls to avoid cluttering assistant configurations.

tools.name: Retrieve Batch
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a batch by ID to check its status, progress, and results. Use when you need to check the current state of a batch job, view completion statistics, or access output file IDs.

tools.name: Retrieve container
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific container by its ID. Use when you need to fetch container configuration, status, or metadata.

tools.name: Retrieve container file
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata for a specific file in a container. Use when you need to get details about a container file including its size, path, and creation timestamp.

tools.name: Retrieve container file content
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the content of a file within a container. Use when you need to download or access the actual file data from a container.

tools.name: Retrieve engine
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific engine. Use when you need to confirm engine availability and metadata before using it.

tools.name: Retrieve file
tools.description: Tool to retrieve information about a specific file. Use when you need to check the details, status, or metadata of a file by its ID.

tools.name: Retrieve fine-tuning job
tools.description: Tool to retrieve information about a fine-tuning job. Use when you need to check the status, progress, or details of an existing fine-tuning job.

tools.name: Retrieve model
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific model, confirming its metadata (ownership, created date) and verifying access under your org — a model appearing in OPENAI_LIST_MODELS does not guarantee access. Use before depending on a model ID in downstream calls.

tools.name: Retrieve run
tools.description: Tool to retrieve an Assistants run by ID to check status, errors, and usage. Use when polling run status until it reaches a terminal state (completed, failed, cancelled, incomplete, expired) before reading thread messages.

tools.name: Retrieve thread
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata of a specific thread by its ID — does not include message bodies or assistant replies (those require a completed run and separate message listing). Use before listing messages. After thread creation or message appending, wait 2–3 seconds before polling; use exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) for HTTP 429 responses. Avoid concurrent OPENAI_CREATE_MESSAGE writes during retrieval to prevent inconsistent message states.

tools.name: Retrieve Vector Store File Content
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the parsed contents of a vector store file. Use when you need to access the actual text content that has been processed and chunked for a file in a vector store.

tools.name: Run grader
tools.description: Tool to run a grader to evaluate model performance on a given sample. Use when you need to evaluate model outputs against expected results using various grading strategies like string matching, text similarity, custom Python code, or model-based scoring.

tools.name: Search Vector Store
tools.description: Tool to search a vector store for relevant chunks based on a query and file attributes filter. Use when you need to find specific content within a vector store for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or custom search workflows.

tools.name: Submit Tool Outputs to Run
tools.description: Tool to submit tool call outputs to continue a run that requires action. Use when a run has status 'requires_action' and required_action.type is 'submit_tool_outputs'. All tool outputs must be submitted together in a single request.

tools.name: Update Chat Completion
tools.description: Tool to update metadata for a stored chat completion. Use when you need to modify tags or metadata for a completion that was created with store=true.

tools.name: Update Conversation
tools.description: Tool to update a conversation's metadata. Use when you need to modify metadata for an existing conversation.

tools.name: Update Eval
tools.description: Tool to update certain properties of an evaluation (name and metadata). Use when you need to rename an evaluation or update its metadata without changing the data source configuration or testing criteria.

tools.name: Update Vector Store File Attributes
tools.description: Tool to update custom attributes on a vector store file. Use when you need to add or modify metadata associated with files in a vector store.

tools.name: Upload file
tools.description: Tool to upload a file for use across OpenAI endpoints. Use before referencing the file in tasks like fine-tuning. Returns a `file_id` that must be explicitly passed to endpoints like OPENAI_CREATE_ASSISTANT or OPENAI_CREATE_MESSAGE — uploaded files are not auto-discovered. Files exceeding size limits return HTTP 413; split or compress oversized content before retrying. Verify uploads via OPENAI_LIST_FILES before referencing `file_id`, as unsupported formats may be silently rejected. Repeated uploads accumulate against storage quotas; delete unused files with OPENAI_DELETE_FILE.

tools.name: Validate grader configuration
tools.description: Tool to validate a grader configuration for fine-tuning jobs. Use when you need to verify that a grader is correctly configured before using it in a fine-tuning job.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your secret OpenAI API key, starting with 'sk-' or 'sk-proj-'. Create or copy one at platform.openai.com/api-keys and keep it private.

optional.name: organization_id
optional.description: Only needed if you're in multiple OpenAI organizations. Looks like 'org-AbC123xyz' — find it under Settings → Organization → General. Most users can leave this blank.

name: OpenAlex
description: OpenAlex is an open catalog of scholarly works, authors, institutions, sources, topics, and related research metadata.

tools.name: Add Collection Entities
tools.description: Bulk-add one or more matching OpenAlex entity IDs to an owned collection without duplicating existing memberships.

tools.name: Autocomplete Entities
tools.description: Resolve a partial name or title to likely OpenAlex entity IDs before filtering or retrieving metadata.

tools.name: Create Collection
tools.description: Create a private, single-entity-type OpenAlex collection, optionally with an initial bounded set of entity IDs.

tools.name: Delete Collection
tools.description: Permanently delete exactly one owned private OpenAlex collection and all of its collection memberships. This does not delete the underlying OpenAlex entities.

tools.name: Download Work Content
tools.description: Download an OpenAlex-cached PDF or gzipped GROBID TEI file for a work. Choose the format matching the work's has_content flags. Each call currently costs $0.01, and source copyright terms still apply. Downloads are limited to 25 MB; compressed TEI must also remain within 25 MB after expansion.

tools.name: Get Changefile
tools.description: Retrieve changed entity counts and JSONL/Parquet download details for one OpenAlex changefile date. Requires an OpenAlex paid plan; inspect GET_RATE_LIMIT_STATUS for daily capacity and current endpoint cost.

tools.name: Get Collection
tools.description: Get metadata for one private OpenAlex collection owned by the connected user.

tools.name: Get Concept
tools.description: Retrieve one item from the deprecated, frozen OpenAlex Concepts taxonomy for legacy workflows. Prefer Topics through GET_ENTITY for new work; use select to limit returned fields.

tools.name: Get Metadata Entity
tools.description: Retrieve one OpenAlex work, author, source, institution, topic, keyword, publisher, funder, award, taxonomy item, country, continent, or language by its supported identifier. Returns the provider's entity object directly; use select to limit its top-level fields.

tools.name: Get Rate Limit Status
tools.description: Validate the connected OpenAlex API key and inspect daily budget, prepaid balance, reset timing, and current endpoint costs before expensive queries or downloads.

tools.name: Infer Topics from Text
tools.description: Use OpenAlex's deprecated legacy classifier to infer topics from a required title, optionally accompanied by an abstract. Not recommended for new projects; costs $0.01 per request.

tools.name: List Changefiles
tools.description: List all available OpenAlex changefile dates and detail URLs. Requires an OpenAlex paid plan. Keep aggregate traffic below 100 requests per second and inspect GET_RATE_LIMIT_STATUS for daily capacity and current endpoint cost.

tools.name: List Collection Entities
tools.description: List one page of entity IDs in an owned private collection together with collection metadata and page totals.

tools.name: List My Collections
tools.description: List private OpenAlex collections owned by the connected API-key user, optionally finding collections that contain an entity.

tools.name: Query Concepts
tools.description: Query the deprecated, frozen OpenAlex Concepts taxonomy for legacy workflows. Prefer Topics through QUERY_ENTITIES for new work. Returns one cursor-controlled page; keep aggregate traffic below 100 requests per second and monitor the connected key's daily USD budget.

tools.name: Query Metadata Entities
tools.description: Search, filter, sort, sample, select, or group one OpenAlex metadata resource other than works, including authors, venues, organizations, taxonomy, geography, awards, and enumerations. Returns one cursor-controlled page.

price.description: $0.001 per 10 list/filter calls or $0.001 per search calls

tools.name: Query Works
tools.description: Search, filter, sort, sample, select, or group scholarly works. Returns one cursor-controlled page and its OpenAlex query cost; use the snapshot for whole-catalog exports.

price.description: $0.001 per 10 list/filter calls or $0.001 per search calls

tools.name: Remove Collection Entities
tools.description: Bulk-remove one or more entity memberships from an owned private OpenAlex collection without deleting the underlying OpenAlex entities.

tools.name: Update Collection
tools.description: Update a private collection's name or description, or change its entity type while the collection is empty. Provide at least one of display_name, description, or entity_type.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your OpenAlex API key. Sign in to OpenAlex, open https://openalex.org/settings/api, and copy the key shown in API settings. The same key authorizes public metadata, full-text content, and your private collections.

name: Opencage
description: OpenCage Geocoder provides a simple API for forward and reverse geocoding using open data sources.

tools.name: Forward Geocode Address
tools.description: Tool to convert a human-readable address into geographic coordinates. Use when you need to retrieve latitude and longitude from an address.

tools.name: Geocode to GeoJSON
tools.description: Geocode addresses or coordinates and return results in GeoJSON FeatureCollection format. Use this tool when you need: - Geographic data in standard GeoJSON format for mapping applications - Forward geocoding: convert addresses to coordinates - Reverse geocoding: convert coordinates to addresses The response includes coordinates, formatted addresses, and optional annotations like timezone, currency, and sun times for each location.

tools.name: Geocode with JSONP
tools.description: Geocode an address and return results wrapped in a JavaScript callback function (JSONP format). Use this tool when you need geocoding results that can be directly consumed by JavaScript through a callback function, typically for cross-domain AJAX requests in browser environments. The response wraps standard geocoding JSON with your specified callback function name. Example response: myCallback({"results":[{"geometry":{"lat":52.5,"lng":13.4},"formatted":"Berlin, Germany",...}],...})

tools.name: Geocode Google v3 JSON
tools.description: Tool to perform forward geocoding and return results in Google Geocoding API v3 compatible JSON format. Use when you need Google v3 compatible output for legacy integrations. Note: This is a legacy format that may be discontinued; using the standard JSON format is recommended.

tools.name: Reverse Geocode Coordinates
tools.description: Tool to convert coordinates to a human-readable address. Use when you have latitude and longitude and need a readable location.

tools.name: Geocode XML
tools.description: Geocode a location query and return results in XML format. Supports both forward geocoding (address to coordinates) and reverse geocoding (coordinates to address). Use this when you need XML-formatted output instead of JSON.

tools.name: Check API Health
tools.description: Tool to check API health and connectivity. Returns 'pong' if the API is reachable. Use when you need to verify that the OpenCage API is accessible and operational.

required.name: generic_key
required.description: Your OpenCage Geocoding API key.

name: OpenFunnel Agent Primitives
description: OpenFunnel Agent Primitives provides composable company search, research, lookup, and enrichment APIs for AI sales agents.

tools.name: Cancel Bulk Lookalike Search
tools.description: Irreversibly request cancellation of a pending or running bulk lookalike job. The response only acknowledges the asynchronous request; use GET_BULK_LOOKALIKE_RESULTS afterward to observe terminal cancelled status and retrieve partial results. Companies delivered before cancellation remain available and billable.

tools.name: Get Bulk Lookalike Results
tools.description: Check an asynchronous bulk lookalike job and return one result page. Use status to determine completion: pending, running, and cancelling jobs remain pollable even when next_cursor is null.

tools.name: Get Credit Balance
tools.description: Return total, used, and remaining credits for the connected OpenFunnel account before or after paid searches.

tools.name: List Country Codes
tools.description: List all ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes accepted by tech-search country filters, ordered by company volume.

tools.name: List Firmographic Options
tools.description: List the live funding stages, location codes, and employee bounds accepted by lookalike search filters.

tools.name: Lookup Companies
tools.description: Resolve a batch of 1-100 company names, domains, or LinkedIn URLs to ordered candidate records. Exact identifiers can still return multiple matches, so every candidate is preserved.

tools.name: Research Company
tools.description: Qualify one known company from recent hiring activity, current team composition, or both, with cited evidence. Each successful call is charged at the workspace-configured per-call credit price; an unresolved-domain 404 is free.

tools.name: Search Companies by Tech Stack
tools.description: Return one fixed page of 50 companies whose recent job postings mention a technology. A live non-enriched full page consumed 25 credits; enrichment or firmographic filters may cost more. Follow next_cursor only when needed.

tools.name: Search Lookalike Companies
tools.description: Find up to 100 companies similar to a natural-language trait or seed domains. Each returned company consumes 1 credit, and even an unexpected semantic match is billable, so choose limit deliberately.

tools.name: Start Bulk Lookalike Search
tools.description: Start an asynchronous lookalike job for up to 10,000 companies. Delivered results are billed when the job completes, so choose limit deliberately and use GET_BULK_LOOKALIKE_RESULTS to monitor the returned job_id.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your OpenFunnel Agent Primitives API key beginning with "of_". To obtain or recover it, follow the email verification flow at https://docs.openfunnel.dev/agent-primitives/authentication: request a six-digit code with your email, then verify the code to receive the key. Keep it secret.

name: OpenGraph.io
description: OpenGraph.io provides a simple API to retrieve Open Graph data from websites, even those without properly defined Open Graph tags.

tools.name: Capture Screenshot
tools.description: Tool to capture high-quality screenshots of any webpage programmatically. Supports full-page captures, custom dimensions, device presets, element-specific screenshots, and quality settings. Screenshots are available for 24 hours after generation. Use when you need to capture visual snapshots of websites with specific rendering requirements or device simulations.

tools.name: Extract Site Metadata
tools.description: Tool to extract site metadata. Use when you need to retrieve Open Graph and other meta signals from a website.

tools.name: Scrape Site
tools.description: Tool to scrape a site for its raw HTML and social/OpenGraph metadata. Use when you need the full page content and metadata. Use after confirming the URL.

tools.name: Scrape URL for HTML

name: OpenRouter

Response format varies across models; use explicit prompt instructions to standardize output. Provider-level rate limits and moderation policies differ per model.

price.description: Billed at the selected model's OpenRouter token rate, from $0.02 per 1M input tokens and $0.04 per 1M output tokens; capped at $2 per call

tools.description: Submit an asynchronous video generation job to OpenRouter.

tools.name: Get Credits
tools.description: Tool to get the current API credit balance for the authenticated user. Use before large or batch jobs to verify sufficient balance. A successful response may return total_credits=0, which confirms authentication but will cause all paid model generations to fail. Avoid polling this endpoint; call only as needed.

tools.name: Get Current Key
tools.description: Tool to get information about the currently authenticated API key. Use to check usage limits, spending, and key metadata.

tools.name: Get Generation
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a generation result by its unique ID. Use after a generation completes to fetch metadata like token counts, cost, and latency.

tools.name: Get Models Count

tools.name: Get Video Content

tools.name: Get Video Generation
tools.description: Poll a video generation job for its status, outputs, and usage.

tools.name: List Available Models
tools.description: Tool to list available models via OpenRouter API. Use after confirming authentication to fetch the model catalog. Use exact model IDs returned here in OPENROUTER_CREATE_CHAT_COMPLETION or OPENROUTER_CREATE_COMPLETION calls — hard-coded IDs may break when the catalog changes. Use exact author and slug values from this response as inputs to OPENROUTER_LIST_MODEL_ENDPOINTS. Models have varying capabilities (e.g., tools, reasoning); verify individual model capabilities before downstream use. Pricing and latency metadata may be null or approximate — handle missing values in routing logic.

tools.name: List Embedding Models
tools.description: Tool to list all available embeddings models via OpenRouter API. Returns a list of embeddings models with their properties including architecture, pricing, and capabilities.

tools.name: OpenRouter List Model Endpoints

Some metadata fields (e.g., latency, pricing) may be null or approximate; handle missing values in routing logic.

tools.name: OpenRouter List Providers

Providers differ in latency, context window sizes, and rate limits — switching providers affects these constraints. Newly added providers may not appear immediately due to catalog propagation delays.

tools.name: List User Models

tools.name: List Video Models
tools.description: List video generation models and their supported capabilities.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your native OpenWeb Ninja API key. Sign in at https://app.openwebninja.com/, open Account, then Settings, and copy the key from the API Key card. The key is sent in the 'x-api-key' header and can access only the native products to which your account is subscribed. Keep it secret. RapidAPI marketplace keys are not supported by this connection.

name: OPNForm
description: OPNForm is an open-source form builder for creating forms, managing workspaces, collecting submissions, and configuring integrations.

tools.name: Cancel Workspace Invite
tools.description: Cancel and remove a pending workspace invitation before it is accepted. Requires a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

tools.name: Create Form
tools.description: Create an OpnForm form in a workspace from a title, ordered field or layout blocks, and optional validated form settings. Optional retention settings permanently delete future submissions after the configured period. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Create Form Integration
tools.description: Create a generic webhook or Make integration for an OpnForm form. This registers an external destination for future form submission data; an active integration can begin sending submissions to that destination immediately, while an inactive integration remains configured without delivery. Requires a personal access token with the manage-integrations ability.

tools.name: Create Submission
tools.description: Submit answers to a public OpnForm form. A completed submission may immediately send its data to active webhook or Make integrations; optionally save a partial submission with completion and campaign-attribution metadata.

tools.name: Create Workspace
tools.description: Create an OpnForm workspace. Account workspace limits may reject creation even when the personal access token has write access. Requires a personal access token with the workspaces-write ability.

tools.name: Delete Form
tools.description: Permanently delete a form and all of its submissions by numeric ID. This irreversible operation cannot be undone. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Delete Form Integration
tools.description: Permanently remove a webhook integration from a form and stop its future deliveries. This operation cannot be undone. Requires a personal access token with the manage-integrations ability.

tools.name: Delete Submission
tools.description: Permanently delete one submission from a form using both numeric IDs. This irreversible operation cannot be undone. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Delete Submissions
tools.description: Permanently delete 1-25 submissions from one form through sequential provider requests. This operation is irreversible and not atomic: confirmed earlier deletions are not rolled back. Processing continues after item-local invalid or not-found responses, but stops after authentication, permission, rate-limit, server, or ambiguous transport failures. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Delete Workspace
tools.description: Permanently delete a workspace and its contained resources. This irreversible operation cannot be undone and requires repeating the workspace ID as explicit confirmation. Requires a personal access token with the workspaces-write ability.

tools.name: Get Current User
tools.description: Return the name and email of the OpnForm user associated with the connected personal access token.

tools.name: Get Form
tools.description: Retrieve a form by its public slug, including its complete field and layout definitions. Requires a personal access token with the forms-read ability.

tools.name: Invite Workspace Member
tools.description: Add an existing OpnForm user to a workspace or email an invitation to a new user. Sending an invitation email cannot be undone. OpnForm Cloud requires a Pro plan and a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

tools.name: Invite Workspace Members
tools.description: Add or invite 1-10 users to one workspace through sequential provider requests. Each successful item may send an invitation email that cannot be undone, and the batch is not atomic. Processing continues after item-local validation failures but stops after authentication, permission, plan, rate-limit, server, or ambiguous transport failures. OpnForm Cloud requires a Pro plan and a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

tools.name: List Form Integrations
tools.description: List webhook and Make integrations configured for a form, including IDs, status, and endpoint configuration. Requires a personal access token with the manage-integrations ability.

tools.name: List Forms
tools.description: Return one page of lightweight form summaries from a workspace. Pass the returned cursor back to continue; use Get Form for complete field definitions. Requires a personal access token with the forms-read ability.

tools.name: List Integration Events
tools.description: Inspect past delivery attempts for one form integration, including the attempt date, Success or Error status, and a downstream HTTP status when available. Requires a personal access token with the manage-integrations ability.

tools.name: List Submissions
tools.description: Return one searchable page of completed, partial, or all submissions for a form. Pass the returned cursor back unchanged to continue with the same filters. Requires a personal access token with the forms-read ability.

tools.name: List Workspace Invites
tools.description: List pending and accepted invitations for a workspace where the connected user is an administrator. Requires a personal access token with the workspaces-write ability.

tools.name: List Workspace Members
tools.description: List members of a workspace with their user IDs, names, emails, and workspace roles. Requires a personal access token with the workspace-users-read ability.

tools.name: List Workspaces
tools.description: List workspaces accessible to the connected user, including IDs, plan tier, role flags, usage counts, enabled features, and plan limits. Requires a personal access token with the workspaces-read ability.

tools.name: Remove Workspace Member
tools.description: Remove a specified member from a workspace without deleting the member's OpnForm account. Requires a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

tools.name: Resend Workspace Invite
tools.description: Send another invitation email for an existing pending workspace invite. Each successful call sends an external email to the invite recipient and requires a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

tools.name: Update Form
tools.description: Replace or change an existing form's field definitions and settings using its numeric form ID. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Update Form Integration
tools.description: Change a generic webhook integration's delivery URL or active status. Requires a personal access token with the manage-integrations ability.

tools.name: Update Form Submission Retention
tools.description: Change or disable a form's automatic submission-retention policy. Expired submissions are permanently deleted and cannot be restored; shortening the period can make existing submissions eligible for the next hourly cleanup. Requires a personal access token with the forms-write ability.

tools.name: Update Workspace
tools.description: Change a workspace's name and icon without affecting its membership or forms. Both values are required because OpnForm clears an omitted icon. Requires a personal access token with the workspaces-write ability.

tools.name: Update Workspace Member Role
tools.description: Change an existing workspace member's role to admin, user, or readonly. Requires a personal access token with the workspace-users-write ability.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create a scoped token in your OpnForm Cloud dashboard under Settings -> Access Tokens. Select the abilities required by the tools you plan to use, then copy the token when it is shown; OpnForm displays it only once.

name: OptimoRoute
description: OptimoRoute is an online route optimization and planning solution for delivery, logistics, and field service companies.

tools.name: Create Order
tools.description: Tool to create a new order or update an existing order in OptimoRoute. Use when you need to add delivery, pickup, or task orders to the system with location, time windows, and other constraints.

tools.name: Create or Update Orders
tools.description: Tool to bulk create, update, or replace multiple orders at once without geocoding. Use when you need to add new orders or modify existing ones efficiently. Supports up to 500 orders per request.

tools.name: Delete All Orders
tools.description: Tool to remove all orders and planned routes for a specified date. Use when you need to clear orders for a specific date or delete all orders system-wide if no date is provided.

tools.name: Delete Order
tools.description: Tool to remove a single order from the OptimoRoute system. Use when you need to delete a specific order by its orderNo.

tools.name: Delete Orders
tools.description: Tool to delete one or more orders from the system in bulk (max 500 per request). Use when you need to remove orders, either individually or in batch operations.

tools.name: Get Order Completion Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve completion details for one or more orders including proof of delivery data. Use when you need to check order completion status, timing details, and form data.

tools.name: Get Drivers
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all drivers in the system. Use when you need up-to-date driver data including status and contact information.

tools.name: Get Mobile Events
tools.description: Tool to retrieve mobile events from drivers' field operations. Use when you need to track order completions, status changes (success, failed, on_duty, off_duty), and other field events for the currently active plan.

tools.name: Get Orders
tools.description: Tool to retrieve one or more orders from OptimoRoute. Use when you need detailed order information including location, time windows, and assignment details.

tools.name: Get Planning Status
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the status of an active planning/optimization process. Use when you need to check the progress of a planning job by providing its ID.

tools.name: Get Planned Routes
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all planned routes for a given date. Use when you need a detailed view of routes including optional stops, route parameters, and unassigned orders.

tools.name: Get Order Scheduling Info
tools.description: Tool to retrieve scheduling information for a specific order. Use when you need to check if an order is scheduled and get details like driver assignment, timing, and position.

tools.name: Search Orders
tools.description: Tool to search for orders in OptimoRoute based on criteria. Use when you need to find orders by date range, order identifiers, or order status. At least one of 'orders' or 'date_range' must be provided.

tools.name: Start Planning
tools.description: Tool to start the planning/optimization process for a specified date or date range. Use when you need to generate optimized routes for orders and drivers. Requires orders to be created before planning can begin.

tools.name: Stop Planning
tools.description: Tool to stop an active planning/optimization process. Use when you need to halt a running planning job by providing its ID.

tools.name: Update Driver Parameters
tools.description: Tool to update driver parameters for a specific date including work times, vehicle assignment, and start/end locations. Use when you need to modify driver availability or routing constraints. Note that this unschedules existing routes for the driver on the specified date.

tools.name: Update Drivers Parameters
tools.description: Tool to update parameters of multiple drivers for specified dates in bulk (max 500 per request). Use when you need to modify driver configuration including work hours, vehicle assignments, and location settings. Note: Existing routes for the specified drivers and dates will be unscheduled.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API key required for authenticating requests to the OptimoRoute API.

name: Order Desk
description: Order Desk is an order management platform for managing orders, shipments, inventory, and store data across ecommerce integrations.

tools.name: Add Order History Note
tools.description: Append a timestamped note permanently to an existing order's history. Order history is append-only, so this tool cannot edit or remove the entry.

tools.name: Add Order Item
tools.description: Add one line item to an existing order.

tools.name: Add Order Items
tools.description: Add two to 10 line items sequentially to the same order and return a result for every processed item. This batch is not atomic.

tools.name: Create Inventory Item
tools.description: Create one inventory item with a unique SKU and return its positive Order Desk ID and complete created representation.

tools.name: Create Inventory Items
tools.description: Create two to 10 inventory items sequentially and return each created ID or error. This batch is not atomic.

tools.name: Create Shipments
tools.description: Create one or more shipment records across orders in one request and report the success or error returned for every shipment.

tools.name: Delete Inventory Item
tools.description: Permanently delete one inventory item by its positive Order Desk ID. This destructive action cannot be undone; verify the ID before calling it.

tools.name: Delete Order Item
tools.description: Permanently remove one line item from an order. This destructive action cannot be undone by this tool; verify both IDs before calling it.

tools.name: Delete Shipment
tools.description: Permanently remove one shipment record from an order. This destructive action cannot be undone by this tool; verify both IDs before calling it.

tools.name: Get Inventory Item
tools.description: Get one inventory item by its positive Order Desk ID.

tools.name: Get Order
tools.description: Get one order and its addresses, line items, shipments, metadata, notes, and discounts by Order Desk internal ID.

tools.name: Get Store Metadata
tools.description: Return safe store identity, locale, timezone, page-size settings, and folder IDs and names without exposing credentials or email configuration.

tools.name: List Inventory Items
tools.description: Search inventory items in the connected store by ID, SKU, name, metadata, manufacturer SKU, location, or update time.

tools.name: List Order Items
tools.description: Return all line items for one order.

tools.name: List Orders
tools.description: Find orders in the connected store using at least one narrowing filter and return one bounded page. Use next_cursor to continue the same query.

tools.name: List Order Shipments
tools.description: Return all shipments recorded for one order.

tools.name: Move Orders
tools.description: Move one or more orders to exactly one destination folder selected by positive ID or exact name, with a result for every order.

tools.name: Update Inventory Items
tools.description: Safely update selected fields on one or more inventory items while preserving every omitted field.

tools.name: Update Order Item
tools.description: Safely update selected fields on one order line item while preserving every omitted field.

tools.name: Update Shipment
tools.description: Safely update selected fields on one shipment while preserving every omitted field.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API key for this Order Desk store. In your Order Desk store, open Store Settings, select API, create an API key if needed, and copy it here. Keep this value secret.

required.name: generic_id
required.description: The Store ID shown alongside your API key in Order Desk. In your Order Desk store, open Store Settings, select API, and copy the Store ID for the store this connection should access.

name: Ordinal
description: Ordinal is a collaborative social media planning platform for creating, reviewing, scheduling, and analyzing content across connected channels.

tools.name: Add Idea To Calendar
tools.description: Convert an existing Ordinal idea into a regular calendar post on a chosen date. This does not schedule or externally publish the returned post.

tools.name: Create Idea
tools.description: Create reusable Ordinal content for one or more supported social channels without adding it to the publishing calendar or publishing it externally.

tools.name: Create Post
tools.description: Create an Ordinal calendar post with content for one or more social channels. This only creates the post: it does not schedule or publish anything; call SCHEDULE_POST separately to schedule external publication.

tools.name: Get Post
tools.description: Return one Ordinal post by ID with its full channel content, attached assets, labels, profiles, status, and publish timing.

tools.name: Get Profile Analytics
tools.description: Return follower history or post performance for one connected LinkedIn or X scheduling profile over a date range. Requires a matching profile ID from LIST_PROFILES with profile_type='scheduling'; analytics are unavailable until that social profile is connected.

tools.name: Get Workspace
tools.description: Return the workspace bound to the connected Ordinal API key, including its ID, name, slug, timezone, and creation time.

tools.name: List Ideas
tools.description: List non-archived content ideas with filters and one cursor-controlled page of results.

tools.name: List Labels
tools.description: Return workspace labels and their IDs for filtering or labeling posts and ideas.

tools.name: List Posts
tools.description: List non-archived workspace posts with filters and one cursor-controlled page of results.

tools.name: List Profiles
tools.description: List connected social profiles by capability so their IDs can be used for scheduling, analytics, or auto-engagement workflows.

tools.name: Schedule Post
tools.description: Schedule or reschedule an Ordinal post for external publication to its configured social channels. WARNING: this creates or changes a future external social publication. It can be cancelled with UNSCHEDULE_POST before it fires, but publication is irreversible once sent. The post must contain at least one channel with a connected scheduling profile.

tools.name: Unschedule Post
tools.description: Cancel a pending scheduled publication and change the Ordinal post status to Finalized. This only cancels publication that has not occurred and cannot retract content that has already been published.

tools.name: Update Post
tools.description: Update selected fields or channel content on a non-archived Ordinal post. This does not schedule or publish the post.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: An Ordinal workspace API key beginning with ord_. In Ordinal, open the workspace you want to connect, then go to Settings > Integrations > API and create or copy an API key. This key grants access only to that workspace; do not use an Enterprise company key beginning with ord_c_.

name: Orgo
description: Orgo provides cloud computers that agents can create, control, automate, and manage through an API.

tools.name: Control Pointer
tools.description: Perform one pointer action on a running Orgo computer: click, drag, or scroll. The action is applied immediately and a click may submit forms or trigger irreversible effects. Inspect a fresh screenshot and verify the intended effect before acting.

tools.name: Create Computer
tools.description: Create and automatically start a virtual computer in an accessible workspace. This may consume quota or incur usage charges; call only after the user confirms the target workspace and requested resources.

tools.name: Delete Computer
tools.description: Permanently delete one Orgo computer and its data. This cannot be undone. Call only when the user explicitly confirms the exact computer ID and permanent deletion.

tools.name: Execute Code
tools.description: Execute arbitrary Bash or Python code on an Orgo computer. Code can read secrets, alter data, access networks, or delete files. Show the exact code and target computer to the user and call only after explicit confirmation. A provider-reported execution failure is returned as result data.

tools.name: Get Computer
tools.description: Get current details and status for one Orgo computer. Use after creation or a power operation to observe state.

tools.name: Get Screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current display of a running Orgo computer for visual inspection before deciding on mouse or keyboard input.

tools.name: List Templates
tools.description: List either templates owned by the connected account or Orgo-maintained curated templates. Returns refs that can be supplied when creating a computer.

tools.name: List Workspaces
tools.description: List workspaces accessible to the connected Orgo key, including the computers in each workspace. Use this to discover workspace and computer IDs before other calls.

tools.name: Run Computer Agent
tools.description: Run one non-streaming computer-use agent task on a running Orgo computer. The agent acts immediately and autonomously: it can click or submit forms, type content, execute shell commands, access external services, modify files or accounts, and take destructive or irreversible actions. Use only when the requested task and target computer are authorized. Returns Orgo's complete OpenAI-compatible JSON response without assuming an unverified success shape.

tools.name: Send Keyboard Input
tools.description: Send either literal text or one key or key combination to the current keyboard focus on a running Orgo computer. Input is applied immediately and may submit forms or trigger irreversible effects. Inspect a fresh screenshot first, and do not type secrets unless the user explicitly directs it.

tools.name: Set Computer Power State
tools.description: Start, stop, or restart one Orgo computer after explicit user confirmation. Stop preserves disk but releases the host, start may assign a new host, and restart rotates connection credentials. The response only acknowledges that Orgo accepted the operation; use GET_COMPUTER afterward to observe current state.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: A workspace-scoped Orgo API key. Sign in at https://www.orgo.ai/start, open the workspace you want to connect, then go to Settings > API Keys and create or copy a key. Orgo shows a newly created key's plaintext only once.

name: Orshot
description: Orshot generates images, PDFs, and videos from templates and manages workspace templates, brand assets, and social publishing.

tools.name: Add Brand Color
tools.description: Save a hex, RGB, HSL, or gradient color to the workspace brand assets and return its new ID.

tools.name: Delete Brand Color
tools.description: Permanently delete one saved workspace brand color by ID. This deletion cannot be undone; use it only for a color the caller explicitly intends to remove.

tools.name: Get Profile
tools.description: Return the authenticated Orshot profile and the IDs, names, and slugs of its accessible workspaces.

tools.name: Get Studio Template
tools.description: Return one Studio template's metadata, pages, and available render modifications by template ID. A 403 response can mean the template is missing or is not owned by the connected workspace; the API does not distinguish those conditions.

tools.name: List Brand Assets
tools.description: List one category of workspace brand assets, optionally requiring all supplied tags. Brand colors are limited by Orshot to the 200 most recent values.

tools.name: List Social Accounts
tools.description: Return connected social-account IDs and platforms, optionally checking whether each account needs reconnection.

tools.name: List Studio Templates
tools.description: Return one filtered page of Studio templates in the API key's workspace, with an opaque cursor for the next page.

tools.name: Render Studio Template
tools.description: Render an owned Studio template as an image or PDF URL/base64 result. This consumes render credits and does not publish to social accounts.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your workspace API key from the Orshot dashboard. Open Orshot, select API Keys in the sidebar, and copy the key you want this connection to use. Keep this value secret.

name: OSV
description: OSV provides an open vulnerability database and API for querying vulnerabilities by package, version, commit, or vulnerability identifier.

tools.name: Determine Version
tools.description: Experimentally rank probable versions of an OSS-Fuzz C/C++ library from relative source-file paths and base64-encoded MD5 hashes. Results may be empty or change because the API is experimental.

tools.name: Get Import Findings
tools.description: Experimentally list OSV records from one exact import source that failed import-time quality checks; intended for OSV source maintainers and may return no records.

tools.name: Get Vulnerability
tools.description: Return the complete OSV record for one case-sensitive vulnerability ID, including affected versions, ranges, severity, references, and aliases.

tools.name: Query Vulnerabilities
tools.description: Find full OSV vulnerability records affecting one package, package version, package URL, or commit. Use next_cursor to continue a large result set.

tools.name: Query Vulnerabilities Batch
tools.description: Check up to 1,000 packages, package versions, package URLs, or commits in one request and return position-matched compact vulnerability IDs. Continue unfinished items with their individual page tokens.

name: Otter.ai MCP
description: Otter.ai MCP lets agents retrieve the authenticated user's profile, search authorized meetings and conversations, and fetch complete transcripts for analysis and summarization.

tools.name: Otter fetch
tools.description:
Fetch one meeting's complete verbatim transcript by ID - full speaker-attributed, timestamped content, plus its AI summary, action items, outline, and attendees. READ-ONLY.

    Returns the speaker-turn structure, not just a summary. Supports meetings captured or imported into Otter from platforms including Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, in-person, and phone calls.

    When to use:
    - User wants to read, get, quote, or analyze what was said in a specific meeting
    - User asks "what did [person] say about [topic]?" and you have a meeting ID
    - User wants the full transcript, not just a summary
    - User wants to cite specific moments with speaker attribution
    - Follow-up after `otter_search` when the user wants deeper content than the summary

    When NOT to use:
    - User has not yet identified the meeting - use `otter_search` first
    - User only needs the summary or action items - those are in `otter_search` results

    Tool selection: once you have an Otter meeting ID, use this tool for verbatim
    quotes and speaker-attributed transcript analysis rather than a platform-native
    recording tool.

    Input: accepts ONLY a meeting ID, not a URL. If the user provides an Otter URL of
    the form https://otter.ai/u/{ID}, extract the ID before calling.

tools.name: Otter get user info
tools.description:
Get current Otter.ai user's name, email, and current date/time (PST) - READ-ONLY.

    Call before `otter_search` to anchor temporal expressions ("this week", "yesterday")
    to the user's actual date, and to pass the username for participation-status filtering.

    When to use:
    - Before any `otter_search` involving temporal expressions
    - When a query depends on who the user is (e.g. meetings they attended vs. shared with them)
    - Once per session is enough; cache the result

tools.name: Otter search
tools.description:
Search meetings across platforms by date, attendee, topic, keyword, or title. READ-ONLY.

    Primary tool for finding meetings captured or imported into Otter from Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet, Webex, in-person meetings, and phone calls. Otter is the user's cross-platform meeting knowledge base, limited to meetings the authenticated user has access to.

    Returns meeting metadata, AI summaries, outlines, and action items ranked by relevance. Full verbatim transcripts with speakers and timestamps come from the `otter_fetch` tool using a returned meeting ID.

    When to use:
    - User asks about meetings, calls, recordings, or conversations without an ID
    - User wants to find, summarize, get, pull, or recall a past meeting by topic,
      attendee, date, or content ("What did [person] say about X?", "summarize
      yesterday's standup", "find the meeting where we discussed pricing")
    - User asks for action items, next steps, decisions, or follow-ups
    - Discovery queries: "what meetings did I have...", "who talked about..."

    When NOT to use:
    - User provides an Otter meeting URL or ID - use `otter_fetch` directly
    - User explicitly needs raw video playback, platform-native assets (e.g.
      whiteboards), or a meeting not available in Otter - defer to the
      platform-native tool

    Tool selection: for meeting content (transcripts, summaries, action items,
    decisions, quotes), prefer Otter when the meeting may exist in the user's
    account, even if another platform is named; defer to a platform-native tool
    only for raw video/assets.

    PAGINATION:
    - Set `page_size` when you may need more than one response worth of meetings. Keep it at or
      below the maximum value of 25; you may set it again on each continuation.
    - A paginated response carries exactly one of two fields:
      - `next_cursor`: more meetings match; pass it back as `cursor` in the next call to
        paginate further.
      - `pagination_completion_reason`: paging is over, so stop. Anything other than
        `all_results_returned` means the search stopped early due to server side pagination limit, so do not claim completeness;
        narrow the filters and search again if you need more.
    - If a cursor is rejected or expired, start a new search.
    - Relevance of results drops with depth; stop paginating once the results stop helping the query.

    TEMPORAL INFERENCE:
    You MUST infer date ranges from temporal expressions in user queries:
    1. ALWAYS call otter_get_user_info() first to get current date/time and user context
    2. Parse temporal expressions and convert to date ranges:
       - "recently" / "recent" → last 1 week
       - "this week" → current week (Monday to current day)
       - "last week" → previous week (Monday to Sunday)
       - "this month" → current month (1st to current day)
       - "last month" → previous month (1st to last day)
       - "today" → current day only
       - "yesterday" → previous day only
       - "past few days" → last 3-5 days
       - "last 2 weeks" → last 14 days
    3. Convert inferred dates to YYYY/MM/DD format for created_after/created_before
