tools.description: List immutable snapshots of a template, including version numbers and optional tags.

tools.name: Merge PDFs
tools.description: Concatenate two or more PDFs in the supplied order and return a temporary result URL. Each successful merge consumes 1 TemplateFox credit.

tools.name: Revise Template With Agent
tools.description: Queue TemplateFox's authoring agent to revise an existing image template from feedback. This irreversibly mutates account content and costs 10 credits when queued; TemplateFox refunds the credits if the job fails. Use a template ID returned by the list-templates tool because TemplateFox may return a server error when it cannot verify template access.

tools.name: Rotate PDF
tools.description: Rotate all pages or selected pages in a PDF and return a temporary result URL. Each successful rotation consumes 1 TemplateFox credit.

tools.name: Save and Test S3 Configuration
tools.description: Create or update the connected account's S3-compatible storage credentials, then test access to the configured bucket. This sensitive Business-plan operation persists third-party credentials in TemplateFox. If validation fails, the credentials remain saved; credential values are never returned.

tools.name: Update Template Version
tools.description: Change or clear the tag and/or description metadata of a template version; the immutable snapshot content is not changed.

tools.name: Validate S3 Configuration
tools.description: Validate that TemplateFox can access and write a small test object to the configured S3-compatible bucket without changing the saved credentials. Use this after SAVE_S3_CONFIG reports that credentials were saved but validation was interrupted. S3 integration is documented as Business-plan functionality.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create or copy an API key from the API Keys section of the TemplateFox dashboard. TemplateFox API keys start with sk_ and are sent in the x-api-key header. Keep this value secret.

name: Temporal
description: Cloud-native workflow orchestration platform for building reliable distributed applications

tools.name: Batch Cancel Workflows
tools.description: Request cancellation of selected Temporal Workflows. Cancellation is cooperative: Workflow code can perform cleanup and external side effects before closing. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Batch Delete Workflows
tools.description: WARNING: Permanently delete selected Temporal Workflow Executions and their Event Histories. This cannot be undone. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Batch Reset Workflows
tools.description: WARNING: Irreversibly reset selected Temporal Workflows. Each successful reset terminates the current run and creates a new run; replay and reapplied events can repeat application code and external side effects. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Batch Signal Workflows
tools.description: Send a named Signal to selected Temporal Workflows. Signal handlers run application code and can cause arbitrary, non-idempotent external side effects. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Batch Terminate Workflows
tools.description: WARNING: Irreversibly terminate selected Temporal Workflows immediately; Workflow cleanup code does not run. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Batch Update Workflow Options
tools.description: Update typed execution options on selected Temporal Workflows. Worker routing, task priority, and virtual-time changes can cause application and external side effects. Preview the exact Visibility query with COUNT_WORKFLOWS and obtain approval for the observed scope; its approximate count is not a hard upper bound because matches can change. Use explicit target_executions when a fixed cardinality bound is required. A stable job_id identifies this operation but does not make retries idempotently successful. After an ambiguous timeout, a retry may return 409 because Temporal rejects duplicate job IDs. Call DESCRIBE_BATCH_OPERATION with the same namespace_id and job_id to reconcile before creating any other batch operation. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Cancel Workflow
tools.description: Irreversibly request cooperative cancellation of a running Temporal Workflow Execution. Temporal records a cancellation-requested event and schedules a Workflow Task, but the Workflow may delay or ignore cancellation depending on its code. A request for an already-closed Workflow succeeds. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Count Schedules
tools.description: Return an approximate count of Temporal Schedules matching a Schedule Visibility query, including grouped counts when requested. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Count Workflows
tools.description: Return an approximate count of Workflow Executions matching a Temporal Visibility query, including supported grouped counts. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Create and Apply Workflow Rule
tools.description: Create a Namespace-wide Temporal Workflow Rule and immediately start a batch job applying it to matching currently running Workflows. This may pause Activities across many executions and cause irreversible operational effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Create Export Sink
tools.description: Create a persistent Temporal Cloud Workflow History export sink asynchronously. Requires Namespace Admin access. Warning: an enabled sink writes closed Workflow Histories to external storage on an ongoing schedule and may incur storage costs. Validate the destination first, use a disposable sink for testing, and arrange teardown.

tools.name: Create Schedule
tools.description: Create a Temporal Schedule that starts a configured Workflow on cron, interval, calendar, or structured-calendar times. The Workflow may perform arbitrary application side effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Create Workflow Rule
tools.description: Create a Namespace-wide Temporal Workflow Rule that can pause matching Activities when its trigger occurs. This does not scan currently running Workflows; use Create and Apply Workflow Rule for that separate intent. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Delete Export Sink
tools.description: Delete a Temporal Cloud Workflow History export sink asynchronously. Requires Namespace Admin access. WARNING: this irreversibly stops future exports from the sink. Files already exported to external storage remain there and must be managed separately. Confirm the Namespace, sink name, and current resource version before calling.

tools.name: Delete Namespace
tools.description: Permanently and irreversibly delete a Temporal Cloud Namespace and all of its Workflow data asynchronously. WARNING: there is no recovery or undo. Use only for a verified disposable Namespace after confirming its full ID, contents, latest resource version, and that deletion protection is disabled.

tools.name: Delete Schedule
tools.description: Permanently delete one Temporal Schedule from a Namespace. WARNING: schedule deletion cannot be undone, but it does not terminate or otherwise affect Workflow Executions the Schedule already started. Confirm the Namespace and Schedule ID before calling. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Delete Workflow Rule
tools.description: Permanently delete one configured Temporal Workflow Rule from a Namespace. WARNING: deletion cannot be undone; after deletion the rule no longer applies to new triggering events. Confirm the Namespace and rule ID before calling. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Describe Batch Operation
tools.description: Return progress, state, selection query, type, and failure counts for one batch operation in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Describe Namespace
tools.description: Return one Temporal Cloud Namespace's configuration, resource version, routing endpoints, state, limits, and capacity. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Describe Schedule
tools.description: Return the complete current definition, state, execution information, Memo, Search Attributes, and conflict token for one Temporal Schedule. Use this before a full replacement update to preserve intended fields and guard against concurrent changes. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Describe Workflow
tools.description: Return configuration, status, pending work, callbacks, and child state for one Workflow Execution in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. Omit run_id to describe the current run. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Describe Workflow Rule
tools.description: Return one configured Temporal Workflow Rule, including its trigger, Visibility query, actions, expiration, creation metadata, and description. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Fail Over Namespace Region
tools.description: Switch a multi-region Temporal Cloud Namespace's active region asynchronously. WARNING: This operation disrupts current Namespace routing while failover completes. Require explicit approval and a documented rollback or failback plan before calling it.

tools.name: Get Async Operation
tools.description: Return the current state and failure details of a Temporal Cloud asynchronous operation.

tools.name: Get Export Sink
tools.description: Return one Temporal Cloud Workflow History export sink, including its resource version, destination configuration, state, and health. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Get Namespace Capacity
tools.description: Return a Temporal Cloud Namespace's capacity mode, available limits, and seven-day actions-per-second statistics. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Get Cloud Region
tools.description: Return details for one Temporal Cloud region, including its cloud provider, provider-specific identifier, and human-readable location.

tools.name: Get Workflow History
tools.description: Return one page of a Temporal Workflow Execution's Event History in forward or reverse order. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Archived Workflows
tools.description: Return one page of archived Workflow Executions matching an exact Temporal Visibility query. Requires Namespace Read access and a Namespace deployment with archival visibility configured and available; the probed Namespace returned HTTP 403 even with inherited Namespace Admin access.

tools.name: List Batch Operations
tools.description: Return one page of batch operations in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Export Sinks
tools.description: Return one page of Workflow History export sinks configured on a Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Namespace Assignments
tools.description: Return one page of users, User Groups, or Service Accounts assigned to a Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Namespaces
tools.description: Return one page of Temporal Cloud Namespaces visible to the API-key identity, optionally filtered by name or Project.

tools.name: List Cloud Regions
tools.description: List currently available Temporal Cloud regions for Namespace placement.

tools.name: List Schedule Matching Times
tools.description: List times within a required start-to-end range that match one Temporal Schedule's timing specification. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Schedules
tools.description: Return one filtered page of Temporal Schedules in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Workflow Rules
tools.description: Return one page of Workflow Rules configured for an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: List Workflows
tools.description: Search one page of Workflow Executions in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace using Temporal Visibility query syntax. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Move Namespace To Project
tools.description: Move a Temporal Cloud Namespace to another Project asynchronously. WARNING: this disruptive operation can change inherited access and connectivity. Verify the source and destination Projects, preserve required connectivity rules, and obtain explicit approval before calling it.

tools.name: Patch Schedule
tools.description: Apply targeted changes to a Temporal Schedule without replacing its definition: pause or unpause it, trigger one immediate action, or backfill historical times. Immediate and backfill operations start application Workflows and may cause arbitrary external side effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Pause Workflow
tools.description: Pause one Temporal Workflow Execution. Temporal changes its status to PAUSED, records a WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_PAUSED event, stops dispatching new Workflow and Activity Tasks, pauses executing Activities, and rejects Queries and Updates; an executing Workflow Task may still complete and server-side events continue. This operational side effect can halt business processing. Always call UNPAUSE_WORKFLOW during teardown, even if a later step fails. Requires Namespace Write access. This Temporal API is experimental.

tools.name: Query Workflow
tools.description: Run a synchronous, read-only Query handler against one Temporal Workflow Execution. The handler runs in Workflow context but cannot mutate Workflow state. Requires Namespace Read access.

tools.name: Register Namespace
tools.description: Create a billable, persistent Temporal Cloud Namespace asynchronously and return its full Namespace ID and operation ID. The name and replicas are immutable, and custom Search Attributes cannot be deleted. Use a unique disposable name for testing and arrange teardown only after creation completes.

tools.name: Remove Namespace Access
tools.description: Remove one user's, user group's, or service account's direct permission on a Temporal Cloud Namespace by setting PERMISSION_UNSPECIFIED. Requires Namespace Admin. WARNING: this can immediately remove access or lock out the selected identity; verify inherited access and never remove the caller's or sole administrator's access.

tools.name: Rename Custom Search Attribute
tools.description: Rename one custom Search Attribute in a Temporal Cloud Namespace asynchronously. This is a potentially breaking schema mutation: Temporal does not rewrite application Visibility queries or dashboards that reference the old name. Verify all consumers and use the latest Namespace resource version before starting the rename.

tools.name: Replace Workflow
tools.description: Replace a running Workflow Execution with a new execution using the same Workflow ID. WARNING: if that ID is running, Temporal irreversibly terminates the existing execution before starting the replacement. This may interrupt in-flight work, and the new Workflow may cause arbitrary external side effects. Use only when termination is explicitly intended, and use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Reset Workflow
tools.description: WARNING: Irreversibly reset a Temporal Workflow to a selected Workflow Task event. Temporal terminates the current run and creates a new run; replay and reapplied events can repeat application code and external side effects. Verify the source run, event ID, and reapply policy before calling.

tools.name: Set Namespace Access
tools.description: Set one user's, user group's, or service account's direct ADMIN, WRITE, or READ permission on a Temporal Cloud Namespace. The new permission replaces that principal's current direct access; setting a lower permission may lock out the caller or the Namespace's sole admin. Requires Namespace Admin.

tools.name: Signal With Start Workflow
tools.description: Atomically signal a running Temporal Workflow or start and signal it when absent. This may run application code and trigger external side effects; use a stable request_id when retrying the same intent. The TERMINATE_EXISTING conflict policy and deprecated TERMINATE_IF_RUNNING reuse policy can terminate a running execution before starting and signaling its replacement.

tools.name: Signal Workflow
tools.description: Send an asynchronous Signal to one running Temporal Workflow Execution. This records a history event, schedules Workflow code, and may trigger arbitrary external business side effects. Temporal's successful response only confirms acceptance, not handler completion. Use request_id to make retries idempotent. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Start or Get Workflow
tools.description: Start a Workflow Execution, or return the already-running execution when the Workflow ID conflicts. This action never replaces the running execution. The response has started=false when it returns the existing execution. Starting a Workflow dispatches application code and may cause arbitrary external side effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Start Workflow
tools.description: Start a new Workflow Execution in an authorized Temporal Cloud Namespace. The request fails if the Workflow ID is already running; use Start or Get Workflow or Replace Workflow only when those different conflict semantics are intended. This dispatches application code and may cause arbitrary external side effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Stop Batch Operation
tools.description: Request that Temporal stop an in-progress batch operation. This does not roll back Workflows already processed by the batch: their cancellations, terminations, signals, deletions, resets, or option changes remain in effect. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Terminate Workflow
tools.description: Immediately and irreversibly terminate one Temporal Workflow Execution. WARNING: termination bypasses cooperative cancellation and Workflow cleanup logic, so finally blocks, compensation, and pending work may not run. Use cancellation instead when the Workflow can clean up safely. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Trigger Workflow Rule
tools.description: Trigger an existing configured Temporal Workflow Rule against one Workflow Execution. This irreversible request evaluates the rule and, when its conditions match, may run configured actions with destructive or arbitrary external side effects. Verify the Workflow and rule before calling; do not test against production or an unknown rule. A successful request can return applied=false when the rule conditions do not match. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Unpause Workflow
tools.description: Resume a paused Temporal Workflow Execution. Unpausing changes its status to running, records an unpaused history event, and resumes application code in Workflow and Activity Tasks, which may produce external side effects. Use request_id for idempotent retries. This Temporal API is experimental and requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Update Export Sink
tools.description: Update an existing Temporal Cloud Workflow History export sink asynchronously using optimistic concurrency. WARNING: this replaces the sink's destination configuration or enabled state for future exports and may redirect or stop Workflow History delivery; already exported files are not moved or undone. Confirm the complete current specification, destination, and resourceVersion before calling.

tools.name: Update Namespace
tools.description: Update a Temporal Cloud Namespace specification asynchronously using the latest resource version for optimistic concurrency. WARNING: this full-spec replacement can change retention, regions, capacity, authentication, deletion protection, and high-availability behavior; newly added custom Search Attributes cannot be deleted. Preserve every unchanged field and verify API-key access and deletion protection before calling. Requires Namespace Admin access.

tools.name: Update Namespace Tags
tools.description: Upsert or permanently remove tags on a Temporal Cloud Namespace asynchronously; removed tags no longer exist on the Namespace. At least one of tags_to_upsert or tags_to_remove must be non-empty, and the same key cannot appear in both. The API-key owner must be a Global Admin or Account Owner; Namespace Admin access alone is insufficient.

tools.name: Update Schedule
tools.description: Fully replace an existing Temporal Schedule's spec, Workflow-start action, policies, and state. Omitted values in those structures are not preserved; supply the complete desired replacement configuration. The replacement can change when application Workflows run and may cause irreversible external side effects. Supply conflict_token to reject a stale update. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Update Workflow
tools.description: Send a durable Update to one Temporal Workflow Execution and wait for the requested lifecycle stage. The Workflow handler may mutate state and cause arbitrary external business side effects. Reuse update_id only when retrying the same intended Update. An admitted or accepted response can omit outcome; the returned update_ref identifies the still-running Update. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Update Workflow Options
tools.description: Update selected options on one Temporal Workflow Execution using an exact protobuf FieldMask. This mutation can reroute Workflow Tasks to different Workers, change task priority, or alter virtual-time behavior and thereby cause application side effects. Use only on an intended execution, capture the prior options, and restore them when testing. Requires Namespace Write access.

tools.name: Validate Export Sink
tools.description: Validate a Temporal Cloud Workflow History export sink configuration. WARNING: this is not read-only; Temporal writes an empty test object to the configured external bucket or container. Use only an owner-approved disposable bucket or container.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create an API key at https://cloud.temporal.io/profile/api-keys. For access across multiple intended Namespaces, use a key owned by an account- or project-level Service Account with the required RBAC grants on each Namespace; do not use a Namespace-scoped Service Account key, which is limited to one Namespace.

tools.name: Delete Label

tools.name: Get Campaign

tools.name: Get Workspace

tools.name: List Archives
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of message and run archives. Use when you need to browse or manage existing archives after authenticating.

tools.name: List Broadcasts

tools.name: List Campaign Events 2

tools.name: List Classifiers

tools.name: List Contacts
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of contacts. Use when you need to fetch contacts with optional filters (UUID, URN, group, or modified date). Use after authenticating your client.

tools.name: List custom contact fields
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of custom contact fields. Use when you need to view or filter all defined contact fields with pagination and optional search.

tools.name: List Flows
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of flows for your organization. Use when you need to fetch automated conversation flows with optional filters (UUID, type, archived status, or modified date).

tools.name: List Flow Starts

tools.name: List Globals

tools.name: List Groups

tools.name: List Handwriting Styles

tools.name: List Mailing Lists
tools.description: Tool to list all mailing lists. Use when you need to fetch existing lists before managing recipients.

tools.name: List Message Templates
tools.description: Tool to list available message templates. Use when selecting a template for a mailing.

tools.name: Buy Radius Search Mailing List
tools.description: Tool to buy or append a radius search mailing list based on address and radius. Use when you need targeted mailing lists around a specified address.

tools.name: Preview letter send

tools.name: Preview Notecard
tools.description: Tool to preview a notecard send. Use when you need front and back images before placing an actual notecard order.

tools.name: Preview Windowless Letter
tools.description: Tool to preview a windowless letter send. Use when you need a PDF preview of the cover-only letter before placing an order.

tools.name: List Orders

tools.name: Search Orders by Recipient Street Address

description: ThoughtSpot Spotter MCP brings governed enterprise analytics, natural-language questions, deep research, root-cause analysis, and insight generation to agents.

tools.name: Check connectivity
tools.description: Ping tool to test connectivity and authentication. You can use this if other tool calls are failing to verify if the connection is working.

tools.name: Create analysis session
tools.description: Start an analytical session with the Analytics Agent. This is the first step in a three-step workflow: create a session, send a message, then poll for updates. Once created, you can use the returned `analytical_session_id` to send analytical questions via `send_session_message` and retrieve answers via `get_session_updates`. Sessions are conversational, so you can ask follow-up questions in the same session without creating a new one. Using a single analytical session is preferable, because it reuses the same data source selection.

tools.name: Create dashboard
tools.description: Create a dashboard from a list of answers, allowing the user to revisit the results later. You can use this if the user asks for a dashboard or liveboard, or asks to save the results from the analysis. This can be a useful way to save the results to revisit later, or present them to other users.

tools.name: Get session updates
tools.description: Get the latest updates from the Analytics Agent. You can call this after `send_session_message` to retrieve the Agent's response. If `is_done` is false, you can call this tool again to continue polling, as the Agent is still generating a response. Even if `is_done` is false, you can use the updates to show status updates or progress to the user, so that they are informed about the ongoing process. An empty `session_updates` list while `is_done` is false is normal; it means the Agent is still thinking. When `is_done` is true, the Agent has finished and the results in `session_updates` are complete, so you can present them to the user. You can also send a follow-up message in the same session after `is_done` is true. If the completed response indicates that no data or no results were found, AND the `list_orgs` tool is available to you, the requested data may live in a different org or the user may not have access to it in the current org: tell the user this and that they can call `list_orgs` to see their orgs (the active one is marked `is_active`) and `switch_org` to switch to another org, then retry. If `list_orgs` is not available, do not mention orgs.

tools.name: List orgs
tools.description: List the Orgs the authenticated user can access on the ThoughtSpot instance, including the ID, name, and description of each Org. The Org marked `is_active: true` is the one currently active for your account, which all tool calls operate against. Use this to tell the user which Org they are in. Only available when authenticated via OAuth. If the list is large , summarize or show only the most relevant orgs (e.g. the active one and a few others) rather than listing all of them, unless the user explicitly asks to see all orgs.

tools.name: Search objects
tools.description:
Search for objects (Answers, Liveboards, Worksheets) in ThoughtSpot matching a given search term. Supports optional filters (types, owner, tag, modified_since, verified_only) and pagination (limit, cursor). Returns `results` (ranked), plus `next_cursor`. Each result carries: object_id, title, type (LIVEBOARD | ANSWER | LIVEBOARD_VIZ | WORKSHEET; LIVEBOARD_VIZ is a viz pinned on a Liveboard — render it as 'Liveboard viz'), author_name, description, tags, last_modified (ISO-8601), verified, external_link, query (Answer/viz sage tokens; null for Liveboards) and confidence. Returns identifiers and metadata only — never the object's data or contents, and it does not run queries.

How to present the results:
• Render as a table with fixed columns in this order: Object (the name, linked to `external_link`) · Type · Owner · Verified (✓ or —) · Last Modified.
• Put the description and, for an Answer/viz, the `query` tokens as sub-lines under the name (e.g. '↳ sales by region, last 3 months') — never as their own columns.
• Render `last_modified` as a plain date (2026-05-15), never the raw timestamp.
• Lead with the top match; if the top 2–3 are close, present them as ranked candidates.
• Never surface `next_cursor` or the numeric `confidence` in your prose.

Outcomes other than a hit list:
• `status: "no_results"` — the search ran but nothing matched. Tell the user nothing matched, and suggest broadening the term or dropping a filter. Do not invent results.
• `status: "error"` — the search failed. Tell the user briefly using `error.message`; if `error.retryable` is true, offer to try again. Never show `error.code`.

tools.name: Send session message
tools.description: Send a message to a session with the Analytics Agent. The Agent may take some time to think and generate a response, so the response will not be returned immediately. Instead, you can use the `get_session_updates` tool to query for the latest updates on the session. After the Agent finishes responding (when `get_session_updates` returns `is_done: true`), you can send another message to the same session to ask follow-up questions without creating a new session. Do not send a new message until the Agent has finished responding to the previous message (when `get_session_updates` returns `is_done: true`). If the user wants to create a dashboard, do not send a message with that request; instead use the `create_dashboard` tool.

tools.name: Switch org
tools.description: Switch the active Org. After switching, all subsequent tool calls (analysis sessions, answers, data sources, dashboards) operate against the selected Org. Pass an `org_id` returned by `list_orgs`. If you do not have access to the Org, the switch fails and the active Org is unchanged. The selection is durable and shared across all of your sessions — it persists across reconnects and applies to your other active conversations; it resets only on re-authentication or after prolonged inactivity. Only available when authenticated via OAuth.

name: Ticketmaster
description: Ticketmaster provides APIs for event discovery, inventory management, and ticketing solutions.

tools.name: Execute Season Ticketing Command
tools.description: Tool to execute Season Ticketing API commands for ticket management operations. Use when you need to interact with Ticketmaster's Archtics Season Ticketing system for administrative tasks, account management, or event discovery. Supports commands: ping (test connectivity), customer_query (get account info), seats_sold (retrieve sold seat details), event_search (search events), event_details (get event attributes), get_attendance (retrieve attendance data). Note: API may return 202 ACCEPTED for asynchronous operations - caller must poll with provided cookies until receiving 200 OK response.

tools.name: Get Attraction Details V2
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific attraction by ID from Ticketmaster Discovery API v2. Use when you need attraction details with optional licensed content filtering.

tools.name: Get Ticketmaster Attractions
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of attractions. Use when you need to search for artists, teams, or performers by various criteria such as keyword, classification, or country.

tools.name: Get Classification Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific classification. Use after obtaining a classification ID.

tools.name: Get Classifications
tools.description: Retrieves event classifications from Ticketmaster's Discovery API. Classifications provide a hierarchical taxonomy for categorizing events: - Segment: Top-level category (Music, Sports, Arts & Theater, Family, Film, Miscellaneous) - Genre: Secondary category within a segment (e.g., Rock, Baseball, Comedy) - Subgenre: Tertiary category for specific classification (e.g., Alternative Rock, MLB) Use this tool to discover available categories before searching for events, or to understand how events are organized in the Ticketmaster system. The classifications can be filtered by locale, country, or specific classification ID.

tools.name: Get Event Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific event by ID. Use when you have an event's unique identifier and need its full details.

tools.name: Get Event Images
tools.description: Tool to retrieve images for a specific event by ID. Use when you need to fetch image URLs and metadata for an event.

tools.name: Search Events
tools.description: Search for events on Ticketmaster using various filters including location, date range, keywords, classifications, and more. This action queries the Ticketmaster Discovery API to find events matching your criteria. Results are paginated and can be sorted. Use this when you need to: search for concerts/shows/games, find events in a specific location, filter by date range, or discover events by artist/venue. Key capabilities: - Location search: by city, state, postal code, lat/long, or radius - Time filtering: events within date ranges or on-sale dates - Classification: filter by segment (Music/Sports/Arts), genre, subgenre - Keyword search: find events by name or description - Venue/Attraction: get events at specific venues or by specific artists/teams Note: Deep paging limit - size * page must be < 1000. Maximum 200 results per page.

tools.name: Get Genre Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific genre. Use when you need metadata for a single genre before filtering events by genre.

tools.name: Get Section Map Image
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the section map image for an event showing venue layout. Use when you need a visual representation of a venue's seating sections for a specific event. Optionally highlights specific sections or seats.

tools.name: Get Segment Details
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific Ticketmaster event segment, including all associated genres and subgenres. Segments are the top-level classification categories for events (e.g., Music, Sports, Arts & Theatre, Family, Film, Miscellaneous). This action returns the segment's metadata along with a complete list of genres and their subgenres that fall under this segment. Use this action after obtaining a segment ID from Get Classifications or from event classification data.

tools.name: Get Subgenre Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve detailed information about a specific subgenre. Use when you have a subgenre ID and need its details.

tools.name: Get Advanced Suggestions
tools.description: Get advanced auto-complete search suggestions from Ticketmaster's Discovery API. Returns matching attractions (artists, teams, performers), venues (concert halls, stadiums, theaters), and events based on search criteria with extensive filtering options. Use this when you need more control over suggestions including location filtering, source filtering, fuzzy matching, and spell checking. Perfect for implementing type-ahead search functionality with advanced filters or helping users discover entertainment options based on location, segment, and other criteria.

tools.name: Get Venue Details (Enhanced)
tools.description: Tool to retrieve comprehensive details about a specific venue by ID. Use when you need detailed venue information including location, box office info, images, and social media data.

tools.name: Get Venues
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of venues based on specified criteria. Use when you need venue details by name, location, or ID.

name: Ticktick
description: TickTick is a cross-platform task management and to-do list application designed to help users organize their tasks and schedules efficiently.

tools.name: Add Task Comment
tools.description: Add a discussion comment to a task in a TickTick project.

tools.name: Batch Create Or Update Tasks
tools.description: Create and update up to 50 TickTick tasks per operation in one request.

tools.name: Complete Task
tools.description: Marks a TickTick task as complete. Requires both the project_id and task_id, which can be obtained from TICKTICK_LIST_ALL_TASKS or TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK actions. This action is idempotent - completing an already-completed task will succeed without error. Completed tasks are removed from default/active views and appear only in completed task filters.

tools.name: Create Column
tools.description: Create a named column in an existing TickTick project.

tools.name: Create Project
tools.description: Create a new project (list) in TickTick. Projects organize tasks and notes. Use this to set up a new project with optional customizations like color, view mode, and type. The created project's ID can be used with other actions like TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK.

tools.name: Create Task
tools.description: Tool to create a new task in TickTick. Use after you have task details such as title, dates, and optional reminders or subtasks.

tools.name: Create Task (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK instead. Tool to create a new task in a specified project. Use when you need to create a task with required title and projectId, plus optional dates, priority, reminders, and subtasks.

tools.name: Delete TickTick Project
tools.description: Permanently deletes a TickTick project by its ID. All tasks within the project will also be deleted. Note: This operation is idempotent - deleting a non-existent project ID returns success. Use TICKTICK_GET_USER_PROJECT to list available projects and their IDs before deletion.

tools.name: Delete Task
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete a specific task — irreversible, no recovery. Use when you need to remove a task from a project after confirming both project and task IDs. Returns an empty data object on success; check status/success flags rather than response payload. When moving tasks between projects via create+delete, comments and history are lost.

tools.name: Filter Tasks
tools.description: Return tasks matching project, start-date, priority, tag, kind, and status filters.

tools.name: Get Project By ID
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific TickTick project by its unique ID. Use when you need detailed information about a particular project after obtaining its project ID.

tools.name: Get project with data
tools.description: Retrieve a project's associated data (incomplete tasks, columns). IMPORTANT: This endpoint only returns INCOMPLETE tasks. Completed tasks are automatically filtered out by the TickTick API. An empty tasks list means either the project has no tasks at all, or all tasks have been completed. For completed tasks, check the TickTick app or web interface directly. Columns are only present for kanban-style projects; list-view projects return an empty columns array. Join tasks to columns via each task's columnId field. For large projects, results may paginate at ~100 items per page — iterate all pages and deduplicate by taskId. Multiple tasks can share the same title; always use taskId for follow-up create, update, or delete calls. All filtering by name, tag, or other fields must be done client-side. Scope is project-only — Inbox and other projects are excluded.

tools.name: Get Task By Project And ID
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific TickTick task by project ID and task ID. Use when you need detailed information about a particular task within a project.

tools.name: Get User Projects
tools.description: Retrieves all projects accessible to the authenticated user, including personal and shared projects. Use this tool to list available projects before creating tasks or to get project IDs for other operations. Returns project metadata including name, color, view mode, and organization details. Always use returned projectId values (not project names) when calling TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK, TICKTICK_UPDATE_TASK, or TICKTICK_GET_PROJECT_WITH_DATA. The inbox project may not appear in results — omit projectId in TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK to target the inbox. Non-kanban projects return an empty columns array; check viewMode before assuming columns exist.

tools.name: List All Tasks
tools.description: Tool to list all open/undone tasks across all user projects in one call. This is a composite operation that internally fetches all projects and aggregates their tasks. Use when you need a comprehensive view of pending work across the entire account. Note: Only returns open/undone tasks; completed task history is not available in TickTick OpenAPI v1.

tools.name: List Completed Tasks
tools.description: Return up to 200 completed tasks, optionally filtered by project and completion date.

tools.name: List Project Members
tools.description: List the users who belong to a TickTick project.

tools.name: List Tags
tools.description: List the tags available to the connected TickTick account.

tools.name: List Task Comments
tools.description: List discussion comments attached to a task in a TickTick project.

tools.name: Move Tasks
tools.description: Move one or more existing tasks between TickTick projects.

tools.name: Generate OAuth2 Authorization URL
tools.description: Tool to generate the TickTick OAuth2 authorization URL. Use to redirect the user to obtain the authorization code (step 1). Re-run this tool if downstream TickTick calls return HTTP 401 (expired/invalid token) to obtain a fresh authorization code.

tools.name: Update Project
tools.description: Tool to update an existing project. Use when you need to modify project details like name, color, sort order, view mode, or kind after selecting a project ID.

tools.name: Update Task
tools.description: Tool to update an existing task. Use after confirming the taskId and projectId. Omitting optional fields resets them to null — include all existing field values in every payload. Cannot move a task to a different project; use TICKTICK_CREATE_TASK + TICKTICK_DELETE_TASK instead. Fields outside the input schema (e.g., columnId, assignee) are silently ignored.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create an API key at https://user.tikhub.io/users/api_keys and copy it when first shown. Allow the TikHub social-platform and /api/v1/tikhub/user/ routes you intend to use. No platform cookies or proxy credentials are required.

name: Tiktok
description: TikTok short-form video platform + creation tools + social sharing

tools.name: Fetch publish status
tools.description: Check the processing status of a TikTok video or photo post using its publish_id. Use this action to poll the status of content after initiating an upload or post. The API returns detailed information about processing stages (upload, download, moderation) and any errors that occurred. Non-terminal statuses mean processing is still pending — never re-initiate TIKTOK_PUBLISH_VIDEO for the same publish_id. Use exponential backoff when polling (e.g., 5s→10s→20s) to avoid the 30 requests/minute per access token rate limit.

tools.name: Get user stats
tools.description: Fetches TikTok user information and statistics for the authenticated user. Retrieves user stats (follower_count, following_count, likes_count, video_count) and can optionally fetch profile fields (display_name, username, bio_description, etc.) and basic info (open_id, union_id, avatar URLs). Returns only the fields requested in the fields parameter. Only works for the authenticated account; cannot fetch arbitrary public profiles. Stats may be delayed and not reflect the most recent activity.

tools.name: List videos
tools.description: Lists the authenticated user's own **public** TikTok videos, newest first. Only public posts are returned — private/`SELF_ONLY`, friends-only, and draft videos never appear (this is a property of the underlying `video.list` scope, not a bug), so on an account with no public posts the list is empty. Cannot list an arbitrary creator's videos, and does not provide a global TikTok-wide feed. Returns a single page (up to `max_count`, capped at 20). It does NOT auto-loop: when `has_more` is true, call again passing the returned `cursor` to fetch the next page. Accounts with more than `max_count` public videos are otherwise silently truncated.

tools.name: Post photo
tools.description: Create a photo post (1-35 images) on TikTok via Content Posting API. Supports two modes: - MEDIA_UPLOAD: Uploads photos to user's inbox for review/editing before posting - DIRECT_POST: Immediately posts photos to user's TikTok account IMPORTANT: Photo URLs must be from your TikTok-verified domain. Unverified domains will return 403 Forbidden. Unaudited apps can only post with privacy='SELF_ONLY'. Rate limit: 6 requests per minute per user access token. Reference: https://developers.tiktok.com/doc/content-posting-api-reference-photo-post

tools.name: Publish video
tools.description: Publishes a video to TikTok by pulling it from a public URL. TikTok downloads the video from the provided URL and publishes it directly to the creator's profile. Publishing is asynchronous — after calling this action, poll TIKTOK_FETCH_PUBLISH_STATUS with the returned publish_id to check completion. For uploading video files instead of URLs, use TIKTOK_UPLOAD_VIDEO.

tools.name: Query creator info
tools.description: Queries the authenticated creator's info and current posting options. Returns the account's available `privacy_level_options` and interaction settings (comment/duet/stitch), which the Content Posting API requires you to read before a direct post — the valid `privacy_level` values for an account are only discoverable here. Call this to pick a real privacy level instead of guessing (unaudited apps only ever get SELF_ONLY).

tools.name: Query videos
tools.description: Fetches metadata for specific TikTok videos by ID (1-20 per request). Verifies the videos belong to the authenticated user and returns their details, refreshing the cover-image URL's expiration. Unlike List videos, this looks up known video IDs rather than walking recent uploads.

tools.name: Upload video
tools.description: Uploads a video to TikTok via the Content Posting API. This action initializes an upload session to obtain a presigned upload URL, then uploads the file in one or more sequential PUT requests with TikTok-compatible ranges. Use a subsequent action to publish the post. Ensure the video file is fully generated and available before calling this action.

tools.name: Upload videos (batch)
tools.description: Uploads multiple videos to TikTok concurrently.

name: TikTok Ads

tools.name: Bind an event source to a catalog

tools.name: Cancel asynchronous report task
tools.description: Cancel a queued or processing asynchronous TikTok report task. Confirm the advertiser and disposable task ID before calling because cancellation is irreversible.

tools.name: Cancel the R&F ad order
tools.description: Cancel the R&F ad order. This operation is destructive or irreversible; confirm exact disposable targets before calling. This operation can affect billing, credit, invoices, budgets, contracts, or payments; require explicit approval and an isolated account.

tools.name: Create Business Center Organization Account

tools.name: Create a campaign

tools.name: Create an Offline Event Set

tools.name: Create rules

Automatically generated ad names cannot be updated. This does not target retired DYNAMIC ACO.

tools.name: Update Smart Creative Material Status
tools.description: Enable or disable current Smart Creative materials. Enabling a material can make it eligible for delivery and spend. This does not target retired DYNAMIC ACO.

tools.name: Update Smart+ Ad
tools.description: Update an existing Smart+ ad and its material configuration; at least one field to update must be provided.

tools.name: Update Smart+ Ad Group
tools.description: Update an existing Smart+ ad group's name, bid, budget, schedule, pacing, comment or sharing settings, and audience targeting. Omitted settings remain unchanged; at least one field to update must be provided.

tools.name: Update Smart+ Ad Group Budgets
tools.description: Update immediate total budgets or next-day scheduled daily budgets for Upgraded Smart+ ad groups. Provide a non-empty budget or scheduled_budget list. For CBO campaigns where budget_optimize_on is true, a min_budget or max_budget or both must already be configured before a scheduled-budget update; non-CBO ad groups have no such prerequisite.

tools.name: Update Smart+ Ad Material Status
tools.description: Enable or disable up to 20 materials belonging to a Smart+ ad. Enabling materials can make them eligible for delivery and spend.

tools.name: Update Smart+ Campaign
tools.description: Update an existing Smart+ campaign's supported fields; at least one field to update must be provided. Perform mutation QA only on a disabled or draft campaign; this action does not enable or publish it.

tools.name: Update the time of a split test
tools.description: Update the start and end time of a split test.

tools.name: Set or update the Brand Safety Hub settings of an ad account
tools.description: Set or update an advertiser account's Brand Safety Hub settings. Setting cover_all_ad_objectives to true is irreversible and cannot be reverted.

tools.name: Upload verification documents
tools.description: Upload one or two verification document images.

tools.name: Upload Business Certificate Image
tools.description: Upload a business certificate image for an ad account through a Business Center where the connected user is an administrator.

tools.name: Upload catalog products
tools.description: Upload up to 5,000 products using the fields documented for each catalog type.

tools.name: Upload products via a file URL
tools.description: Ingest a CSV catalog feed from a directly accessible HTTP or HTTPS URL. INCREMENTAL preserves omitted products; OVERWRITE permanently removes omitted products, so confirm the complete source file before using it.

tools.name: Upload Catalog Videos by File URL
tools.description: Upload catalog videos from a file URL.

tools.name: Upload an Audience File
tools.description: Upload a CSV or TXT customer file after verifying its supplied MD5 signature.

tools.name: Upload a file in chunks
tools.description: Upload one image, video, or music file through TikTok's start, ordered chunk-transfer, and finish workflow. Chunk signatures are computed internally.

tools.name: Upload an image
tools.description: Upload an advertiser image by local file, URL, or temporary file ID.

tools.name: Upload a piece of music
tools.description: Upload advertiser music or update a Carousel Ads music list.

tools.name: Upload a file
tools.description: Upload a temporary image, music, video, or playable file by file or URL.

tools.name: Upload a video
tools.description: Upload an advertiser video by local file, URL, temporary file ID, or existing video ID.

tools.name: Upload a playable asset
tools.description: Upload a playable ZIP package or reference a file already in TikTok's file repository. Direct packages must be 5 MB or smaller, contain index.html and config.json at the root, and must not load external network resources.

tools.name: Validate a URL
tools.description: Get TikTok verification results for a URL.

tools.name: Check the status of a playable asset
tools.description: Check validation status and failure details for one playable asset.
