name: TimelinesAI
description: TimelinesAI enables teams to manage and automate WhatsApp communications, integrating with various CRMs and tools to streamline workflows.

tools.name: Delete File
tools.description: Tool to delete an uploaded file by its UID. Use after confirming the file is no longer needed.

tools.name: Delete Webhook
tools.description: Tool to delete a webhook subscription by its ID. Use when you need to remove an existing webhook after confirming the webhook ID. Example: "Delete the webhook with ID '9f6a8c3d-56b7-4a1e-8f2e-abcdef123456'."

tools.name: Get Chat Messages
tools.description: Tool to get messages from a specific chat in TimelinesAI. Use when you need to retrieve message history or recent messages from a chat. Example: "Get the last 20 messages from chat 'chat_123abc'."

tools.name: Get Chats
tools.description: Tool to get full or filtered list of all chats. Use when you need to browse or search chats with optional filters. Example: "List all unread chats assigned to me."

tools.name: Get File Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve metadata and temporary download URL for an uploaded file. Use after uploading a file or when needing its URL.

tools.name: Get Webhook
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific webhook subscription by its ID. Use this action to: - Check webhook configuration (URL, event type, enabled status) - Monitor webhook health (error counter) - Verify webhook existence before updating or deleting Prerequisites: You must have a valid webhook ID. Use the Get Webhooks action to list all available webhooks first.

tools.name: Get Webhooks
tools.description: Retrieves all webhook subscriptions configured for the workspace. Webhooks notify external systems about events (e.g., 'message:new', 'chat:new') in real-time. Use this to view existing webhook configurations, check their status, or retrieve webhook IDs for updates/deletion. Supports optional pagination via limit and offset parameters.

tools.name: Get WhatsApp Accounts
tools.description: Tool to list all WhatsApp accounts connected to the workspace. Use after configuring WhatsApp integration to verify accounts.

tools.name: List Uploaded Files
tools.description: Tool to list files uploaded in your TimelinesAI workspace. Use when you need to retrieve all uploaded files.

tools.name: Send WhatsApp Message to Number
tools.description: Tool to send a WhatsApp text message to a phone number via TimelinesAI. Use this to send messages to any recipient phone number using one of your connected WhatsApp accounts as the sender. The message will be delivered immediately if the recipient number is reachable on WhatsApp. Example: Send 'Hello, how can I help you today?' from +15105566777 to +14151231234.

tools.name: Create Webhook Subscription
tools.description: Tool to create a new webhook subscription. Use when you have the event type and callback URL ready.

tools.name: Update Webhook
tools.description: Tool to update an existing webhook subscription. Use after confirming the webhook ID when you need to change the URL, subscribed event types, or enable/disable a webhook.

tools.name: Send Message to Chat
tools.description: Send a WhatsApp message to an existing chat in TimelinesAI. Use this action when you have a chat ID from the Get Chats action and want to send a message to that conversation. For sending messages to new phone numbers (not existing chats), use the 'Send WhatsApp Message to Number' action instead. Example: "Send message 'Hello world' to chat with ID 'chat_123abc'."

triggers.name: New WhatsApp Message Received
triggers.description: Polling trigger that monitors for new messages received in TimelinesAI WhatsApp chats.

required.name: bearer_token
required.description: The API token generated from the TimelinesAI Integrations section.

name: Timelink
description: Timelink is a time tracking application designed to simplify and enhance the process of recording work hours, offering both software and hardware solutions for efficient time management.

tools.name: Delete Person
tools.description: Tool to delete a person record. Use when you need to remove a person by their unique identifier after confirming this detail.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: The API token used for authenticating requests to the Timelink API.

name: TinyFish
description: TinyFish provides web automation, live search, content extraction, research, browser sessions, reusable browser profiles, and run management through native REST APIs.

tools.name: Cancel Profile Setup Session
tools.description: Cancel a Browser Context Profile setup session and permanently discard its unsaved cookies and browser storage.

tools.name: Cancel Research Run
tools.description: Cancel one running TinyFish research run. Cancellation is irreversible but idempotent: terminal runs return their current status with cancelled=false.

tools.name: Cancel Runs
tools.description: Idempotently cancel one or up to 100 asynchronous or SSE runs. Active cancellation is irreversible; synchronous runs cannot be cancelled, and already-terminal runs are returned with their actual status.

tools.name: Create Browser Session
tools.description: Create an isolated TinyFish remote browser session and return its CDP connection URL. This action starts billable browser infrastructure: TinyFish meters Browser usage until the session ends or becomes inactive. You must call Terminate Browser Session with the returned session_id immediately after browser work finishes, including after failures, to stop further usage charges. Creation can return before startup navigation completes.

tools.name: Create Monitor
tools.description: Create a scheduled Page or Topic Monitor and immediately capture its paid baseline. Each completed baseline costs $0.005, failed runs are not charged, and an account can hold at most 50 Monitors. A timeout or server error can leave the Monitor created; list Monitors before manually resubmitting.

tools.name: Create Profile
tools.description: Create a reusable Browser Context Profile for cookies and browser storage; this changes persistent account state.

tools.name: Delete Monitor
tools.description: Permanently delete a TinyFish Monitor and its schedule. Its Monitor run history becomes unavailable and this action cannot be undone. If the outcome is ambiguous, verify with Get or List Monitors before another delete.

tools.name: Delete Profile
tools.description: Permanently delete a Browser Context Profile and all browser state saved in it. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: Delete Profile Domain
tools.description: Permanently remove saved cookies and browser storage for one domain from a Browser Context Profile. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: Fetch URLs
tools.description: Render and extract content from 1-10 URLs in one provider-native batch. Always inspect both results and errors because HTTP 200 can contain successful pages and per-URL failures together.

tools.name: Get Monitor
tools.description: Get one TinyFish Page or Topic Monitor by ID, including its immutable target config, schedule, lifecycle status, webhook, and last error.

tools.name: Get Profile
tools.description: Get one Browser Context Profile and its saved-domain metadata.

tools.name: Get Research Run
tools.description: Read one saved TinyFish research run, including status, partial or final reports, plan, evidence, and iteration count. Inspect status before treating any report as complete; unsuccessful runs can retain partial results.

tools.name: Get Runs
tools.description: Get summary records for 1-100 TinyFish automation run IDs in one request. The response separately reports IDs that were not found or are not owned.

tools.name: Get Wallet
tools.description: Get the TinyFish wallet balance, auto-reload and pending-top-up state, and current Agent and Browser rates. Monetary values are returned as exact decimal strings. Legacy-credit accounts report FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE rather than an authentication failure.

tools.name: List Monitors
tools.description: List all Page and Topic Monitors owned by the connected TinyFish account, including IDs needed for read, update, run-now, and delete operations.

tools.name: List Profiles
tools.description: List Browser Context Profiles available to the connected TinyFish account. Use the returned IDs when attaching or managing reusable browser state.

tools.name: List Research Runs
tools.description: List saved TinyFish research runs with optional status, query, date, and sort filters, returning one cursor-controlled page.

tools.name: List Runs
tools.description: List automation runs with optional status, goal, date, and sort filters, returning one cursor-controlled page.

tools.name: List Usage
tools.description: List one page of Search, Fetch, or Browser usage history. Search and Fetch usage reads are free; Browser usage requires the paid Browser service.

tools.name: List Vault Connections
tools.description: List display-safe metadata for password-manager vaults connected to TinyFish. Credentials and secret values are excluded.

tools.name: List Vault Items
tools.description: List display-safe metadata for items synchronized from password-manager vaults connected to TinyFish. Secret field values are never returned.

tools.name: Run Monitor Now
tools.description: Run an existing Page or Topic Monitor immediately and save its result. Each completed run costs $0.005 and sends no webhook or email notification. A timeout or server error does not prove rejection, so never retry blindly. A confirmed RETRY_REQUIRED conflict means no run was created.

tools.name: Save Profile Setup Session
tools.description: Persist cookies and browser storage from a completed setup session into a Browser Context Profile, then clean up the temporary session. Persisted state and successful session cleanup cannot be undone. The response retains domain-level skips and failures plus cleanup status so partial success remains visible.

tools.name: Search Web
tools.description: Search live web pages, news, or research papers with domain and time filters, optionally fetching result pages inline, and return exactly one caller-selected zero-based result page.

tools.name: Start Profile Setup Session
tools.description: Start a billable temporary remote browser session for establishing login state in a Browser Context Profile. The returned browser state is not saved automatically: after setup, always call Save Profile Setup Session to persist it or Cancel Profile Setup Session to discard it and tear down the session.

tools.name: Start Research Async
tools.description: Start a paid TinyFish research run in the background and return its durable run ID. Poll Get Research Run for saved partial or final results. A timeout does not prove rejection, so never automatically submit the same research again.

tools.name: Sync Vault Items
tools.description: Refresh display-safe item metadata from all password-manager vaults already connected to TinyFish. Synchronization can add, update, or remove mirrored items. Returns synchronization counts and allowlisted item metadata without credential or secret values.

tools.name: Terminate Browser Session
tools.description: Idempotently terminate a remote TinyFish browser session to stop further browser usage charges. Already-ended sessions are also successful.

tools.name: Update Monitor
tools.description: Pause or resume a TinyFish Monitor, or edit its schedule and delivery metadata. Status changes cannot be combined with schedule or metadata edits; type and target config are immutable. On an ambiguous failure, get the Monitor before repeating the update.

tools.name: Update Profile
tools.description: Rename a Browser Context Profile or change its default and proxy-country settings. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

tools.name: Upload Profile State
tools.description: Upload cookies and local or session storage directly into a Browser Context Profile. This changes persistent login state and may transmit authentication secrets; call it only with the credential owner's explicit authorization. TinyFish provides no rollback endpoint, so restoring prior state requires a caller-held copy or deleting the affected domains.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Create or copy a TinyFish REST API key from the API Keys page at https://agent.tinyfish.ai/api-keys. The same key authenticates Agent, Search, Fetch, and Browser REST requests. Keep it secret.

name: TinyFish MCP
description: TinyFish MCP lets authorized agents search and fetch live web content, run and inspect browser automations, manage browser sessions and monitors, and review usage and wallet status.

tools.name: Batch cancel
tools.description: Only use when the user explicitly asks to stop multiple running or pending automations. Never cancel because runs are slow, still pending, or a status call returned without results — keep waiting instead. Cancels runs by ID. Idempotent: already-terminal runs return their current status.

tools.name: Batch status
tools.description: Only use after batch_create to poll progress for multiple automation runs. Checks status by ID for up to 8 runs and returns status, result, and error for each. Poll every 30-60s until all runs reach a terminal state (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED).

tools.name: Cancel run
tools.description: Only use when the user explicitly asks to stop a running or pending automation. Never cancel because a run is slow, still pending, or a wait/poll call returned without a result — keep waiting instead. Cancels a run by ID. Idempotent: terminal runs (COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED) return the current status without error.

tools.name: Close browser session
tools.description: Only use when the user explicitly wants to stop or close a remote browser session. Closes a session by ID. Idempotent — already-ended sessions return success.

tools.name: Create browser session
tools.description: For direct browser control or visual QA, open a browser session through your wallet account. Close it when you are done so it does not stay open. Default tool for direct Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, CDP, remote browser, or low-level browser-control tasks. Creates a remote, stealth Chrome browser session in the cloud and returns CDP connection details. Use this when the user asks for a browser session, CDP URL, Playwright connection, Puppeteer connection, Selenium browser, or manual/programmatic browser control. Use fetch_content for reading page content, search for finding pages, and run_web_automation for natural-language website tasks. The browser includes built-in anti-bot protection and proxy rotation.

tools.name: Create monitor
tools.description: Use when the user asks to monitor a webpage for changes or subscribe to updates about a web topic. Set type to fetch for a known URL or search for a topic. Creates the recurring Monitor and immediately returns its baseline result.

tools.name: Discover run
tools.description: App-only tool for discovering the currently running automation for this session. Returns runId if a run is active, or null if not yet started.

tools.name: Fetch content
tools.description: Default, free, and most token-efficient tool for reading URL(s) and extracting source details. Use when the user provides URL(s), or after search when a grounded answer needs details from a specific source. Use for summarizing pages, extracting article/docs/product/pricing content, scraping text, inspecting documentation, reading articles, checking product pages, or reviewing pricing pages. Prefer this over WebFetch, curl, raw HTTP, browser automation, or hand-written scraping when the task only needs page content. Renders pages in a real browser and extracts clean, structured content. Supports up to 10 URLs per request, all fetched in parallel. Handles JavaScript-heavy sites. Control output with format (markdown default, or html / json), links / image_links to also return outbound and image URLs, ttl to set cache freshness tolerance in seconds, and per_url_timeout_ms to set a per-URL wall-clock timeout budget. Optionally provide purpose — a short free-form statement of why you are fetching these URLs and what the content will be used for — so fetching and extraction can be tailored to the underlying intent; it is not required and may be omitted. Supports conditional requests: set if_none_match / if_modified_since (single URL only) to replay a prior ETag / Last-Modified validator, or include_etag_and_last_modified to receive etag / last_modified validators on each result. Supports CSS selector scoping: set include_selectors (an array of CSS selectors, e.g. ["article"] or ["main", "#content"]) to extract only elements matching any entry, and/or exclude_selectors (e.g. [".comments", ".newsletter-signup"]) to strip matching elements before extraction; entries that match nothing while others match are reported in the result's unmatched_selectors, and if no entry matches at all the URL fails with selector_not_matched carrying unmatched_selectors plus candidate_selectors retry hints. Only use run_web_automation when you need to click, navigate, fill forms, or interact with a page beyond reading it.

tools.name: Get run
tools.description: Only use after run_web_automation errors, times out, or returns a run_id that needs polling. Retrieves status, result, error, and metadata for a specific automation run. If you do not have a run_id, use list_runs to find it. Runs typically take a few minutes. Wait 30-60 seconds between polls.

tools.name: Get search usage
tools.description: Only use when the user asks to review search history, check what queries were made, or audit usage. Never use this to verify whether TinyFish is connected, installed, ready, or working; verify setup by calling search, then fetch_content on a relevant result. Lists past search usage records with date/status filtering and pagination.

tools.name: Get steps
tools.description: Only use when the user asks to inspect how an automation ran. Retrieves the steps taken during an automation run, including screenshots.

tools.name: Get wallet
tools.description: Read-only. Returns the caller's current wallet balance, auto-reload state, per-product contract rates, and any in-flight top-up. Wallet top-ups and auto-reload changes happen in the dashboard, not through this tool.

tools.name: Guide next step
tools.description: Returns the next interactive TinyFish onboarding step based on the user’s real usage. Ask for the user’s input and wait before running the suggested tool.

tools.name: List browser sessions
tools.description: Only use when the user asks to check active browser sessions, review browser usage history, or find a specific browser session by ID. Lists sessions with filtering and pagination.

tools.name: List fetch usage
tools.description: Only use when the user asks to review fetch history or audit fetch usage. Never use this to verify whether TinyFish is connected, installed, ready, or working. Lists past fetch_content requests with optional filtering by date range and status. Does not include the fetched text content itself.

tools.name: List runs
tools.description: Only use when you need to find a run_id for a recently created automation, usually after run_web_automation timed out before returning one. Lists automation runs with optional filtering by status and pagination. Filter by status=RUNNING to find active runs.

tools.name: Poll status
tools.description: App-only tool for polling the current status of an automation run. Returns status, step, progress, and other metadata.

tools.name: Run web automation
tools.description: Metered web automation is available through your wallet — use it for clicking, forms, login, or dynamic pages. Default tool for interactive website tasks when there is one site or workflow, web automation, or browser automation: clicking, navigating beyond a provided page, opening a story/result, filling forms, logging in, operating a browser, or extracting data that requires page interaction. Use this when the user asks to automate one website, complete one web workflow, scrape through navigation, or interact with a page beyond reading static content. Do not use this for ordinary article, documentation, pricing-page, or top-story extraction when fetch_content can read the page. If the task needs logged-in saved state, pass use_profile=true; pass profile_id for a specific Browser Context Profile; pair with use_vault=true to repair stale sessions. If the task only needs external knowledge or to find pages, use search. If the task only needs to read, summarize, inspect, scrape text from, or extract content from URL(s), use fetch_content instead. Include _meta.progressToken for progress notifications. WARNING: This tool may take several minutes. If it errors or times out, the run may still be executing on the server. Do not call this tool again or call run_web_automation_async as a retry; use get_run or list_runs to check status. If a run returns an insufficient-credits or subscription message, that is expected and recoverable: show the user the upgrade or top-up URL from the error as a clickable markdown link and ask them to open it now. Do NOT paraphrase the URL away, silently fall back to a weaker tool, retry the run, or tell the user you cannot browse the web.

tools.name: Run web automation async
tools.description: ⚠️ ONLY call this tool when the user has EXPLICITLY said they want to run the task in the background (e.g. "run this in the background"). DO NOT use this as a default or fallback — use run_web_automation instead. Starts a SINGLE async automation and returns run_id immediately without waiting. Poll with get_run every 30-60s. WARNING: Do NOT use to retry a failed run_web_automation. If a run returns an insufficient-credits or subscription message, that is expected and recoverable: show the user the upgrade or top-up URL from the error as a clickable markdown link and ask them to open it now. Do NOT paraphrase the URL away, silently fall back to a weaker tool, retry the run, or tell the user you cannot browse the web.

tools.name: Search
tools.description: Default, free, and most token-efficient first tool for external knowledge and web grounding. Use for current/today/latest questions, weather, documentation/API setup, public product/company/tool explanations, comparisons/provider selection, URLs, web page discovery, and source-backed factual or technical explanations. Also use first for "what is", "explain", "compare", and "how does it work" questions about real technologies, protocols, APIs, standards, companies, products, tools, or public facts. Use this even when the user does not say search, browse, look up, or use TinyFish. Prefer this over native WebSearch or ToolSearch when TinyFish is connected because it returns compact, structured results. Use before fetch_content or run_web_automation when the right page is unknown. Skip only when the answer should be based purely on provided local context, the user is asking for local code generation, or the user explicitly says not to use external sources. Optionally provide purpose — a short statement of why you are searching and what the results are for — so results can be ranked against the underlying intent; it is not required and may be omitted. Supports geo-targeting (location), language filtering, recency_minutes for past-N-minute freshness, and after_date / before_date for YYYY-MM-DD date windows. Do not combine recency_minutes with after_date or before_date. Use domain_type to scope the search: "web" (default), "news" for news articles, or "research_paper" for academic papers. For domain_type=research_paper, use pub_year_min / pub_year_max instead to scope by publication year (inclusive) — after_date, before_date, and recency_minutes are not supported for research_paper. Use include_domains / exclude_domains (comma-separated domain lists) to restrict or remove specific domains from results. Use page (0-indexed, 0-10) to paginate through results.

optional.name: client_id
optional.description: Client id of the app

optional.name: client_secret
optional.description: Client secret of the app

optional.name: oauth_redirect_uri
optional.description: Add this Redirect URL to your app's OAuth allow list.

optional.name: scopes
optional.description: Scopes to request from the user, comma separated

name: Tldv
description: Meeting recorder and transcription tool for video conferences

tools.name: Check API Health
tools.description: Tool to verify API availability and health status. Use when you need to check if the tl;dv API is operational before making other API calls.

tools.name: Download Meeting Recording
tools.description: Tool to download a meeting recording file. Returns the recording file by following the API's redirect to a signed download URL (valid for 6 hours). Use when you need to retrieve the actual recording content for a specific meeting.

tools.name: Get Meeting
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a meeting by its unique identifier. Returns detailed meeting metadata including id, name, date, URL, duration, organizer, invitees, template, and extra properties. Use when you need to fetch information about a specific meeting.

tools.name: Get Meeting Highlights
tools.description: Tool to retrieve meeting notes (highlights) by meeting ID in human-readable format. Use when you need to fetch notes from a completed meeting. Highlights are only returned if the transcript is complete.

tools.name: Get Meeting Transcript
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the complete transcript of a meeting by its ID. Returns transcript segments with speaker names, text, and timestamps. The transcript is only returned if it is complete.

tools.name: Import Meeting
tools.description: Tool to import a meeting, recording, or other media from a publicly accessible URL. The URL must point to media in a supported format (mp3, mp4, wav, m4a, mkv, mov, avi, wma, flac). Returns a job ID to track the import progress. Use when you need to add external recordings to tldv.

tools.name: List Meetings
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a paginated list of meetings from tldv. Returns meeting metadata including id, name, occurrence date, URL, duration, organizer details, invitees, and template information. Use when you need to view recorded meetings or search for specific meeting details.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your tl;dv API key for accessing your meetings and transcripts. Create one in tl;dv under Settings → Personal Settings → API Keys (requires a paid plan).

name: Todoist MCP
description: Todoist MCP lets agents read, create, update, organize, and complete tasks and projects through Todoist's hosted Streamable HTTP server.

tools.name: Add-comments
tools.description: Add multiple comments to tasks or projects, optionally notifying collaborators. Each comment must specify either taskId or projectId.

tools.name: Add-filters
tools.description: Add one or more new personal filters. Filters are saved custom views using query syntax to organize tasks.

tools.name: Add-labels
tools.description: Add one or more new personal labels.

tools.name: Add-projects
tools.description: Add one or more new projects.

tools.name: Add-reminders
tools.description: Add reminders to tasks. Supports three types: "relative" (minutes before due), "absolute" (specific date/time), or "location" (geofence-triggered). Each reminder must specify a taskId.

tools.name: Add-sections
tools.description: Add one or more new sections to projects.

tools.name: Add-tasks
tools.description: Add one or more tasks to a project, section, or parent. Supports assignment to project collaborators.

tools.name: Analyze-project-health
tools.description: Trigger a new health analysis for a project. Use this when the health data is stale or you want a fresh assessment. The analysis may take time to complete — use get-project-health afterward to see updated results.

tools.name: Complete-tasks
tools.description: Complete one or more tasks by their IDs.

tools.name: Delete-object
tools.description: Delete a project, section, task, comment, label, filter, reminder, or location_reminder by its ID. Projects can be deleted whether active or archived (find archived ones via find-projects with archivedStatus); note a workspace project must be archived before it can be deleted, while personal projects can be deleted regardless.

tools.name: Export-project-template
tools.description: Export an existing project as a Todoist template, either as CSV content or as a shareable URL. Use it to duplicate a project, share its structure, or hand the CSV to import-project-template. To read a project rather than export it, use find-tasks instead — it returns structured tasks rather than raw CSV. Nothing is modified.

tools.name: Fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full contents of a task or project by its ID. The ID should be in the format "task:{id}" or "project:{id}".

tools.name: Fetch-object
tools.description: Fetch a single task, project, comment, or section by its ID. Use this when you have a specific object ID and want to retrieve its full details. Set includeChildren to also get its direct subtasks or sub-projects.

tools.name: Find-activity
tools.description: Retrieve activity logs to monitor and audit changes in Todoist. Shows events from all users by default (use initiatorId to filter by specific user). To answer what someone completed in a period, including recurring task occurrences, use objectType "task", eventType "completed", and dateFrom/dateTo. For a first-person question ("what did I get done"), also set initiatorId to the current user from user-info, or the answer includes collaborators' completions. Track task completions, updates, deletions, project changes, and more with flexible filtering. Activity history availability and retention depend on the user plan.

tools.name: Find-comments
tools.description: Find comments by task, project, or get a specific comment by ID. Exactly one of taskId, projectId, or commentId must be provided.

tools.name: Find-completed-tasks
tools.description: Get completed tasks in a date range. For "what did I complete/get done" questions, use find-activity instead — it reports completion events, including every occurrence of a recurring task, which this tool does not. since/until are optional and default to a 7-day window when omitted. Includes all collaborators by default. Person-specific queries (summaries, plans, reports) require responsibleUser.

tools.name: Find-filters
tools.description: List all personal filters or search for filters by name. Filters are saved custom views that use query syntax to organize tasks (e.g. "today & p1", "#Work & overdue").

tools.name: Find-labels
tools.description: List personal labels and shared labels. Personal labels have full metadata (id, name, color, order, isFavorite) and support pagination and name search (partial, case insensitive). Shared labels are labels used on tasks shared with you — they are returned as names only (no IDs or metadata). When searching, all matching personal labels are fetched across all pages and returned as a single result set (limit and cursor are ignored). When not searching, personal labels are returned with pagination.

tools.name: Find-project-collaborators
tools.description: Find Todoist users (collaborators, teammates) by name or email to look up their user ID. Use this whenever the user asks to find, look up, or identify a person — e.g. "find Carrie's user ID", "who is Ernesto", "look up a user". When projectId is omitted, searches across the collaborators of every shared project the authenticated user has access to, plus the authenticated user themselves — an empty result means the person is not a collaborator on any project you share with them, not necessarily that they do not exist in Todoist. When projectId is provided, searches only that project. Partial, case-insensitive match on name and email.

tools.name: Find-projects
tools.description: List all projects or search for projects by name. By default only active projects are returned; use archivedStatus ('archived' or 'all') to include archived projects. When searching or when archivedStatus is 'all', all matching projects are returned (pagination is ignored). Otherwise projects are returned with pagination.

tools.name: Find-reminders
tools.description: Find reminders by task ID (returns all reminder types), or get a specific reminder by its ID. Use reminderId for time-based reminders and locationReminderId for location reminders.

tools.name: Find-sections
tools.description: Search for sections by name or other criteria in a project. When searching, uses server-side search to avoid fetching all sections.

tools.name: Find-tasks
tools.description: Find tasks by text search, project/section/parent container, responsible user, labels, a raw Todoist filter string, or a saved filter by ID or name (filterIdOrName). At least one filter must be provided.

tools.name: Find-tasks-by-date
tools.description: Get tasks by date range. startDate='today' includes overdue items. Default responsibleUserFiltering='unassignedOrMe' excludes others' tasks.

tools.name: Get-overview
tools.description: Get a Markdown overview. If no projectId is provided, shows all projects with hierarchy and sections (useful for navigation). If projectId is provided, shows detailed overview of that specific project including all tasks grouped by sections.

tools.name: Get-productivity-stats
tools.description: Get comprehensive productivity statistics including daily/weekly completion breakdowns, goal streaks (current, last, max), karma score and trends, and historical karma data. Useful for productivity analysis and tracking goal progress. Reports counts, streaks and karma only, never the tasks themselves — for "what did I complete", use find-activity.

tools.name: Get-project-activity-stats
tools.description: Get daily and optional weekly task completion counts for a project over a configurable time window (1-12 weeks). Useful for identifying completion trends and patterns.

tools.name: Get-project-health
tools.description: Get a comprehensive health assessment for a project including completion progress, health status (EXCELLENT, ON_TRACK, AT_RISK, CRITICAL), and optional detailed context with project metrics and task-level data. Use includeContext=true for that full detail.

tools.name: Get-workspace-insights
tools.description: Get aggregated health and progress insights across all projects in a workspace. Accepts workspace name or ID, with optional project ID filtering. Useful for a cross-project health overview.

tools.name: Import-project-template
tools.description: Import a template into an existing project, adding its tasks, sections and comments to whatever is already there. Source it by template ID/URL or by passing CSV content from export-project-template. To start a new project from a template, create the project with add-projects first, then import into it. This writes immediately and cannot be undone, so only run it against a project the user named.

tools.name: List-workspaces
tools.description: Get all workspaces for the authenticated user. Returns workspace details including ID, name, plan type (STARTER/BUSINESS), user role (ADMIN/MEMBER/GUEST), link sharing settings, guest permissions, creation date, and creator ID.

tools.name: Manage-assignments
tools.description: Bulk assignment operations for multiple tasks. Supports assign, unassign, and reassign operations with atomic rollback on failures.

tools.name: Project-management
tools.description: Archive or unarchive a project by its ID.

tools.name: Project-move
tools.description: Move a project between personal and workspace contexts.

tools.name: Reorder-objects
tools.description: Reorder sibling projects or sections, and optionally move projects to a new parent. For projects: set order to reorder siblings, and/or set parentId to move under a new parent (use "root" for top level). For sections: set order to reorder within a project.

tools.name: Reschedule-tasks
tools.description: Reschedule tasks to new dates while preserving recurring schedules. Unlike update-tasks (which replaces the entire due string and can wipe recurrence), this tool changes only the date, keeping recurrence patterns intact. Use this when moving recurring tasks to a different date without altering their repeat pattern.

tools.name: Search
tools.description: Search across tasks and projects in Todoist. Returns a list of relevant results with IDs, titles, and URLs.

tools.name: Uncomplete-tasks
tools.description: Uncomplete (reopen) one or more completed tasks by their IDs.

tools.name: Update-comments
tools.description: Update multiple existing comments with new content.

tools.name: Update-filters
tools.description: Update one or more existing personal filters with new values.

tools.name: Update-labels
tools.description: Update one or more existing labels. Personal labels (identified by ID) can have their name, color, order, and favorite flag updated. Shared labels (identified by name) can only be renamed.

tools.name: Update-projects
tools.description: Update multiple existing projects with new values.

tools.name: Update-reminders
tools.description: Update existing reminders. Each reminder must specify its type ("relative", "absolute", or "location") and ID. Only include fields that need to change.

tools.name: Update-sections
tools.description: Update multiple existing sections with new values.

tools.name: Update-tasks
tools.description: Update existing tasks including content, dates, priorities, and assignments. Send only the fields that change.

tools.name: User-info
tools.description: Get comprehensive user information including user ID, full name, email, timezone with current local time, week start day preferences, current week dates, daily/weekly goal progress, and user plan (Free/Pro/Business).

tools.name: View-attachment
tools.description: View a file attachment from a Todoist comment. Pass the fileUrl from a comment's fileAttachment field. Supports images (returned inline), text files (returned as text), and binary files like PDFs (returned as embedded resources).

optional.description: Client id of the app

optional.name: client_secret
optional.description: Client secret of the app

optional.description: Add this Redirect URL to your app's OAuth allow list.

optional.description: Scopes to request from the user, comma separated

name: Toggl
description: Toggl is a time tracking application that helps users monitor and manage their work hours efficiently.

tools.name: Create Client
tools.description: Tool to create a new client in a workspace. Use when you need to add a client to a workspace after workspace setup.

tools.name: Create Group
tools.description: Tool to create a new group in a Toggl organization. Use when organizing users into teams and controlling access to workspaces. Groups help manage user permissions and workspace assignments at the organization level.

tools.name: Create Invitation
tools.description: Tool to send invitations to join a Toggl organization. Use when you need to invite users by email to an organization and its workspaces. At least one email and one workspace (or project_invite) are required.

tools.name: Create Organization
tools.description: Tool to create a new organization with a default workspace in Toggl Track. Use when initializing a new organization and workspace in one step. The authenticated user becomes the organization owner.

tools.name: Create Project
tools.description: Creates a new project in a Toggl workspace. Projects are used to organize time entries and track work for specific initiatives. Required parameters: workspace_id (integer) and name (string). Optional parameters include client assignment, privacy settings, billable status, and time estimates. Note: Some features (custom colors, templates, fixed fees, hourly rates) require a premium Toggl plan.

tools.name: Create Tag
tools.description: Tool to create a new tag in a workspace. Use when you need to add a tag after confirming workspace ID and desired tag name.

tools.name: Create Time Entry
tools.description: Tool to create a new time entry in the specified workspace. Use when you have workspace ID, start time, and client name ready.

tools.name: Add User to Workspace Project
tools.description: Tool to add a user to workspace project users. Use when you need to assign a user to a project within a workspace with optional manager privileges and custom rates.

tools.name: Delete Toggl Client
tools.description: Tool to delete a client in Toggl. Use when you have confirmed the workspace and client IDs and want to remove a client permanently.

tools.name: Delete Group
tools.description: Tool to delete a group from a Toggl organization. Use when you need to permanently remove a group and its associated permissions. Requires organization and group IDs.

tools.name: Delete Project Group
tools.description: Tool to delete a project group from a Toggl workspace. Use when you need to remove a project group permanently. Requires workspace and project group IDs.

tools.name: Delete Subscription
tools.description: Tool to delete a webhook subscription in Toggl. Use when you want to remove an existing subscription for a specific workspace.

tools.name: Delete Tag
tools.description: Deletes a tag from a Toggl workspace. Requires workspace and tag IDs. Only workspace or organization administrators can delete tags. Returns success status upon deletion.

tools.name: Disable Weekly Report
tools.description: Tool to disable weekly report email notifications. Use when you want to unsubscribe from weekly reports using the code provided in report emails.

tools.name: Bulk Edit Time Entries
tools.description: Tool to bulk edit multiple time entries in a workspace using JSON Patch operations. Use when you need to update the same field(s) across multiple time entries at once (e.g., changing descriptions, billable status, or project associations). Maximum 100 time entries per request.

tools.name: Get All Plans
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all available Toggl subscription plans and their features. Use when you need to display plan options, compare plans, or check available features for different subscription tiers.

tools.name: Get Client Details
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific client in Toggl Track by its client ID and workspace ID. Use this tool when you need to: - Get complete client details including name, notes, and metadata - Verify if a client exists in a workspace - Check client archive status, timestamps, or external references - Retrieve integration information for JIRA/Salesforce linked clients

tools.name: Get Countries
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all countries supported by Toggl. Returns country details including tax information, default currencies, and postal code requirements. Use when you need to validate country data or retrieve country-specific settings for billing.

tools.name: Get Country Subdivisions
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all subdivisions (states, provinces, regions) for a specific country in Toggl Track. Use when you need to get geographical subdivision data for a country, such as US states or Canadian provinces.

tools.name: Get Currencies
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the list of all currencies supported by Toggl Track. Use when you need currency codes and symbols for financial operations or display.

tools.name: Get Current Time Entry
tools.description: Retrieves the currently running time entry for the authenticated user. Returns null if no timer is active. Use this to check timer status or get details about the active time entry.

tools.name: Get Event Filters
tools.description: Retrieve the list of supported event filters for Toggl webhooks. Use this when you need to know which event types are available for webhook subscriptions (e.g., client created, project updated, time entry deleted).

tools.name: Get JWKS Keys
tools.description: Retrieves the current JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) keyset used to sign JWT tokens. Use this to obtain public keys for verifying JWT token signatures issued by Toggl.

tools.name: List Clients
tools.description: Retrieve a list of clients from a Toggl Track workspace with optional filtering by status and name. Use this tool to: - List all clients in a workspace - Filter clients by active/archived status - Search for clients by name (case-insensitive) - Get client details including IDs, names, timestamps, and permissions By default, only active clients are returned unless specified otherwise.

tools.name: Get My Location
tools.description: Retrieves the authenticated user's last known location information including city, state, country, and coordinates. Use this to determine user's geographic location for timezone or region-specific features.

tools.name: Get My Quota
tools.description: Tool to retrieve API rate limit quota for the authenticated user. Use when you need to check remaining API calls before making further requests or to monitor rate limit status.

tools.name: Get Organization Details
tools.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific Toggl organization including subscription plan, trial status, user count, and workspace settings. Requires a valid organization ID that the authenticated user has access to.

tools.name: Get Organization Groups
tools.description: Retrieves all groups within a Toggl organization, including group members and workspace assignments. Groups are used to organize users and control access to workspaces. Returns an empty list if no groups exist in the organization.

tools.name: Get Organization Users
tools.description: Retrieves a list of users belonging to a Toggl organization. Returns detailed information about each user including their email, name, role, workspace memberships, and group memberships. Supports filtering by name/email, status (active/inactive/invited), admin privileges, and pagination. Use this when you need to list organization members or find specific users within an organization.

tools.name: Get Project Details
tools.description: Tool to retrieve details of a specific project. Use after confirming the workspace ID and project ID.

tools.name: Get Projects
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a list of projects from a Toggl workspace. Use after confirming workspace ID. Returns filtered and paginated projects with optional client details.

tools.name: Get Project Summary Report
tools.description: Load aggregate tracked-time and billing totals for one Toggl project.

tools.name: Get Public Subscription Plans
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all publicly available subscription plans from Toggl. Use when you need to display available pricing tiers or plan options to users.

tools.name: Get Webhooks Status
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the Toggl Webhooks server status. Use when you need to check if the webhooks service is operational before registering or managing webhook subscriptions.

tools.name: Get Tags
tools.description: Retrieve all tags in a Toggl workspace. Returns a list of tags with their IDs, names, and metadata. Use this when you need to list available tags for categorizing time entries or when searching for a specific tag by name. Returns an empty list if the workspace has no tags.

tools.name: List Tasks
tools.description: Tool to list tasks in a workspace or within a specific project.

tools.name: Get Time Entries
tools.description: Retrieve time entries for the authenticated user with flexible filtering options. Use this tool to: - List all recent time entries (no parameters needed) - Filter entries by date range (start_date + end_date) - Get entries modified since a specific time (since parameter for syncing) - Include project/tag metadata and sharing information Returns comprehensive details including project names, tags, duration, and billable status.

tools.name: Get Time Entry
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific time entry by its ID. Use when you have the entry ID and need its full details.

tools.name: Get Timezone Offsets
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all available timezone offsets from Toggl. Use when you need to display timezone information or validate timezone selection for time entry operations.

tools.name: Get Timezones
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all available timezones supported by Toggl Track. Use when you need to validate timezone values or display available timezone options to users.

tools.name: Get User Clients
tools.description: Retrieves all clients accessible to the authenticated user across all their workspaces. Returns a complete list of client details including workspace associations, archive status, notes, and integration information. Use this to view all clients the current user has access to without needing to specify individual workspace IDs.

tools.name: Get User Preferences
tools.description: Retrieves the authenticated user's preferences including timezone, date/time formats, notification settings, and enabled alpha/experimental features. Useful for understanding user display preferences or checking which optional features are available.

tools.name: Get User Projects
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all projects for the authenticated user. Use after authenticating to list available projects.

tools.name: Get User Tags
tools.description: Tool to retrieve tags associated with the current user. Use when you need to list all tags visible to your account across all workspaces, or to get tags that have been created/modified/deleted since a specific date for incremental syncing.

tools.name: Get User Tasks
tools.description: Retrieve all tasks across all workspaces accessible to the authenticated user. Returns tasks from projects the user can access, including task details like name, active status, estimated time, and tracked time. Use this to get a comprehensive list of tasks without needing to specify workspace or project IDs.

tools.name: Get User Workspaces
tools.description: Tool to retrieve all workspaces the authenticated user belongs to. Use when you need to list accessible workspaces before performing workspace-specific operations. Verify the correct workspace ID from the returned list before use — an incorrect workspace ID will misroute entries and skew reports.

tools.name: Get Workspace Details
tools.description: Retrieves comprehensive details and settings for a specific Toggl workspace by ID. Returns workspace configuration including premium/business status, admin permissions, default settings for projects/billing, time tracking preferences, and organizational details. Use this when you need to inspect workspace properties or validate access before performing workspace-specific operations.

tools.name: Get Workspace Logo
tools.description: Tool to get workspace logo. Use when you need to retrieve the logo associated with a specific workspace.

tools.name: Get Workspace Preferences
tools.description: Retrieves workspace preferences including the initial pricing plan and whether start/end times are hidden. Use this after obtaining a workspace ID to check workspace-level preference settings.

tools.name: Get Workspace Users
tools.description: Retrieves all users who belong to a specific Toggl workspace. Returns user details including their name, email, admin status, and activity status. Use this to list workspace members, check user roles, or verify user access to a workspace.

tools.name: Stop Time Entry
tools.description: Tool to stop a running time entry in a workspace. Use when a time entry needs to be ended.

tools.name: Disable Product Emails
tools.description: Tool to disable product emails for the authenticated user using a disable code. Use when the user wants to unsubscribe from Toggl product emails using a code from an unsubscribe link.

tools.name: Update Tag
tools.description: Tool to update an existing tag in a specified workspace. Use after confirming the workspace_id and tag_id when renaming a tag. Example: rename tag 'urgent' to 'high_priority'.

tools.name: Search Detailed Report Time Entries
tools.description: Search detailed-report time entries; provide at least one report filter.

tools.name: Send Demo Email
tools.description: Tool to send a demo request email through Toggl's system. Use when someone wants to request a product demo.

tools.name: Send Email to Contact
tools.description: Tool to send an email to a contact via Toggl's smail service. Use when you need to send a message to a specific contact by providing their email, name, and message content.

tools.name: Send Smail Meet
tools.description: Tool to send an email for meet. Use when you need to send a meet invitation email to a specific recipient with a location.

tools.name: Update Client
tools.description: Updates an existing client in a Toggl workspace. Use this to modify a client's name or notes. Note: The Toggl API requires the 'name' field when updating any client property.

tools.name: Update Project
tools.description: Update one Toggl project; provide at least one field to change.

tools.name: Trelloreadboard
tools.description: Read Trello boards. Supports listing boards the authenticated user is a member of, listing all boards a user can access within a specific workspace (regardless of membership), fetching a single board by ARI or URL, listing labels on a board, listing a board's custom field definitions, and listing a board's action/history.

tools.name: Trelloreadcard
tools.description:
Fetch a Trello card's full details, or list cards across a board or list to surface open work items.
Use this tool when you know the specific board, list, or card you want to inspect.
For keyword-based discovery across all boards/cards, use trelloSearch instead.
Actions:
- "get": fetch a single card by id or card URL (cardIdOrUrl required). Returns core card
  fields, labels (up to 25; truncation signalled via labelsHasMore), and comments
  (up to 25; truncation signalled via commentsHasMore).
- "list_by_board": fetch all cards for a board grouped by list (boardIdOrUrl required).
  Response: { lists: [{ id, name, cards: [...] }], hasNextPage, nextCursor }.
  Each page contains up to 5 lists (configurable via limit); each list contains all its cards.
  Filter by card state: "open" (default), "archived", or "all".
  Use cursor/limit to paginate over lists (max 50 lists per page).
- "list_by_list": fetch cards in a Trello list (listId required) with cursor-based pagination.
  Use this when the user asks for cards in a list or all cards from a specific list.
  Response: { cards: [...], pageInfo: { hasNextPage, endCursor } }.
  Filter by card state: "open" (default), "archived", or "all".
  Use cursor/limit to paginate (max 50 cards per page).
- "get_comment": fetch a single comment on a card by its action ID (cardIdOrUrl and commentId required).
  For this action, cardIdOrUrl must be a Trello card ARI so the workspace is explicit for authorization.
  Response: { id, text, createdAt, lastEditedAt, creator, cardId }.
- "list_comments": list comments on a card, newest first (cardIdOrUrl required).
  Response: { comments: [{ id, text, createdAt, lastEditedAt, creator }], pageInfo: { hasNextPage, endCursor } }.
  Use cursor/limit to paginate (default 25, max 50 comments per page).
- "list_attachments": list files and links attached to a card (cardIdOrUrl required).
  Response: { attachments: [{ id, name, fileName, url, mimeType, bytes, createdAt, isUpload, isMalicious }], pageInfo: { hasNextPage, endCursor } }.
  Use cursor/limit to paginate (default 25, max 50 attachments per page).
- "list_custom_field_items": list the custom field values set on a card (cardIdOrUrl required).
  Pairs with trelloReadBoard "list_custom_fields" for the field definitions these values belong to.
  Response: { customFieldItems: [{ id, customField: { id, name, type }, value: { text, number, date, checked, optionId } }], pageInfo: { hasNextPage, endCursor } }.
  Only the value field matching the customField.type is populated (e.g. text fields set value.text). optionId references a customField option for list/dropdown fields.
  Use cursor/limit to paginate (default 25, max 50 items per page).
- "list_activity": list a card's full activity history, newest first (cardIdOrUrl required).
  Unlike "list_comments" this is unfiltered: comments, moves between lists, member add/remove,
  due-date changes, attachments and checklist item state changes all appear in one feed.
  Response: { activity: [{ id, type, displayKey, date, creator, ...typeSpecificFields }], pageInfo: { hasNextPage, endCursor } }.
  Every entry has id, type, displayKey, date and creator. Type-specific fields are present only
  for their own action type and omitted otherwise: commentText/commentLastEditedAt, listBefore/listAfter,
  member, attachment, dueDate, checkItem. Other action types appear with the common fields alone.
  Trello reuses "type" across different edits (a list move and a due-date change are both "updateCard"),
  so branch on "displayKey" or on which type-specific field is present, rather than on "type" alone.
  Same entry shape as trelloReadBoard "list_activity", minus its "card" field.
  Every entry is an action on the card you asked for; name that entity type when you report one.
  Use "list_comments" when the user only wants the discussion; use "list_activity" for
  "what happened to this card" or "who changed this and when".
  Use cursor/limit to paginate (default 25, max 50 entries per page).

Due date timezone handling: Card due dates (due.date) are stored as UTC ISO 8601 timestamps.
For "today" or date-based due-date requests, first call trelloReadMember (get_me) for prefs.timezone and interpret due dates in the user's local time.

tools.name: Trelloreadchecklist
tools.description: Read Trello checklists (and their check items) attached to a card. Supported actions: "list_by_card" — list checklists on a card (cardId required); cursor/limit page the checklists. "get" — fetch a single checklist by id (checklistId required). In both actions each checklist is returned with its complete `items` list embedded.

tools.name: Trelloreadinbox
tools.description: Triage and review the authenticated user's Trello Inbox — the personal quick-capture board where new cards and notifications land. Use this specifically for the user's Inbox board. For cards on other boards or lists, use trelloReadCard instead. Actions: "get" — return the Inbox board details (id, objectId, lastActivityAt). No additional arguments are needed. "list_cards" — list cards in the Inbox with optional filtering and pagination. Each card includes labels and up to 25 checklists (truncation signalled via checklistsHasMore). Filter by card state: "open" (default), "archived", or "all". Use cursor/limit to paginate (limit defaults to 25, max 50).

tools.name: Trelloreadlist
tools.description:
Read Trello lists. Supported actions: "list_by_board" — list the open lists on a board (id, name, position, objectId) with cursor-based pagination (limit defaults to 25, max 50); "get" — return a single list by id, including up to 25 nested cards (id, name).
- "list_activity" — page through open cards currently in a list and return each card's recent activity. Only the cards are paginated (cursor/limit, defaults to 25 cards, max 50); each card returns its 25 most recent activity entries. Use trelloReadCard to get a single card's full history.
  Every entry is an action on the card it is grouped under; name that entity type when you report one.

tools.name: Trelloreadmember
tools.description: Get a Trello member's profile. Call action="get_me" FIRST before any due-date query (e.g. "cards due today", "overdue cards") to get prefs.timezone (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles") so due dates can be interpreted in the user's local time rather than UTC. Also use action="get_me" to look up the current user's username, fullName, email, or avatarUrl. Supported actions: "get_me" — returns the authenticated user's Trello member profile (id, username, fullName, email, avatarUrl, url, prefs) via the Trello GraphQL API. "get" — returns another Trello member's profile (id, username, fullName, avatarUrl, url, prefs) by memberId. "list_by_board" — lists a board's members with their board role (admin, member, observer) by boardId, with cursor-based pagination (limit defaults to 25, max 100). "list_by_workspace" — lists a workspace's members with their workspace role (admin, member) by workspaceId, with the same cursor-based pagination. Workspace membership cannot be filtered by role. "list_by_card" — returns a paginated list of members assigned to a card, with nextCursor and hasMore.

tools.name: Trelloreadplanner
tools.description: Read Trello Planner information for the authenticated user. Supported actions: "get" — returns the current member's planner (id, primaryAccountId, primaryCalendarId, primaryCalendar details); "list_events" — lists calendar events for a given planner calendar in a time window (plannerCalendarId, providerAccountId, start, end required; limit defaults to 25, max 50; cursor-based pagination supported); "get_event" — returns a single calendar event by provider event id (eventId, providerAccountId, plannerCalendarId required). Timezone handling: start and end must be UTC ISO 8601. For relative time queries like "today" or "this week", first use the "get" action to retrieve primaryCalendar.timezone, then convert to UTC before calling "list_events".

tools.name: Trelloreadworkspace
tools.description: Read Trello workspaces (organizations) the current user has access to. Supported actions: "list" — list workspaces visible to the authenticated user (cursor-based pagination, limit defaults to 25, max 100); "get" — fetch detailed data for a single workspace by id (typically used after "list" to drill into a workspace).

tools.name: Trellosearch
tools.description: Discover Trello boards or cards by keyword across all workspaces. Use this when the user wants to find something by name or content but does not know which board it is on. If the user already knows the board or list they want to browse, use trelloReadCard (list_by_board or list_by_list) instead — it is faster and returns richer grouped results. Supported actions: "search_boards" — search for boards by name, always include each board's `url` verbatim in the response; "search_cards" — search for cards by name/content. Both support optional workspace scoping and cursor-based pagination. Both actions return open (non-archived) results by default. To search archived items instead, include `is:archived` in the query. "search_cards" additionally supports boardIds scoping and qualifiers: label:, board:, list:, member:, due:, has:. For archived/closed cards, use `is:archived` or `is:closed` (they are equivalent for cards only). For archived boards, use `is:archived` only — boards do not support the `is:closed` alias. Due date timezone handling: Trello due-date search qualifiers use UTC boundaries. For "today" or date-based due-date queries, first call trelloReadMember (get_me) for prefs.timezone and account for the user's local timezone.

tools.name: Trellowriteboard
tools.description: Create Trello boards. Supported actions: "create" — create a Trello board in a workspace with a name, visibility, and optional preferences.

tools.name: Trellowritecard
tools.description: Create, update, move, archive, mark Trello cards done, or manage labels on cards. Supported actions: "create" — create a card on a list (listId and name required; desc, due, pos optional); "update" — update an existing card (cardId required; at least one of name, desc, due required); "move" — move a card to another list, optionally across boards (cardId and listId required, where listId is the destination list; boardId is optional and only needed when moving to a list on a different board; pos is optional and sets the card position in the destination list); "archive" — archive a card (cardId required); "mark_done" — mark a card as complete (cardId required); "attach_label" — attach a label to a card (cardId and labelId required); "detach_label" — detach a label from a card (cardId and labelId required). "add_comment" — post a comment on a card (cardId and text required); "update_comment" — replace the text of an existing comment on a card (cardId, commentId and text required).

tools.name: Trellowritechecklist
tools.description: Write Trello checklists and their check items. Actions: "create" — add a new checklist to a card by cardId and name, optionally placed at "top", "bottom", or an explicit numeric position. Returns the created checklist as a TrelloChecklist (id, objectId, name, position, checkItems[]). "add_item" — append a new check item to an existing checklist by checklistId and text, optionally placed at "top", "bottom", or an explicit numeric position. Returns the created check item (id, name, state, position) using the same normalized shape as trelloReadChecklist. "update_item" — update an existing check item by checklistId and itemId; supports renaming (text), toggling completion (checked), repositioning (pos), and moving to another checklist on the same card (toChecklistId). Returns the updated check item. "update" — rename a checklist (`name`) and/or change its position on its card (`pos`) by checklistId. At least one of `name` or `pos` must be supplied. Returns the resulting checklist in the same normalized shape as trelloReadChecklist (id, name, position, checkItems[]).

tools.name: Trellowriteinbox
tools.description: Write Trello Inbox cards. Supported actions: "create" — create a new card in the Trello Inbox (name required; desc and due are optional). The Inbox list is resolved automatically — no listId needed. "update" — update fields on an existing Inbox card (cardId required; at least one of name, desc, or due required). "move" — move an Inbox card to another list and board (cardId, listId, and boardId required; pos optional). "archive" — archive an existing Inbox card (cardId required; no other fields allowed). Returns the created, updated, moved, or archived card including its id.

tools.name: Trellowritelist
tools.description: Create, update, archive, or move a Trello list. Supported actions: "create" — create a new list on a board (boardId and name required; pos optional); "update" — rename an existing list (listId and name required); "archive" — soft-delete (close) a list (listId required); "move" — reposition a list, optionally moving it to another board (listId and pos required; boardId is optional and only needed when moving the list to a different board).

tools.name: Trellowriteplanner
tools.description: Create Trello Planner calendar events and manage card-event links. Supported actions: "create_event" — create a calendar event (title, start, and end required; if cardId is provided, the event is linked to that card and title defaults to the card name); "link_card_to_event" — link an existing card to an existing event (cardId and eventId required); "unlink_card_from_event" — unlink a card from an event (cardId and eventId required). providerAccountId and calendarId are optional for all actions; when omitted the user's primary calendar account is used.

Use this tool when you need to find hotels in a city, region, or geographic area. Provide a TripAdvisor location ID (e.g., '60745' for Boston, '60763' for New York City, '186338' for London) to get nearby hotels with their names, addresses, and distances from the center point. The tool performs a two-step process: 1. Retrieves location details (coordinates) for the given location_id 2. The API returns a maximum of 5 photos per request with no pagination options. Use this to display location images for hotels, restaurants, attractions, or destinations.

tools.name: Get Location Reviews V2

tools.name: Check Model Riggability

tools.name: Complete Mesh
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to complete selected segmented parts or cap open boundaries. Requires a successful segmentation bare task UUID and returns a new bare task UUID for GET_TASK or GET_TASKS.

tools.name: Convert Model
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to convert a model format and optionally alter topology, textures, orientation, scale, or animation export. Returns a bare UUID task ID.

tools.name: Create Presigned Upload
tools.description: Reserve a presigned URL and file token for a client-managed upload. This action only reserves the upload and does not upload bytes. A separate raw PUT to presigned_url is required without Tripo Authorization or any connected-account credentials; the file token is usable only after that PUT completes successfully.

tools.name: Decimate Mesh
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to reduce a model's polygon count using basic decimation or smart retopology. Returns a bare UUID task ID.

tools.name: Edit Image
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to edit one or more reference images. Returns a bare UUID task ID; completed generated image URLs are temporary.

tools.name: Edit Multiview
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to apply view-specific text edits to a multiview set. Returns a bare UUID task ID; completed view URLs are temporary.

tools.name: Generate Image from Text
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous image-generation task from a text prompt. Returns a bare UUID task ID; use GET_TASK or GET_TASKS to retrieve the result, and download the temporary generated_image_url promptly.

tools.name: Generate Model from Image
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to generate a 3D model from one image, file token, or successful image-task UUID. Returns a bare UUID task ID for GET_TASK or GET_TASKS.

tools.name: Generate Model from Multiview
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to generate a 3D model from multiple views or one multiview task UUID. Returns a bare UUID task ID for later status queries.

tools.name: Generate Model from Text
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to generate a 3D model from text. Returns a bare UUID task ID immediately; query it with GET_TASK or GET_TASKS and download completed output URLs promptly.

tools.name: Generate Multiview from Image
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to generate front, left, back, and right views from one image. Returns a bare UUID task ID; use GET_TASK or GET_TASKS to retrieve the result, and download the four temporary view URLs promptly.

tools.name: Generate Splat from Image
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to generate a Gaussian Splat scene from one image. Returns a bare UUID task ID; use GET_TASK or GET_TASKS to retrieve the result, and download the temporary .splat model URL promptly.

tools.name: Get Balance

tools.name: Get Task
tools.description: Get status, progress, errors, credits, timestamps, and type-specific output for one asynchronous task. Use a bare UUID without a task_ prefix. Download successful output URLs promptly because they are temporary.

tools.name: Get Tasks
tools.description: Get snapshots for up to 100 asynchronous task UUIDs in one request. Inspect missed even on success because it lists unknown IDs. Prefer this tool when polling parallel jobs every 1-2 seconds, and download successful output URLs promptly because they are temporary.

tools.name: Import Model

tools.name: Retarget Animation

tools.name: Rig Model
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to attach a biped or creature skeleton to a model. Run CHECK_MODEL_RIGGABILITY first and use its recommended rig type. Returns a bare UUID task ID for GET_TASK or GET_TASKS.

tools.name: Segment Mesh
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to split a model into geometry-based or semantically labeled parts. Returns a bare UUID task ID used by COMPLETE_MESH or task-status tools.

tools.name: Texture Model
tools.description: Submit a credit-consuming asynchronous task to apply or regenerate textures on an existing model. Returns a bare UUID task ID; completed model and preview URLs are temporary.

tools.name: Upload File
tools.description: Upload one image or model to Tripo3D and return a reusable file token for generation or processing tools. Provider operations may still accept supported public URLs where their input schema permits.

tools.description: Resolve a company, investor firm, or person by providing exactly one supported search field: name, id, domain, linkedin, crunchbase, or twitter. Use this lightweight lookup before a full detail read or filtered discovery; it can consume fractional credits.

name: Twenty
description: The #1 Open-Source CRM. Modern, powerful, affordable platform to manage your customer relationships.

tools.name: Batch Create CRM Records
tools.description: Create 1-60 records of one type. Supported standard fields: companies (name, domainName, linkedinLink, annualRevenue, address, accountOwnerId); people (name, emails, linkedinLink, jobTitle, phones, avatarUrl, companyId); opportunities (name, amount, closeDate, stage, companyId, pointOfContactId, ownerId); tasks (title, bodyV2, dueAt, status, assigneeId). Custom fields, workspace-specific enum variants, and upsert are not supported.

tools.name: Create CRM Record
tools.description: Create one company, person, opportunity, or task using the supported standard fields in the parameter schema. Custom fields and workspace-specific enum variants are not supported.

tools.name: Delete CRM Record
tools.description: Permanently delete one company, person, opportunity, or task by UUID. Use only for a specifically identified record; this does not delete by filter or in bulk.

tools.name: Get CRM Record
tools.description: Get one company, person, opportunity, or task by its Twenty UUID, optionally including direct relations.

tools.name: List CRM Fields
tools.description: List field definitions from the connected Twenty workspace to discover exact field names, types, editability, nullability, uniqueness, and relation targets for schema inspection and filters. Record writes accept only fields exposed by the Create or Update CRM Record parameter schema.

tools.name: List CRM Objects
tools.description: List standard and custom object definitions in the connected Twenty workspace for schema inspection. Record tools currently support only companies, people, opportunities, and tasks.

tools.name: List CRM Records
tools.description: List companies, people, opportunities, or tasks with Twenty filter syntax, ordering, relation depth, and forward cursor pagination.

tools.name: Update CRM Record
tools.description: Partially update one company, person, opportunity, or task by UUID using the supported standard fields in the parameter schema; only supplied fields change. Custom fields and workspace-specific enum variants are not supported.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: In your Twenty Cloud workspace, go to Settings -> API & Webhooks -> + Create key. Copy the API key immediately because Twenty displays it only once.

name: TwitterShots
description: TwitterShots renders public X posts as screenshots and retrieves tweet content and API usage.

tools.name: Generate Temporary Screenshot URL
tools.description: Render a public tweet or post and return a provider-hosted temporary URL. Download the result promptly or use Generate Tweet Screenshot when it must be retained. A successful render consumes one API credit.

tools.name: Generate Tweet Screenshot
tools.description: Render a public tweet or post as an SVG, PNG, or HTML file suitable for saving. A successful render consumes one API credit.

tools.name: Get API Usage
tools.description: Return the remaining and total TwitterShots API credits for the connected API key. This read does not consume a credit.

tools.name: Get Bulk Tweet Content
tools.description: Fetch up to 100 public tweets as one Markdown document. Inspect the returned Markdown for a 'Failed to fetch tweets' section because individual IDs can fail within an HTTP 200 response. A successful bulk request consumes one API credit.

tools.name: Get Tweet Content
tools.description: Fetch one public tweet as structured Markdown, with optional statistics, media links, and quoted-tweet content. A successful call consumes one API credit.

required.name: generic_api_key
required.description: Your TwitterShots API key. Create or copy it from Account Settings > API Keys at https://twittershots.com/settings/keys, then keep it secret.

name: Twocaptcha
description: 2Captcha is a service that provides automated CAPTCHA solving solutions, enabling developers to bypass various types of CAPTCHAs in their applications.

tools.name: Create CAPTCHA Task
tools.description: Creates a new CAPTCHA-solving task and returns a taskId for retrieving results. Supports multiple captcha types: reCAPTCHA v2/v3, hCaptcha, image recognition, and more. After creating a task, use the returned taskId with getTaskResult to retrieve the solution. Requires sufficient account balance to process tasks.

tools.name: Get Account Balance
tools.description: Tool to retrieve your 2Captcha account balance in USD. Use when you need to check available funds before creating captcha-solving tasks.

tools.name: Report Incorrect CAPTCHA
tools.description: Report that a CAPTCHA solution was declined by the target website. Use this action to provide feedback when a solved CAPTCHA is rejected, enabling 2Captcha to improve accuracy and potentially issue refunds for incorrectly solved tasks.

tools.name: Report Incorrect Image Captcha
tools.description: Report that an image captcha solution was incorrect. Alias for reportIncorrect method. Use this when you receive an incorrect captcha solution from 2Captcha to report the issue. Made for compatibility with certain software libraries. Successful reports may result in refunds.

tools.name: Test Request Parameters
tools.description: Debug method to verify how the API parses request parameters. Use when troubleshooting integration issues or validating parameter formats.

required.name: generic_key
required.description: Your unique API key for accessing 2Captcha services.

name: Typecast
description: Typecast is an AI voice platform for generating expressive speech, discovering voices, and managing custom voices.

tools.name: Compose Speech
tools.description: Generate one audio file from an ordered sequence of speech and pause segments.

tools.name: Generate Speech
tools.description: Generate a complete WAV or MP3 audio file from text using a Typecast voice.

tools.name: Generate Speech With Timestamps
tools.description: Generate speech plus word, character, or both alignment timestamp arrays.

tools.name: Get Subscription
tools.description: Get the connected Typecast API plan, credit usage, concurrency limit, and custom-voice allowance.

tools.name: Get Voice
tools.description: Get one voice's metadata, supported models, and available emotions by voice ID.

tools.name: List Voices
tools.description: List available built-in and owned custom Typecast voices, optionally filtered by speech model, gender, age, use case, and voice type. Returns each voice ID with the model versions and emotions it supports for use in speech synthesis.

tools.name: Recommend Voices
tools.description: Find and rank Typecast voices that match a natural-language description.

required.name: generic_api_key
